title: fix(core): Add connection timeout and diagnostics to S3 object store
body:
## Summary

Fix `ObjectStoreService.checkConnection()` hanging indefinitely when an S3 host is misconfigured (most commonly: `https` against an HTTP-only S3-compatible endpoint such as SeaweedFS), which blocks all route registration and leaves the editor UI unreachable while `/healthz` still returns 200.

**Root cause:** `HeadBucketCommand.send()` has no timeout. When TCP connects but the TLS handshake never completes, the call hangs forever, and because `objectStoreService.init()` is awaited during startup, no other routes ever register.

**Changes**

- **Hard timeout on the connection check.** `checkConnection()` now passes `AbortSignal.timeout(connectionTimeoutMs)` to `HeadBucketCommand`, so the check fails fast even when TLS hangs.
- **Defense-in-depth at the transport layer.** The S3 client now uses an explicit `NodeHttpHandler` with `connectionTimeout` and `requestTimeout`, so socket-level hangs are also bounded.
- **New env var `N8N_EXTERNAL_STORAGE_S3_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT`** (default `10000` ms). Operators on higher-latency networks can tune it.
- **Startup visibility.** Logs the resolved S3 endpoint, bucket, region, and `forcePathStyle` at info level, so operators can immediately verify the configuration.
- **Actionable error message.** On failure, the error names the resolved endpoint and points to the relevant env vars (`N8N_EXTERNAL_STORAGE_S3_HOST`, `N8N_EXTERNAL_STORAGE_S3_PROTOCOL`).
- **Explicit dependency.** `@smithy/node-http-handler` is now declared in `packages/core/package.json` (it was previously only available transitively via `@aws-sdk/client-s3`).

The defaults are unchanged for everyone else — existing working deployments behave identically.

### How to test

**Minimal local repro** (no SeaweedFS needed):

```bash
# Terminal 1 — silent TCP listener that accepts but never responds
nc -kl 9999

# Terminal 2 — start n8n pointed at it (defaults to https)
N8N_EXTERNAL_STORAGE_S3_HOST=127.0.0.1:9999 \
N8N_EXTERNAL_STORAGE_S3_BUCKET_NAME=test \
N8N_DEFAULT_BINARY_DATA_MODE=s3 \
pnpm start
```

- **Before this change:** n8n hangs after "Registered runner"; "Editor is now accessible" never prints.
- **After this change:** within ~10 s, n8n logs `S3 binary storage configured: endpoint=https://127.0.0.1:9999, ...` and then fails startup with `Failed to connect to S3 at https://127.0.0.1:9999 (bucket: test). Verify that N8N_EXTERNAL_STORAGE_S3_HOST includes the port, N8N_EXTERNAL_STORAGE_S3_PROTOCOL is correct, and the endpoint is reachable.`

**Unit tests:** new assertions cover the abort signal, the request handler, the new error message, and the startup log line. Run with:

```bash
cd packages/core && pnpm test object-store
```

### Lockfile changes

`pnpm-lock.yaml` is updated as a side-effect of declaring `@smithy/node-http-handler` (`^4.0.4`) as a direct dependency. All churn is confined to `@smithy/*` and `tslib` and is pure deduplication (the lockfile previously had three coexisting versions of `@smithy/node-http-handler`; it now consolidates to one).

title: refactor(editor): Extract per-thread runtime from Instance AI store (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Move per-thread state and methods out of \`instanceAi.store.ts\` (1110 lines) into a new \`instanceAi.threadRuntime.ts\` module (~900 lines). The store shrinks to ~280 lines covering instance-level concerns (thread list, credits, settings delegation, research/debug mode) and orchestrates a single mutable runtime via \`switchTo(threadId)\`.

The store re-exports the runtime's refs/methods, so its external surface is unchanged — none of the 23 consumer files (components, composables, tests) need updates.

### What's in the runtime

- All per-thread state: \`messages\`, \`activeRunId\`, \`archivedWorkflowIds\`, \`latestTasks\`, \`debugEvents\`, \`resolvedConfirmationIds\`, \`pendingMessageCount\`, \`hydratingThreadId\`, \`sseState\`, \`lastEventIdByThread\`, \`amendContext\`
- All per-thread methods: \`sendMessage\`, \`cancelRun\`, \`cancelBackgroundTask\`, \`amendAgent\`, \`confirmAction\`, \`confirmResourceDecision\`, \`resolveConfirmation\`, \`findToolCallByRequestId\`, \`copyFullTrace\`, \`loadHistoricalMessages\`, \`loadThreadStatus\`, \`connectSSE\`, \`closeSSE\`
- The reducer state, SSE connection, and hydration tokens (previously module-level \`let\` declarations) are now closure-level inside \`createThreadRuntime\` — necessary precondition for future multi-thread runtimes, and gives test isolation today

### Pure helpers extracted along the way

- \`collapseDeltaEvents(events)\` — pulls the text-delta/reasoning-delta merging out of \`copyFullTrace\` so it's independently testable
- \`buildRoutingFromMessages(messages)\` — pulls the \`runStateByGroupId\`/\`groupIdByRunId\` rebuild loop out of \`loadHistoricalMessages\`

### Hooks boundary

The runtime no longer reads store state directly. Cross-runtime callbacks go through \`ThreadRuntimeHooks\`:

- \`getResearchMode()\` — read at \`sendMessage\` time
- \`onTitleUpdated(threadId, title)\` — SSE \`thread-title-updated\` event
- \`onRunFinish()\` — refresh thread list to pick up server-generated titles
- \`syncThread(threadId)\` — promote a not-yet-persisted thread to server-side

### Why

Sets up the structural separation needed to later support multiple simultaneous live threads (\`Map<threadId, ThreadRuntime>\` with provide/inject), without introducing them in this PR. Each runtime is fully self-contained — call \`createThreadRuntime()\` N times and you get N independent instances.

## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts

n/a — no behavior change.

When a user asks the n8n Instance AI to share or use a Form Trigger production URL, the agent currently builds it from the webhook base URL — producing `<base>/webhook/<id>`, which 404s. title: fix(core): Allow profile edits when SSO is no longer active
body:
## Summary

After enabling and then disabling SAML SSO, users who previously authenticated via SAML were permanently blocked from updating their profile (name, email) through `PATCH /me`. The endpoint returned `400: "SAML user may not change their profile information"`, requiring a manual `auth_identity` row deletion in the database to unblock them.

The guard at `me.controller.ts` checked only for the existence of an `auth_identity` row; it did not check whether the user's SSO provider was still active. This PR fixes the guard so it gates on the matching provider also being currently licensed/enabled, restoring profile-edit capability when SSO has been switched off.

## Why

Bug report: an instance owner enabled SAML, authenticated through it (which created their `auth_identity` row), then disabled SAML to fall back to email auth. The `auth_identity` row persists by design (it's still meaningful data in case SAML is re-enabled), but the profile guard was ignoring whether the provider was actually serving traffic. Net effect: a high-impact lockout in an Enterprise feature surface, with the only workaround being a DB row deletion.

## How to test manually

Prerequisites: a self-hosted instance with the SAML feature licensed (`feat:saml`).

1. Sign in as the instance owner with email auth.
2. Enable SAML SSO (Settings → SSO → SAML), point it at any IdP, complete the loginEnabled toggle.
3. Authenticate as the owner via SAML (creates the `auth_identity` row of type `saml`).
4. Disable SAML SSO (toggle `loginEnabled` off).
5. Go to Settings → Personal and change the first name. Save.
   - **Before this PR**: `400 "SAML user may not change their profile information"`.
   - **After this PR**: `200`, profile updates persist.
6. Re-enable SAML and repeat step 5 — the request should be rejected again with `400` (regression guard).
7. Repeat the cycle for an OIDC-enabled instance — same behavior expected (profile edits allowed when OIDC is disabled, blocked while OIDC is the active method).

Edge cases covered by automated tests:
- LDAP active vs. disabled with a stale `ldap` `auth_identity`.
- Email change is also unblocked once SAML is disabled (separate guard inside `validateChangingUserEmail`).
- A `token-exchange` `auth_identity` no longer blocks profile edits regardless of OIDC state.
- Email-only users (no `auth_identity`) are unaffected.

## Key implementation decisions

- **Per-provider active check.** Added `isAuthIdentityActive(authIdentity)` to `MeController`, dispatching on `providerType`:
  - `saml` → `isSamlLicensedAndEnabled()`
  - `oidc` → `isOidcCurrentAuthenticationMethod()`
  - `ldap` → `isLdapCurrentAuthenticationMethod()`
  - default (incl. `token-exchange`) → `false`
  Chose this over a single "is the user's provider the current auth method?" check so each provider can keep its own licensing/enable semantics (SAML in particular must also be licensed, not just current).
- **No `auth_identity` cleanup on SSO disable.** Considered but rejected — the rows are intentionally retained so re-enabling the provider doesn't lose binding state. Fixing the guard is the correct layer.
- **Test layer split.**
  - Unit tests in `me.controller.test.ts` cover the guard branches (SAML/LDAP/OIDC active vs inactive, `token-exchange`, no-op payload).
  - One integration test in `saml/saml.api.test.ts` exercises the full flow with a real DB and the `setSamlLoginEnabled` toggle, mirroring the reported repro.
- **Test performance.** Refactored the `me.controller.test.ts` away from `mock<User>(...)` / `mock<AuthIdentity>(...)` / `mock<AuthenticatedRequest>(...)` to plain literals + `as unknown as Type` casts. The `jest-mock-extended` deep proxies were causing severe super-linear slowdown when many tests ran in the same file (CI saw the file at **436 s**, with `should allow profile update for non-env-managed owner` alone at **322 s**). After the refactor the whole file runs in **~3 s** (47 tests). The slow tests were not new — they have been silently dominating backend unit-test wall time.

title: fix(core): Advance Postgres IDENTITY sequences after entity import
body:
## Summary

Manually verified locally - workflow indexing no longer throws the error message I posted in the ticket.

Claude generated below:

The entity importer inserts rows with explicit ids, but Postgres IDENTITY sequences only advance on implicit (`nextval`-driven) inserts. After import, the next implicit insert into any affected table starts the sequence at 1, colliding with rows the import just wrote and failing the PK constraint.

This adds `advanceIdentitySequences` to `ImportService`, which runs `setval(pg_get_serial_sequence(table, col), MAX(col))` for every IDENTITY column in every imported table. SQLite is unaffected (its `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` auto-bumps on explicit-id inserts), so the helper is gated on `dbType === 'postgres'`.

### How to reproduce (before this fix)

1. Run `n8n export:entities --outputDir=/tmp/export` against a SQLite instance with at least one workflow.
2. Run `n8n import:entities --inputDir=/tmp/export --truncateTables` against a fresh Postgres instance (matching encryption key).
3. Start that Postgres-backed n8n. The workflow-index builder runs on startup and errors:

   > duplicate key value violates unique constraint "PK_52325e34cd7a2f0f67b0f3cad65"

   Affects every imported table with an integer auto-id PK, including `workflow_dependency`, `workflow_publish_history`, `insights_by_period`, `insights_metadata`, and `user_favorites`.

### Verification

End-to-end smoke test against a fresh Postgres 16 container after import:

| table | MAX(id) | sequence last_value |
|---|---|---|
| workflow_dependency | 116 | 116 |
| workflow_publish_history | 13 | 13 |
| user_favorites | 2 | 2 |
| insights_metadata | 1 | 1 |
| insights_by_period | 12 | 12 |

Pre-fix `workflow_dependency` was at sequence value `12` against `MAX = 67`, which produced the duplicate-key error on the first downstream write.

## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts

https://linear.app/n8n/issue/ADO-5179 — discovered while testing https://linear.app/n8n/issue/ADO-5143 against Postgres.

title: fix: Replay sub-agent conversation on credential-setup nudge (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary


> User asks the assistant to set up a credential (e.g. "Set up a Slack OAuth2 credential for me in n8n").
> The assistant opens Chrome and the user watches it work — navigates to [api.slack.com](http://api.slack.com/), creates a new app, picks a workspace, types the app name, clicks "Create App", lands on the App Credentials page. The Client ID is visible on screen. Everything looks right.
> 
> The assistant pauses for ~5–10 seconds. Nothing visibly happens.
> The assistant abruptly says something like:
> 
> "I apologize for the confusion, but I don't have an active browser session or context about which credential setup we were working on. It appears the conversation may have been interrupted or I'm missing the previous context.


When the credential-setup sub-agent ends without calling `pause-for-user`, the orchestrator nudges it via a second `subAgent.stream(nudgeText)` call. Each Mastra `agent.stream()` invocation starts a fresh conversation, so the nudged sub-agent receives only the nudge string with no memory of what it just did. It apologetically replies *"I don't have an active browser session or context"*, that text becomes the orchestration tool's return value, and the parent agent surfaces the apology back to the user — mid-credential-setup, with the relevant Chrome tab still showing the answers on screen.

**Fix:** replay the prior conversation as input to the nudge stream call by passing `activeStream.messageList.get.all.aiV5.model()` plus the nudge as a final user message. The sub-agent now sees `system → briefing → assistant turns + tool calls + tool results → nudge` and can compose the missing `pause-for-user` from real context. The nudge prompt and input-building helper live in a small Mastra-free module (`browser-credential-setup.nudge.ts`) so they're unit-testable without scaffolding the orchestration.

Adds a developer CLI in `@n8n/instance-ai` that renders the final system prompt for the main Instance Agent and every orchestration sub-agent, then writes one markdown file per agent into the package's gitignored `.output/prompts/` directory.

Useful for auditing the full prompt verbatim, diffing prompts across branches, or sharing them outside the codebase.

```bash
cd packages/@n8n/instance-ai
pnpm prompts:print
```

- `subagent-builder-tool.md` and `subagent-builder-sandbox.md` (both builder variants)
- `subagent-researcher.md`

- `subagent-browser-gateway.md` and `subagent-browser-chrome-mcp.md` (both browser-tool sources)

title: feat(core): Add eval-data agent tool and quality evaluation suite (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Adds a new instance-ai orchestration tool, **`eval-data`**, that asks the user whether to populate an existing eval DataTable with synthetic rows, then dispatches a sub-agent to generate them. Also adds **`evaluations/eval-data-quality/`** — an eval harness that mirrors `eval-setup-topology/` but validates that the generated dataset is compliant with the workflow's eval shape.

### Tool — `packages/@n8n/instance-ai/src/tools/`
- `orchestration/eval-data-agent.tool.ts` — the tool itself (suspend/resume confirmation, background-task dispatch, cleanup paths)
- `evals/eval-data-requirements.service.ts` — analyzes a workflow to find eval DataTable targets and infer input/expected/actual columns
- `evals/generate-sample-rows.service.ts` — drives the sample-row generation across diverse facets
- `evals/detect-ai-nodes.ts` — shared utility to detect AI/LLM nodes in a workflow
- Registered in `tools/index.ts` under `createOrchestrationTools`
- Schema: `'eval-data'` added to `DATA_TABLE_RENDER_HINT_TOOLS` in `instance-ai.schema.ts` so the UI renders the data-table card

### Eval suite — `packages/@n8n/instance-ai/evaluations/eval-data-quality/`
- `runner.ts` — creates an empty DataTable, rewrites the workflow's `dataTableId`, sends the prompt, auto-approves the eval-data confirmation, waits for settle, fetches rows, runs the verifier, cleans up
- `dataset-verifier.ts` — three-layer check:
  1. **Structural** — row count, column names + types, system-column tolerance
  2. **Schema-vs-shape** — input + expected_output cells populated, actual_* cells empty
  3. **Semantic** — pluggable LLM judge (`SemanticJudgeFn`) per declared criterion
- `tool-selection.ts` — verifies the agent actually called the eval-data tool
- `default-judge.ts` — Haiku-backed default judge (skippable via `--skip-judge`)
- `cli.ts` — CLI: `pnpm eval:data-quality [--filter ...] [--skip-judge]`
- `fixtures.ts`, `types.ts`, `exit-policy.ts`, `summary.ts`
- 6 test files / 44 unit tests

### Fixtures (hand-authored)
- Empty `data/eval-data-quality/{workflows,expectations}/` with `.gitkeep` placeholders. Each fixture is a workflow JSON with eval setup pre-applied + a `<slug>.dataset.json` declaring required columns, min row count, and semantic criteria.

### Client additions — `evaluations/clients/n8n-client.ts`
Additive only (no signature changes to existing methods):
- `createWorkflow`, `createDataTable`, `getDataTableRows`
- `WorkflowCreatePayload`, `DataTableCreateColumn`, `DataTableCreatePayload`, `DataTableResponse`, `DataTableRowOutput`, `DataTableRowsResponse`

## How to test

- Run unit tests: `cd packages/@n8n/instance-ai && pnpm test src/tools/evals src/tools/orchestration/__tests__/eval-data-agent.tool.test.ts evaluations/eval-data-quality/`
- Run typecheck + lint: `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint`
- Drop a workflow + sidecar into `evaluations/data/eval-data-quality/` and run `pnpm eval:data-quality` against a live n8n instance with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set

## Summary

This PR refactors all public API handlers to use the unified `PublicAPIEndpoint<TReq>` type defined in `handler.types.ts`. Previously, each handler returned inconsistent types (some used `Response`, some used `Promise<Response>`, some were untyped). The `PublicAPIEndpoint` type enforces a consistent signature — a tuple of optional middlewares followed by a strictly-typed handler — across all 16 handler files.

Changes:
- Updated `handler.types.ts` to export `PublicAPIEndpoint<TReq>` with a trailing `PublicAPIEndpointHandler<TReq>` tuple type
- Applied the type to all handlers: audit, community-packages, credentials, data-tables (columns, rows, main), discover, executions, folders, insights, projects, source-control, tags, users (EE), variables, workflows
- Standardized error handling patterns in handlers to align with the new type contract
- Added integration tests for the source-control public API handler

body:
## Summary

Adds `SHA1` as a selectable algorithm under the Crypto node's HMAC action (both V1 and V2). A number of existing signature schemes still require HMAC-SHA1 for interoperability with legacy APIs. The underlying `createHmac` call already supports it, so this is a UI-visible enum addition only — no changes to credentials, execution logic, or the Hash action's algorithm list.

HMAC-SHA1 is not cryptographically broken: HMAC's security does not depend on collision resistance of the underlying hash function, and NIST SP 800-107 continues to permit HMAC-SHA1 for interoperability with legacy APIs. fix(core): Throw on bare OutputSelector passed to .add()/.to()
body:
## Summary

When the workflow SDK received a bare `node.output(n)` (an `OutputSelector`) in `.add()` or `.to()`, it silently dropped the connection. The `OutputSelector` was cast to `NodeInstance`, `_currentNode` was left unset, and the chained `.to(target)` became a no-op because of the `if (this._currentNode)` guard. `validate_workflow` only complained when the target had zero incoming edges, so any target with another incoming wire hid the drop entirely.

This is the LLM-facing failure mode described in the ticket: models write `.add(node.output(n)).to(target)` instead of the correct `.add(node.output(n).to(target))` and the misuse fails silently.

The fix detects `OutputSelector` at the entry of `.add()` and `.to()` (and inside their array paths) and throws a `TypeError` that names the source node, the output index, and the correct shape.

### How to test

```ts
import { workflow, node, trigger } from '@n8n/workflow-sdk';

const t = trigger({ type: 'n8n-nodes-base.webhookTrigger', version: 1, config: {} });
const ifNode = node({ type: 'n8n-nodes-base.if', version: 2, config: { name: 'Branch' } });
const target = node({ type: 'n8n-nodes-base.set', version: 3, config: {} });

// Throws with a clear message instead of silently dropping the connection
workflow('id', 'wf').add(t).add(ifNode.output(0)).to(target);
//                              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ TypeError now points at .to() chained the wrong way
```

The documented form keeps working:

```ts
workflow('id', 'wf').add(t).add(ifNode.output(0).to(target));
```

Tests cover:
- `OutputSelector` passed to `.add()` (top-level and inside an array)
- `OutputSelector` passed to `.to()`
- The correct `node.output(n).to(target)` form still produces the expected connection

title: fix(core): Clarify 0-based indexing in workflow SDK prompts and JSDoc
body:
## Summary

The AI workflow builder occasionally generates workflows where parallel branches are wired to a Merge node starting at `.input(1)` instead of `.input(0)`, silently dropping the first branch. The root cause is ambiguous documentation — `.input(1)` reads naturally as "the first input" if you don't know it's 0-based.

This PR clarifies 0-based semantics everywhere the LLM sees indices:

- **JSDoc** on `NodeInstance.input(n)` / `.output(n)` and the `merge()` factory: explicit "0-based: `.input(0)` is the FIRST input" note, with corrected examples (`sourceA.to(merge.input(0))` rather than `nodeA.to(mergeNode.input(1))`).
- **SDK reference prompts** (`workflow-patterns.ts`, `workflow-patterns-detailed.ts`, `additional-functions.ts`, and the parallel copy in `ai-workflow-builder.ee`): annotate every `.input(n)` example with `// first input (index 0)` / `// second input (index 1)` so the pattern the model copies is unambiguous.
- **`workflow-rules.ts`**: new rule #5 stating the convention explicitly, with a wrong/right counter-example showing the exact off-by-one shape we're trying to prevent.

No runtime behaviour change — all edits are documentation/prompt strings.

title: fix(ai-builder): Resolve HitlTool variants to base node in get_node_types
body:
## Summary

`get_node_types` failed for every HITL tool variant (`slackHitlTool`, `chatHitlTool`, `emailSendHitlTool`, etc.) because:

1. HITL tools are synthesized at runtime by `createHitlTools()` and have no static type-definition files.
2. The existing `*Tool`-suffix fallback stripped only 4 chars, producing nonsense intermediate names (`slackHitlTool` → `slackHitl`) that don't exist either.
3. The error message reported the *last attempted* (stripped) ID rather than the original request — so users saw an error mentioning a name they never typed.

This change adds a `HitlTool` (8-char) fallback in `findNodeDir` and in `getNodeFilePath`'s outer fallback so HITL variants resolve to their base node (`slackHitlTool` → `slack`). When all fallbacks fail, the original node ID is preserved in the error message.

### How to test

```bash
pushd packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee
pnpm test code-builder-get.tool.test
popd
```

The new `tool variant fallback` describe block covers:
- HITL → flat-structure base (`emailSendHitlTool` → `emailSend`)
- HITL → langchain base (`@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.chatHitlTool` → `chat`)
- HITL → split-structure base with discriminators (`slackHitlTool` + resource/operation)
- Original ID preserved in error for unresolved `HitlTool` and plain `Tool` variants

End-to-end smoke test against the live MCP server confirmed all four scenarios resolve correctly through `mcp__n8n-mcp__get_node_types`.

## Summary

title: fix: Improve browser-use connection stability (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Hardens the connection between the n8n browser-use stack (CDP relay ↔ MV3 extension) and Playwright so credential-setup runs don't hang on idle service workers, never-firing `load` events, or wedged debugger sessions.

Changes:

- **JSON ping/pong heartbeat between the CDP relay and the browser extension.** Receiving an application-level JSON message resets the MV3 service worker's idle-termination timer; protocol-level `ws.ping` is handled by the browser without invoking JS, so it never reset the SW idle timer. Protocol-level ping is kept alongside for backward compatibility with older extensions.
- **Default `page.goto` `waitUntil` from `'load'` to `'domcontentloaded'`** in the Playwright adapter and the public navigation tool. Many SaaS dashboards never fire `load` because of analytics/long-poll connections, which surfaced as spurious navigation timeouts.
- **Drop per-CDP-command timeout from 30s to 10s** and add a watchdog in the extension's `forwardCDPCommand` that force-detaches the debugger session on hang. The next call re-attaches fresh via `ensureAttached()` instead of inheriting a wedged session. The watchdog timer is cleared in a `finally` so it never fires for commands that already returned.
- **Reset the browser session at the end of every credential-setup orchestration run** (success or failure). Stale tab/debugger state from a previous run could wedge CDP commands on the next run. The reset call is in a `finally` block so it runs on every exit path and never throws (best-effort, errors are logged).

### How to test

1. Start an instance-ai credential-setup run that uses the gateway browser tools (`browser_*`) against a SaaS dashboard with heavy analytics (e.g. Notion, Linear, Slack).
2. Verify the run completes without `'load' event` timeouts and that subsequent runs in the same session start with a fresh tab/debugger state.
3. Leave the relay idle for >30s and confirm the MV3 service worker stays alive (no `heartbeat_timeout` in relay logs).

title: feat(core): Accept merge.input(n) inside ifElse/switch branch targets in workflow-sdk
body:
## Summary

Make `IfElseTarget` and `SwitchCaseTarget` accept an `InputTarget`, so the natural composition

```ts
.to(isDirectory.onTrue(processTrue.to(merge.input(0))).onFalse(merge.input(1)))
```

works end-to-end. Previously the SDK only allowed nodes/chains/builders inside `.onTrue` / `.onFalse` / `.onCase`, even though the workflow JSON, the merge validator, and `NodeInstance.to()` already understood `merge.input(n)` as a terminal target. Builder agents repeatedly tried this exact shape and got rejected by `MERGE_SINGLE_INPUT` validation because the IF branch processing hardcoded `index: 0`.

The branch-processing helpers in `branch-handler-utils.ts` now use `target.inputIndex` when the target is an `InputTarget`, matching the existing behavior of `NodeInstance.to(merge.input(n))`. This is an additive change: existing valid code is unchanged.

## What changed

- `types/base.ts`: `IfElseTarget` and `SwitchCaseTarget` now include `InputTarget`.
- `branch-handler-utils.ts`: handle `InputTarget` in `getTargetNodeName`, `getTargetNodeId`, `addBranchTargetNodes`, and use `target.inputIndex` (not hardcoded `0`) in both `processBranchForBuilder` and `processBranchForComposite`.
- `merge-node-validator.ts`: extend the `MERGE_SINGLE_INPUT` error message with a hint pointing at the working `.input(0)` / `.input(1)` idioms.
- `merge.test.ts`: two new tests for IF and Switch wiring branches directly to merge inputs via `.input(n)`.
- `test-fixtures/committed-workflows/9.json`: round-trip fixture exercising the new shape from the JSON side.

title: fix(editor): Suppress execution error toasts for AI-initiated test runs
body:
## Summary

Builds on [INS-122](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/INS-122/error-toasts-not-appearing-on-canvas-when-running-workflow), which introduced execution error toasts in the Instance AI builder canvas. The toasts also fire for AI-driven test runs, which is confusing — the user didn't trigger them and the AI surfaces failures in its own UI.

This change differentiates the two cases by tagging events relayed from the AI builder so the editor's error toast is suppressed for those, while user-triggered manual runs from inside the canvas still surface the toast. It also suppresses the separate failed-execution toast emitted when the AI preview reloads the completed execution after polling.

### How it works
1. `InstanceAiWorkflowPreview.relayPushEvent` tags relayed events with `source: 'ai'`.
2. `usePostMessageHandler` records the relayed `executionId` in a new `aiInitiatedExecutionIds` set on the UI store before dispatching the event.
3. `handleExecutionFinishedWithErrorOrCanceled` checks the set and skips the error toast when the execution was AI-initiated.
4. `WorkflowPreview` can pass `suppressExecutionErrorToast` to the iframe when loading an execution.
5. `useCanvasOperations.openExecution` skips its failed-execution toast only when that explicit option is set.
6. The set entry is cleared once the execution finishes so it doesn't leak.

### Test plan
- [ ] Open the Instance AI builder and ask the AI to build/test a workflow that fails (e.g. missing credential). Verify no error toast appears.
- [ ] In the same builder canvas, click "Test workflow" manually so it fails. Verify the error toast still shows.

body:
## Summary

Convert `GET /encryption/keys` from a bare-array endpoint into a paginated, sortable, filterable list endpoint that returns `{ count, items }`. The Settings → Encryption keys table is now fully server-driven (page, page size, sort, and date-range filter).

### How to manually verify

1. Build the app and start n8n locally; sign in as the **instance owner**.
2. Navigate to **Settings → Encryption keys**. The table should load and display the existing key(s).
3. Rotate the key several times via **Rotate key** so you have ~25+ rows. New rows should appear with the latest active key on top.
4. **Pagination:** change the page size between 10 / 25 / 50 — count is shown by the table footer; navigate forward/back through pages. Each change should trigger a server fetch (visible in DevTools → Network as a `GET /encryption/keys?skip=…&take=…` request).
5. **Sorting:** use the **Sort by** select to switch between *Activated date*, *Archived date*, and *Type*. Each change should trigger a fresh fetch with `sortBy=field:direction` and reset the page to 1. Order should match the chosen sort.
6. **Date-range filter:** click the funnel icon, pick a date range that includes the activation day of one of your keys, click **Apply**. Only matching keys should remain. Clicking **Clear** restores the full list. Picking the same day for *from* and *to* should still return keys created during that local day.
7. **Bad input:** in DevTools, manually fire `GET /encryption/keys?type=bogus` or `?sortBy=foo:asc` or `?activatedFrom=not-a-date` — each should return **400**. `?activatedFrom=2026-04-30T00:00:00.000Z&activatedTo=2026-04-01T00:00:00.000Z` should return **400** as well.
8. **Permission:** sign in as a non-owner member; the page should still gate the request to **403**.
9. **Rotation behaviour:** while on page 2 with sort *Activated:asc*, click **Rotate key** and confirm — the table should jump back to page 1 sorted by *Activated:desc* with the freshly active key on top.

title: fix(core): Improve AI chat file upload handling and error states
body:
## Summary

Fixes a UX loop in the AI chat where uploading a `.docx` or `.html` file produced an opaque error that then repeated on every follow-up message — even after the file was removed.

Two changes land together:

**1. Boundary validation closes the error loop.** Unsupported attachment MIME types are now rejected at the API boundary (`POST /instance-ai/chat/:threadId` and the chat-hub upload path) with a structured `BadRequestError` *before* anything is persisted. The chat-hub transaction rolls back the human-message row + binary, so nothing reaches LangChain memory and the next turn starts clean. Previously, a bad file rode through validation as `*/*`, was stored, entered conversation memory, and got replayed on every subsequent turn.

**2. Broader format support.** The `parse-file` tool now handles plain text, markdown, HTML, PDF, DOCX, and XLSX in addition to the existing CSV/TSV/JSON. PDFs and DOCX are extracted to text via `pdf-parse` and `mammoth`; XLSX is read by SheetJS and routed through the existing JSON pipeline so column normalization and type inference are reused. HTML is converted to markdown via linkedom + turndown.

A new `@n8n/instance-ai/parsers` subpath export keeps the cli boundary lean (no Mastra ESM contamination in jest).

### How to test

1. Open the AI chat. Attach a `.zip` (or any unsupported binary) → expect a clear toast/inline rejection without a fake AI reply.
2. Send a follow-up text-only message → expect a normal AI response with no echo of the prior failure.
3. Attach `.docx`, `.html`, `.pdf`, `.xlsx`, `.txt`, `.md` → expect the LLM to receive the extracted content and answer.
4. Image uploads (`.png`, `.jpg`) on a vision-capable model still work via multimodal.

feat(core): Add n8n-object-validation ESLint rule for community nodes
body:
## Summary

Adds a new ESLint rule `@n8n/community-nodes/n8n-object-validation` that validates the structure of the `n8n` object in community node `package.json` files.

The rule enforces:
- A top-level `n8n` object must exist
- `n8nNodesApiVersion` must live inside `n8n` (not at the root) and be a positive integer
- `n8n.nodes` must be a non-empty array of strings, each starting with `dist/`
- `n8n.credentials` (optional) must be an array of strings, each starting with `dist/`

The `dist/` prefix is required because community nodes ship compiled JavaScript; n8n cannot load TypeScript sources at runtime. Variants such as `./dist/...` or `DIST/...` are rejected to match the convention used by `@n8n/node-cli` and `@n8n/create-node` templates.

Registered as `error` in both `recommended` and `recommendedWithoutN8nCloudSupport` configs, so it runs both in `@n8n/node-cli` (developer-side linting) and `@n8n/scan-community-package` (Cloud admission scanner).

### Subsumes external rules (prep for [CE-856](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/CE-856))

This rule replaces the following rules from `eslint-plugin-n8n-nodes-base`, so that dependency can be removed in a follow-up PR:

| External rule | Replaced by |
|---|---|
| `community-package-json-n8n-missing` | `missingN8nObject` |
| `community-package-json-n8n-api-version-missing` | `missingNodesApiVersion` |
| `community-package-json-n8n-api-version-not-number` | `invalidNodesApiVersion` |
| `community-package-json-n8n-nodes-missing` | `missingN8nNodes` |
| `community-package-json-n8n-nodes-empty` | `emptyN8nNodes` |

### Behaviour change vs. upstream

The new rule is **stricter** than `community-package-json-n8n-api-version-not-number`: per the ticket spec, `n8nNodesApiVersion` must be a *positive integer*, so values like `0`, `-1`, or `1.5` are now rejected (upstream only checked for non-number). Newly published community packages with a non-integer API version will fail the Cloud scan.

title: feat(core): Ensure agent feature works on multi-main and queue modes
body:
## Summary

Run the n8n agents module safely in multi-main mode. 

### Before
Without this change, every main instance independently activates chat integrations and schedule triggers on startup — Telegram polling fetches the same updates from each node, `setWebhook` registrations race, and `*/N` cron schedules fire once per main per tick.

### After
- `AgentsModule.init()` skips the startup `reconnectAll()` for both `ChatIntegrationService` and `AgentScheduleService` if the instance is not the leader.
- `@OnLeaderTakeover` on `ChatIntegrationService.reconnectAll()`, so a follower-turned-leader re-activates integrations on failover.
- `@OnLeaderTakeover` on `AgentScheduleService.reconnectAll()`, to re-initialize the cron jobs
- `@OnLeaderStepdown()` on a new `ChatIntegrationService.disconnectAll()` method, which tears down every active connection.
- `@OnLeaderStepdown()` on `AgentScheduleService.stopAll()` duplicates the deregistration of cron jobs already happening on instance shutdown

### Out of scope

- **Per-agent `connect()` from the publish/update API.** When a user publishes an agent through the UI, the receiving main runs `connect()` directly. This path is not leader-gated, so a follower receiving the API call will hold a chat session. **Production deployments with sticky sessions are unaffected** — sticky sessions pin a session to one main, so the operational impact is bounded. A future PR can route these calls through a leader proxy if needed.

title: fix(core): Accept placeholder() inside node credentials slot
body:
## Summary

The instance-ai workflow builder occasionally emits `placeholder('hint')` inside a node's `credentials: {}` slot instead of `newCredential('Name')`. Two failure modes resulted:

- **Type error** — `tsc --noEmit` (run inside the LLM's sandbox loop) rejected `PlaceholderValue` because the slot was typed `Record<string, CredentialReference | NewCredentialValue>`. The agent then wasted retries fighting the type error.
- **Runtime garbage** — when the agent submitted anyway, `PlaceholderImpl.toJSON()` returned the literal `<__PLACEHOLDER_VALUE__hint__>` string, which leaked into the saved workflow as a bogus credential value.

This PR makes `placeholder()` and `newCredential()` interchangeable inside the credentials slot at the SDK level — no prompt edits, no AST rewriters, no submit-time post-processing.

**What changed (workflow-sdk only):**
- `NodeConfig.credentials` widened to also accept `PlaceholderValue`
- `NodeInstanceImpl` and `SubnodeInstanceImpl` constructors normalize any `placeholder()` value in `credentials` to `newCredential(hint)` at config ingest, via a new `normalizeNodeConfig` helper
- `json-serializer` narrows credentials back to the resolvable shape at the boundary (and keeps the legacy primitive-string credential case — e.g. post-redaction `'[REDACTED]'` — intact)
- `pin-data-utils` adds a comment confirming the post-normalization invariant
- `node-builder.test.ts` adds 5 targeted tests covering the rewrite, JSON serialization, no `__PLACEHOLDER_VALUE__` leakage, mixed slots, and the `update()` path

Downstream code (`resolveCredentials` in instance-ai, `hasNewCredential` in pin-data-utils, the `NewCredentialImpl.toJSON()` path) is unchanged — credential slots only ever observe `__newCredential` markers or `CredentialReference` shapes.

### How to test

```bash
cd packages/@n8n/workflow-sdk
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test workflow-builder/node-builders/node-builder.test.ts
pnpm test  # 11,618 tests pass
pnpm build
```

End-to-end: any sandbox build where the agent emits `placeholder('hint')` inside `credentials: {...}` should now type-check, serialize to `undefined`, and flow through `resolveCredentials` identically to `newCredential('hint')`.

title: fix(Notion Node): Paginate Get Many operations beyond 100-item API cap
body:
## Summary

The Notion "Get Many" operations (database pages, databases, blocks) were capped at 100 results because the node made a single API call with `page_size` set to the user's limit. Since Notion's API caps `page_size` at 100, any limit > 100 was silently truncated.

title: fix/docker permission error on community node installation due to missing tar flag
body:
## Summary

Busybox `tar` (used in the Alpine-based n8n Docker image) preserves UID/GID from archive headers even for non-root users. npm tarballs carry `uid=0/gid=0` headers, so extracted files end up owned by `root` when n8n runs as a custom UID — causing `EACCES` on the subsequent `package.json` read.

**Fix:** add `--no-same-owner` to the `tar` invocation in `downloadPackage`. Both GNU tar and busybox tar honour this flag, instructing tar to use the current process UID/GID instead of the archive's stored ownership.

## Root cause

The official n8n Docker image is Alpine-based, where `tar` is provided by busybox. Busybox `tar`, unlike GNU `tar`, by default preserves UID/GID metadata from the tarball even when extracting as a non-root user. npm-published tarballs typically contain `uid=0/gid=0` in their headers, so files end up owned by `root`. When n8n then tries to read `package.json` as the runtime UID, it gets `EACCES`.

This only surfaces when overriding the user via `docker run --user <UID>:<GID>`, which is the documented and recommended way to control file ownership on bind-mounted volumes.

## Changes

- `community-packages.service.ts` — adds `--no-same-owner` to the `tar` args
- `community-packages.service.test.ts` — updates the `execFile` assertion to match

No behaviour change for users running as `root` or the default `node` user (UID 1000).

title: fix(core): Add timeout to external secrets provider update to prevent startup hang
body:
## Summary

Backport of https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/29679 to `1.x`.

External secrets providers whose HTTP client hangs (e.g. due to a network issue or a slow secrets store) would cause `provider.update()` to never resolve. This blocked both the n8n startup sequence and the periodic refresh loop indefinitely, making the instance appear unresponsive.

This PR wraps every `provider.update()` call in a `Promise.race` with a 20 s timeout (`EXTERNAL_SECRETS_PROVIDER_UPDATE_TIMEOUT_MS`). When the timeout fires an `OperationalError` is thrown and caught, allowing startup and refresh to complete normally. The error is logged with the full error object for observability.

**How to test:**
1. Configure an external secrets provider whose backend is intentionally unreachable/slow.
2. Start n8n — it should finish initializing within ~20 s instead of hanging forever.
3. The periodic refresh cycle should also complete, with an error logged for the timed-out provider.

title: fix(MCP Client Node): Surface errors as node failures in new node versions
body:
## Summary

The MCP Client node and the MCP Client Tool node were ignoring the `isError: true` flag in MCP tool call responses. When an upstream MCP server returned a tool-level error per the MCP spec (`{ isError: true, content: [...] }`), n8n treated it as a successful execution — the node stayed green and the error content was silently passed through as output data.

**Fix:** Both nodes now check `result.isError` after each tool call and throw a `NodeOperationError` with the error message from the response content. This turns the node red with the error surfaced, and respects "Continue On Fail (using error output)" if enabled.

**Versioning:** The fix is applied only to new node versions to avoid breaking existing workflows:
- **MCP Client** node: fixed in v1.1 (new default), v1 keeps legacy behaviour
- **MCP Client Tool** node: fixed in v1.3 (new default), v1/1.1/1.2 keep legacy behaviour

**To test:**
1. Set up an MCP server that returns error
2. Drop a fresh **MCP Client** node (v1.1) or **MCP Client Tool** node (v1.3) → execute → node should turn red with "boom" as the error message
3. Enable "Continue On Fail (using error output)" → node should stay green and emit the error message as output
4. Downgrade to v1 / v1.2 → node should stay green (legacy behaviour preserved)

title: fix(core): Show AI Builder draft workflows in workflow list (backport to release-candidate/2.19.x)
body:
# Description
Backport of #29670 to `release-candidate/2.19.x`.

## Checklist for the author (@aalises) to go through.

- [ ] Review the backport changes
- [ ] Fix possible conflicts
- [ ] Merge to target branch

After this PR has been merged, it will be picked up in the next patch release for release track.

# Original description

## Summary

When the AI Builder creates a workflow, it inserts a row into `ai_builder_temporary_workflow` to mark it as a draft. The orchestrator clears the marker on success (`clearAiTemporary`) or archives the workflow at run-finish (`reapAiTemporaryFromRun`). Both paths require the orchestrator to reach a terminal state.

If the run never finalizes (LangSmith proxy 401 cascade, OOM, kill, tampering throw mid-build, …), the marker stays in place and the workflows-listing filter — a `NOT EXISTS` subquery in `WorkflowRepository.applyFilters` — hides the workflow until the thread expires by TTL. On David's instance this left **11 workflows** invisible with no self-recovery path.

This PR removes the `applyAiBuilderTemporaryFilter` so the marker becomes pure metadata. Mark / promote / reap logic in `instance-ai` is **unchanged** — the table still drives `archiveIfAiTemporary` at run-finish — it just no longer hides the row from listings. Crashed-run workflows immediately become recoverable, and David's 11 zombie workflows reappear with no DB intervention after deploy.

The trade-off is that drafts are visible in the workflows list during a build. Worth a follow-up for a "draft" badge if it turns out to be confusing.

### Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Unconditional startup sweep that archives orphaned markers whose threads have no active orchestrator (instead of waiting for `threadTtlDays`).
- Investigate the LangSmith proxy 401 cascade that brought the process down on David's instance (separate ticket).

title: fix(core): Acquire expression isolate for dynamic node parameter requests
body:
## Summary

When `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE=vm` is enabled, `DynamicNodeParametersService` builds a temporary `Workflow` for each editor request (RLC, loadOptions, resourceMapper, actionHandler) but never calls `acquireIsolate()` on it. Any credential authentication that resolves expressions (e.g. `googlePalmApi` with `={{$credentials.apiKey}}`) hits the VM evaluator without a bridge, producing:

> No bridge acquired for this context. Call acquire() first.

This affects the Gemini and Gemini Chat Model nodes on cloud (>= 2.19.x where the VM engine is active), and potentially any node whose credentials use expression-based generic authentication.

**Fix:** Wrap all five `DynamicNodeParametersService` entry points in a new `withExpressionIsolate` helper that calls `acquireIsolate()` before and `releaseIsolate()` after evaluation, matching the contract used by full workflow executions.

title: fix(Microsoft Outlook Trigger Node): Use per-folder endpoints for folder-scoped message polling
body:
## Summary

`GET /me/messages` in Microsoft Graph does not support `$filter` on `parentFolderId` — the filter is silently ignored, returning messages from all folders regardless of the "Folders to Include" setting. This caused the trigger to fire on emails from all folders in production, while appearing to work correctly in editor test mode (which uses `$top=1` with no date filter and happens to return a recent message).

**Fix:** Replace the single `/messages` request with per-folder `GET /me/mailFolders/{id}/messages` calls (one per selected folder), run in parallel via `Promise.all`, and merge the results. When no folders are specified, falls back to `/messages` as before.

**How to test:**
1. Create two folders in Outlook and add an email to each.
2. Set up a Microsoft Outlook Trigger with "Folders to Include" set to only one of the folders.
3. In editor test mode — should return an email from that folder.
4. Activate the trigger and send a new email to the included folder → workflow fires.
5. Send a new email to the excluded folder → workflow does not fire.

title: fix: prevent fixedCollection multipleValues from iterating expression string characters
body:
## Problem

When a node parameter is declared as a `fixedCollection` with `typeOptions: { multipleValues: true }`, and the user sets that parameter via an expression (e.g. `={{ $json.items }}`) instead of typing items literally into the UI, `NodeHelpers.getNodeParameters` iterates the **expression string's characters** instead of the resolved array, producing N schema-default items where N is the string's character length.

For example, setting `itemValues` to `={{ $json.items }}` (18 characters) produces 18 default-filled items instead of the expected real items.

Reported in [#29619](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/29619).

## Root Cause

In `packages/workflow/src/node-helpers.ts` (line ~933), the code does:

```js
for (const nodeValue of (propertyValues as INodeParameters)[itemName] as INodeParameters[]) {
```

When `propertyValues[itemName]` is a string (an unresolved expression), `for...of` iterates the string's characters. Each character is treated as a fixedCollection row and processed with schema defaults.

## Fix

Added an `Array.isArray` check before the iteration loop to skip non-array values:

```js
const itemValues = (propertyValues as INodeParameters)[itemName];
if (!Array.isArray(itemValues)) {
    continue;  // skip unresolved expression strings
}
for (const nodeValue of itemValues as INodeParameters[]) {
```

This prevents the character-iteration bug while preserving the expression string in the raw parameters for later evaluation by the workflow runtime.

## Testing

1. Define a custom node with a `multipleValues: true` fixedCollection parameter
2. Set the parameter to an expression like `={{ $json.items }}`
3. Verify the node does not receive N default items (where N = expression string length)

title: feat(Sms77 Trigger): Add webhook trigger for inbound seven events
body:
## Summary

Adds a webhook trigger node for the seven (sms77) integration, completing the action+trigger pair for the seven service.

> **Stacked on #29637.** This PR's actual change is the most recent commit (`feat(Sms77 Trigger): Add webhook trigger for inbound seven events`). The earlier commit comes from #29637 and will disappear from this diff once that PR is merged. Please review #29637 first.

## What's in the trigger

Subscribes to seven's webhook system (`/api/hooks`) and emits incoming events into the workflow. Multi-select event picker covering all current event types:

- `sms_mo` (inbound SMS)
- `dlr` (delivery reports)
- `tracking` (URL click/view tracking)
- `voice_call`, `voice_status`, `voice_dtmf`
- `rcs`
- `wa_mo` (inbound WhatsApp)

Subscriptions are managed automatically: one subscription per selected event when the workflow activates, all deleted when it deactivates. When all events are selected, a single `event_type=all` hook is created instead of one per type. Subscription requests use `request_method=json` (the modern format), legacy GET/form-encoded modes are not exposed.

## Signature verification

Implements HMAC-SHA256 verification of incoming requests following https://docs.seven.io/en/rest-api/signing:

```
HMAC-SHA256(timestamp + '\n' + nonce + '\n' + method + '\n' + url + '\n' + md5(body))
```

Headers checked: `X-Signature`, `X-Timestamp`, `X-Nonce`. Replay protection via 30-second timestamp window. The signing key is supplied as a node parameter (from the seven Developer area). Empty signing key skips verification (opt-in behavior).

## Why

The current node only supports SMS and Voice send. seven.io's API has grown significantly since the original node was added (RCS, WhatsApp, lookups, account analytics, numbers, contacts/groups, etc.). This PR brings the node up to par with the live API surface, authored by seven (the API vendor).

title: feat(ai-builder): Guarantee user-visible output on terminal states
body:
## Summary

Guarantee that Instance AI terminal and waiting states produce current-run user-visible output when the model stream is silent, cancelled, exhausted, disconnected, or fails before emitting a final response.

This keeps the frontend event protocol unchanged and enforces the contract in the backend: terminal fallbacks are emitted before `run-finish`, confirmation payloads are checked for displayable UI, and background task outcomes are persisted/replayed into both live events and rich-message history.

Key changes:
- Add `InstanceAiTerminalResponseGuard` for completed, errored, cancelled, and waiting states.
- Add typed `isDisplayableConfirmationRequest()` handling so metadata-only confirmation payloads do not leave users stuck waiting.
- Persist and replay `TerminalOutcome` lines for background task completion, failure, and cancellation.
- Parse stored terminal outcomes per entry, so one malformed record does not discard valid undelivered outcomes.
- Keep terminal fallback output current across reloads: dedupe by `responseId`, preserve agent-tree snapshots/run IDs, create snapshots when no tree exists, and hydrate orphan terminal snapshots into rich messages when there is no matching Mastra assistant row.
- Always publish valid confirmation events after suspension, and validate waiting confirmations before treating prior root text/error as visible output.
- Sanitize fallback errors by error class while keeping raw details in logs/tracing.
- Clear malformed confirmation suspensions with a visible error, run cancellation, tracing finalization, `run-finish`, and snapshot save.
- Save resumed cancellation/failure snapshots so reload/history stays aligned with live output.

title: fix(core): Detect conflicting webhook endpoint paths at startup
body:
## Summary

Fail-fast validation for the `N8N_ENDPOINT_*` env vars used to register webhook-style routes. Throws a clear startup error when one endpoint value is equal to or a path-segment prefix of another, naming the offending env vars.

The form/webhook/mcp/waiting routes are registered on Express with greedy `*path` (or multi-segment) patterns, and Express dispatches in registration order. When one endpoint value path-segment-prefixes another, the earlier-registered route silently swallows the later one's traffic — producing confusing 404s with no warning at boot. The customer report in the linked ticket hit this with `N8N_ENDPOINT_WEBHOOK="…/yee"` and `N8N_ENDPOINT_WEBHOOK_TEST="…/yee/test"`: test-webhook URLs were being routed to the production handler, which then 404'd because the production handler couldn't find a webhook at the (test-webhook) path.

The validator runs once in `AbstractServer`'s constructor before any routes are registered. Default configuration still passes (e.g. `webhook` vs `webhook-test` is fine — no shared path segment). Multi-segment values are still allowed as long as they don't collide (e.g. `a/prod` + `a/test` passes).

### How to test

```bash
N8N_ENDPOINT_WEBHOOK="prefix" \
N8N_ENDPOINT_WEBHOOK_TEST="prefix/test" \
pnpm --filter n8n start
```

Should error at startup with a message naming both env vars. Removing either var (or making them not share a leading segment) lets startup proceed.

Unit tests in `packages/@n8n/config/test/endpoints.config.test.ts` cover the default config, prefix-shadow, equal values, multiple conflicts reported together, prefix-substring (not segment) false-positives, and multi-segment values that don't collide.

title: fix(editor): Fix OAuth2 credential showing "Needs first setup" after connecting
body:
## Summary

When setting up an OAuth2 credential (e.g. Slack), the credential card in the list would continue to show the "Needs first setup" warning badge immediately after closing the modal, even though the OAuth flow had completed successfully. A page refresh would clear the badge correctly, confirming this was a stale state issue rather than a real setup problem.

**Root cause:** The credential list performs a `fetchAllCredentials` via a `$onAction` listener when `saveCredential()` is called — but this happens *before* the OAuth popup opens. By the time the user completes the OAuth flow in the popup and closes the modal, the list holds pre-OAuth data from that earlier fetch, with no mechanism to re-sync.

**Fix:** A `pendingOAuthRefresh` flag is added to the credentials store and set to `true` when the OAuth connect flow is initiated in `CredentialEdit`. When the credential edit modal closes, `CredentialsView` checks this flag and only triggers a `fetchAllCredentials` if it is set (resetting it immediately after). This ensures:

- The credential list reflects the post-OAuth server state when the modal closes.
- Regular (non-OAuth) credential saves are unaffected — they continue to use the existing single `$onAction` refetch with no extra calls.

**To test:**

1. Go to **Credentials** and create a new Slack OAuth2 credential (or any OAuth2 type).
2. Complete the OAuth flow in the popup.
3. Close the modal.
4. Verify the credential card no longer shows "Needs first setup".

title: fix(FTP Node): Queue concurrent handshakes per credential
body:
## Summary

Workflows that fan out to multiple SFTP nodes against the same SSH user fail intermittently with `getConnection: Timed out while waiting for handshake`. Each FTP/SFTP node creates its own `ssh2-sftp-client` and calls `.connect()` independently, so the SSH server sees a burst of handshakes from one user and throttles them (`MaxStartups`). n8n's 10s `readyTimeout` surfaces the throttle as a hard failure.

This PR adds a per-credential semaphore around `connect()` keyed by `host:port:user:protocol`. Concurrent handshakes for the same destination queue instead of racing. Items inside one node already share one connection, so item-level behaviour is unchanged.

- New `packages/nodes-base/nodes/Ftp/HandshakeQueue.ts` — process-level `Map<credentialHash, Bucket>` with a tiny promise semaphore, `makeHandshakeKey()`, `withHandshakePermit()`. No new dependencies.
- `packages/nodes-base/nodes/Ftp/Ftp.node.ts` — wraps the 6 `connect()` call sites (FTP/SFTP credential test + execute path).
- Default cap is 5, configurable via `N8N_SFTP_HANDSHAKE_CONCURRENCY` (range 1–32, invalid values fall back to default).

### Why default 5?

The relevant ceiling is the server's `MaxStartups` (OpenSSH default 10 before drops). 5 sits below that, lets normal 3–4-node fan-outs run unqueued, and stops the burst pattern that triggered this bug. Stricter servers tune via the env var.

This PR is the safety net: it caps concurrency, but doesn't reduce handshake volume. A connection pool would do that — tracked as a follow-up.

### Test plan

- Unit tests for `HandshakeQueue`: ordering under load, permit release on `connect()` resolve and reject, isolation across credentials, env var parsing for valid/invalid/out-of-range values.
- Existing `Ftp.node.test.ts` continues to pass.
- Manual repro pending — to be validated by sharing this branch with the original reporter against their reproducer workflow.

body:
## Summary

Cap the day-of-month jitter at 28 to prevent skipping executions in February.

Previously, when you created a Schedule trigger to run at a monthly interval, we would pick a random day. We picked from the range 1-30. This means that if we picked 29 or 30, the February execution would just get skipped.

The simplest solution is just to cap at 28. We lose some of the spread of executions because we will no longer schedule for the 29, 30, or 31, but this is quite marginal compared to skipping executions.

Currently, each workflow must be published manually, or with a shell loop. Since n8n needs to restart with each iteration, the process can take more time than necessary on low-end hardware.

Functionally, publishing all workflows works perfectly and I don't see any reason to prevent this behavior.

Shell loop:

```sh
n8n list:workflow --onlyId --active=false | while read -r workflow_id; do
  [ -n "$workflow_id" ] && n8n publish:workflow --id="$workflow_id"
done
``` 

I didn't submit a doc update yet, but happy to write it once this PR is validated.

title: feat(instance-ai): Reuse workflow builder sandboxes (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary
This PR reduces latency and token growth for Instance AI workflow-builder follow-up turns while preserving sandbox continuity.

It keeps completed workflow-builder sandboxes warm for 10 minutes by default, keyed per thread/workflow, so simple follow-up edits can reuse the existing workspace, source files, installed dependencies, and dedicated builder memory thread. The builder memory thread is compacted after successful runs into a synthetic summary message that keeps the useful state (workflow/work item IDs, source path, node list, triggers, mocked credentials, verification state, last requested change, and final result) while deleting bulky raw tool transcripts from persisted memory.

It also compacts `verify-built-workflow` responses by default. The tool now returns concise evidence (`executionId`, `success`, `status`, executed nodes, and per-node previews), while preserving the full execution data internally for cleanup and workflow-task verification records. Full data remains available via `includeData: true`.

Additional changes:

- Reuse successful structured builder verification evidence in orchestrator post-build/checkpoint flows instead of running duplicate verification.
- Preserve builder stream resume options so suspended builder streams keep memory, save-per-step, temperature, and provider options.
- Repair missing workflow SDK installs in builder sandboxes, including the unpublished pinned-version fallback.
- Include current input tokens in orchestrator context-compaction decisions.
- Pass completed dependency context into planned sub-agent tasks.
- Remove temporary `[InstanceAI]...` debug console logs added during tuning.

## Before / after validation

LangSmith comparison on the meeting-booking workflow scenario (initial build, Gmail recipient follow-up, Slack DM follow-up) showed:

| Metric | Before | After | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Wall time | 10m27.7s | 5m59.1s | -4m28.6s (-42.8%) |
| LLM calls | 64 | 54 | -10 (-15.6%) |
| Tool calls | 64 | 51 | -13 (-20.3%) |
| Reported total tokens | 530,677 | 434,031 | -96,646 (-18.2%) |
| Prompt tokens | 486,755 | 400,103 | -86,652 (-17.8%) |
| Completion tokens | 43,922 | 33,928 | -9,994 (-22.8%) |

Builder-specific changes:

| Builder run | Before | After | Finding |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Initial build turns | 19 | 10 | Fewer builder turns |
| Initial build wall time | 3m08.8s | 1m57.9s | -70.9s (-37.6%) |
| Initial build with cache | 1,031,351 | 529,969 | -501,382 (-48.6%) |
| Gmail follow-up wall time | 35.8s | 28.4s | -20.7% |
| Slack follow-up wall time | 1m32.6s | 57.1s | -38.4% |

Verification behavior:

- Before: 7 `verify-built-workflow` calls, including 3 duplicate orchestrator-side verifications after the builder had already verified.
- After: 3 `verify-built-workflow` calls, all from the workflow-builder, with no duplicate orchestrator verification.
- Before: verify outputs returned full top-level `data` payloads.
- After: verify outputs return compact evidence (`executionId`, executed nodes, and `nodePreviews`) by default.

The comparison confirms the main intended behavior: warm builder continuity and structured verification reuse reduce end-to-end latency, tool calls, and token usage while preserving builder verification evidence.

title: fix(editor): Use workflowId prop on evaluations views
body:
## Summary

PR #29297 renamed every route param from `:name` to `:workflowId` but
left the `defineProps<{ name: string }>` declarations in the eval views
in place. With Vue Router's `props: true` the views now receive a
`workflowId` prop and `props.name` is always `undefined`, so:

- "Run test" issued `POST /rest/workflows/undefined/test-runs/new` and the request 404'd.
- The runs filter (`workflowId === props.name`) never matched, so the runs list looked empty.
- Telemetry events recorded `workflow_id: undefined`.

This PR renames the prop to `workflowId` in `EvaluationsView.vue` and
`EvaluationsRootView.vue` (the only two views in `evaluation.ee/views/`
that use route props) and updates the corresponding component tests.

### Root cause

Origin: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/29297 — `refactor(editor): Provide workflow id and document store at app root`. That PR consistently renamed `:name` → `:workflowId` across `router.ts` and updated the consumers it touched, but the eval feature's view files (which were not part of the diff) still relied on the old `name` route param via `props.name`. The intent was clearly to rename the param to be more descriptive; this PR finishes the rename in the eval views.

### How to test

1. Open a workflow with at least one configured evaluation.
2. Click `Run test`.
3. Verify the request goes to `POST /rest/workflows/<actual-id>/test-runs/new` (not `undefined`) and the run starts.
4. Verify previously-recorded runs for this workflow show up in the runs list.

title: fix(core): Guard leader-stepdown emission on vacant leadership check
body:
## Summary

In `MultiMainSetup.checkLeader()`, the `!leaderId` (vacant leadership) branch unconditionally emitted `leader-stepdown` and called `markAsFollower()` — even when the instance was already a follower. This caused phantom stepdown→takeover cycles where a leader that briefly couldn't see its own Redis key triggered a full workflow deactivation→reactivation for no reason, contributing to workflows failing to reactivate after leader failover.

This PR adds an `isLeader` guard (matching the pattern already used in the `leaderId !== hostId` branch) so that `leader-stepdown` is only emitted when actually transitioning from leader to follower. Tests updated to cover both the follower and leader cases for vacant leadership.

title: feat(editor): Surface cluster information in debug data (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Removes the `Settings → Instance Registry` placeholder UI, instead surfacing the
cluster snapshot — instances and check results — through the existing debug-info
channel that the About modal copies to clipboard and "Report a bug" embeds into
the GitHub issue body. Drops the `N8N_ENV_FEAT_INSTANCE_REGISTRY` env flag and
the `orchestration:read` scope from the controller, so the registry is on by
default for all deployments and the cluster context flows into every bug report.

### Why

This is the final slice of the cluster-visibility initiative. #28936 added the
reconciliation loop and the `/instance-registry` endpoint; #29506 added four
built-in health checks (version mismatch, hostid clash, split brain, lifecycle).
The `SettingsInstanceRegistryView` shipped alongside that work was always a
placeholder behind the env flag — it printed the raw JSON and was never going to
be the long-term presentation. Rather than ship a UI that needs a design pass for
GA, we drop the surface entirely and route the same data into the channels
operators already reach for when filing a bug.

With the project landing in this PR, the env-flag wrapper around the module is
no longer useful. Keeping it would mean shipping a feature that's silently off
in every default deployment. The `orchestration:read` scope is dropped because
the cluster payload (instance keys, hostIds, versions, roles, check status,
warning codes) contains no user PII and has the same operator-debug character
as the existing `## core` block — n8n version, deployment type, license — that
every authenticated user already sees in the About modal.

Example debug data:

```
...

## cluster

- instanceCount: 1
- versions: 2.19.0
- instances:
  - instanceKey: 2792a4c2-64fe-4980-84a7-2ada52f2a241, hostId: main-V60CE4pd3EkxUDtA, instanceType: main, instanceRole: leader, version: 2.19.0
- checks:
  - check: hostid-clash, status: succeeded, warnings: -
  - check: lifecycle, status: succeeded, warnings: -
  - check: split-brain, status: succeeded, warnings: -
  - check: version-mismatch, status: succeeded, warnings: -

...
```

### How to test manually

1. Start n8n (no env vars needed any more — single instance is fine, queue-mode
   multi-main makes the cluster section more interesting).
2. Confirm the *removal*:
   - Open `Settings`. There should be **no "Instance Registry" entry** in the sidebar.
   - Visit `/settings/instance-registry` directly — the route should not resolve.
3. Confirm the *debug-data integration*:
   - Open the user menu → "About n8n" → click **Copy debug information**.
   - Paste anywhere. The output should include a `## cluster` section with
     `instanceCount`, `versions`, an `instances:` bullet list, and a `checks:`
     bullet list showing every check that ran with `status` and warning codes.
4. Confirm the *bug-report integration*:
   - Sidebar → Help → **Report a bug**. The GitHub issue page should open with
     the `## cluster` block already in the body, under `## Debug info`.
   - Right-click the menu item → "Copy link" should still produce a usable URL.
   - Open the command bar (Cmd-K / Ctrl-K) → "Report a bug". Same URL, same
     content.
5. Confirm *no scope barrier*:
   - Sign in as a regular member (not owner/admin). Repeat steps 3 and 4. The
     cluster section should appear for them too — `GET /rest/instance-registry`
     returns 200, not 403.
6. Confirm *queue-mode multi-main detection*:
   - Run `mains: 2, workers: 1` (the existing playwright fixture configuration).
     The `instances:` list should show all three processes; the `checks:` block
     should reflect their status.

### Key implementation decisions

- **Pinia store + synchronous reads, not `async generateDebugInfo`.** The fetch
  lives in a small `useInstanceRegistryStore`; `useDebugInfo` reads `clusterInfo`
  synchronously and omits the section when `null`. Keeping `getReportingURL()`
  synchronous preserves middle-click / "copy link" semantics on the help-menu
  item and avoids popup-blocker pitfalls in the command-bar `window.open` path.
  Fetches are triggered on natural hooks (sidebar mount, About-modal mount,
  "Report a bug" click).
- **All check results, not just failures.** The `checks:` rendering surfaces
  every check that ran (with `status: succeeded` and `warnings: -` where the
  check passed) so a reviewer can see what the cluster watchdog actually
  evaluated, not only what it complained about.
- **Per-instance fields are a deliberate subset.** `registeredAt` / `lastSeen`
  timestamps are omitted — they change every reconciliation cycle, add no
  debugging value, and would churn snapshot tests.
- **Errors are swallowed.** Transient network errors leave the previous snapshot
  in place and never break debug generation. The bug-reporting affordance must
  remain functional even if the endpoint is briefly unreachable.
- **Stacks on top of #29506.** Base branch is `iam-333-built-in-health-checks`.
  No shared files, but the cluster `checks` summary this PR renders is
  populated by the checks added there.

title: refactor(core): Remove global builder node guides
body:
## Summary

Removes the seven always-on node-specific guides from the Instance AI builder system prompt and relies on generated type definitions, `@builderHint`, defaults, and live `explore-resources` lookups as the source of truth.

## Prompt Budget Impact

Token counts are estimated with `chars / 4`.

| Prompt | Before | After | Saved |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Builder tool prompt | ~14,596 tokens | ~9,148 tokens | ~5,448 tokens (37.3%) |
| Sandbox builder prompt | ~18,895 tokens | ~13,448 tokens | ~5,448 tokens (28.8%) |

The removed static guide block is `21,791` characters, or ~`5,448` estimated tokens, per builder run.

## What changed

- Removed inline `IF_NODE_GUIDE`, `SWITCH_NODE_GUIDE`, `SET_NODE_GUIDE`, `HTTP_REQUEST_GUIDE`, `TOOL_NODES_GUIDE`, `EMBEDDING_NODES_GUIDE`, and `RESOURCE_LOCATOR_GUIDE` from `composeSdkRulesAndPatterns()`.
- Did not add an on-demand `nodes(action="guide")` fallback. The builder should not keep static guide content as a secondary source of truth.
- Kept a compact `NODE_CONFIGURATION_SAFETY_RULES` block that points the builder to type definitions, `@builderHint`, defaults, and `explore-resources`, and tells it not to guess from static node-shape memory.
- Surfaced node-level `builderHint.message` through `nodes(action="type-definition")`, so direct utility-node lookups retain node-level guidance even when the builder skips search.
- Fixed stale Set-node guide content that conflicted with the v3.4 generated types: arrays/objects no longer require `JSON.stringify()`.

## Why

The previous static guides were always appended to the builder prompt even when the workflow did not use those node types. That increased context cost and latency, and it created a stale-instruction risk: at least the Set guide had drifted from generated definitions.

Generated node definitions and `@builderHint` are the fresher source of truth. This change removes the builder-facing static guide path and fixes the missing node-level hint bridge in type-definition responses.

title: fix(core): Wire EncryptionKeyProxy provider on bootstrap
body:
## Summary

`EncryptionKeyProxy.isConfigured()` always returned `false` at runtime, causing `encryptV2`/`decryptV2` to silently fall through to the legacy AES-256-CBC path even when `N8N_ENV_FEAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY_ROTATION=true` was set.

**Root cause:** `EncryptionBootstrapService.run()` seeded the CBC and GCM keys in the database but never called `encryptionKeyProxy.setProvider()`. The proxy had no provider wired up, so the GCM path in `Cipher` was unreachable.

**Fix:**
- `KeyManagerService` now explicitly declares `implements IEncryptionKeyProvider`
- `EncryptionBootstrapService` injects `EncryptionKeyProxy` and calls `setProvider(keyManager)` after the bootstrap is complete

With this change, the proxy becomes configured at startup and the key rotation feature flag actually gates the GCM encryption path as intended.

title: fix(core): Restore peer project discovery in share dropdowns (backport to release-candidate/2.18.x)
body:
# Description
Backport of #29537 to `release-candidate/2.18.x`.

## Checklist for the author (@afitzek) to go through.

- [ ] Review the backport changes
- [ ] Fix possible conflicts
- [ ] Merge to target branch

After this PR has been merged, it will be picked up in the next patch release for release track.

# Original description

## Summary

`global:member` users could not share personal workflows or credentials: the
"add users" field in the share modal was empty, regardless of the Personal
Space Sharing policy. This restores peer-personal-project discovery for the
share dropdowns by routing them through a new dedicated endpoint, while
keeping the existing `GET /rest/projects` listing intentionally strict.

### Why

The share modal is wired to a server-paginated project search introduced in
#27036, which originally returned every personal project plus the caller's
own relations — exactly what the dropdown needs to surface other users as
share targets.

#27206 (Instance AI module) bundled a change to
`ProjectRepository.getAccessibleProjectsAndCount` that tightened the query
to `INNER JOIN projectRelations WHERE userId = :userId`. The same tightening
was also applied to `getAccessibleProjects` (non-paginated), where it was
correct: that variant is consumed by the Instance AI agent's `listProjects`
tool and the favorites filter set, both of which want only projects the
caller can manipulate. The paginated variant, however, backs the share
dropdowns — conflating the two semantics broke peer discovery for members.

This PR makes the two semantics first-class so they can't be silently
conflated again:

- `getAccessibleProjectsAndCount` keeps its post-#27206 strict semantics
  ("projects I can manipulate"). Backs `GET /rest/projects`.
- `getShareableProjectsAndCount` (new) restores the wide semantics
  ("projects I can pick as share targets, including peer personal
  projects"). Backs `GET /rest/projects/sharing-candidates`.
- The share / transfer / user-deletion modal composable
  (`useRemoteProjectSearch`) is switched to call the new endpoint.

The new endpoint is gated by `@GlobalScope('user:list')` — the same boundary
`GET /rest/users` enforces, since the dropdown surfaces user identity
(`First Last <email>` is the personal project name). Members already carry
this scope; restricted roles like chat-only users do not and receive 403.

### How to test manually

1. Run an Enterprise build (license with Personal Space Sharing).
2. Create one instance owner and at least two members (e.g. Alice, Bob);
   complete signup so both members have passwords.
3. Sign in as Alice → open any of Alice's personal workflows → Share.
4. Click the "add users…" field. **Expected:** Bob's personal project (and
   any other peer personal projects) appears in the dropdown.
5. Type `bob` in the field. **Expected:** the dropdown narrows server-side
   and Bob remains visible.
6. Repeat steps 3–4 from a credential's Sharing tab. Same expected
   behaviour.
7. Sign in as the instance owner → Share modal → confirm the full project
   list still appears (no admin regression).
8. In DevTools, confirm the share dropdown issues
   `GET /rest/projects/sharing-candidates?...take=50&...` (200) and not
   `GET /rest/projects`. Confirm the response `data[]` contains every
   member's personal project.
9. Optional negative check: as a chat-only user, request
   `GET /rest/projects/sharing-candidates` directly. **Expected:** 403.

### Key implementation decisions

- **Dedicated endpoint instead of a query-param flag.** The two list
  semantics are genuinely different, so they get distinct names at every
  layer (route, service, repository).
- **Don't touch `getAccessibleProjects` (non-paginated).** Its tightening
  in #27206 is correct and load-bearing for Instance AI and favorites.
- **Don't gate the listing on the Personal Space Sharing license/policy.**
  That license controls whether a user can be the *source* of sharing from
  their personal space; it's enforced at write-time on the share endpoints.
  Visibility of peer personal projects in the listing is an orthogonal
  concern, consistent with the design from #27036.

- Closes #29002
- Regressing commit: `629826ca1d` (PR #27206)
- Original correct design: `3b00e1bafe` (PR #27036)

title: fix(editor): Restore read-only mode for archived workflows on canvas
body:
## Summary

Archived workflows were incorrectly rendered as editable on the canvas after a refactor of `workflowDocument.store.ts`. This caused autosave to fire and fail with repeated 403/404 toast errors, since the backend correctly rejects writes to archived workflows.

**Root cause:** `isCanvasReadOnly` and `canExecuteOnCanvas` in `NodeView.vue` were reading `isArchived` from `editableWorkflow` (always `false` after the refactor) instead of `workflowDocumentStore`, which is the correct source of truth.

**Changes:**
- `NodeView.vue`: Read `isArchived` from `workflowDocumentStore` in both `isCanvasReadOnly` and `canExecuteOnCanvas`
- `CanvasNode.vue`: Skip rendering the toolbar entirely when `readOnly && !canExecute`, so the toolbar DOM element is absent (not just opacity-hidden)
- `CanvasNodeToolbar.vue`: Hide the overflow "⋯" button when `readOnly`

**How to test:**
1. Create and save a workflow
2. Archive it via the workflow menu
3. Open the archived workflow — canvas should be in read-only mode (no plus button, no toolbar actions)
4. Verify no autosave requests fire
