title: fix(Airtable Node): Fix typecast option dropping attachment field updates
body:
## Summary

When the Typecast option is enabled on the **Airtable** create/update/upsert operations,
`skipValidation: true` is passed to `getNodeParameter`, which bypasses the type
coercion step that normally converts JSON strings to arrays for `array`-type fields
(multipleAttachments). As a result, attachment field values entered as JSON strings
in the resource mapper were sent to the Airtable API as plain strings, which the API
silently ignored — forcing users to split the operation into two separate steps.

This fix adds a post-processing step that uses the resource mapper schema to identify
`array`-type fields and parses any string values as JSON arrays before the API request
is made. Also fixes upsert, which was missing `skipValidation: true` entirely, causing
typecast to fail with a validation error when entering new select option values.

title: fix(Notion Node): Support app.notion.com URL format for page and block ID extraction
body:
## Summary

Notion is migrating its primary web domain from `notion.so` to `app.notion.com`. The new URL format (`https://app.notion.com/p/<Title>-<id>`) is already being returned by the Notion API, but n8n's Notion node failed to parse it, throwing `Invalid URL, could not find block ID or page ID` on any \"By URL\" mode operation (reading blocks, updating pages, etc.).

The fix updates `baseUrlRegexp` in `constants.ts` to also accept `app.notion.com` as a valid domain and the optional `/p/` path prefix. All five URL extraction/validation regexps used by the node are derived from this one constant, so the single change fixes all affected operations.

**To test:**
1. In the Notion node, set Resource to **Block**, Operation to **Get Child Blocks**, Block to **By URL**
2. Enter a new-format URL such as `https://app.notion.com/p/some-document-name?source=copy_link`
3. Execute — it should return child blocks instead of throwing `Invalid URL`

title: fix(core): Round fractional time saved values before inserting into insights BIGINT column
body:
## Summary

https://www.loom.com/share/b0bf0894234949a993b09a115787c23b

Fixes a `QueryFailedError: invalid input syntax for type bigint` crash that occurred when dynamic time saved workflows produced fractional minute values (e.g. `9.799999999999999`). PostgreSQL's `BIGINT` column rejects non-integer JavaScript numbers.

**Two-layer fix:**
- **Backend:** Added `integerValueForInsightsRaw()` which rounds values with `Math.round()` before inserting into `insights_raw.value`. Also handles non-finite values (returns 0).
- **Frontend/Node:** Added `precision: 0` / `:precision="0"` to the time saved inputs in `WorkflowSettings.vue` and `TimeSaved.node.ts` so the UI prevents fractional input at the source.

**How to test:**
Note: This should be tested with n8n in docker with postgres
1. Create a workflow with a Time Saved node set to dynamic mode
2. Set a decimal value (e.g. `5.4` minutes) via expression
3. Execute the workflow and wait for the insights flush cycle
4. Verify no `QueryFailedError` appears in logs and insights are recorded correctly

title: ci(ai-builder): Parallelize Instance AI eval CI across multiple n8n containers
body:
## Summary

Parallelizes the Instance AI eval CI workflow across multiple n8n containers and reuses the prebuilt n8n Docker image. Wall-clock drops from ~16 min on master to ~5-6 min while keeping full pass@k signal (n=3 iterations).

## What changed

### \`.github/workflows/test-evals-instance-ai.yml\`
- Reuse the prebuilt n8n Docker image from \`prepare-docker\` via \`load-n8n-docker\` (replaces ~3-5 min \`pnpm build:docker\`). Falls back to local build if cache is missing.
- Start 9 n8n containers on ports 5678–5686, each running independently.
- Runner: \`blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2204\`.
- Healthcheck timeout 60s → 120s to absorb parallel container boot contention.
- Pin \`N8N_AI_ASSISTANT_BASE_URL=\"\"\` so builds always route directly to Anthropic.
- \`--concurrency 16\` → \`32\` to keep the work-stealing pool fed.

### \`.github/workflows/ci-pull-requests.yml\`
- \`instance-ai-workflow-evals\` job now \`needs: [install-and-build, prepare-docker]\`. Eval still runs when \`prepare-docker\` is skipped (e.g. PRs touching only \`.github/**\`); a fallback step handles cache misses.

### Eval CLI (\`packages/@n8n/instance-ai/evaluations/cli/\`)
- \`--base-url\` accepts comma-separated URLs; one lane per URL. Multi-lane runs authenticate, seed credentials, and snapshot pre-existing workflow IDs in parallel.
- New \`LaneAllocator\`: work-stealing dispatch enforcing a single rule — *a lane never runs the same prompt twice concurrently*. Builds acquire a least-loaded lane that isn't already running their prompt; scenarios re-use the lane that built their workflow.
- Iterator round-robins scenarios across test cases and iter-interleaves per scenario, so the in-flight build set spans all lanes from the start instead of concentrating on one test case alphabetically.
- Per-lane LangSmith trace metadata (filterable by lane in the UI).
- Build/scenario log lines tagged \`[lane N/M]\` for debuggability.
- Background-task wait log throttled to count-changes + 20s heartbeat (~10× quieter during stable waits).

## Why work-stealing over static distribution

Concurrent same-prompt builds on a single n8n container break the agent reliably (~33% build failure rate, agent times out with \"Plan approved. On it!\" never producing a workflow). An earlier static \`(file, iter) → lane\` round-robin fixed this but coupled three places (mapping, lookup, iterator order) to a non-obvious math invariant (\`lanes >= iterations\`) that silently degraded if iteration count grew past lane count.

The allocator enforces the actual rule at runtime instead. No constraint to remember; works for any \`(lanes, iterations)\` combination including local single-lane n=3.

## Tests

- \`__tests__/lane-allocator.test.ts\` — acquire/release, prompt exclusion, FIFO wait queue, capacity cap, conflict-aware wake-up.
- \`__tests__/lanes.test.ts\` — \`partitionRoundRobin\` math.
- \`__tests__/args.test.ts\` — comma-separated \`--base-url\` parsing.

## Test plan

- [ ] PR CI eval job completes in ~5-6 min with 27/27 builds successful.
- [ ] \`[lane N/M]\` tags visible in build/scenario log lines.
- [ ] Single LangSmith experiment per run (no fragmentation).
- [ ] No CPU contention symptoms on 4vcpu runner (healthcheck failures, build timeouts).

## Related

- #29507 — filter fix that gated the eval workflow on the right paths
- #29543 — concurrency 4→16 (superseded; bundled here)

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- TRUST-55: speed up cross-team-linear-report (currently dominates wall-clock floor at ~3-4 min)
- Consolidate LangSmith experiments — currently one per CI run, but lane metadata could feed a single rolled-up view

title: ci(ai-builder): Raise eval scenario concurrency from 4 to 16
body:
## Summary

The eval workflow's `--concurrency 4` flag was unnecessarily serializing the cheap part of the run.

`--concurrency` controls how many `target()` invocations LangSmith's `evaluate()` runs in parallel. It does **not** control build pressure on n8n — builds are independently capped at `MAX_CONCURRENT_BUILDS = 4` in the CLI (`evaluations/cli/index.ts:57`), which is the comment-blocked safety against n8n degradation.

So the existing `4` only slowed scenario execution, not protect anything.

## Measured impact

Against the latest TRUST-27 CI run that already runs at `--concurrency 16`:
- Build phase: 27 builds × 146s ÷ 4 concurrent ≈ **16 min** (unchanged — build cap is the floor)
- Exec phase: 87 scenarios × ~60s ÷ 16 concurrent ≈ **6 min**  *(vs ÷ 4 ≈ 22 min)*
- **Total wall ≈ 23 min** *(vs ~38 min at concurrency 4)*

This brings PR-level CI well clear of the 45-min workflow cap.

## How to test

The next eval run on this PR (or any PR after merge) will surface this directly — the workflow time should drop from ~38 min to ~23 min on a clean dataset.

title: fix(editor): Preserve decimal suffix when duplicating a node
body:
## Summary

Duplicating a node whose name ends with a version-like decimal (e.g. `Claude Sonnet 4.6`, `GPT 5.10`, `Gemini 2.0`) produces a malformed name with a dangling period instead of an incremented suffix.

**Before**

| Source name | Duplicate produces |
|---|---|
| `Claude Sonnet 4.6` | `Claude Sonnet 4.` ❌ |
| `GPT 5.10` | `GPT 5.` ❌ |
| `Gemini 2.0` | `Gemini 2.` ❌ |

**After**

| Source name | Duplicate produces |
|---|---|
| `Claude Sonnet 4.6` | `Claude Sonnet 4.61` |
| `GPT 5.10` | `GPT 5.101` |
| `Gemini 2.0` | `Gemini 2.01` |

### Root cause

In [useUniqueNodeName.ts:94](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/app/composables/useUniqueNodeName.ts#L94) the regex `/(?<base>.*\D+)(?<suffix>\d*)/` greedily consumes any non-digit at the end of `base`, including a `.`. For `"Claude Sonnet 4.6"` it captures `base = "Claude Sonnet 4."`, `suffix = "6"`, and then the function strips `suffix` because it's interpreted as a counter — leaving the dangling period the issue describes.

### Fix

Detect the dangling-period case after the regex match: if `base` ends with `<digit>.` and a `suffix` was captured, re-attach the `suffix` to `base` and treat the whole thing as the name. The standard counter logic (`base + index++` in the while loop) then appends the next available number, producing the expected `Claude Sonnet 4.61`.

5 lines of post-processing, no regex change, no impact on plain integer-suffixed names (`MyNode42 → MyNode43`).

### Test

`pnpm test useUniqueNodeName` — 7/7 passing (3 existing + 4 new):

- decimal name with single trailing digit → `4.6` → `4.61` → `4.62`
- multi-digit decimal → `5.10` → `5.101`
- multi-segment decimal → `2.0.5` → `2.0.51`
- regression: integer suffix without decimal still increments → `MyNode42` → `MyNode43`

To repro manually: add an Anthropic Chat Model, rename it to `Claude Sonnet 4.6`, then `Ctrl+D` to duplicate and verify the new node is named `Claude Sonnet 4.61`.

## Summary

Adds a Playwright smoke spec that boots the editor against the **Vite dev server** (not the production bundle) and fails on any error-level console message or uncaught page error during load. Wires it into CI on PRs touching files known to influence dev-server module resolution.

Nothing pre-merge caught it. This spec does.

### What's in the diff

- **New spec** `packages/testing/playwright/tests/dev-server-smoke/dev-server-boots.spec.ts` — covers home, blank canvas, credentials. Fails on `console.error` and `pageerror`. Manual capture (rather than the existing context-scoped `consoleErrorFixtures`) because that fixture only attaches diagnostics, never fails the test, and doesn't observe `pageerror`.
- **New Playwright project** `dev-server-smoke` registered in `playwright-projects.ts` with its own `testDir` so it's not picked up by the container e2e modes.

title: fix(editor): Preserve JSON value types when importing cURL commands
body:
## Summary

Importing a cURL command with a JSON body silently coerces non-string values to strings. For example, `curl ... --data-raw '{"size":100}'` ends up sending `{"size":"100"}` to the server because the body is routed through keypair mode, which calls `value.toString()` on every entry.

This PR switches the JSON-import branch to use raw JSON body mode whenever any top-level value is non-string (numbers, booleans, nulls, arrays, nested objects). Pure-string JSON bodies still use keypair mode for the better editing UX, so this is a no-op for that path.

**Before**

```bash
# Import this:
curl 'http://hostname' -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-raw '{"size":100}'

# Node sends:
{"size":"100"}
```

**After**

```bash
# Same import, node sends:
{"size":100}
```

### Changes

- `useImportCurlCommand.ts` — rename `jsonHasNestedObjects` to `jsonHasNonStringValues` and broaden it to flag any non-string value, not just nested objects/arrays. Add a `typeof json !== 'string'` guard to keep the existing URLSearchParams path for string-typed `data`.
- `useImportCurlCommand.test.ts` — 4 new tests covering integer, boolean, null, and mixed-type JSON bodies, plus an added `specifyBody === 'keypair'` assertion on the existing all-strings test as a regression guard.

### Test

- `pnpm test useImportCurlCommand` — 59/59 passing (55 existing + 4 new)
- `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm lint` (changed files) — 0 errors

To repro manually: paste `curl 'http://hostname' -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-raw '{"size":100}'` into HTTP Request → Import cURL, then execute and inspect the request body.

title: fix(core): Restore peer project discovery in share dropdowns
body:
## Summary

`global:member` users could not share personal workflows or credentials: the
"add users" field in the share modal was empty, regardless of the Personal
Space Sharing policy. This restores peer-personal-project discovery for the
share dropdowns by routing them through a new dedicated endpoint, while
keeping the existing `GET /rest/projects` listing intentionally strict.

### Why

The share modal is wired to a server-paginated project search introduced in
#27036, which originally returned every personal project plus the caller's
own relations — exactly what the dropdown needs to surface other users as
share targets.

#27206 (Instance AI module) bundled a change to
`ProjectRepository.getAccessibleProjectsAndCount` that tightened the query
to `INNER JOIN projectRelations WHERE userId = :userId`. The same tightening
was also applied to `getAccessibleProjects` (non-paginated), where it was
correct: that variant is consumed by the Instance AI agent's `listProjects`
tool and the favorites filter set, both of which want only projects the
caller can manipulate. The paginated variant, however, backs the share
dropdowns — conflating the two semantics broke peer discovery for members.

This PR makes the two semantics first-class so they can't be silently
conflated again:

- `getAccessibleProjectsAndCount` keeps its post-#27206 strict semantics
  ("projects I can manipulate"). Backs `GET /rest/projects`.
- `getShareableProjectsAndCount` (new) restores the wide semantics
  ("projects I can pick as share targets, including peer personal
  projects"). Backs `GET /rest/projects/sharing-candidates`.
- The share / transfer / user-deletion modal composable
  (`useRemoteProjectSearch`) is switched to call the new endpoint.

The new endpoint is gated by `@GlobalScope('user:list')` — the same boundary
`GET /rest/users` enforces, since the dropdown surfaces user identity
(`First Last <email>` is the personal project name). Members already carry
this scope; restricted roles like chat-only users do not and receive 403.

### How to test manually

1. Run an Enterprise build (license with Personal Space Sharing).
2. Create one instance owner and at least two members (e.g. Alice, Bob);
   complete signup so both members have passwords.
3. Sign in as Alice → open any of Alice's personal workflows → Share.
4. Click the "add users…" field. **Expected:** Bob's personal project (and
   any other peer personal projects) appears in the dropdown.
5. Type `bob` in the field. **Expected:** the dropdown narrows server-side
   and Bob remains visible.
6. Repeat steps 3–4 from a credential's Sharing tab. Same expected
   behaviour.
7. Sign in as the instance owner → Share modal → confirm the full project
   list still appears (no admin regression).
8. In DevTools, confirm the share dropdown issues
   `GET /rest/projects/sharing-candidates?...take=50&...` (200) and not
   `GET /rest/projects`. Confirm the response `data[]` contains every
   member's personal project.
9. Optional negative check: as a chat-only user, request
   `GET /rest/projects/sharing-candidates` directly. **Expected:** 403.

### Key implementation decisions

- **Dedicated endpoint instead of a query-param flag.** The two list
  semantics are genuinely different, so they get distinct names at every
  layer (route, service, repository).
- **Don't touch `getAccessibleProjects` (non-paginated).** Its tightening
  in #27206 is correct and load-bearing for Instance AI and favorites.
- **Don't gate the listing on the Personal Space Sharing license/policy.**
  That license controls whether a user can be the *source* of sharing from
  their personal space; it's enforced at write-time on the share endpoints.
  Visibility of peer personal projects in the listing is an orthogonal
  concern, consistent with the design from #27036.

- Closes #29002

- Original correct design: `3b00e1bafe` (PR #27036)

title: feat(agents): Expose triggers configuration in agent JSON config
body:
## Summary

Exposes scheduled and chat integration triggers through `AgentJsonConfig.integrations` so the builder agent can read and modify them via `write_config` / `patch_config`, the same way it manages `tools` today.

- **API types & validation**: new `integrations` discriminated union (`schedule` + chat platforms) added to `AgentJsonConfig` with Zod schema. Chat entries now carry `credentialName` next to `credentialId`. The legacy "Connect" controller endpoint resolves and stores `credentialName` so existing UI flows match the new schema shape.
- **Storage stays put**: `agent.integrations` column remains the source of truth — no DB migration. `composeJsonConfig` / `decomposeJsonConfig` merge it with `agent.schema` on read and split it back on write.
- **Lifecycle sync**: `updateConfig` now diffs old vs new integrations and drives `AgentScheduleService.applyConfig` (cron registration) and `ChatIntegrationService.syncToConfig` (connect/disconnect chat platforms) so the runtime tracks the persisted config without requiring a publish.
- **Builder integration**: new `list_integration_types` tool for discovering available chat platforms plus an `INTEGRATIONS_SECTION` in the system prompt explaining the workflow (`list_integration_types` → `ask_credential` → `patch_config`).

**How to test:**
1. Open an agent in the builder and ask "What triggers does my agent have?" — the LLM should report the actual integrations.
2. On an **unpublished** agent, ask "Connect this agent to my Slack workspace" — the LLM calls `list_integration_types`, then `ask_credential`, then `patch_config`. The integration is persisted but not connected; check the integrations status endpoint to confirm.
3. Publish the agent — the Slack connection now activates (status flips to `connected`, webhook live).
4. Ask the LLM to set the cron to `not-a-cron` — `patch_config` fails at the schema stage with an "Invalid cron expression" error.
5. Ask the LLM to set `active: true` on an unpublished agent — `patch_config` is rejected with a publish-gate error.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- **`AgentPublishedVersion` snapshot** — integrations still live on the live entity, not the published version. Existing schedule activation requires a published agent; that contract is unchanged.
- **`AgentScheduleTriggerCard` local-state dance** — the card maintains `lastSavedCronExpression` / `hydrating` flags to coordinate its debounced save against server fetches. A Pinia-backed store would let cards subscribe to a single source of truth and remove that local plumbing entirely.
- **`AgentIntegrationsPanel.vue` cleanup** — the component is no longer mounted in production after the `AgentBuilderEditorColumn` restructure on `n8n-agents` (only test mocks reference it). Removal is out of scope for this PR.

title: fix(core): Add missing @n8n/tournament alias to Vite config (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

After `@n8n/tournament` was moved into the monorepo (#29358), its Vite alias was never added to `editor-ui/vite.config.mts`. All other monorepo packages have an alias redirecting bare imports to their `src/` directory so Vite serves TypeScript directly in dev mode. Without this alias, Vite resolved `@n8n/tournament` via the `exports` map, which points both `import` and `require` conditions to the CJS `dist/index.js`. CJS re-exports of `recast` named exports (like `astVisit`) don't surface as ESM named imports, causing the dev server crash:

```
Uncaught SyntaxError: The requested module '/@fs/.../packages/@n8n/tournament/dist/index.js'
does not provide an export named 'astVisit'
```

**Fix:** Add one alias entry pointing `@n8n/tournament` → `src/`, consistent with every other monorepo package alias in the file.

**To test:** Run `pnpm dev:fe` -> browser should load without the SyntaxError.

title: fix(core): Persist execution context before writing to db (backport to release-candidate/2.19.x)
body:
# Description
Backport of #28973 to `release-candidate/2.19.x`.

## Checklist for the author (@phyllis-noester) to go through.

- [ ] Review the backport changes
- [ ] Fix possible conflicts

After this PR has been merged, it will be picked up in the next patch release for release track.

# Original description

## Summary

**Change:** Before `WorkflowRunner.run()` calls `activeExecutions.add()` (which triggers the DB write via
  `executionPersistence.create()`), it now builds a `Workflow` + `additionalData` and calls `establishExecutionContext()`. Guarded by
  `if (data.executionData)` so manual executions without pre-populated data skip the call.

  **Files:**
  - `packages/cli/src/workflow-runner.ts` — the fix, plus new `n8n-core` import
  - `packages/cli/src/__tests__/workflow-runner.test.ts` — 3 tests (ordering, masked-data-persisted, undefined-guard)
  - `packages/core/src/execution-engine/index.ts` — exports `establishExecutionContext`
  - `packages/core/src/execution-engine/__tests__/execution-context.test.ts` — worker idempotency test

  # Why

  **Problem:** In queue mode, raw `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>` headers from webhook triggers were written to PostgreSQL before
  anything masked them. The worker masked in memory later, but the DB held the raw token until (and unless) the worker wrote an updated
   record. A worker crash left the raw JWT as the final row.

  **Why in `WorkflowRunner.run()`:** Every execution path funnels through here (webhooks, chat, wait-tracker resumes, manual, CLI, MCP,
   AI-builder). Placing the call at this choke point gives uniform coverage and co-locates context establishment with the
  enqueue-vs-local decision and the DB write.

  **Why it's safe to run twice:** `establishExecutionContext` early-exits if `runtimeData` is already set. The worker still calls it
  inside `WorkflowExecute.processRunExecutionData`, but finds `runtimeData` populated and returns immediately — no double-processing.

  **Why the minimal build (not the thread-through refactor):** `runMainProcess()` does more than `establishExecutionContext` needs
  (staticData loading, pinData, timeouts). Lifting that would change `loadStaticData` semantics in queue mode. Building one extra
  `Workflow` + `additionalData` per execution is cheap and keeps the diff tightly scoped to the security fix.

## Testing

  These steps verify that webhook headers are redacted in the persisted execution
  data **while the execution is still running** (not just after completion).

  ### Prerequisites

  - Docker running
  - A workflow JSON that starts with a Webhook trigger and has a long-running step
  afterwards (e.g. a `Wait` node set to several minutes). An example workflow file
  is attached to this PR.

  ### 1. Start n8n in queue mode

  From `packages/testing/containers/`:

  ```bash
  args=(--queue)
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    args+=(--env "$line")
  done < <(grep -v '^\s*#\|^\s* ../../../.env)
  npx tsx ./n8n-start-stack.ts "${args[@]}"
  ```

  Note the project name printed in the logs (e.g. `n8n-stack-htdxh`) — you'll need
  it to connect to Postgres.

  ### 2. Import and activate the test workflow

  1. Open the n8n URL printed by the stack starter.
  2. Import the attached workflow JSON.
  3. Activate the workflow so the webhook is live.

  ### 3. Trigger the webhook

  Call the webhook URL with some headers that should be redacted (e.g.
  `Authorization`):

  ```bash
  curl -X POST <webhook-url> \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer secret-token-123" \
    -H "Cookie: session=abc123" \
    -H "X-Custom: visible-value"
  ```

  The workflow will start and pause on the long-running node, keeping the execution
  in a running state.

  ### 4. Inspect the persisted execution data

  While the execution is still running, open a psql shell against the stack's
  Postgres container:

  ```bash
  docker exec -it <project-name>-postgres psql -U n8n_user -d n8n_db
  ```

  Find the running execution's ID:

  ```sql
  SELECT id, status FROM execution_entity WHERE status = 'running' ORDER BY id DESC
  LIMIT 5;
  ```

  Check the persisted payload for that execution:

  ```sql
  SELECT data FROM execution_data WHERE "executionId" = '<id>';
  ```

  ### 5. Verify

  - Sensitive headers (e.g. `Authorization`, `Cookie`) appear **redacted** in the
  `data` column.
  - Non-sensitive headers (e.g. `X-Custom`) appear with their original values.
  - The row exists **before the execution finishes** — confirming the context is
  persisted pre-completion.

title: feat(core): Decouple insights pruning max age from license
body:
- Default N8N_INSIGHTS_MAX_AGE_DAYS is 365.
- Caps max age at 730 days (INSIGHTS_MAX_AGE_DAYS_CAP).
- Legacy -1 maps to 730.
- Invalid / non-finite / < 1 (except -1) fall back to the default.

## Summary

Deletion of self-hosted insights data is now controlled only by the environment variable (`N8N_INSIGHTS_MAX_AGE_DAYS`). License max age is no longer combined with the env var. The default retention window is 365 days, with a maximum of 730 days. The legacy -1 value is treated as maximum, so behavior stays consistent and there is no separate “unlimited” mode via this variable.

### Context
Previously, effective pruning used `min(license quota: insights retention max age, env)`, with a common license default of 180 days when the env default was -1. That coupling is removed.

### Impact

| What the customer has today | Parsed config | Effective days kept before prune | Notes |
|------------------------------|----------------|-----------------------------------|--------|
| **Unset** (never defined) | default `365` | **365** | Default is **365**; not license-derived. Customers who previously had no env and saw ~180 from license logic will retain **more** data unless they set `180` explicitly. |
| **Positive integer** `1`–`730` | same as env | **Same as set** | Explicit value is used as-is. |
| **Integer > 730** (e.g. `9999`) | number | **730** | Capped at the maximum allowed retention. |
| **`-1`** (legacy “max” / unlimited style) | `-1` | **730** | Mapped to the cap (same as maximum). |
| **`0` or other < 1** (not `-1`) | e.g. `0` | **365** | Falls back to the default. |
| **Not a finite number** (invalid / bad coercion) | non-finite | **365** | Invalid values use the default. |

body:
## Summary

Adds a new **Reveal redacted data** permission to the Executions section of the custom roles configuration UI, giving admins granular control over who can reveal redacted execution data within a project.

The `execution:reveal` scope already existed in the backend permissions system and was enforced by the `ExecutionRedactionService`. This change surfaces it in the custom roles UI so it can be granted or withheld per role.

**Before:** there was no way to configure the reveal capability in a custom role — only fixed system roles (admin/owner) had access.

**After:**
- A new **Executions** section appears in the custom roles permissions matrix.
- The **Reveal redacted data** checkbox controls whether users with that role can reveal redacted execution data.
- Existing admin and personal project owner roles retain reveal access by default (no change to built-in role scopes).

### Changes
- `projectRoleScopes.ts` — adds `execution: ['reveal']` to `UI_OPERATIONS` and `'execution'` to `SCOPE_TYPES`
- `en.json` — adds `projectRoles.type.execution`, `projectRoles.execution:reveal`, and `projectRoles.execution:reveal.tooltip`

### Manual testing steps

**Setup:** you need an n8n instance with the Enterprise plan (custom roles feature), and a workflow with execution data redaction enabled (Workflow Settings → Save execution data → Redact).

1. Go to **Settings → Project Roles** and create a custom role.
2. Confirm an **Executions** section is visible with a **Reveal redacted data** checkbox.
3. Create one role **with** the permission checked and one **without**.
4. Assign each role to a different team member in a project containing the redaction-enabled workflow.
5. Trigger a production execution of the workflow.
6. **As the user with the permission:** open the execution in the editor, click a node — confirm the "Reveal data" button is shown and works.
7. **As the user without the permission:** open the same execution — confirm no reveal button is shown and the redacted state message indicates they lack permission.

## Summary

Fixes the silent stuck-channel bug described in #29372 by detecting per-runner consecutive task-accept timeouts and disconnecting the runner so its launcher can restart it via the existing recovery path. Adds 6 new unit tests.

The bug: in `N8N_RUNNERS_MODE=external`, the broker↔runner WebSocket can enter a state where the transport layer is healthy (`/healthz` returns 200, ping/pong passes) but the application-level message channel is dead. Every task request times out at 60s indefinitely; stuck windows of 10–37 hours are documented in the issue.

The diagnosis: the broker has no per-runner failure tracking and no signal that connects "this runner stopped acknowledging accepts" to the existing connection-recovery machinery. Each `TaskRunnerAcceptTimeoutError` is currently logged and discarded.

The fix: count consecutive `TaskRunnerAcceptTimeoutError`s per runner. After 3 consecutive failures (~6s at the default 2s accept timeout), emit a new lifecycle event `runner:unresponsive` with the offending runner's id. `TaskBrokerWsServer` subscribes to the event and disconnects the runner via the existing `removeConnection()` path. The launcher then restarts the runner the same way it does on any connection-loss, restoring the channel within seconds.

Detection latency drops from "hours" to ~6 seconds for the failure mode where the runner accepts offers but never acknowledges accepts.

## Approach

This follows the pattern accepted in #25959: surface real health on existing signals rather than building a parallel monitoring mechanism. `TaskRunnerAcceptTimeoutError` is an existing signal that the broker already generates and already logs — this PR just counts the failures per-runner and acts on the pattern.

The reporter's stated framing in the issue maps directly to this shape:

> "the broker should treat N consecutive task timeouts to a given runner as a connection failure and disconnect that runner. Once the connection drops, the existing launcher and orchestrator paths take over and recovery happens within seconds rather than hours."

The `TaskRunnerAcceptTimeoutError` carries `runnerId` at construction (`task-broker.service.ts` `acceptOffer` line ~549), so attribution is direct — in multi-runner deployments, only the stuck runner is disconnected, not healthy peers.

## Changes

**`task-REDACTED.ts`** — adds `'runner:unresponsive': { runnerId: string }` to the typed event map. First event in this map with a payload (existing two are `never`).

**`task-broker.service.ts`** — adds:
- private `runnerConsecutiveAcceptTimeouts: Map<TaskRunner['id'], number>` tracking per-runner consecutive failure counts
- private static `STUCK_RUNNER_ACCEPT_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD = 3`
- private `recordAcceptTimeoutFor(runnerId)` helper called from the existing `TaskRunnerAcceptTimeoutError` catch in `acceptOffer`
- counter reset on successful accept (right after the existing `clearTimeout(request.timeout)`) and on `deregisterRunner`

**`task-broker-ws-server.ts`** — subscribes to `runner:unresponsive` in `start()` and unsubscribes in `stop()`. Handler calls `removeConnection(runnerId, 'failed-heartbeat-check', WsStatusCodes.CloseProtocolError)` — re-using the existing disconnect reason because the recovery semantics are identical (WS connection terminated, runner deregistered, launcher restarts).

**Tests added (6 new):**

`task-broker.service.test.ts`:
- `should emit 'runner:unresponsive' after 3 consecutive accept timeouts on the same runner`
- `should reset the consecutive accept-timeout counter when the runner is deregistered`
- `should not emit 'runner:unresponsive' when timeouts are spread across different runners` (verifies per-runner attribution)

`task-broker-ws-server.test.ts`:
- `should disconnect the named runner when the broker emits 'runner:unresponsive'`
- `should not disconnect other runners when one is reported unresponsive`
- `should unsubscribe on stop so events after stop do not disconnect runners`

The existing `task runner accept timeout` test (broker should handle a single timeout) continues to pass unchanged.

## Scope boundary (deferred follow-up)

This fix detects "runner accepts offers but never acks accepts." It does NOT detect the variant where a runner is connected (WS pings pass) but stops sending offers entirely — in that case, the broker's `acceptOffer` is never called, so the counter never increments. This variant is acknowledged in #29372's stuck-window data but appears less common than the no-ack variant; addressing it would require a per-runner offer-arrival timestamp check, which is a separate concern from accept-timeout tracking. Happy to follow up with a second PR if maintainers want both variants in this iteration.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test` for the cli package — 6 new tests pass; existing accept-timeout and deregisterRunner tests still pass (48 / 48 in the two affected files).
- [x] Typecheck clean.
- [ ] Manual repro of the original bug requires a Cloud Run / sustained external-runner deployment; not feasible in a development checkout. The diagnosis is grounded in code-path tracing — every line of the fix maps to the cited file:line locations referenced in the issue body.
- [ ] Maintainer review.

Closes #29372 (pending validation).

title: fix(ai-builder): Filter LangSmith eval dataset by local file slugs
body:
## Summary

The eval CLI was reading scenarios directly from the LangSmith dataset when no `--filter` was given. The dataset is additive (`syncDataset` never deletes — see comment in `evaluations/langsmith/dataset-sync.ts`), so orphans from past branches and deleted test cases accumulate over time. PR runs end up evaluating both current scenarios and the orphans, roughly doubling the workload and pushing recent runs over the 45-minute workflow cap.

This PR always filters by the slugs of the local `data/workflows/*.json` files at query time. Local files are the source of truth; orphans get skipped without any change to the sync logic.

**How to test**

Locally with `LANGSMITH_API_KEY` set:

```bash
cd packages/@n8n/instance-ai
dotenvx run -f ../../../.env.local -- pnpm eval:instance-ai --filter cross-team-linear --iterations 2
```

Look for `Local test cases matched N split(s):` (or `Filter "..." matched N split(s):` when `--filter` is passed) in the log — confirms the filter is being applied.

**Why split out from TRUST-27**

The same fix is already part of [PR #29456](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/29456) (TRUST-27 regression detector), but that PR is large. Splitting this small fix lets it merge quickly to unblock anyone whose master CI eval is timing out due to orphan accumulation.

title: feat(core): Add built-in cluster health checks (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Adds four built-in cluster health checks on top of the reconciliation infrastructure shipped in #28936. Each check runs every 3 minutes on the leader, evaluates a snapshot of the cluster state, and emits warnings (surfaced via the `/instance-registry` REST endpoint) and audit events (delivered to log-streaming destinations) when issues are detected.

- **Version Mismatch** — instances running different n8n versions (typical during rolling upgrades).
- **HostId Clash** — multiple instances sharing the same `hostId` (cloned VMs or misconfiguration).
- **Split-Brain** — multiple instances claiming the `leader` role (data-corruption risk).
- **Lifecycle** — audit trail of instances joining or leaving the cluster.

### Why

This is the second slice of the cluster-visibility initiative. #28936 added the reconciliation loop and the `@ClusterCheck()` decorator infrastructure, plus a stub `VersionMismatchCheck` so the loop had something to run. This PR replaces that stub with the spec'd version (audit events + dedup) and adds the remaining three checks. After this PR, operators get out-of-the-box detection of the most common distributed-deployment failure modes.

### Key implementation decisions

**Stateless deduplication via `previousState` fingerprinting.** The three stateful checks (version-mismatch, hostid-clash, split-brain) compute a deterministic fingerprint of their finding from `context.currentState` and compare it to one derived from `context.previousState`. Same fingerprint → warning only (so the REST `checks` summary stays accurate); changed → fresh audit event; cleared → one-shot `*.resolved` audit event; then silence. No `CacheService`, no in-memory state on the check — survives leader handoffs cleanly because `previousState` is already persisted by `InstanceRegistryService.saveLastKnownState`.

**Lifecycle check uses `diff.added` / `diff.removed` directly.** No fingerprinting — the diff is already one-shot per cycle.

**Direct audit emission, no `EventService` relay.** Checks declaratively describe their audit events via `ClusterCheckResult.auditEvents`; `CheckService` forwards them to `MessageEventBus.sendAuditEvent()` directly. This diverges from the typical `EventService.emit() → @Redactable() relay → sendAuditEvent()` pattern but is appropriate here because checks are pluggable and own their audit semantics. Cluster payloads contain no user PII (instance keys, hostIds, versions, leader info), so redaction isn't needed. The 8 cluster audit names are registered in `eventNamesAudit`; from there they reach log-streaming destinations via prefix match (`hasSubscribedToEvent` in `message-event-bus-destination.ee.ts`) — no relay map entry required.

**No push notifications.** Earlier draft of this PR added a `ClusterCheckPushMessage` push type for real-time UI updates; removed after team discussion. The REST endpoint already exposes `checks` summaries, and audit events cover the long-lived observability story.

body:
## Summary

Add a warning HITL approval gate before `build-workflow-with-agent` can spawn the builder for a pre-existing workflow edit. This closes the gap where Instance AI could choose a similar existing workflow and start modifying it without surfacing the `updateWorkflow` approval contract.

The gate now respects `updateWorkflow` permissions before builder spawn, includes the workflow name/id and edit reason in the confirmation message, and returns the admin-blocked and user-denied paths without spawning the builder.

## Behavior

- Pre-existing workflow selected for edit: prompt for approval before the builder starts.
- Workflow created by Instance AI earlier in the active plan cycle: skip the extra edit prompt so the builder can keep iterating on its own draft.
- Admin-blocked `updateWorkflow`: reject before either the same-cycle bypass or the approval prompt.
- Replan/checkpoint follow-ups: continue without double-prompting.

Also update planned `build-workflow` permission overrides so approved plans always allow workflow create/update/run/publish, and add unit plus Instance AI E2E replay coverage for approving and denying pre-existing workflow edits.

title: fix(ai-builder): Handle properties with contradicting displayOptions as OR alternatives instead of AND
body:
## Summary

Properties declared multiple times with the same name are OR alternatives - the BigQuery `sqlQuery` field shown for useLegacySql SQL is the canonical example, declared in [`packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/BigQuery/v2/actions/database/executeQuery.operation.ts`](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/BigQuery/v2/actions/database/executeQuery.operation.ts) as:

```ts
{
    displayName: 'SQL Query',
    name: 'sqlQuery',
    type: 'string',
    displayOptions: {
        hide: { '/options.useLegacySql': [true] },
    },
    placeholder: 'SELECT * FROM dataset.table LIMIT 100',
    description: 'SQL query to execute … Standard SQL syntax used by default …',
},
{
    displayName: 'SQL Query',
    name: 'sqlQuery',
    type: 'string',
    displayOptions: {
        show: { '/options.useLegacySql': [true] },
    },
    placeholder: 'SELECT * FROM [project:dataset.table] LIMIT 100;',
    hint: 'Legacy SQL syntax',
    description: 'SQL query to execute … about Legacy SQL syntax …',
},
```

The schema generator was naively union-merging the variants' `show`/`hide` independently, producing a self-contradicting predicate that rejected every valid configuration. The original repro trace showed instance AI burning 4 `submit-workflow` retries on `[INVALID_PARAMETER] sqlQuery: only allowed when /options.useLegacySql=true` before giving up and setting `useLegacySql: true` as an incorrect workaround (the query was standard SQL).

The agent was also reading a `.d.ts` whose JSDoc said:

```
@displayOptions.show { resource: ["database"], operation: ["executeQuery"], /options.useLegacySql: [true] }
@displayOptions.hide { /options.useLegacySql: [true] }
```

- directly self-contradictory, reinforcing the wrong mental model.

## What this PR fixes

This PR fixes both layers:

- **Runtime validator**: new `resolveOneOfSchemas` helper picks the first variant whose displayOptions match at evaluation time, with full DSL support (`@version`, `@tool`, `_cnd` operators, root paths) and correct required-when-visible enforcement (a naive `z.union` of per-variant `resolveSchema` calls would silently mask required because each inactive variant's "must-be-undefined" branch matches `undefined`).
- **JSDoc emitter**: `tryMergeUxForkVariants` collapses two-variant partitions into a single honest predicate so the `.d.ts` agents read no longer contradicts the validator. Handles the clean-partition case (BigQuery: same values on hide and show ⇒ drop the key) and the subset case (Pushbullet: `hide: K=[a,b]` + `show: K=[a]` ⇒ `hide: K=[b]`). Multi-key forks fall through and keep variant 1; the runtime path still uses `resolveOneOfSchemas` so validation stays correct.
- **String-operator hardening**: `_cnd.includes` / `startsWith` / `endsWith` / `regex` now return `false` instead of crashing when the referenced parameter isn't a string. Split variants now reach these operators where the old AND-merge happened to short-circuit past them (e.g. evaluating OpenAI image-edit's `/modelId: { _cnd: { includes: 'gpt-image' } }` when `modelId` is unset).

After the fix, the same BigQuery prompt produces zero `INVALID_PARAMETER sqlQuery` errors and the agent correctly leaves `useLegacySql` unset.

The simplified JSDoc reads:

```
@displayOptions.show { resource: ["database"], operation: ["executeQuery"] }
```

## Coverage across the 12 originally-flagged nodes

- **Simplifier kicks in** (clean .d.ts): BigQuery v2/v2.1 (`sqlQuery`), Git v1/v1.1 (`repositoryPath`), Firebase RealtimeDB v1 (`path`), Summarize v1/v1.1 (`fieldsToSplitBy`), Pushbullet (`value`).
- **False positives in original scan** (single declarations with deliberate symmetric show/hide, no fix needed): CoinGecko, Flow Trigger.
- **Falls through JSDoc simplifier** (runtime still correct via `resolveOneOfSchemas`): Cortex (`parameters`) — 5-variant `entityType` fork with extra `responder` constraints. The pairwise simplifier bails on multi-key forks; documented limitation.

- [x] Unit tests on `resolveOneOfSchemas` covering 0/1/many visible variants, required-when-visible, and the combined "A OR B …" error message.

title: fix(core): add execution_status tag to continueErrorOutput items
body:
## Problem
When a node uses `continueErrorOutput`, items are routed to success 
or error output pins by `handleNodeErrorOutput`. However, nothing in 
the item data indicates which branch was taken. Downstream nodes 
(e.g. Switch) have no way to distinguish execution path and can 
only read user input — they are execution-blind.

Fixes #29334

## Root cause
`handleNodeErrorOutput` in `workflow-execute.ts` splits items into 
success/error buckets but never tags which path they came from.

## Fix
Inject `execution_status: 'success' | 'error'` onto `item.json` 
at all three `push` call sites inside `handleNodeErrorOutput`.

## Changes
- `packages/core/src/execution-engine/workflow-execute.ts` — 3 line changes
- `packages/core/src/execution-engine/__tests__/workflow-execute.test.ts` — updated assertions + 2 new tests
- `packages/core/src/helpers/constants.ts` — updated fixture expected output

## Testing
- All 110 existing tests pass
- 2 new tests added covering success and error tagging
- Manually verified with HTTP node + continueErrorOutput + Switch workflow

## Note on existing test changes
Existing `handleNodeErrorOutput` test assertions were updated to 
include `execution_status` in their `toEqual` checks. This is 
intentional — those tests assert the full shape of `item.json`, 
so they must reflect the new field. The routing logic being tested 
is unchanged. Only the expected output shape is updated to match 
the fix.

title: feat: Add instance-level JWKS URI endpoint for JWE public key distribution
body:
## Summary

Adds a new instance-level JWKS endpoint at `GET /rest/.well-known/jwks.json` that serves all active OAuth JWE public keys from the `deployment_key` table, along with a JWKS URI display in the OAuth2 credential UI so admins can copy it into their IdP configuration.

In enterprise OIDC setups, n8n is typically registered as a single OAuth client whose IdP needs to fetch a JWKS document to encrypt tokens (JWE). One instance-level endpoint matches the IdP's single `jwks_uri` field per client and is configured once for all JWE-enabled credentials. The endpoint is feature-flagged, so instances that have not opted in expose zero new public surface.

## Why

Part of the OAuth JWE credential support initiative ([Notion PoC](https://www.notion.so/n8n/PoC-Meta-OIDC-Custom-Credential-with-JWE-Decryption-3415b6e0c94f80c0bb89d6f66fabac30), [Approach](https://www.notion.so/n8n/3425b6e0c94f80d8b8ecc2178d534a37)). The underlying key generation/storage already exists in `OAuthJweKeyService` (one active private JWK per algorithm in `deployment_key`, with `kid` and a public-field allow-list). This PR wires up the HTTP surface and the credential UI display — no new domain logic.

Key design decisions:
- **Instance-level, not per-credential** — one IdP client → one `jwks_uri`; per-credential endpoints would also leak credential IDs.
- **Feature-flagged at module init** — when `N8N_ENV_FEAT_OAUTH2_JWE` is off, the controller is never imported, so the route is never registered (genuine 404, not a runtime check). Matches the `token-exchange` module pattern.
- **Defense-in-depth Zod schema** — every JWK is validated against a strict (`.strict()`) public-only schema before it reaches the response, on top of the service-side allow-list. Malformed JWKs are dropped with a `logger.warn` so a bad row never breaks the endpoint for the rest of the keys.
- **Forward-looking schemas** — discriminated union on `kty` with both RSA and EC variants, even though only RSA-OAEP-256 is generated today. Adding EC support is a service-side change only.
- **Server-supplied absolute URL for the UI** — `jwksUri` is constructed in `frontend.service.ts` using `urlService.getInstanceBaseUrl()`, mirroring how `oauthCallbackUrls` flow. This honours the configured public host (e.g. behind a reverse proxy) instead of constructing a relative path on the frontend.
- **Path: `/rest/.well-known/jwks.json`** — closer to OIDC convention than `/rest/oauth2/jwks.json`. Still under `/rest`, so a strict OIDC discovery client must use it via explicit `jwks_uri` configuration (which is the intended flow).

## How to test manually

Prerequisites: a fresh n8n main with the JWE module initialised (it auto-generates an `RSA-OAEP-256` key in `deployment_key` on first boot).

**Flag OFF (default):**
```bash
pnpm start
curl -i http://localhost:5678/rest/.well-known/jwks.json
# Expected: 404 Not Found — route is not registered
```

**Flag ON:**
```bash
N8N_ENV_FEAT_OAUTH2_JWE=true pnpm start
curl -i http://localhost:5678/rest/.well-known/jwks.json
# Expected: 200 OK with:
#   Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600, must-revalidate
#   Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
# Body:
#   { "keys": [ { "kty": "RSA", "kid": "...", "use": "enc", "alg": "RSA-OAEP-256", "n": "...", "e": "AQAB" } ] }
```

**Rate limit (optional):**
- Hit the endpoint > 60 times/minute from the same IP. The 61st call should be rejected with 429. Tunable via `N8N_OAUTH_JWE_JWKS_PER_MINUTE`.

**UI verification:**
1. With `N8N_ENV_FEAT_OAUTH2_JWE=true`, open the editor, create or open an **OAuth2 API** credential.
2. Confirm a new copyable field **OAuth2 JWKS URI** appears below the existing **OAuth Redirect URL**.
3. Confirm the value is the **absolute** URL (e.g. `http://localhost:5678/rest/.well-known/jwks.json`), not a relative path. Click → toast confirms copy.
4. Restart with the flag unset; the JWKS URI field should not render.

**Security:**
- Decode the JWK from the response and confirm only public RSA fields are present (`kty, kid, use, alg, n, e`). No `d`, `p`, `q`, `dp`, `dq`, `qi`. The Zod schema (`.strict()`) drops anything else, and a unit test asserts this on a JWK that contains a leaked `d` field.

## Related Links

- closes https://linear.app/n8n/issue/IAM-478

## Notes for reviewers

- The spec example uses `"alg": "RSA-OAEP"`; the implementation actually serves whatever `OAuthJweKeyService` generates, which is `RSA-OAEP-256` (the more secure AES-key-wrap variant). The endpoint is intentionally a passthrough of what the service produces.

title: feat(core): Add JWE decryption to OAuth2 credential flow
body:
## Summary

Adds JWE decryption to the OAuth2 credential flow on both the authorization-code callback (`OAuth2CredentialController.handleCallback()`) and the refresh path (`refreshOrFetchToken` in the execution engine, plus the `clientCredentials` first-time acquisition). Decryption uses the instance JWE key from `OAuthJweKeyService` (shipped in IAM-476) — no per-credential keypairs.

A new `OAuthJweServiceProxy` lives in `packages/cli/src/oauth/`, outside the module; the `oauth-jwe` module wires the real `OAuthJweDecryptService` at `init()` time via a setter (mirroring the `ExecutionRedactionServiceProxy` pattern). The same proxy is exposed to `packages/core` via `additionalData['oauth-jwe']`. Plaintext rejection is response-level: the response must contain at least one JWE-shaped token (`access_token` or `id_token`); fully plaintext responses are rejected. This permits the common OIDC shape where `access_token` is opaque while `id_token` is JWE-wrapped.

Behaviour is gated behind `N8N_ENV_FEAT_OAUTH2_JWE` and a per-credential `jweEnabled` toggle on `OAuth2Api`. A temporary unauthenticated `GET /rest/oauth-jwe/jwks` endpoint is included for local IdP testing — to be replaced when IAM-478 ships the proper JWKS endpoint.

**Testing:** unit tests cover the proxy (flag-off/no-handler short-circuits, delegation, error propagation), the decrypt service (happy path, mixed JWE+plaintext acceptance, all-plaintext rejection, malformed JWE), the callback path (decrypted persist, plaintext rejection rendering, no-op passthrough), and the refresh path (proxy decrypts via `additionalData`, absent-provider no-op, plaintext rejection fails the refresh).

title: fix(editor): Never block publishing on node execution issues
body: ## Summary **Bug**: If a node has an issue that only appears after execution, you can publish the workflow before running it. However, once the node is executed and errors, publishing is blocked with "1 node has issues, fix them before publishing." title: fix: Handle IMAP fetch errors to prevent instance crash and stuck workflows
body:
## Summary

Fixes two bugs in `@n8n/imap` that caused the IMAP trigger to either crash the n8n instance or leave workflows permanently stuck.

In `imap-simple.ts`, removing the error listener from the fetch object in `fetchOnEnd` left a window where a late 'error' event had no handler, producing an uncaught exception that killed the process. In `get-message.ts`, the message parsing promise had no reject path, so a stream error during fetch caused it to hang forever — blocking the `onMail` callback indefinitely.

## Summary

Redesigns the Instance AI chat threads sidebar (Notion-style collapsible panel) and fixes thread ordering so the list actually reflects last activity.

### Sidebar redesign
- Sidebar is collapsed by default; a clock icon in the chat-area header opens it. Inside the sidebar, a chevron collapses it and a `+` starts a new thread.
- Collapse state is session-scoped (sessionStorage) and resets when the user navigates outside the chat namespace, so refreshing keeps it but re-entering from elsewhere starts collapsed.
- Sidebar slides in/out with a 200ms width + opacity transition; the chat-history entry-point button fades in/out so it doesn't pop in abruptly when the sidebar collapses.

- All chat-area header icon buttons (`history`, `cog`, `bug`, `panel-right`) and the thread-list header buttons (`chevrons-left`, `+`) now use `size="small"` + `icon-size="large"` to match the main n8n sidebar (16px SVGs).
- Tightened header padding (`2xs` vertical / `xs` horizontal in the chat area; `2xs` vertical in the thread list).
- Removed the bespoke `.settingsButton` padding override that was tuned for the old `medium` size.

### Thread ordering — fixes the long-standing "Older" bug
- **Backend (`fix(core)`):** `saveMessages` now bumps the parent thread's `updatedAt` after persisting messages. Previously the thread's timestamp was only set at creation, so an existing thread receiving new messages stayed stuck at its creation time and got buried in the "Older" bucket despite being actively used.
- **Frontend (`fix(editor)`):** the sidebar grouping now uses `thread.updatedAt ?? thread.createdAt` instead of `createdAt`, matching the backend's `ORDER BY updatedAt DESC` and the chatHub sidebar's `groupConversationsByDate` behavior.

## Summary

Adds the `node-operation-error-itemindex` ESLint rule to `@n8n/eslint-plugin-community-nodes`. This migrates `node-execute-block-error-missing-item-index` from the external `eslint-plugin-n8n-nodes-base` package as part of the dependency removal effort (CE-856).

**What the rule does:** Inside the `execute()` method of `INodeType` classes, any `new NodeOperationError(...)` or `new NodeApiError(...)` thrown inside an item loop must include `{ itemIndex }` in the options object (third argument). **Scope-narrowing (avoids false positives):** The rule only fires inside detected item loops — `for` or `for...of` statements that iterate over the result of `this.getInputData()`. Errors in webhook handlers, trigger setup, or credential helpers are not flagged. This addresses the false-positive problem from the earlier attempt in #29382.

title: fix(core): Skip disabled tool nodes when mapping AI Agent tool sources
body:
## Summary

When a tool node connected to an AI Agent was disabled but kept its connection wire, tool calls for tools after the disabled node in the connection order were routed to the wrong node.

In `getConnectedTools` (`packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/utils/helpers.ts`), two arrays were zipped together by index to assign each tool its `sourceNodeName`:

- `toolkitConnections` — from `getInputConnectionData`, which **excludes** disabled nodes (it internally calls `getConnectedNodes`, which filters via `node.disabled !== true`).
- `parentNodes` — from `getParentNodes`, which **includes** disabled nodes and only annotates them with a `disabled` flag.

Once a disabled-but-connected node was present, `parentNodes[index]` shifted out of alignment with `toolkitConnections[index]`, and every tool after the disabled one was tagged with the previous parent's name — sending its execution to the wrong node.

The fix filters disabled entries out of `parentNodes` so both arrays stay in sync.

### How to test

1. Create a workflow with an AI Agent and three Code Tools: Tool Alpha, Tool Bravo, Tool Charlie.
2. Connect all three tools to the agent.
3. Disable Tool Bravo (keep the wire).
4. Ask the agent to call Tool Alpha or Tool Charlie.
5. Before the fix: Tool Bravo executes for Charlie's call. After the fix: each call routes to the correct tool.

A unit test in `helpers.test.ts` covers the regression.

title: feat(ai-builder): Add per-PR eval regression detection vs LangSmith baseline
body:
## Summary

Adds per-PR regression detection to the Instance AI eval framework. When `LANGSMITH_API_KEY` is set, every eval run automatically compares its results against the most recent pinned baseline (`instance-ai-baseline-*`) on LangSmith and surfaces verdicts in the PR comment.

**What it adds**

- **Tiered classifier** per scenario: regression / soft regression / notable movement / improvement / stable / unreliable_baseline / insufficient_data. Uses Fisher's exact test plus a reliability gate, calibrated for the small N PR runs use.
- **Run-level failure-category drift** (orthogonal signal that catches broad model-quality shifts that per-scenario flags can miss — e.g. a sudden jump in `framework_issue` rate or a brand-new category appearing).
- **Two output files**: `eval-results.json` (structured data only — `comparison.result`) and `eval-pr-comment.md` (the rendered PR comment, including aggregate, sections per tier, per-test-case results, failure details).
- **Redesigned PR comment** for human readability: GitHub alert at top (`[!CAUTION]` / `[!WARNING]` / `[!NOTE]` / `[!TIP]`) with a one-line verdict, conditional sections (only render when they have content), arrow indicators on deltas, and `🆕` markers for newly-appeared failure categories.
- **Terminal formatter** for the local console with aligned-column tables — same structure as the markdown, no ANSI escapes, same data backing both views.
- **N=5 by default in CI** (was N=3) — meaningful detection-power gain on bimodal scenarios at modest CI cost (~10-12 min wall time on the multi-container parallel runner).
- **Best-effort**: comparison failures never fail the eval run; the `eval-pr-comment.md` still renders a useful summary when no baseline exists yet.

**How to test**

1. Locally:
   ```bash
   cd packages/@n8n/instance-ai
   dotenvx run -f ../../../.env.local -- pnpm eval:instance-ai --filter cross-team-linear --iterations 2
   ```
   Look for the aligned terminal block at the end of the run, plus two output files in the package dir: `eval-results.json` and `eval-pr-comment.md`.
2. In CI: the workflow `cat`s `eval-pr-comment.md` straight into the PR-comment update — the eval CLI owns the entire rendered comment now (the previous jq pipeline is gone).

**Validation**

Validated across 13 eval runs covering same-code stability + 4 deliberate regression injections (HubSpot 503 runtime, Haiku model swap, prompt-level injections):

- Zero false-positive hard flags across 8 same-code N=3/N=10 comparisons against the pinned baseline.
- 2 hard flags on the HubSpot-503 runtime injection (the two HubSpot scenarios) — high signal, no noise.
- 6 hard + 3 soft flags on a Haiku model-swap injection. The failure-category drift table separately caught the same regression via `framework_issue` rate moving from 0% → 6%, demonstrating the orthogonality.

**Note on commit history**: this branch has 4 incremental commits. They all pertain to the same feature (initial detector → format redesign → N=5/wording fix → fix wiring) and will collapse into a single commit on merge.

title: feat(core): Export and import data table user-row contents
body:
## Summary

> [!NOTE]
> Stacked on top of #29454 — review that one first. This PR's diff is only the row-contents addition.

The previous PR (#29454) recreates empty backing tables on import, restoring basic functionality. This PR completes the round trip by exporting the rows themselves so a true backup/restore of data tables is possible.

### Export
- Adds \`exportDataTableUserTables\` after the entity-metadata loop. Uses keyset pagination on \`id\` (auto-increment) instead of \`OFFSET\` so large tables don't degrade on Postgres.
- Encrypts to \`data_table_user_<id>.jsonl\` (paginated 500 rows/file) using the same cipher and zip path as the rest of the archive.
- Adds \`--includeDataTableRows\` flag (default \`true\`) so users can opt out of row contents and produce schema-only archives.

### Import
- Routes \`data_table_user_*.jsonl\` files in \`getImportMetadata\` into a separate bucket keyed by data table id. Old archives (or schema-only ones) without those files still import cleanly — the backing tables are recreated empty.
- Extends \`recreateDataTableUserTablesFromRegistry\` to load and insert rows from the bucket, preserving \`id\`, \`createdAt\`, and \`updatedAt\` on the destination.
- Normalises booleans (sqlite stores 0/1 INTEGER, Postgres BOOLEAN) and dates (sqlite TEXT lacks timezone info, treated as UTC) so cross-DB exports round-trip correctly.
- Resets the Postgres IDENTITY sequence to \`MAX(id)\` after inserts since explicit-id inserts don't auto-advance it.

### How to test

**Same-DB round trip (sqlite → sqlite or Postgres → Postgres):**
1. On a source, create a data table with columns of every type (string, number, boolean, date) and add a few rows.
2. \`n8n export:entities --outputDir=./out\`
3. On a fresh destination, \`n8n import:entities --inputDir=./out --truncateTables\`
4. Verify the data table on the destination has the same rows with the same ids and timestamps.
5. Add a new row via the UI on the destination — confirm the auto-id continues from \`MAX(id)+1\` (no collision).

**Cross-DB round trip (sqlite → Postgres):** repeat with two instances on different DB engines and confirm boolean and date values survive correctly.

**Schema-only export:** \`n8n export:entities --includeDataTableRows=false\` then import. Backing tables are created empty on the destination.

title: fix(core): Recreate data table backing tables on entity import
body:
## Summary

`n8n export:entities` captures rows in `data_table` and `data_table_column`, but the backing `data_table_user_<id>` tables are pure runtime DDL with no TypeORM entity, so they aren't recreated on the destination during `import:entities`. After import the data tables appear in the UI but any read or write fails because the backing tables don't exist on the destination.

This PR fixes the import side only — it does not change export. After import, data tables are visible and usable, but contain zero rows. [A follow-up PR](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/29455) extends this with row export/import for full round-trip backups.

### What it does
- Injects `DataTableDDLService` into `ImportService`
- Adds `dropExistingDataTableUserTables` — runs before `--truncateTables` so dynamic backing tables don't end up orphaned once the registry is wiped
- Adds `recreateDataTableUserTablesFromRegistry` — runs after the entity import phase, drops any stale backing table, then creates an empty one with the imported column metadata
- Tests cover: drop on existing registry, prefix handling, missing-registry skip, columns sorted by index, drop-then-create order, registry-empty no-op

### How to test
1. On a source instance, create a few data tables with columns and rows in the UI.
2. Run `n8n export:entities --outputDir=./out`.
3. On a fresh destination, run `n8n import:entities --inputDir=./out --truncateTables`.
4. Open the destination — the data tables appear with their columns intact (rows will be empty, that's expected for this PR).
5. Verify you can add rows, edit columns, and delete the tables — all operations now work.

title: ci: Fix licensed test filter for fork PR e2e runs
body:
## Summary

Fork PRs were running `@licensed` tests despite the CI command having a `--grep-invert="@licensed"` filter. Caused by shell quoting — the literal double quotes inside the YAML expression were preserved as part of the argv value, so Playwright received the regex `"@licensed"` (with quote characters) instead of `@licensed`, matched zero tests, and filtered nothing.

Evidence from a failing fork PR run — note the literal quotes in the resolved command:

```
playwright test --project='sqlite:e2e' '--grep-invert="@licensed"' --workers=1 ...
```

## Root cause

`.github/workflows/ci-pull-requests.yml:218` defined the fork-PR test command as:

```yaml
'pnpm --filter=n8n-playwright test:container:sqlite:e2e --grep-invert="@licensed"'
```

When `test-e2e-reusable.yml` later runs `$TEST_COMMAND --workers="$WORKERS" $SHARD_ARGS`, bash word-splits the variable but does not re-process the embedded `"` characters, so Playwright receives the literal value `"@licensed"`.

## Fix

Drop the inner double quotes — `@licensed` has no spaces and doesn't need them:

```diff
- ... --grep-invert="@licensed"
+ ... --grep-invert=@licensed
```

title: fix: Allow 5-field cron expressions with step values in polling nodes

## Summary

Custom cron expressions like */15 9-17 * * * (every 15 minutes, 9am–5pm) were incorrectly rejected with "The polling interval is too short" because the validation assumed all expressions were 6-field (seconds + minutes + ...) and checked field 0 for a wildcard. For 5-field standard cron expressions, field 0 is minutes — not seconds — so */15 was misread as a sub-minute seconds value.

Fix: Only apply the seconds-wildcard check when the expression has 6 fields. 5-field expressions have minute-level granularity by definition.

The append operation was making 3 redundant GET requests per execution cycle (fetching the header row in `getData`, `autoMapInputData`, and` convertObjectArrayToSheetDataArray)`. With the 60 reads/minute quota, this caused 429 Too Many Requests errors after ~20 loop iterations.

Changes:

- Added `columnNamesHint` side-channel on `GoogleSheet` — set once by the caller, consumed and cleared by `convertObjectArrayToSheetDataArray` to skip its own fetch
- append.operation.ts now extracts the header row from the already-fetched `sheetData` and passes it down, reducing reads per append from 3 to 1
- `autoMapInputData` accepts an optional `prefetchedColumnNames` param to skip its internal `getData` call and stores the - final column list (including newly-added columns) via `setColumnNamesHint`
- Fixed a bug where newly-discovered columns were added to the sheet header but their values were silently dropped from the data row

body:
# Description
Backport of #26848 to `1.x`.

## Checklist for the author (@tomi) to go through.

- [x] Review the backport changes

After this PR has been merged, it will be picked up in the next patch release for release track.

# Original description

## Summary

This fix addresses intermittent task runner connection failures by validating authentication **before** the WebSocket upgrade, preventing opaque close frames when auth fails. The reason why it hang was that the connection was closed by sending a HTTP response **after** the connection had already been upgraded. This meant the other end was expecting WS frames instead of HTTP, which meant the `error` handler attached to `ws` never fired and the connection wasn't closed. This also adds a logic to shutdown the runner if the connection drops since it can't be recovered due to single use token.

**Key changes:**
- Validate grant tokens during the HTTP upgrade request phase (401/403 errors are now returned before upgrade)
- Exit process on unexpected connection close, but skip exit during graceful shutdown
- Improved error logging and test coverage for authentication and connection lifecycle

title: feat(core): Improve Redis queue mode TLS, cluster, and connection options
body:
## Summary

Expand the Redis client used by queue mode (`packages/cli/src/services/redis-client.service.ts`) with richer TLS/mTLS support, cluster-friendly DNS handling, IPv6 selection, auto-pipelining, and improved connection diagnostics. All new options are opt-in and backward compatible — existing `QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_TLS=true` and `QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_DUALSTACK` deployments are unaffected.

### What's new

**TLS / mTLS configuration** (`RedisTlsConfig` in [scaling-mode.config.ts](packages/@n8n/config/src/configs/scaling-mode.config.ts))

Previously TLS was an on/off switch with default Node.js settings. New env vars allow full control, including mTLS for AWS ElastiCache and other managed Redis offerings:

| Env var | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_TLS_CA_FILE` | Root CA certificate (PEM) |
| `QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_TLS_CERT_FILE` | Client certificate (PEM) |
| `QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_TLS_CERT_KEY_FILE` | Client private key |
| `QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_TLS_CERT_KEY_PASS` | Passphrase for encrypted private key |
| `QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_TLS_SERVERNAME` | SNI servername for TLS handshake |
| `QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED` | Reject unauthorized certs (default `true`) |

Cert files are validated as absolute paths and read once on client creation. If TLS files/options are configured but `QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_TLS` is `false`, the process exits with a clear error rather than silently ignoring the config.

**Cluster + TLS DNS handling**

AWS ElastiCache clusters with TLS frequently fail certificate validation because resolved IPs don't match the certificate's hostname. The cluster client now uses an explicit `dnsLookup` function driven by `QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_DNS_LOOKUP_STRATEGY` (`LOOKUP` | `NONE`) so the original hostname can be passed through to the TLS handshake. See [ioredis ElastiCache notes](https://github.com/redis/ioredis?tab=readme-ov-file#special-note-aws-elasticache-clusters-with-tls).

**IPv6 / dual-stack selection**

New `QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_IPV6` joins the existing `QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_DUALSTACK`. Resolved address family is now determined explicitly (`4` default, `6` if `IPV6=true`, `0` if `DUALSTACK=true`). Setting both errors out.

**Auto-pipelining**

`QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_ENABLE_AUTO_PIPELINING` (default `false`) exposes ioredis auto-pipelining for high-throughput deployments. See [ioredis docs](https://github.com/redis/ioredis?tab=readme-ov-file#autopipelining). To be evaluated on real workloads before enabling broadly.

**Connection lifecycle and diagnostics**

- Clients now use `lazyConnect: true` and an explicit `client.connect()` after listeners are registered, so the initial connection error (TLS handshake failures, auth, DNS) is logged instead of being swallowed by ioredis auto-connect.
- Reconnection errors are surfaced via `reconnectOnError` to help diagnose transient TLS / network issues.
- `QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_DEBUG=true` enables ioredis's `debug` namespace (`ioredis:*`) and merges with any existing `DEBUG` env value, instead of requiring users to set `DEBUG` manually before the process starts.
- The connection name now combines `hostId` and client `type` for clearer identification on the Redis side (`CLIENT LIST`).
- Fixes `lazyConnect` not being respected by the cluster client when only set in `redisOptions`.

**Refactor**

- Extracted `RedisTlsConfig` as a `@Nested` config class.
- Both `createRegularClient` and `createClusterClient` now return `{ client, nodes }` for unified logging.
- Centralized `exitWithError` helper replaces ad-hoc `process.exit(1)` calls.

title: fix(ai-builder): Add boundaries on the workflow builder remediation loops
body:
## Summary

This bounds the Instance AI workflow builder's `submit-workflow` -> `verify-built-workflow` -> repair loop.

The change adds hard remediation guards around the sandbox builder so successful submits are preserved, non-code setup blockers stop further workflow-code edits, and code-fixable repairs are limited to a small post-submit budget.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Start(["Builder run"]) --> Submit["submit-workflow"]

    Submit -->|"Fails before any workflow is saved"| PreSaveFailures{"Pre-save failures used"}
    PreSaveFailures -->|"1 or 2"| RetryBeforeSave["Edit and retry submit"]
    RetryBeforeSave --> Submit
    PreSaveFailures -->|"3"| BlockBeforeSave["Block before save"]

    Submit -->|"success true"| Saved["Workflow saved and post-submit budget starts"]
    Saved -->|"Setup signals present"| SetupBlock["Ask user for setup and block code edits"]
    Saved -->|"Ready to verify"| Verify["verify-built-workflow"]

    Verify -->|"Passes"| Done["Done"]
    Verify -->|"needs_setup or blocked"| SetupBlock
    Verify -->|"code_fixable"| Signature{"Duplicate failure signature"}

    Signature -->|"Yes"| SignatureBlock["Block without spending repair budget"]
    Signature -->|"No"| RepairBudget{"Post-submit repair submits used"}

    RepairBudget -->|"0 or 1"| RepairAllowed["Allow repair or direct resubmit"]
    RepairAllowed --> CountRepair["Count one post-submit submit"]
    CountRepair --> Submit
    RepairBudget -->|"2"| BudgetBlock["Block further edits and preserve workflow"]

    BlockBeforeSave --> End(["End"])
    SetupBlock --> End
    SignatureBlock --> End
    BudgetBlock --> End
    Done --> End
```

Key behavior:

- Keep separate budgets for pre-save submit failures and post-submit remediation submits.
- Treat any `submit-workflow` success as a successful submit, including workflows saved with mocked credentials.
- Classify remediation into `code_fixable`, `needs_setup`, and `blocked`.
- Preserve saved workflows when verification is blocked by credentials, placeholders, setup, external services, or terminal guard state.
- Enforce terminal remediation at `submit-workflow`, `verify-built-workflow`, and `report-verification-verdict`.
- Scope terminal guard checks to the active `runId` so a later user message gets a fresh budget.
- Emit telemetry when the remediation guard fires.

title: fix(core): Make MCP client registration cap tunable and surface a proper limit error
body:
## Summary

This PR addresses ADO-5107 with a hotfix-style approach: instead of restructuring the quota to be per-user, the existing instance-wide cap is made configurable and the limit error is made meaningful. The original architectural fix (per-user list scoping + per-user quota) is split out for a follow-up PR.

The Connected Clients list under MCP settings was instance-wide with a hardcoded 200-client cap. Customers (e.g. Canva) hit it organically because Claude Code/Desktop register a new OAuth `client_id` on every reauth via DCR, and accumulated registrations across many users exhausted the shared pool. The DCR endpoint then returned a generic `500 server_error / Internal Server Error`, which made the failure look like an internal bug to third-party support.

This PR:

- Raises the default for `N8N_MCP_MAX_REGISTERED_CLIENTS` from 200 to 10000 and keeps it as a tunable env var, so admins can adjust to their fleet size.
- Returns a structured `503` with a descriptive `error_description` when the cap is hit (instead of the SDK's opaque `500`), and adds server-side warn logging so admins can see when this triggers.
- Fixes the `expires_in` field on the `authorization_code` token response to read from the configured access token lifetime instead of being hardcoded to `3600`. Latent bug; harmless today because both happen to equal 1h, but a footgun the moment the constant moves.
- Paginates the Connected Clients table client-side via `N8nDataTableServer` (related to ADO-5101).

2. Select `Cloud (OAuth2)` in the Jira node's _Jira Version_ dropdown
3. Connect the credential and run any Jira operation — API calls should succeed against `api.atlassian.com`
