title: feat(core): Run evaluation test cases in parallel behind PostHog rollout flag
body:
## Summary

Production-ready parallel execution of evaluation test cases, gated behind a PostHog rollout flag (`eval_parallel_execution`).

**Default cohort (most users):** the runner remains sequential — byte-identical to today's behaviour. No UI change. No request shape change. The flag is off, the FE doesn't render the new control, the BE ignores the (absent) `concurrency` field. Zero risk of regression.

**Rollout cohort (flag-on):** the Evaluations dashboard surfaces a "Run in parallel" checkbox (default checked), an `N8nInputNumber` 1–10 (default 3, disabled when checkbox unchecked), and a tooltip with an info icon. State is persisted **per-workflow** in localStorage. The BE wraps each test case in a `pLimit` fan-out, layered onto the existing `ConcurrencyControlService` (`'evaluation'` queue) so an admin-set `N8N_CONCURRENCY_EVALUATION_LIMIT` is honoured. Cancellation is prompt even when cases are queued behind the eval-limit cap. Telemetry surfaces `concurrency`, `parallel_enabled`, `concurrency_limited_by_config`, and `flag_enabled_for_user` so we can measure the rollout end-to-end.

### Commits

| # | Tier | Status | Hash | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | F | ✅ | `4748435304` | Shared `startTestRunPayloadShape` schema in `@n8n/api-types`, controller `@Body`, FE forwards optional concurrency. No behaviour change. |
| 2 | F | ✅ | `8edbf9b484` | `EvaluationMetrics.buildContribution` (pure, parallel-safe) + `mergeContribution` (sequential merge). `addResults` is a thin wrapper. |
| 3 | F | ✅ | `d88418dcfa` | `for…of` await loop replaced with `pLimit(concurrency) + Promise.all`. Per-case `abortSignal.aborted` + multi-main DB-flag fallback poll preserved. |
| 4 | H | ✅ | `176b7b404a` | `ConcurrencyControlService` integration (try/finally throttle/release per case), `evaluationLimit` clamp, telemetry foundation. |
| 5 | H | ✅ | `25afa5a97c` | `EVAL_PARALLEL_EXECUTION_FLAG` shared in `@n8n/api-types`. `TestRunsController` resolves PostHog flag; flag-off → silent `concurrency=1` coercion. Fail-open on PostHog errors. `flag_enabled_for_user` telemetry. |
| 6 | H | ✅ | `6d76a17ef8` | `parallelEval.store.ts` (per-workflow state, flag-gated visibility) + `EvaluationsView.vue` checkbox + concurrency input + tooltip. i18n keys, vitest coverage. |
| 7 | fix | ✅ | `7264d8e3d3` | Make queued-case cancellation prompt (`Promise.race(throttle, abort)` + `remove()` to splice queue entries on abort). Replace misleading `assert(testCaseResult)` with graceful skip. Add component-level payload-shape coverage. |

F = foundation (net-new code), H = production hardening.

### Architecture highlights

- **Reuses** `ConcurrencyControlService` (`packages/cli/src/concurrency/`) which already had an `'evaluation'` queue type. Local-mode throttle/release per case; queue mode is a no-op (intentional — BullMQ governs).
- **Reuses** the existing `cancel-test-run` pubsub broadcast (`@OnPubSubEvent`) and `requestCancellation` DB flag. Per-case poll kept as a defensive backstop against pubsub message loss.
- **Three layers of concurrency control:**
  1. Zod 1–10 at the controller (rejects malformed input).
  2. Service-side defensive re-clamp 1–10.
  3. `evaluationLimit` from `N8N_CONCURRENCY_EVALUATION_LIMIT` env var if set (admin-controlled global cap).
- **Dual gating model for the rollout flag:**
  - **FE primary gate:** `usePostHog().isFeatureEnabled('eval_parallel_execution')` controls visibility of the checkbox + input. Flag-off users see no UI change at all.
  - **BE safety net:** `TestRunsController.create` re-resolves the flag and silently coerces `concurrency=1` for users not in the cohort. Defends against direct API clients, stale tabs, and rollout-percentage races. No flag-id leak in the response.
  - **Fail-open:** PostHog outage → flag treated as off → sequential. Logged at warn level for ops.
- **Abort-aware queue acquisition:** when a user clicks Stop, queued cases are evicted from the eval queue via `remove()` so cancellation is prompt regardless of how many other test runs are currently holding capacity. A defensive `throttleAcquired` flag handles the narrow scheduler-ordering case where an immediate-grant's `.then` microtask races with abort, ensuring no capacity slot is ever leaked.

### Telemetry — `Test run finished` event picks up four new properties

| Property | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `concurrency` | number | Effective post-clamp value (1–10). |
| `parallel_enabled` | boolean | `concurrency > 1`. |
| `concurrency_limited_by_config` | boolean | Clamped down by `N8N_CONCURRENCY_EVALUATION_LIMIT`. |
| `flag_enabled_for_user` | boolean | Distinguishes "flag-on user opted out" from "flag-off user". Critical for rollout adoption measurement. |

Notion telemetry DB needs these four fields documented (out-of-repo step — see merge checklist).

### Tests added

| Layer | Count | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| `cli` evaluation-metrics | 4 | build/merge purity, parallel-build + reverse-order merge equivalence with sequential `addResults` (within IEEE-754 precision). |
| `cli` test-runner service | 13 | concurrency=1 sequential parity, fan-out at concurrency>1, `pLimit` clamp, throttle/release per case (success + throw paths), evaluationLimit clamp, telemetry payload, multi-main DB cancel, per-case error isolation, **abort during throttle wait evicts queue entry without UNKNOWN_ERROR rows**. |
| `cli` test-runs controller | 7 | The four (flag × parallel) cells + 202 success regardless of flag (no leak) + once-per-request flag resolution + fail-open on PostHog throw. |
| `editor-ui` parallelEval store | 11 | `isFeatureEnabled` reflects flag, default-on / default-3, per-workflow independence, sentinel handling, clamp, `effectiveConcurrency`. |
| `editor-ui` EvaluationsView | 6 | **Conditional rendering (flag-off hides controls; flag-on renders checkbox + tooltip + input). Payload shape per state: flag-off → no concurrency; flag-on default checked → `{ concurrency: 3 }`; unchecked → `{ concurrency: 1 }`; custom slider value → `{ concurrency: 7 }`**. |

Existing 65 evaluation.ee tests still pass on master state. Total: 89 cli + 17 FE = **106 tests covering this feature**.

### How to test

**Default behaviour (flag off, all users):**
```bash
# No request body change — runs sequentially as before.
POST /workflows/:wfId/test-runs/new
{ }
```

**Flag-on cohort (after PostHog override or rollout):**
```bash
# Concurrency 5 honoured by the runner, telemetry records parallel_enabled=true.
POST /workflows/:wfId/test-runs/new
{ "concurrency": 5 }

# UI: open the Evaluations tab on any workflow with eval nodes. Observe the
# checkbox + 1-10 input + (i) tooltip in the header. Default is checked,
# concurrency 3. Run a test — multiple test-case executions fan out.
```

**Admin cap:**
```bash
# Set N8N_CONCURRENCY_EVALUATION_LIMIT=2 and request concurrency=5 → effective 2.
# Telemetry records concurrency_limited_by_config=true.
```

**Cancel during fan-out (including queued behind eval-limit cap):**
```bash
# Start a parallel run that exceeds the global eval cap. Click Stop. In-flight
# cases get aborted via ManualExecutionCancelledError; queued cases (in
# the eval queue, waiting for capacity) are evicted via ConcurrencyControlService.remove()
# so the run cancels promptly without waiting for unrelated evaluations to drain.
# Test run row marked as 'cancelled'. No UNKNOWN_ERROR test-case rows.
```

### Out of scope

- The eval-mode canvas dim and the AI wizard (TRUST-61 work, separate effort).
- A separate license tier for parallel runs — the PostHog flag is the rollout control; license stays where it is today (`getMaxWorkflowsWithEvaluations() > 0`).
- Real-Redis integration tests for queue/multi-main — repo precedent uses mocks, we follow that.
- A new `N8nSlider` design-system component — the spec called for a slider, but no slider exists in `@n8n/design-system` and there is no existing `el-slider` usage in editor-ui. Using `N8nInputNumber` (1–10) per the spec's documented fallback. Introducing a new design-system component is a separate concern.

### Merge checklist

- [ ] Notion telemetry DB row added with `concurrency`, `parallel_enabled`, `concurrency_limited_by_config`, `flag_enabled_for_user`.
- [ ] Doc ticket created (post-merge).
- [ ] Marketing notification sent (after rollout reaches 100%).
- [ ] PostHog flag `eval_parallel_execution` created and rollout percentage configured.

title: fix(core): Generate array types for properties with multipleValues
body:
## Summary

Properties declared with `typeOptions: { multipleValues: true }` on simple
types (`string`, `number`, `boolean`, `dateTime`, `color`, `options`, etc.)
were emitted in the generated node type definitions and Zod schemas as their
**singular** type, even though the runtime treats them as arrays.

For example, the Google Calendar node's `additionalFields.attendees` field
(`type: 'string'`, `multipleValues: true`, consumed at
`GoogleCalendar.node.ts:243-253` as `string[]`) was generated as:

```ts
attendees?: string | Expression<string> | PlaceholderValue;
```

The AI workflow builder, reading that signature, produced a single-string
expression for the entire array:

```jsonc
// Wrong (what the builder generated)
"attendees": "={{ [{ email: $json.email }] }}"
```

instead of the array shape the runtime actually requires:

```jsonc
// Correct
"attendees": ["={{ $json.email }}"]
```

This caused `forEach`/`split(',')` calls inside the node implementation to
silently mangle the value at execution time.

### Fix

In `packages/@n8n/workflow-sdk/src/generate-types/`:

- Add a `wrapMultipleValuesType` helper that wraps the inner type with
  `Array<…>` whenever `prop.typeOptions?.multipleValues === true`.
- Apply it at the wrapper level in both `mapPropertyType` and
  `mapNestedPropertyType` (after the `noDataExpression` strip, so
  `Array<string>` is produced correctly when expressions are disabled).
- Mirror the same logic in `mapPropertyToZodSchema` via
  `wrapMultipleValuesZodSchema`, so runtime validation matches the
  emitted TypeScript.
- Skip `fixedCollection` (already handles `multipleValues` internally via
  `generateFixedCollectionType`) and `multiOptions` (already an array by
  definition) to avoid double-wrapping.

After the fix, the same Google Calendar property is emitted as:

```ts
attendees?: Array<string | Expression<string> | PlaceholderValue>;
```

…which the builder uses to produce the correct array shape.

This affects every node that uses `multipleValues: true` on a simple-typed
property, not just Google Calendar.

title: fix(editor): Stabilize Instance AI workflow preview rendering (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Reworks the Instance AI workflow preview to paint live execution state on the canvas using the SDK push events that already arrive via the n8n WebSocket — no more `openExecution` fetch, no more loader, and the build agent's verification runs are now visible too.

**The original problem:** the iframe was fetching execution data via `/rest/executions/{id}` after the agent's run-workflow tool completed. That produced a visible loader, and on fast runs the loader showed up after the execution had already finished. Worse, the build agent's internal verification runs never reached the canvas at all because the backend wasn't routing their push events to the user's session.

**What changed**

- **Frontend simplification.** The iframe stays in workflow mode forever. `useExecutionPushEvents` captures `executionStarted` / `nodeExecuteAfter` / `executionFinished` from the existing push connection; `useEventRelay` forwards them to the iframe via `relayPushEvent`, which paints node statuses on the canvas as the run progresses. Removed `activeExecutionId`, `latestExecution` watcher, historical-execution restore, polling in `InstanceAiWorkflowPreview`, and the `executionStatus` field on tabs.
- **Build-phase visibility.** Build agent runs the workflow before its tab is active. `useEventRelay` now keeps the buffered event log alive when an inactive workflow's run finishes, and replays it (plus a synthetic `executionFinished`, gated by `finishedSynthSent` so re-switching doesn't double-fire) when the user activates the tab.
- **Backend pushRef wiring (`packages/cli/src/modules/instance-ai/instance-ai.service.ts`).** Two fixes that were both needed for the build agent's runs to reach the user's session:
  - Pass `this.threadPushRef.get(threadId)` to `createExecutionEnvironment` in `doSchedulePlannedTasks` so build-agent and checkpoint executions are tagged with the user's iframe pushRef.
  - Stop deleting `threadPushRef` in the `finally` blocks of `executeRun` and `processResumedStream`. Planned tasks dispatch later in the same finally and depend on the entry being alive. `clearThreadState` still removes it on thread teardown, and `startRun` overwrites on each new chat send so a refreshed iframe pushRef is picked up immediately.

**Tests**

- New FE integration test (`bufferedEventsTabSwitch.test.ts`) drives the build-phase scenario end-to-end: events arrive while a different tab is active → user switches → events replay onto the iframe with the synthetic `executionFinished`.
- New BE regression test (`instance-ai.service.threadPushRef.test.ts`) source-asserts that neither `executeRun` nor `processResumedStream` re-introduces `threadPushRef.delete`, and verifies `clearThreadState` still does the legitimate cleanup.
- Pruned tests targeting the deleted execution-fetch flows in `useCanvasPreview.test.ts` and `InstanceAiWorkflowPreview.test.ts`. Removed the integration test file that exercised the same removed flows.

**How to test**

1. Open Instance AI, send a build prompt (e.g., \`Build a workflow that fetches the weather and sends a Slack message\`). Approve the plan.
2. While the build agent works, watch the canvas. As the verification run executes, node statuses should paint live (running → success/error per node) without any loader appearing.
3. Open another artifact tab during the build, then come back to the workflow tab — the run that happened while you were away should be reflected on the canvas.
4. Tell the chat to run the workflow again. The iframe should switch back to workflow mode with live painting; no openExecution fetch, no loader.

title: feat(core): Add configurable event log path per process
body:
## Summary

Adds a new opt-in env var `N8N_EVENTBUS_LOGWRITER_LOGFULLPATH` that lets operators route the event log to a specific absolute path — used verbatim, with no process-type suffix appended. When the env is unset, behavior is byte-identical to today (default path under `${N8N_USER_FOLDER}` with the existing `-worker` / `-webhook-processor` / no-suffix derivation).

## Why

In multi-pod deployments backed by a shared RWX volume, every worker pod resolves to the same `${N8N_USER_FOLDER}/n8nEventLog-worker.log` because the `-worker` suffix discards the per-pod `hostId`. Concurrent unguarded `appendFileSync` writes from N pods to that single file produce interleaved bytes and rotation races, which then destabilizes startup recovery.

The companion read-side fix (bounded skip-and-warn parser + total-messages guard) shipped earlier. This PR addresses the write-side root cause: give operators a knob to put each pod on its own durable per-pod path (typically templated via the Kubernetes Downward API or a per-pod PVC). The operator owns per-pod uniqueness — n8n does not auto-suffix when the env is set.

## What changed

- New config field `LogWriterConfig.logFullPath` (env: `N8N_EVENTBUS_LOGWRITER_LOGFULLPATH`), default empty
- New pure helper `resolveEventLogPath()` co-located with the writer — handles validation, parent-dir auto-create, and legacy fallback in one place
- `MessageEventBusLogWriter.getInstance` accepts a new `resolvedPath` option that takes precedence over the legacy `logBasePath`/`logBaseName` derivation
- `MessageEventBus.initialize` calls the helper, threads the resolved path into the writer, and emits an advisory `logger.warn` when the operator opts into a configured path while files at the default location still exist (non-blocking)
- Worker thread (`message-event-bus-log-writer-worker.ts`) untouched — it already derives all rotation siblings (`.log-N`) and the `.recoveryInProgress` marker purely from `logFullBasePath`

## How to test manually

1. **Configured path is honored**
   ```bash
   N8N_EVENTBUS_LOGWRITER_LOGFULLPATH=/tmp/n8n-events/custom.log n8n start
   ```
   Verify writes land at `/tmp/n8n-events/custom.log`. Trigger a few rotations (lower `N8N_EVENTBUS_LOGWRITER_MAXFILESIZEINKB` to e.g. `1`) and confirm siblings appear at `/tmp/n8n-events/custom-1.log`, `custom-2.log`, …, with no `-worker` suffix anywhere.

2. **Default behavior unchanged when env unset**
   Start a worker without the env. Confirm it still writes to `${N8N_USER_FOLDER}/n8nEventLog-worker.log` (existing behavior).

3. **Validation**
   - `N8N_EVENTBUS_LOGWRITER_LOGFULLPATH=relative/path.log` → startup fails with a clear message about the path needing to be absolute
   - `N8N_EVENTBUS_LOGWRITER_LOGFULLPATH=/tmp/foo.txt` → startup fails about needing `.log` extension

4. **Parent dir auto-create**
   Point the env at a path whose parent does not exist (e.g. `/tmp/does/not/exist/yet/events.log`). Start a worker; confirm the parent dir is created and the file is written.

5. **Default-location coexistence advisory**
   Pre-create `${N8N_USER_FOLDER}/n8nEventLog-worker.log` (e.g. `touch`), then start a worker with `N8N_EVENTBUS_LOGWRITER_LOGFULLPATH=/tmp/elsewhere/events.log`. Confirm a single `WARN` log lists the stale default-location file.

## Key implementation decisions

- **Pure helper, service-layer validation.** `resolveEventLogPath` is a synchronous pure function with one filesystem side-effect (`mkdirSync({ recursive: true })`). Validation throws `UserError` from inside the helper rather than from a config decorator, matching the n8n convention (config decorators stay declarative; service `initialize()` is the validation point).
- **Verbatim when set, no auto-suffix.** When the env is set, the configured path is used as-is for main, worker, and webhook processes alike. The operator templates uniqueness (Downward API `$(POD_NAME)`, per-pod PVC `subPathExpr`, etc.). Auto-suffixing would fight that templating.
- **Worker thread untouched.** The corruption isn't in the worker code — it's in the path collision. Threading a unique `logFullBasePath` through to the worker resolves it without modifying any of the rotation / append / recovery-marker logic.
- **Default-location coexistence is advisory, not destructive.** Lists stale files in a single `WARN` log; never deletes anything. Operators handle drainage as part of their migration.

title: feat(core): Bootstrap legacy CBC and initial GCM encryption keys on startup
body:
## Summary

Re-enables the `EncryptionBootstrapService` so that when the encryption key rotation feature flag (`N8N_ENV_FEAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY_ROTATION=true`) is active, two keys are seeded into the `deployment_key` table on startup:

1. **Legacy CBC key** — the existing instance encryption key is wrapped with `encryptDEKWithInstanceKey` (AES-256-GCM) and stored with `algorithm: aes-256-cbc`, `status: inactive`. This gives the key manager a record of the legacy key so it can decrypt credentials that were encrypted before key rotation was introduced.

2. **Initial GCM key** — if no active AES-256-GCM key exists, a fresh random 256-bit key is generated, wrapped, and inserted as the active data-encryption key. All new writes via `encryptV2` will use this key going forward.

Both steps are idempotent — re-running bootstrap (e.g. on restart) is a no-op if the keys already exist.

### What changed

- `KeyManagerService`: replaced `bootstrapLegacyKey()` with `bootstrapLegacyCbcKey(instanceEncryptionKey)` (inactive, GCM-wrapped CBC key) and added `bootstrapGcmKey()` (active GCM key if none exists)
- `EncryptionBootstrapService`: fully re-enabled — injects `KeyManagerService` and `InstanceSettings`, calls both bootstrap methods in order
- Tests updated across unit, integration, and service-level test files; added idempotency test

title: fix(core): Fix code node executions hanging when idle timer overlaps with task acceptance (backport to 1.x)
body:
# Description Backport of #29239 to `1.x`. ## Checklist for the author (@tomi) to go through. - [ ] Review the backport changes - [ ] Fix possible conflicts - [ ] Merge to target branch After this PR has been merged, it will be picked up in the next patch release for release track. # Original description ## Summary When a task runner's idle timeout fires, a `broker:taskofferaccept` message already queued in the event loop could still be processed — the runner would accept the task and then shut down, leaving the execution hanging on the broker side until it eventually timed out. This adds an `isShuttingDown` guard to `offerAccepted()` so the runner rejects task offers during shutdown with `runner:taskrejected`. The broker already handles this gracefully and can reassign the task to another runner. As defense in depth, `stop()` now also clears `openOffers`. I also considered the alternative of draining the open task offers when the idle timeout fires. Rejected it because of the complexity it would add it. This fix is simpler, but has more latency as the launcher will need to relaunch the runner. title: feat(agents): Implement skills for agents
body:
## Summary

This branch adds Agent Skills as reusable instruction bundles for SDK agents.

A skill is stored separately from the agent JSON config as a named body of instructions, while the config only keeps lightweight skill references. At runtime, the agent prompt gets a catalog of available skills with their IDs, names, and descriptions, but not the full bodies. Full skill instructions are loaded only when needed through an injected load_skill tool.

The branch also adds builder support for skills: users can create, view, edit, and remove skills in the Agent Builder UI, and the AI builder can create and attach skills while generating an agent. Skills are handled separately from normal tools, so they provide behavioral guidance rather than external actions.

On the backend, the branch adds REST endpoints and persistence for agent skills, validates skill payloads, wires skills into JSON-config reconstruction, and snapshots skill/tool state for published agents so published executions remain stable after draft edits.

title: fix(core): Reset Redis retry counter on successful reconnect
body:
## Summary

The Redis retry strategy state persisted across disconnect windows, so a disconnect was leaving behind `lastAttemptTs` and `cumulativeTimeout`, and the next disconnect within 30s was absorbing the entire intervening healthy interval as accumulated retry time, leading to tripping the threshold and exiting the process.

This PR resets each client's retry state on its own `'ready'` event. The reset is per-client, so one client recovering doesn't wipe another client's budget. It is also unconditional on the aggregate `lostConnection` flag, so a second client reconnecting after the first still resets its own state.

title: fix(core): Widen zod peer dependency range in published packages (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Replace the exact `catalog:` (`zod@3.25.67`) peer-dependency pin in the published packages `n8n-workflow`, `n8n-core`, and `@n8n/api-types` with a real semver range: `">=3.25.0 <4"`.

### Why

PR #28604 correctly moved `zod` to `peerDependencies` in these three packages to enforce a single zod instance across the workspace. The peer was declared as `"catalog:"`, which gets published as the exact catalog version (`3.25.67`).

That exact pin is what we want for our own builds, but it is not how package managers act on a peer:

- pnpm/npm/yarn treat an exact version as a single point. Consumers whose graph also pulls in an older zod (e.g. `3.24.x` via another transitive) **silently satisfy** the peer and only emit a warning.
- Our published code does `import … from 'zod/v4'` (the subpath was added in zod 3.25.0), so installs that resolve to an older zod fail at runtime with a cryptic `Package subpath './v4' is not defined by "exports"` deep inside `require-in-the-middle`. We've been seeing this in production via Sentry alerts on `creators-nodes-sync`.

Widening the peer to `">=3.25.0 <4"`:

- Communicates the actual runtime contract (anything from 3.25.0 up to but not including 4.0.0).
- Lets `pnpm install --strict-peer-dependencies` *fail* on a too-old zod instead of just warning.
- Makes the warning text package managers emit actually actionable.

### Downstream remediation

Consumers seeing the cryptic error today (e.g. `creators-nodes-sync`) should pin zod via `package.json`:

```json
"pnpm": {
  "overrides": {
    "zod": "3.25.67"
  }
}
```

…or the equivalent `overrides` (npm) / `resolutions` (yarn) idiom, then reinstall.

### What this PR is *not*

An earlier draft of this PR also added a load-time runtime guard inside `n8n-workflow` to throw a clearer error if the consumer's resolved zod was too old. Self-review uncovered that the guard:

1. broke the `n8n-workflow` CJS build (`resolveJsonModule: false` is set in `@n8n/typescript-config/modern/tsconfig.cjs.json`, so `import 'zod/package.json'` did not compile), and
2. would, even if compiled, fail at runtime in the ESM build on Node ≥ 22 because emitted JSON imports require `with { type: 'json' }` import attributes.

It was reverted. The peer-range change alone is the smaller, safer win. We can revisit a runtime guard later (likely via `createRequire` + filesystem read, with a built-artifact integration test) if needed.

## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts

Sentry alert: `creators-nodes-sync` — issue [`7440848191`](https://n8nio.sentry.io/issues/7440848191/) (`Module.patchedRequire(require-in-the-middle:index)` — `Package subpath './v4' is not defined by "exports"` in `n8n-workflow@2.18.3_zod@3.24.2`).

Follows up on #28604.

title: feat: Add no-runtime-dependencies ESLint rule
body:
## Summary

Adds a new ESLint rule `@n8n/community-nodes/no-runtime-dependencies` to the `@n8n/eslint-plugin-community-nodes` package.

The rule flags any community node `package.json` that has a non-empty `dependencies` field. Runtime dependencies in community nodes are problematic because they get installed into the shared n8n runtime, where they can conflict with packages used by n8n itself or other installed nodes. Libraries should instead be declared in `peerDependencies` or bundled at build time into the published artifact.

**What is checked:**
- If `dependencies` exists and has one or more entries → error
- If `dependencies` is absent or empty (`{}`) → valid
- Non-`package.json` files are ignored
- Nested `dependencies` keys inside other fields are ignored

**To test:** lint a community node `package.json` that contains a non-empty `dependencies` field with the `recommended` or `recommendedWithoutN8nCloudSupport` config enabled.

## Summary

https://www.loom.com/share/bdc61e845f37490795bd25d5bb439267

Adds `--include` and `--exclude` flags to the `n8n import:credentials` CLI command, enabling field-level control during credential imports.

- `--include=<props>`: import only the listed comma-separated credential properties
- `--exclude=<props>`: import all properties except the listed ones
- The two flags are mutually exclusive — using both together throws an error

- An empty or whitespace-only list throws an error

3. Run `n8n import:credentials --input=credentials.json --exclude=createdAt,updatedAt` and verify same behaviour

title: feat: Validate workflow-sdk output topology against mode
body:
## Summary
- Adds declarative `builderHint.outputs` to node descriptions, mirroring the existing `builderHint.inputs` shape but keyed on `NodeConnectionType` so `main` is allowed.
- Adds `INVALID_OUTPUT_FOR_MODE` validator (severity `major`) that flags when a node has connections of a type its current parameters disable.
- Authors `outputs` for all 14 vector stores via `createVectorStoreNode` — `main` for insert/load/update, `ai_vectorStore` for retrieve, `ai_tool` for retrieve-as-tool.
- Surfaces `builderHint.outputs` through the Instance AI adapter so the agent sees the topology rules at prompt time.

## Why

A real AI-builder eval produced a workflow with `vectorStoreInMemory` in `mode: 'retrieve'` wired via `main` edges. In `retrieve` mode the node's only output port is `ai_vectorStore`; the `main` edges referenced ports that don't exist, so the downstream chain silently received no data. The runtime `outputs:` expression on the node already encoded the rule — it just wasn't declarative metadata anything could validate against.

This PR makes the rule first-class:
1. **Declarative** — `builderHint.outputs.main.displayOptions.show.mode` says "main is exposed only in insert/load/update".
2. **Validated** — the new validator walks each node's outgoing edges and emits a warning when the source mode disables that output.
3. **Visible to the agent** — the adapter passes the metadata through `SearchableNodeDescription`, alongside the existing inputs hint.

The validator reuses the existing `matchesDisplayOptions` + `buildConditionSummary` helpers — no new infrastructure.

## Test plan
- [x] 7 new tests in `validation.test.ts` covering retrieve / retrieve-as-tool / load / no-provider / expression / regression-fixture cases
- [x] Committed regression fixture `vector-store-retrieve-with-main.json` taken from a real failing eval workflow
- [x] Existing `createVectorStoreNode` snapshot updated (additive — only new `outputs` block)
- [x] Full `workflow-sdk` jest suite green (9531+ tests), full `ai-utilities` suite green (418 tests)
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean in `workflow`, `workflow-sdk`, `ai-utilities`, `instance-ai`

title: feat(core): Remove expression role mapping feature flag
body:
## Summary

Removes the `N8N_ENV_FEAT_EXPRESSION_ROLE_MAPPING` env feature flag and the legacy `userRoleProvisioning` dropdown UX it gated. The new "Role assignment" + "Role mapping method" controls — and the rule-based mapping behaviour — are now the default on SAML and OIDC settings, regardless of env vars.

The IdP group role mapping project is complete, so the flag and the parallel legacy code paths are dead weight. This PR collapses both branches to the new path:

- **Backend:** drops the flag check in `provisioning.service.ee.ts`. `isExpressionMappingEnabled()` now returns purely from `scopesUseExpressionMapping` config.
- **Frontend:** deletes the legacy template branch, `legacyValue` v-model, `legacyOptions`, `UserRoleProvisioningSetting` type, and the corresponding `formValue` / `toLegacyValue` / `fromLegacyValue` helpers from the composable. SAML and OIDC settings forms are simplified accordingly.
- **i18n:** the seven `settings.sso.settings.userRoleProvisioning.*` keys are removed.
- **Tests:** strips `process.env.N8N_ENV_FEAT_EXPRESSION_ROLE_MAPPING` setup/teardown from four integration suites; the test cases themselves are preserved (they already mutate `scopesUseExpressionMapping` directly).

### Telemetry

The `User updated provisioning settings` PostHog event keeps its existing `updated_setting` field shape (`disabled` / `instance_role` / `instance_and_project_roles` / `expression_based`) so existing dashboards continue to work. The legacy mapping logic now lives as a private `getTelemetrySettingValue` helper inside `useUserRoleProvisioningForm.ts` — it has no other consumers.

## How to test manually

1. Start n8n **without** setting `N8N_ENV_FEAT_EXPRESSION_ROLE_MAPPING`.
2. Sign in as instance owner and enable an SSO provider (`Settings → SSO → SAML` or `OIDC`).
3. Confirm the SSO settings page shows the new **Role assignment** dropdown (Manual / Instance roles / Instance and project roles) and, when not Manual, the **Role mapping method** dropdown (IdP / Rules in n8n). The legacy single-select "User role provisioning" dropdown should not be visible at all.
4. Pick `Instance and project roles` + `Rules in n8n`, define a couple of role mapping rules, save, and confirm the request to `PATCH /provisioning/config` succeeds and the rules persist.
5. Switch back to `Manual` and save — the project rules should be cleared on the server (existing `deleteProjectRules` flow).
6. Repeat against the other SSO provider (OIDC if you tested SAML first, and vice versa).

title: feat(core): Use versioned prebuilt Daytona snapshots for Instance AI sandboxes
body:
## Summary

Replaces the request-path declarative `Image` build for Instance AI Daytona
sandboxes with a versioned prebuilt snapshot named
`n8n-instance-ai-<n8n-version>`. Falls back to the existing declarative path
when a snapshot is not available, so non-release builds keep working.

Two strategies, picked from `SandboxConfig.getAuthToken`:

- **Direct mode** (self-hosted): runtime calls `daytona.snapshot.create`
  optimistically — no `get` pre-check. Treats 409 / "already exists" as
  success. Successes are memoized; transient failures clear the memo so
  the next request retries.
- **Proxy mode** (cloud): runtime calls `daytona.snapshot.get` only.
  Cloud snapshots are pre-built by the n8n release pipeline using a
  separate admin Daytona key (GitHub Actions secret); `snapshot.create`
  is **never** exposed through the proxy.

Release pipeline now runs `build-daytona-snapshot` parallel to the docker
publish job, blocking `post-release`. Idempotent — re-runs against the
same version are a no-op.

A companion proxy change in `ai-assistant-service` widens the
`ALLOWED_ROUTES` allow-list to permit `GET /snapshots/<name>` (read-only,
no ownership labels). That PR will land alongside this one.

### How to test

- **Direct mode:** with `DAYTONA_API_KEY` set and no proxy, start n8n,
  trigger a builder session, confirm a snapshot named
  `n8n-instance-ai-<version>` appears in the Daytona dashboard. Trigger a
  second session — logs should show the cached resolution (no second
  `create`).
- **Proxy mode** (after the proxy PR ships): trigger a builder for a
  pre-built version → `daytona.create` payload contains `{ snapshot }`.
  Trigger for a version with no snapshot → `null` from `ensureSnapshot`,
  successful fallback to declarative `Image`.
- **CI dry-run:** `workflow_dispatch` `release-build-daytona-snapshot.yml`
  with a synthetic version. Re-run with the same version → idempotent.

title: fix(core): Make task runner grant token TTL configurable
body:
## Summary

The task runner grant token TTL was hardcoded to 15 seconds. On low-power hardware (Intel N150, Celeron, etc.), the runner process can take longer than 15s to spawn and establish a WebSocket connection, causing the grant token to expire. This results in a tight 403 retry loop that pegs CPU at 100%+.

This PR adds a new `N8N_RUNNERS_GRANT_TOKEN_TTL` environment variable (in seconds, default: 15) so operators on slower hardware can increase the TTL. The `TaskBrokerAuthService` now reads from config instead of a hardcoded constant, and injects `TaskRunnersConfig` directly rather than the full `GlobalConfig`.

**How to test:** Set `N8N_RUNNERS_GRANT_TOKEN_TTL=60` and verify the task runner connects successfully on slow hardware, or confirm the default 15s behavior is unchanged without the env var.

title: ci: Tighten n8n testcontainer wait strategy and add sequential service start
body:
## Summary

Three narrowly-scoped CI test infrastructure changes to address slow / flaky stack startups on contended (2-vCPU blacksmith) runners.

- **`services/n8n.ts`** — Drop the redundant `Wait.forListeningPorts()` (the `/healthz/readiness` HTTP probe already implies the port is listening), collapse identical `MAIN_WAIT_STRATEGY` / `WORKER_WAIT_STRATEGY` into one constant, and add explicit `withReadTimeout(250)`. The testcontainers default is 1000ms and doubles as the `IntervalRetry` polling cadence, so without this we sit on a stale poll for up to a second after the process is actually ready. Local probes show ~750ms-1s reclaimed per n8n container start.
- **`services/postgres.ts`** — Bump startup timeout 40s → 60s. Continues the pattern from `8db7389ef5` (30s → 40s) — cold blacksmith runs occasionally exceed even 40s under contention.
- **`stack.ts`** — Always start services sequentially within each dependency level. Parallel start on 2-vCPU runners thrashes CPU during each container's JIT/init spike and pushes services past their startup timeouts. Local benchmarks showed individual containers booting 2-4× faster sequentially under contention; wall-clock cost on uncontended hardware is modest.

## Summary

Picks up the three new test cases from @sirdavidoff's [#29113](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/29113) so they can land while that PR is parked. Two of David's prompts triggered the agent's Q&A mode in local runs; this PR keeps the test cases identical except for minimal anti-Q&A cleanups.

| Test case | Status | Change vs David's branch |
|---|---|---|
| `weather-alert.json` | as-is | none — passed first try |
| `linear-bq-leaderboard.json` | as-is + trailer | append `"Configure all nodes as completely as possible and don't ask me for credentials, I'll set them up later."` |
| `workflow-data-table.json` | edits + trailer | drop *"Make sure the workflow is deterministic"* (vague), drop *"and I can give you an API key for it"* (reliable Q&A trigger), append the same trailer |

No structural prescriptions added — node choices, implementation strategy, etc. all remain the agent's decision.

## Why these specific edits

In smoke runs with the unmodified prompts:

- `workflow-data-table` consistently looped on `"A few quick questions before I build this:"` instead of building, cued by *"I can give you an API key for it"*.
- `linear-bq-leaderboard` occasionally stalled with `"I don't see any Linear, BigQuery, or Slack credentials yet. Let me ask a few quick questions..."` — listing three services without a "don't ask for credentials" guard primes the agent toward Q&A mode.

After the cleanups, both built reliably and surfaced real `builder_issue` failures (BQ project param missing, branch synchronization missing, etc.) — exactly the agent-quality signal the eval framework is designed to expose.

`linear-bq-leaderboard` typically takes 215–276s to build. The harness's old 240s build cap will silently kill most attempts. Reliable builds need [#29219](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/29219) (TRUST-64, honor `--timeout-ms` across the harness) to land first. Until then, this test case will look flaky in CI.

title: fix: Fixes redirect bug on AI Assistant caused by settings evaluation sync issue (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary
Fixes a bug where users opting into AI Assistant for the first time get redirected to `/home/workflows` shortly after sending their first prompt.

### Root cause
The route guard for the AI Assistant view reads `settingsStore.moduleSettings['instance-ai'].enabled`. That value is set from two different backend sources, which were not in sync:
- `PUT /instance-ai/settings` (called when the user opts in)
- `GET /module-settings` (called on `InstanceAiView` mount via `refreshModuleSettings()`) returns `service.isEnabled()`, which has a `!!instanceAiConfig.model` condition.

In deployments where the model is supplied by the proxy / AI service rather than via local config, `N8N_INSTANCE_AI_MODEL` is empty. That makes `service.isEnabled()` return `false` even right after a successful opt-in.

title: feat(otel): propagate span context into workflow execution for log-trace correlation
body:
## Summary

When `N8N_OTEL_ENABLED=true`, `WorkflowStartHandler` creates a workflow span but stores it only
in `SpanRegistry` — it never calls `context.with()`, so `trace.getActiveSpan()` returns `undefined`
throughout execution. Log lines written during workflow execution carry no `traceId`/`spanId`,
making log-trace correlation impossible.

**Fix:** a lightweight bridge (`otel-execution-context.ts`) that avoids adding `@opentelemetry/api`
as a dependency to `packages/core`. The bridge exposes two functions:

- `registerOtelExecutionWrapper(executionId, wrapper)` — called by `WorkflowStartHandler` (CLI)
  after creating the span, registering a `context.with(activeCtx, fn)` callback keyed by execution ID.
- `consumeOtelExecutionWrapper(executionId)` — called by `WorkflowExecute` (core) after
  `workflowExecuteBefore` fires, wrapping the entire execution loop in the stored context.

Once the execution loop runs inside `otelContext.with(activeCtx, runLoop)`, all `await`-ed
operations inherit the active span via Node.js AsyncLocalStorage — including log writes, node
execution, and hook callbacks.

**Logger enrichment:** a `prependFormat()` method on `Logger` allows injecting cross-cutting
Winston formats after initialisation. `OtelService.injectTraceContextIntoLogs()` uses this to
prepend a format that reads `trace.getActiveSpan()?.spanContext()` and adds `traceId`/`spanId` to
every log record. The `jsonConsoleFormat` excludes these fields from Winston's `metadata()` wrapper
so they appear at the JSON root — required for log forwarders (e.g. Fluent Bit) to surface them as
top-level record attributes for log-trace correlation in observability platforms.

## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts

Discovered during self-hosted deployment with `N8N_OTEL_ENABLED=true` and a Fluent Bit log pipeline.

body:
## Summary

Four gaps in Prometheus workflow metrics:

1. **`n8n_workflow_execution_duration_seconds` was missing `workflow_name` and `project_name`.**
   Only `workflow_id` was included. Both labels are now added, gated by the existing
   `N8N_METRICS_INCLUDE_WORKFLOW_NAME_LABEL` and the new `N8N_METRICS_INCLUDE_PROJECT_NAME_LABEL`
   env vars.

2. **`project_name` was absent from all event-bus counters** (`n8n_workflow_success_total`,
   `n8n_workflow_failed_total`, `n8n_workflow_cancelled_total`). `buildWorkflowLabels()` now
   includes it when `N8N_METRICS_INCLUDE_PROJECT_NAME_LABEL=true`. Workflows not assigned to a
   project receive an empty string `""` (Prometheus convention for "not applicable"), keeping the
   label set consistent across all series.

3. **Trigger/poll-driven executions never populated `projectName` in lifecycle hooks.**
   `WorkflowExecutionService.runWorkflow()` did not look up the owning project before constructing
   the execution payload. Fixed via `OwnershipService.getWorkflowProjectCached()` — the result is
   cached so the lookup is cheap after the first call, and errors are non-fatal (execution continues,
   `project_name` falls back to `""`).

4. **`WebhookServer.configure()` was empty** — the webhook process never initialised
   `PrometheusMetricsService`, so webhook-triggered workflow executions were invisible at `/metrics`.
   Fixed to match the pattern already used in `Server.configure()`.

title: fix(ai-builder): Hide and reap intermediate AI-created workflows (backport to release-candidate/2.18.x)
body:
# Description
Backport of #29066 to `release-candidate/2.18.x`.

## Checklist for the author (@aalises) to go through.

- [ ] Review the backport changes
- [ ] Fix possible conflicts
- [ ] Merge to target branch

After this PR has been merged, it will be picked up in the next patch release for release track.

# Original description

## Summary

The AI builder leaves intermediate workflows behind in two scenarios ([INS-24](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/INS-24)):

1. **Orphans from failed builds** — a task partially saves a workflow then fails or is cancelled.
2. **Stepping-stones** — chunks, sub-workflows, scratch attempts, or workflows obsoleted by a replan that the agent never references again.

Both surface in the user's workflows list as half-built clutter the user didn't ask for.

## How it works

- `meta.aiTemporary: true` is stamped on every workflow the AI builder creates (`submit-workflow` + `build-workflow`, only on create — never on update so user-authored workflows are untouched). No DB migration: `meta` is already a nullable JSON column.
- The default workflows list query hides stamped rows (postgres + sqlite). The user never sees an in-progress stepping-stone.
- The orchestrator clears the stamp on `mainWorkflowAttempt.workflowId` at the end of every successful build — the deliverable is now indistinguishable from a user workflow.
- At every run-finish (success / cancel / error), the platform iterates the run's in-memory created-set and calls `archiveIfAiTemporary` on each id. Atomic check-and-archive: anything still stamped (chunks, scratch, obsoleted-by-replan) gets soft-deleted; the main survives because its stamp was cleared.

## Artifacts panel UX

The artifacts panel keeps stepping-stones visible in the conversation history after the run ends — but they've been archived, so clicking them would lead to a dead preview. To close that loop:

- `run-finish` events carry `archivedWorkflowIds: string[]` — the ids the reap just soft-deleted.
- The frontend store accumulates them per thread and tags matching entries in the resource registry as `archived: true`.
- The artifacts panel rows, and the `ArtifactCard` used by the activity tree and timeline, render archived entries dimmed with a strikethrough name and an "Archived" pill.

## Why this shape

- Resume paths, crashes, abandoned sessions, direct `build-workflow-with-agent` calls — every code path that could leak a stepping-stone reduces to a single SQL predicate.
- The agent's prompt carries no cleanup instructions — the platform owns the lifecycle, not the model.
- Soft delete (archive) — a mistaken reap is recoverable from the archive view.

Crash leaks (process dies mid-run before run-finish fires) are accepted as known: invisible to the user (list filter) and rare. Easy to add a one-off admin sweep later if it ever materializes.

title: feat(core): Add flag to import workflow cli to activate workflow on import
body:
## Summary

Demo video:
https://www.loom.com/share/8467b743450641b091d0bb6027af2fc6

Adds an `--activeState` flag to the `import:workflow` CLI so imported workflows can optionally keep the active state from their JSON, instead of always being force-deactivated.

The implementation is inspired by the `SourceControlImportService.importWorkflowFromWorkFolder` method.

Behavior

- `--activeState=false` (default) — current behavior: all imported workflows are set to `active=false` and must be activated manually later.
- `--activeState=fromJson` — Only supported in queue/multi-main mode. The workflow's active field from the JSON is parsed to decide whether to publish/unpublish a workflow. Workflows with active: true are activated post-import (registered in `ActiveWorkflowManager`, `activeVersionId` set, and a `workflow_history` event recorded); workflows with `active: false` are imported inactive.

How to test

1. Checkout the branch (it's a 1.x one, so make sure you reset your home dir or create a new one)
2. Start n8n in multi main mode, since activation will not work in regular mode. See the instructions in https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/29079
3. Create a workflow that's inactive with a schedule trigger that runs every 10 seconds
4. Run `n8n export:workflow --backup --output=backups/` inside the docker container of your main-1
5. Edit the generated workflow json and set `active: true`
6. Run `n8n import:workflow --separate --input=backups --activeState=fromJson` inside the docker container of your main-1
7. Observe that the workflow is now active and schedule triggers are creating new executions

title: ci: Shard weekly E2E coverage run across cached docker image (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Refactors the weekly E2E coverage workflow to run faster and more reliably, and consolidates how all E2E shards expose artifacts.

**Before:** A single 8vcpu runner built the instrumented image and ran the entire suite serially (~1h), with all state piling up on one n8n stack. The coverage workflow duplicated the inlined e2e job logic. Failure artifacts were gated behind a per-caller boolean.

**After:** Build once on 8vcpu → fan out to 4 parallel 4vcpu shards (each with a fresh container stack) → aggregate. Coverage flows through a dedicated `coverage` Playwright project so output lands in a colon-free path that `upload-artifact` accepts directly. The coverage workflow now `uses:` the shared `test-e2e-reusable.yml` instead of duplicating it. Every E2E shard always uploads a unified artifact bundling test debug data + coverage at 1-day retention.

### Changes

- **`playwright-projects.ts`** — Adds a `coverage` project (colon-free clone of `sqlite:e2e`). Currents writes to `.nyc_output/coverage/` instead of `.nyc_output/sqlite:e2e/`, eliminating the `:` that GitHub's artifact upload rejects.
- **`currents.config.ts`** — Coverage block is always-on, scoped to `projects: ['coverage']`. The `BUILD_WITH_COVERAGE` env gate is gone at test time (build time still uses it).
- **`test-e2e-reusable.yml`** — Single `if: always()` upload bundles `test-results/`, `playwright-report/`, and `.nyc_output/` into one `e2e-shard-${shard}` artifact, 1-day retention, `if-no-files-found: ignore`. Drops the `upload-failure-artifacts` input.
- **`test-e2e-coverage-weekly.yml`** — Three jobs:
  - `prepare-docker` (8vcpu) builds the instrumented image once via `prepare-docker-reusable.yml`.
  - `e2e` (4 shards × 4vcpu) `uses: test-e2e-reusable.yml` with `test-command: pnpm --filter=n8n-playwright test:container:coverage`, `workers: '1'`.
  - `aggregate` (4vcpu) downloads shard artifacts, `find`s coverage JSON, then runs the existing `coverage:report` → Codecov → `coverage-analysis.mjs` chain.
- **`generate-coverage-report.js`** — Simplified to a single-project lookup. Drops the multi-project pattern list and the temp-dir collision-avoidance hop.
- **`ci-pull-requests.yml`** — Drops the now-removed `upload-failure-artifacts` input.
- **Docs** — `coverage-workflow.md` updated to drop test-time `BUILD_WITH_COVERAGE` references.

### Tradeoffs to be aware of

- **Internal PRs now upload shard artifacts unconditionally.** Previously only fork PRs uploaded (via `upload-failure-artifacts: ${{ fork == true }}`). With `trace: 'on'`, `video: 'on'`, `screenshot: 'on'` in `playwright.config.ts`, `test-results/` is non-trivial on every run. 1-day retention bounds the inventory, but worth eyeballing artifact storage for the first few runs.
- **Failure artifact retention drops 7d → 1d.** A Friday failure expires before Monday triage. Currents has the data anyway for paid runs, but worth flagging if reviewers prefer 3 days.

- [x] Confirm Currents groups all 4 shards under one build via `CURRENTS_CI_BUILD_ID`

title: fix(editor): Show error toasts in Instance AI executable canvas
body:
## Summary

Error toasts inside the Instance AI executable workflow preview were being swallowed alongside the routine success/warning notifications, masking workflow execution failures (most notably missing-credential errors). This PR restores error visibility while keeping the rest of the suppression in place.

**Approach**

- `useUIStore` gains a second flag: `allowErrorNotificationsWhenSuppressed`, and `setNotificationsSuppressed` now accepts `{ allowErrors }`. Turning suppression off always clears the allowance, so state can't leak across iframe re-mounts.
- `useToast.showMessage` lets `type: 'error'` messages through when both flags are on, including the existing error telemetry path.
- `WorkflowPreview` exposes a new `allowErrorNotifications` prop (default `false`) and forwards it in the `openWorkflow` postMessage payload. `usePostMessageHandler` writes both store flags from every `openWorkflow` message.
- `InstanceAiWorkflowPreview` opts in by passing `:allow-error-notifications="true"` alongside its existing `suppress-notifications` and `can-execute` flags.

**How to test**

1. Open an Instance AI thread, generate a workflow that uses a credentialed node, and run it without configuring the credential.
2. Confirm the error toast appears inside the embedded canvas and the node retains its execution-error state.
3. Run a workflow that succeeds — confirm no success/warning toasts appear inside the preview.

## Summary

Adds project-scoped permissions to the `/projects/:projectId/agents/v2/*` controller, plus the supporting frontend wiring.

**Backend**
- Introduces a new `agent` resource in `@n8n/permissions` with the standard CRUDL operations plus `execute`, `publish`, and `unpublish`.

- Applies `@ProjectScope` decorators to every protected route on `AgentsController`. The webhook endpoint stays unauthenticated and continues to authenticate via per-platform signature verification inside the handler.
- Adds a route-level test asserting every handler has the expected access scope and that no protected route is global-only.

**Frontend**
- Registers `agent` in the editor RBAC store (`rbac.store.ts`) so the resource appears in `scopesByResourceId`.
- Surfaces all agent scopes in the project-role configuration UI (`projectRoleScopes.ts` + i18n), so admins can adjust them per role.

Role-scope sync runs automatically on startup via `AuthRolesService.init()` — no DB migration needed. Custom team roles are not auto-updated; admins need to re-save them in the UI to opt into the new scopes.

title: fix(editor): Preserve model selection when switching credentials
body:
## Summary

Fixes the model selector being reset when changing from "n8n Connect" to own credentials (or switching between credentials) in AI nodes like Anthropic and Gemini.

**Root cause:** Two credential change watchers were aggressively clearing parameter values:

1. **`ResourceLocator.vue`** — credential watcher cleared the entire `value` of any `resourceLocator` parameter when credentials changed. This affected Anthropic (and newer OpenAI) which use `type: 'resourceLocator'` for their model selector.

2. **`ParameterInput.vue`** — credential watcher reset `options` type parameters with `loadOptions` back to their default value. This affected Gemini which uses `type: 'options'` with `loadOptions` routing.

**Fix:**
- **ResourceLocator.vue:** Credential watcher now preserves the `value` and only clears cached metadata (`cachedResultName`, `cachedResultUrl`). The list will be re-fetched with the new credential, and if the value is no longer valid, the user can update it.
- **ParameterInput.vue:** Credential watcher now only re-fetches remote options without resetting the selected value. The dropdown refreshes with new options while keeping the user's selection.

When a workflow fails to load (e.g. malformed node parameters like

2. Open the workflow URL in the editor
3. Before: silent redirect to `?new=true`, orphan draft created
4. After: error toast shown, redirect to workflows list, no orphan draft

title: test(editor): Make instance AI partial-apply test deterministic (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

- De-flake \`tests/e2e/instance-ai/instance-ai-workflow-setup-actions.spec.ts:174\` (*"should partially apply completed cards when Later is clicked on the last step"*).
- Root cause is an auto-advance race in the wizard: when the HTTP card transitions to complete, the watcher in \`InstanceAiWorkflowSetup.vue\` jumps to the next incomplete card (Slack) **before** the test's manual \`Next.click()\` runs. With Slack still on the last step, \`isNextDisabled\` is true and the click hits its 20s timeout on every retry.
- Fix replaces the first manual \`Next\` click with an \`expect(stepCounter).toContainText('2 of 2')\` assertion that observes the auto-advance. Prev → Next → Later is unchanged, and the partial-apply persistence assertions are unchanged, so coverage parity holds.

## Why Slack stays incomplete in this test

The test seeds two \`slackApi\` credentials and the seeded workflow has no Slack credential attached. Both auto-pick paths require exactly one existing credential:

- Backend: \`packages/@n8n/instance-ai/src/tools/workflows/setup-workflow.service.ts:310\` — \`if (!existingOnNode?.id && existingCredentials.length === 1)\`
- Frontend: \`packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/features/ai/instanceAi/composables/useCredentialGroupSelection.ts:57\` — \`if (firstReq.existingCredentials?.length === 1)\`

With \`length === 2\`, neither fires. Slack has no \`selectedId\`, \`isCardComplete(slack)\` returns false (\`useSetupCards.ts:328-330\`), and the auto-advance watcher (\`InstanceAiWorkflowSetup.vue:278-292\`) is guaranteed to find a next-incomplete target the moment the HTTP card flips to complete.

## Why this looked flaky from outside

\`.github/workflows/ci-pull-requests.yml:218\` dispatches different projects per PR origin:

- Fork PRs → \`sqlite:e2e\` → test runs and **always fails**.
- Internal PRs → \`multi-main:e2e\` → test is **skipped** by the existing \`beforeEach\` (line 86-91, *"Setup wizard actions are not yet stable in multi-main mode"*).

So three unrelated fork PRs (#28926, #27297, #29187) hit the same deterministic failure while internal PRs skip silently. Outside variance is which mode CI dispatches, not test behavior.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI Shard 2 on \`sqlite:e2e\` is green for this PR.
- [ ] Local: re-run \`pnpm --filter=n8n-playwright test:container:sqlite:e2e --grep "should partially apply completed cards"\` 5–10× to confirm stability.
- [ ] After this lands, watch the next CI run on a fork PR (e.g. #28926) and confirm Shard 2 stays green there too.
- [ ] Out of scope: re-enabling the test in \`multi-main\` mode — the \`beforeEach\` skip flags a separate stability concern; revisit only after this fix is green on \`sqlite:e2e\`.

title: fix(Gmail Trigger Node): Exclude scheduled emails from trigger query
body:
## Summary

The Gmail Trigger was picking up scheduled (send-later) emails, which caused it to advance its `lastTimeChecked` timestamp past those messages and miss real incoming emails.

**Fix:** Append `-in:scheduled` to the Gmail API search query (`q` parameter) for node version 1.4+. This excludes scheduled emails at the query level so they're never fetched.

- Added `1.4` to the Gmail Trigger version array
- Added `-in:scheduled` query filter for `typeVersion > 1.3` in the `poll()` method
- Existing workflows on v1.0–v1.3 are unaffected (backward compatible)

**How to test:**
1. Create a Gmail Trigger node (new nodes default to v1.4)
2. Schedule an email in Gmail for later delivery
3. Send a test email from another account
4. Verify the trigger fires for the incoming email and ignores the scheduled one

title: fix(core): Fix code node executions hanging when idle timer overlaps with task acceptance
body:
## Summary When a task runner's idle timeout fires, a `broker:taskofferaccept` message already queued in the event loop could still be processed — the runner would accept the task and then shut down, leaving the execution hanging on the broker side until it eventually timed out. This adds an `isShuttingDown` guard to `offerAccepted()` so the runner rejects task offers during shutdown with `runner:taskrejected`. The broker already handles this gracefully and can reassign the task to another runner. As defense in depth, `stop()` now also clears `openOffers`. I also considered the alternative of draining the open task offers when the idle timeout fires. Rejected it because of the complexity it would add it. This fix is simpler, but has more latency as the launcher will need to relaunch the runner. However this should be acceptable since this is a edge case. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant n8n as n8n Main participant Broker as Task Broker participant Runner as Task Runner Note over Runner: Runner is idle, has open offers
pending with the broker rect rgb(255, 20, 230) Note over Runner: ⏰ Idle timeout fires Runner->>Runner: emit('runner:reached-idle-timeout') Runner->>Runner: stop() — sets isShuttingDown = true Runner->>Runner: stopTaskOffers() Note over Runner: ❌ BUG: openOffers NOT cleared
stop() awaits waitUntilAllTasksAreDone() end rect rgb(255, 240, 20) Note over n8n,Broker: Meanwhile, a new execution starts... n8n->>Broker: Execute workflow (Code node) Broker->>Runner: broker:taskofferaccept
(offerId, taskId) Note over Runner: Offer still exists in openOffers! end rect rgb(155, 200, 200) Note over Runner: ❌ BUG: offerAccepted() runs
— no shutdown check! Runner->>Runner: openOffers.delete(offerId) ✓ Runner->>Runner: runningTasks.set(taskId) ✓ Runner->>Broker: runner:taskaccepted Note over Runner: Task is now "running"...
but runner is shutting down end rect rgb(25, 18, 180) Note over n8n: 💀 Execution hangs forever —
task was accepted but never
completed or rejected end ``` - [x] I have seen this code, I have run this code, and I take responsibility for this code. ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts https://linear.app/n8n/issue/CAT-2959 ## Review / Merge checklist - [ ] I have seen this code, I have run this code, and I take responsibility for this code. - [ ] PR title and summary are descriptive. title: fix(ai-builder): Honor --timeout-ms across the eval harness (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

The eval CLI's `--timeout-ms` flag was silently capped or ignored in two places, leaving complex test cases stuck under hidden ceilings:

- **Build phase** clamped to 240s via `Math.min(timeoutMs, 240_000)` even though the flag's documented default is 600s. The cap was always the binding constraint, so the flag effectively did nothing.
- **Scenario execution** used a hardcoded 120s timeout in the n8n client; the CLI flag never reached this path.

After this change `--timeout-ms` is the single per-task budget for both phases, behaving as documented.

- Drop the 240s build cap and the `SCENARIO_BG_TASK_TIMEOUT_MS` constant.
- Plumb `timeoutMs` through `executeScenario` → `runScenario` → `client.executeWithLlmMock`.
- Update both callers (`runWorkflowTestCase` internal, `runWithLangSmith` CLI) to pass `args.timeoutMs`.

Linear: https://linear.app/n8n/issue/TRUST-64

## Validation

Stability run on `linear-bq-leaderboard` with the fix in place (5 iterations of useful data before the local server died for unrelated reasons):

| Iter | Build | Scenario |
|------|-------|----------|
| 1 | ✅ 215s | FAIL `builder_issue` (agent forgot BQ Project param) |
| 2 | ✅ 262s | FAIL `builder_issue` |
| 3 | ✅ 276s | FAIL `builder_issue` |
| 4 | ✅ 241s | **PASS** |
| 5 | ✅ 250s | **PASS** |

**4 of 5 builds (80%) exceeded 240s** — most would have been silently killed by the old cap. Build success rate is 100% with the fix; the framework now surfaces real `builder_issue` failures (missing required params, branch synchronization issues) instead of silent harness aborts. Sibling to TRUST-55, which becomes diagnosable once the cap stops masking real issues.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` and lint clean on changed files (`evaluations/harness/runner.ts`, `evaluations/cli/index.ts`).
- [x] N=10 stability run confirms `--timeout-ms 600000` is honored end-to-end (5 successful build+scenario completions before unrelated server crash).
- [x] No behavioral change for runs where the build naturally finishes under 240s — they take the same path through the harness.

title: fix(instance-ai): Make SANDBOX_LINK_SDK flag bypass Dockerfile SDK install (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary
Fixes sandbox creation in `@n8n/instance-ai` when the host `@n8n/workflow-sdk` version is ahead of what's published on npm (the typical state on `master` between releases).

**Symptom:** sandbox creation fails with `Sandbox failed to become ready within the timeout period` and a `502 Bad Gateway` from the sandbox service.

**Root cause:** the Dockerfile baked by `N8nSandboxImageManager` runs `npm install` against `PACKAGE_JSON`, which pins `@n8n/workflow-sdk` to the host version (e.g. `0.11.4`). When that version isn't on the registry, image build hits a 404 inside the sandbox service — the sandbox never becomes ready.

`N8N_INSTANCE_AI_SANDBOX_LINK_SDK=1` was supposed to be the escape hatch, but it ran *after* sandbox creation, so the failed image build killed it before it could help.

**Fix:** under the flag, bake an SDK-less `PACKAGE_JSON` (only `tsx` + `@types/node`). The post-creation step then `npm install`s the packed workspace tarball as before. If packing fails under the flag, we now throw with a clear `pnpm build` hint instead of silently degrading to a broken sandbox.

title: fix(Snowflake Node): Avoid call stack overflow on large result sets
body:
## Summary

Fixes a `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` crash that occurs when the Snowflake node processes a large number of rows.

**Root cause:** `returnData.push(...executionData)` uses the spread operator to expand all array elements as function arguments. When a query returns tens of thousands of rows, this hits the JS engine's argument-count limit and crashes the execution.

**Fix:** Replace all three occurrences with `returnData = returnData.concat(executionData)`. `Array#concat()` copies elements internally without spread/function-argument expansion, handling any dataset size without stack overflow. The same fix was previously applied to Postgres, MySQL, MSSQL, Google Sheets, and Oracle nodes.

body: ## Summary As specified by the tooltip hint introduced in 70ae90fa3c, hardcoding object names into the expression names is a valid workaround for cases where non-custom objects need to be interacted with that are not part of the predefined objects within the salesforce node. title: feat(OpenAI Chat Model Node): Add OpenAI account OAuth support
body:
## Summary

Add OpenAI account OAuth support to the OpenAI Chat Model node while keeping the existing API key credential path unchanged.

This adds a dedicated `OpenAI Account (ChatGPT)` credential and lets the OpenAI Chat Model node choose between API key and OAuth2 authentication. The OAuth2 credential stays aligned with n8n's existing credential UX: users still use the standard Connect button and popup/BroadcastChannel flow, while the popup hosts OpenAI's device-code login flow instead of asking users to paste an access token manually.

OpenAI account tokens cannot call the public OpenAI Responses API directly, so OAuth-backed chat model execution uses the ChatGPT/Codex account backend and maps LangChain messages, streaming chunks, tool calls, tool results, model discovery, and reasoning effort into that protocol. API key execution continues to use the existing OpenAI/LangChain path.

OpenAI-specific credential UI is kept small: the OAuth redirect URL and HTTP Request domain restriction controls are hidden for this credential because they do not apply to the device-code flow.

title: fix(cli): use valid grant type fallback when authorization server omits grant_types_supported
body:
Fixes #29147

## Problem

When an authorization server omits the optional `grant_types_supported` field from its OAuth discovery metadata (which is valid per [RFC 8414](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8414)), n8n fell back to `['authorization_code', 'implicit']`. However, `selectGrantTypeAndAuthenticationMethod()` requires **both** `authorization_code` **and** `refresh_token` to be present before selecting the auth-code or PKCE flow. Since `implicit` ≠ `refresh_token`, neither the PKCE branch nor the auth-code branch matched, causing:

```
BadRequestError: No supported grant type and authentication method found
```

This broke MCP/OAuth integrations (e.g. Auth0) that:
- Support PKCE (`code_challenge_methods_supported: ['S256', 'plain']`)
- Advertise token auth methods
- But omit `grant_types_supported` from their metadata

## Solution

Change the fallback value for `grant_types_supported` from `['authorization_code', 'implicit']` to `['authorization_code', 'refresh_token']`. This aligns the fallback with what `selectGrantTypeAndAuthenticationMethod()` expects, so PKCE or auth-code flow is correctly selected when the server omits this optional field.

## Testing

Added a unit test in `oauth.service.test.ts` that simulates an authorization server omitting `grant_types_supported` but advertising `S256` PKCE support. The test verifies that `grantType` is correctly set to `'pkce'` without throwing.

title: fix(AI Agent Node): Honor returnIntermediateSteps when persisting tool steps to memory
body:
## Summary

The V3 AI Agent's `saveToMemory` was always called with the full intermediate-step
sequence (`AIMessage` with `tool_calls` + paired `ToolMessage`s) regardless of the
`returnIntermediateSteps` option. On memory reload, those intermediate messages
surfaced in the chat transcript — either as visible `AIMessage` content
(`Calling <tool> with input: ...`) or, on memory backends without `addMessages`
support, as the literal `[Used tools: Tool: X, Input: ..., Result: ...]` string
prepended to the assistant's reply. The flag previously only controlled the
node's output shape, not memory persistence.

The fix gates the `steps` argument to `saveToMemory` on `options.returnIntermediateSteps`
in both the streaming and non-streaming code paths. With the flag disabled (the
default), only `HumanMessage(input)` and `AIMessage(output)` are persisted —
matching the v2.2 agent's `AgentExecutor.saveContext` semantics. With the flag
enabled, the full tool-call sequence is still saved so the LLM retains
multi-turn tool context.

## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts

title: fix(DeepSeek Node): Preserve reasoning_content on tool-calling assistant messages
body:
## Summary

Fixes a regression for users running the AI Agent node with DeepSeek's "thinking mode" models (`deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-chat`, `deepseek-reasoner`) and one or more tools attached.

DeepSeek's thinking mode (V3.2+ / V4) requires that any assistant message containing `tool_calls` is re-sent to the API with its original `reasoning_content` field intact. The OpenAI-compatible client used by `ChatOpenAI` neither preserves `reasoning_content` on the returned message nor forwards it back on subsequent requests, so multi-turn tool-calling fails with:

```
HTTP 400: The reasoning_content in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.
```

Reference: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode

### Approach

Wrap the chat model's `fetch` (via `ClientOptions.fetch`) with a small interceptor scoped to the chat-model instance:

1. On responses, capture `reasoning_content` keyed by each `tool_call.id` it accompanies. Both standard JSON responses and `text/event-stream` streaming responses are handled.
2. On outgoing requests, re-inject the captured `reasoning_content` into any assistant message whose `tool_calls` reference a known id and that does not already carry its own `reasoning_content`.

The capture map is per fetch wrapper (i.e. per chat-model instance), so concurrent executions do not share state. The interceptor is a no-op for non-DeepSeek code paths and for requests with no prior `reasoning_content` in flight.

### How to test

1. Configure a DeepSeek credential and an AI Agent with the DeepSeek Chat Model node (`deepseek-v4-flash` / `deepseek-chat` / `deepseek-reasoner`).
2. Attach at least one tool (sub-workflow or HTTP tool).
3. Send a prompt that requires tool use.
4. Before this PR: `400 Bad Request — The reasoning_content in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.`
5. After this PR: the agent completes the tool round-trip and returns a final response.

Unit tests cover JSON capture + injection, SSE-stream capture, no-op when no reasoning has been seen, no-overwrite of preexisting `reasoning_content`, and pass-through of non-JSON / non-SSE responses and bodies.

title: fix(editor): handle transient WebSocket close codes without hard disconnect
body:
## Summary

Fixes #29118 — The WebSocket `onConnectionLost` handler calls `disconnect()` for all close events, including benign proxy-related codes. This forces a full teardown (removes listeners, explicitly closes socket) even when the server is healthy, causing persistent "Connection Lost" UI flicker behind reverse proxies.

## Problem

Reverse proxies (Traefik, Nginx) and edge networks (Cloudflare) commonly send close codes:
- **1001** (Going Away) — proxy/server graceful shutdown
- **1005** (No Status Received) — common with session resets
- **1006** (Abnormal Closure) — TCP drop, no close frame

The current code treats all of these the same as fatal errors, calling `disconnect()` which tears down the connection and triggers a full reconnect cycle with visible UI disruption.

## Fix

For transient close codes (1001, 1005, 1006), skip the full `disconnect()` teardown. Instead, clean up the dead socket and schedule a reconnect directly. Fatal codes still go through the full `disconnect()` path.

## Testing

- Simulated proxy close with code 1005 → reconnects silently without UI flicker
- Fatal close (e.g., 1008) → full disconnect + reconnect as before
- Existing `useWebSocketClient` test suite passes

title: Bug fix (Slack node)
body:
## Summary

  Fixes a bug where the Slack node's Send and Wait operation ignores the Continue (using error
  output) error-handling setting and incorrectly routes failures through the success output.

  ## Root cause

  The sendAndWait code path in SlackV2.node.ts makes its chat.postMessage API call outside the
  for loop that contains the node's try/catch block. When the Slack API rejects the message
  (e.g. invalid_blocks, channel_not_found), the error propagates directly to the n8n execution
  engine instead of being handled by the node itself.

  The engine's error fallback for continueErrorOutput sets nodeSuccessData to the node's input
  data and routes it through output 0 (the success/regular output). Critically,
  handleNodeErrorOutput — which is responsible for moving error-structured items to the error
  output — is only called on the success path, so it is never invoked here. The result is that
  error data flows out through the success connector, bypassing the error output entirely.

  Before fix — call stack when invalid_blocks is returned:
  1. slackApiRequest throws NodeOperationError
  2. Error propagates past the node (no try-catch wrapping sendAndWait)
  3. Engine catch block: nodeSuccessData = [inputData] → routed to output 0
  4. handleNodeErrorOutput never called → error output receives nothing

  After fix — same scenario:
  1. slackApiRequest throws NodeOperationError
  2. Node's own try-catch catches it
  3. continueOnFail() is true → returns [[{ json: { error: "..." } }]]
  4. handleNodeErrorOutput detects the single-key { error } item → routes to output 1

  ## Changes

  - packages/nodes-base/nodes/Slack/V2/SlackV2.node.ts: Wrapped the postMessage call inside the
  sendAndWait branch with a try-catch that mirrors the error-handling pattern used in the main
  for loop.
  - Node version bumped to 2.5. Existing nodes pinned to earlier versions are unaffected.

  ## How to test

  1. Create a Slack node with operation Message > Send and Wait.
  2. Set On Error to Continue (using error output).
  3. Configure an invalid message body (e.g. attach an image URL that produces invalid_blocks).
  4. Execute — verify the error output fires and the success output does not.
  5. Repeat with a valid message body — verify normal send-and-wait behaviour is unchanged.

## Summary

Adds an `--activeState` flag to the `import:workflow` CLI so imported workflows can optionally keep the active state from their JSON, instead of always being force-deactivated.

title: fix(ai-builder): Stop tombstoning example UUIDs in LangSmith dataset sync (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the recurring `LangSmithConflictError: 409` that aborts eval runs during `syncDataset`. Two compounding design choices caused it:

1. **Deterministic UUIDs** derived from `${testCaseFile}/${scenarioName}`.
2. **Soft-delete on every full sync** for examples missing from the filesystem.

LangSmith soft-delete tombstones UUIDs permanently. Because our UUIDs were a pure function of the derivedId, any later sync reintroducing a previously-deleted scenario collided and the sync aborted before any evaluation could run. Branch rotation between teammates working on different scenario sets was the most common real-world trigger.

**Changes:**
- Drop `deterministicUuid` + `UUID_VERSION`. New examples get a random UUID via `crypto.randomUUID()`. Existing examples continue to be matched by their `(testCaseFile, scenarioName)` inputs — the lookup path was never keyed by UUID anyway, so updates preserve the stored UUID and historical experiment comparisons survive.
- Remove the `toDelete` branch. The sync is now append/update-only. Orphaned examples (files removed from disk) stay in the dataset harmlessly; `evaluate()` only runs against current scenarios. Manual cleanup happens via LangSmith UI or MCP when needed.

Linear: https://linear.app/n8n/issue/TRUST-63

## Why not keep deterministic UUIDs + just catch the 409?

The determinism didn't earn its cost. `syncDataset` already looks up examples by inputs — not by UUID — so determinism adds no value on the read path. The only value claimed was "same scenario has the same UUID across time," but that claim is already broken under renames (change the filename or scenarioName and the UUID changes anyway). Net: we paid complexity for a property we didn't actually have.

## Scenarios validated

| Scenario | Outcome |
|---|---|
| `--filter` run | Unchanged behavior. |
| Local file deleted | Example stays in LangSmith (harmless). No tombstone. |
| New local file / scenario | Fresh random UUID. Works. |
| File or scenario renamed | Old stays, new created. No collision. |
| Inputs changed in place | Existing example updated, same UUID. Unchanged. |
| Branch rotation | Both devs' scenarios accumulate; no soft-deletes; no future 409s. |
| Deleted-then-readded scenario (the bug we're fixing) | Creates fresh; no collision. |

## What's given up

- Auto-removal of stale examples. Replaced by manual cleanup (UI or MCP) when needed — runs at most a few times a year.
- "Recompute an existing example's UUID from its derivedId" as a property. No tool in the repo uses this.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests in `evaluations/__tests__/dataset-sync.test.ts` cover: create-with-random-UUID, update-in-place, no-deleteExamples-call, no-op when matched, and the resurrection path (previously-deleted scenario re-added creates fresh without collision).

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` clean, lint clean on changed files.
