title: fix(instance-ai): Return status from queueCorrection to prevent silent drops
body:
## Summary
- `queueCorrection()` now returns `'queued' | 'task-completed' | 'task-not-found'` instead of `void`
- The `correct-background-task` tool gives the orchestrator accurate feedback when a task has already finished, instead of a false success message
- Prevents the orchestrator from thinking a correction was delivered when the task had already completed, which led to duplicate builder cards via auto-follow-up

## Related
- [Instance AI issues reported](https://www.notion.so/n8n/Instance-AI-issues-reported-3285b6e0c94f802ca27cd2d2e067c5d7)
- Issue: "nothing happened after correct-background-task step"

## Root cause
Race condition: the background task (e.g. data-table-manager) completes before the orchestrator's correction can be delivered. `queueCorrection()` silently returned, the tool reported success, and the auto-follow-up system spawned a duplicate task.

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify existing tests pass (4/4 passing, including 2 new test cases)
- [ ] Verify that when a task has completed, the tool returns a message telling the orchestrator to use a follow-up task instead
- [ ] Verify that when a task is running, corrections are still delivered as before

title: feat(MongoDB Node): add support for JSON-based filter and update operations
body:
feat(MongoDB Node): add support for JSON-based filter and update operations

This PR enhances the MongoDB node update functionality by allowing users to define:

- A JSON-based filter condition
- A JSON-based update object

Previously, updates were limited to a single field (updateKey) and value, which restricted the ability to perform more advanced MongoDB update operations.

### Motivation
Previously, the MongoDB node update operation was limited to a single field (`updateKey`), making complex updates (e.g. `$pull`, `$rename`, multi-field updates) difficult and often requiring aggregation-based workarounds.

This change enables direct support for such operations using JSON-based filter and update objects, aligning the node more closely with native MongoDB capabilities.

### Changes
- Added a new mode to switch between:
  - Simple update (existing behavior)
  - JSON update (new behavior)
- Implemented parsing and execution of JSON filter and update objects
- Supports updating multiple fields in a single operation
- Added validation for empty/invalid inputs

### Backward Compatibility
- Existing workflows using `updateKey` are unaffected
- JSON functionality is opt-in via toggle
- No breaking changes introduced
### Tests
- Added unit tests for:
  - Simple mode
  - JSON mode
  - Edge cases (empty filter, invalid JSON)
- Verified all existing tests in n8n-nodes-base pass

### Summary
This change improves the flexibility of the MongoDB node by enabling advanced update operations directly, reducing the need for workarounds and aligning the node more closely with native MongoDB behavior.

title: feat(core): Add isolate pooling for VM expression engine
body:
## Summary This PR adds isolate pooling to the VM expression engine, following an **isolate-per-workflow** approach: each workflow execution acquires one isolate at start, holds it for the execution's lifetime, and disposes it on completion. The pool pre-warms replacements in the background to eliminate cold-start latency. - Pool size matches the execution concurrency limit, so a warm bridge is always available when an execution starts. - Credential resolution (outside execution context) uses the same acquire/evaluate/release path; if the pool is exhausted it falls back to a cold-start bridge. - The `Expression` instance is the owner key — `acquireIsolate()`/`releaseIsolate()` are instance methods that use `this` as the WeakMap key, replacing the previous `executionId`-based Map. ## Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant WE as WorkflowExecute participant Expr as Expression (instance) participant Eval as ExpressionEvaluator participant Pool as IsolatePool participant Bridge as IsolatedVmBridge participant Isolate as V8 Isolate Note over WE,Isolate: Execution start WE->>Expr: acquireIsolate() Expr->>Eval: acquire(this) Eval->>Pool: acquire() Note over Pool: Pool size = concurrency limit,
bridge always available Pool-->>Eval: bridge Pool->>Pool: replenish() in background Eval->>Eval: bridgesByOwner.set(expr, bridge) Note over WE,Isolate: Expression evaluation (sync, repeats per expression) WE->>Expr: renderExpression(expression, data) Expr->>Eval: evaluate(expression, data, this, { timezone }) Eval->>Eval: getBridge(this) → bridgesByOwner.get(expr) Eval->>Eval: getTransformedCode(expression) → code cache or Tournament Eval->>Bridge: execute(transformedCode, data, { timezone }) Bridge->>Isolate: script.runSync(wrappedCode) Isolate-->>Bridge: result Bridge-->>Eval: result Eval-->>Expr: result Expr-->>WE: result Note over WE,Isolate: Execution end (in .finally()) WE->>Expr: releaseIsolate() Expr->>Eval: release(this) Eval->>Eval: bridgesByOwner.delete(expr) Eval->>Pool: release(bridge) Pool->>Bridge: dispose() Bridge->>Isolate: isolate.dispose() Note over Isolate: V8 heap freed ``` ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts https://linear.app/n8n/issue/CAT-2279 ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

Adds **session-authenticated REST APIs** to create and update **role mapping rules** used for SSO provisioning: expressions are evaluated in order to map users to instance (global) or project roles, with optional project scoping for project rules.

### API

- **`POST /rest/role-mapping-rule`**
  - Requires global scope **`roleMappingRule:create`** (owners/admins).
  - Gated on **provisioning license** (same rule as existing provisioning endpoints: SAML **or** OIDC must be licensed). Otherwise responds with **403** and `{ "message": "Provisioning is not licensed" }`.
  - Request body validated with **`CreateRoleMappingRuleDto`** (`expression`, `role` slug, `type`: `instance` | `project`, `order`, optional `projectIds`).
  - Server-side rules: **instance** rules must target a **global** role and must not carry `projectIds`; **project** rules must target a **project** role and require at least one existing **project** id.
  - Success response uses the standard **`{ data: … }`** wrapper with id, fields, `projectIds`, and ISO timestamps.

### Implementation

- **`@n8n/api-types`**: `CreateRoleMappingRuleDto` + export from dto index.
- **`@n8n/db`**: `RoleMappingRuleRepository` (exported from package).
- **`packages/cli`**: `RoleMappingRuleService` (persistence + validation), `RoleMappingRuleController`, wired via **`ProvisioningModule`** dynamic import alongside the existing provisioning controller.

### Data model

- **`RoleMappingRule`** uses a **UUID** primary key with app-generated ids (`BeforeInsert` + `randomUUID()`), **`WithTimestamps`**, and migration alignment for `role_mapping_rule` / join table id columns.

### Tests

- **Unit**: `RoleMappingRuleService` (validation + success paths with mocked repos), controller unit tests for license gate.
- **Integration**: `role-mapping-rule.api.test.ts` (auth, scope, license, Zod, business validation, happy paths + DB assertions).
- **Test harness**: `setupTestServer` calls **`license.reset()`** after `setDefaults({ features })` so licensed modules see features during `initModules`; new endpoint group **`roleMappingRule`** explicitly imports the controller (integration tests do not run full `loadModules()`, so provisioning module init alone does not register this route).

### How to test

```bash
cd packages/@n8n/db && pnpm build   # if CLI typechecks against built db types
cd packages/cli && pnpm test role-mapping-rule
cd packages/cli && pnpm test:integration -- test/integration/role-mapping-rule.api.test.ts
```

Manually: as an owner with SAML or OIDC licensed, `POST /rest/role-mapping-rule` with a valid JSON body and session cookie; confirm 403 when those features are off.

title: feat(core): Add instance setting to disable public chat in Chat Trigger
body:
Hi everyone,

we noticed that any authenticated n8n user can currently enable public chat for a workflow. That can lead to workflow data being shared publicly when it shouldn’t be.

This PR adds an instance-level setting to disable the public chat mode of the built-in **Chat Trigger**, following a "better safe than sorry" approach.

When `N8N_DISABLE_PUBLIC_CHAT_TRIGGER=true` is set:

- the **Make Chat Publicly Available** option is no longer shown
- fields that only apply to public chat are hidden as well
- **Make Available in n8n Chat Hub** still remains available
- at runtime, `public = false` is still enforced, even if an older workflow JSON still contains that field

This is now implemented in the following places:

- `packages/@n8n/config/src/configs/chat-trigger.config.ts`
  - defines the instance-level config for `N8N_DISABLE_PUBLIC_CHAT_TRIGGER`
- `packages/@n8n/api-types/src/frontend-settings.ts`
  - exposes `chatTrigger.disablePublicChat` to the frontend
- `packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/app/stores/settings.store.ts`
  - stores the setting in frontend state
- `packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/features/ndv/settings/composables/useNodeSettingsParameters.ts`
  - hides public-chat-only Chat Trigger settings in the editor UI
- `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/trigger/ChatTrigger/ChatTrigger.node.ts`
  - enforces `public = false` at runtime when the setting is enabled

This replaces the earlier CLI-side metadata filtering approach.

## How to test

1. Build and run n8n normally without the env var.
   - Confirm the Chat Trigger still shows **Make Chat Publicly Available**.
2. Run n8n with:
   - `N8N_DISABLE_PUBLIC_CHAT_TRIGGER=true`
3. Create or edit a workflow with a Chat Trigger.
4. Confirm:
   - **Make Chat Publicly Available** is hidden
   - public-only fields are hidden
   - **Make Available in n8n Chat Hub** is still visible
5. Confirm runtime behavior still blocks public chat when the env var is enabled.

- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm build:n8n`
- `pnpm test` in `packages/cli`
- `pnpm test` in `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain`
- manual Docker smoke test with `N8N_DISABLE_PUBLIC_CHAT_TRIGGER=true`

title: feat(core): Improve public API middleware to handle different error types
body:
## Summary

Replaces the inline error handler in the public API router with a structured middleware that handles:

1. **n8n domain errors** (`ResponseError` subclasses like `NotFoundError`, `ForbiddenError`, `BadRequestError`) — responds with the error's own HTTP status code and message
2. **OpenAPI validation errors** (from `express-openapi-validator`) — responds with the validator's status code
3. **Unknown errors** — responds with 500 without leaking internals

This means public API handlers can simply `throw` n8n errors and they'll be automatically mapped to the correct HTTP response, instead of needing per-handler try/catch with manual `res.status().json()` calls.

### What has changed?

The middleware runs **after** the handlers. Handlers that catch errors and call `res.status(...).json(...)` themselves do not go through this middleware, so those endpoints are **not affected** by this change (majority of our operations).

This only affects "unhandled" errors — `ResponseError` subclasses now return the actual status code, and `UnexpectedError`/`OperationalError` become 500 instead of 400.

| Thrown value | Before (master) | After (this branch) |
|---|---|---|
| `ResponseError` (e.g. `NotFoundError`) | 400 | Uses `httpStatusCode` (e.g. 404) |
| `ResponseError` with `httpStatusCode === 400` (e.g. `BadRequestError`) | 400 | 400 (unchanged) |
| `UserError` | 400 | 400 (unchanged) |
| `UnexpectedError` | 400 | 500 + generic "Internal server error" |
| `OperationalError` | 400 | 500 + generic "Internal server error" |
| `HttpError` (express-openapi-validator) | `error.status` or 400 | `error.status` or 400 (unchanged) |
| Plain `Error` / unknown | 400 | 500 + generic "Internal server error" |

### How to test

Any public API call that triggers a domain error (e.g. `GET /api/v1/workflows/nonexistent-id`) should return the correct status code and `{ message }` body.

fix(core): prioritize HTTP status codes for retry logic in `httpRequest` nodes
body: ## Summary Fixed a critical bug in the workflow execution engine where nodes (specifically the **HTTP Request** node) would incorrectly trigger a `Retry on Fail` loop when receiving a successful **HTTP 200 OK** response if the JSON body contained an `"error": null` field. The logic now ensures that Transport Nodes (HTTP Request) ignore the body's error field for retry decisions, respecting the HTTP success status and leaving business-level error handling to the workflow. The previous logic used a strict `!== undefined` check on the `json.error` property. In JavaScript, `null !== undefined` evaluates to `true`, causing the system to interpret a successful "no error" response as a node failure. ### Technical Changes The fix involves updating the failure detection logic in the workflow engine to use boolean truthiness coercion (`!!`) instead of a strict inequality check against `undefined`. ### Location: `packages/core/src/execution-engine/workflow-execute.ts` ### Logic Change: **Before:** ```typescript let nodeFailed = !isEngineRequest(runNodeData) && runNodeData.data?.[0]?.[0]?.json?.error !== undefined; ``` **After:** ```typeScript const isTransportNode = executionData.node.type.toLowerCase().includes('httprequest'); const checkFailure = (data) => !isEngineRequest(data) && !!data.data?.[0]?.[0]?.json?.error && !isTransportNode; let nodeFailed = checkFailure(runNodeData); ``` The system now skips the body-error check entirely for HTTP nodes. For all other nodes, it uses boolean truthiness `(!!)` to ensure that `null` or `false` are correctly treated as successes, while actual error strings still trigger retries. --- ## Manual Verification ### Before the Fix (Buggy Behavior) The following screenshots demonstrate that when the field is renamed to status_info, only one request occurs (Control). However, as soon as the field is named error, the engine triggers multiple unintended retries. --- **In this test, I changed the field name to `error: null`. Even though the server still sent a `200 OK`, n8n triggered 3 extra retries. This proves the bug is specifically tied to the name of the "error" field.** --- **In this test, I renamed the field to `status_info: null`. The node worked perfectly and only sent one request. This proves that n8n handles `null` values correctly when the field name is different.** ### After the fix **With the new check `!!` applied, the engine now correctly ignores the `null` value. As shown in the logs, even though the response still contains "error": null, n8n now treats it as a success and only sends one request. The unintended retries are completely resolved.** **I have verified that the logic now correctly handles "errors" where the API returns a `200 OK` but includes an error message in the JSON body (e.g., `{ "error": "value" }`).** --- ### Test Results ``` Test Suites: 1 passed, 1 total Tests: 117 passed, 117 total Snapshots: 0 total Time: 4.077 s, estimated 7 s ``` ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts fixes: #27439 Linear Reference: [GHC-7421](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/GHC-7421) ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] I have seen this code, I have run this code, and I take responsibility for this code. - [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. title: fix(instance-ai): Clear thread-scoped maps on thread deletion to prevent memory leak
body:
## Summary
- Six `Map` instances in `InstanceAiService` (`threadUsers`, `threadResearchMode`, `threadTimeZone`, `threadMessageGroupId`, `runIdsByMessageGroup`, `domainAccessTrackersByThread`) accumulate entries for every thread created but are never cleaned up when threads are deleted or expire, causing unbounded memory growth on long-running instances.
- Adds `clearThreadState(threadId)` method to `InstanceAiService` that removes all in-memory state for a thread (maps + sandbox + event bus).
- Wires cleanup into both the `DELETE /threads/:threadId` controller endpoint and the TTL-based `cleanupExpiredThreads` startup routine.
- Also clears these maps in `shutdown()` for completeness.
- **Fixes stale message-group leak:** each user-initiated message replaces the thread's `messageGroupId` but the previous group's entry in `runIdsByMessageGroup` was never deleted, causing orphaned entries to accumulate for the lifetime of the process. Now the previous group is cleaned up eagerly at the mutation point.
- **Fixes active-state leak on thread deletion:** `clearThreadState` now also aborts active runs, suspended runs, and background tasks belonging to the deleted thread, and auto-rejects any pending HITL confirmations. Previously these maps were only cleaned on full service shutdown, so deleting a thread with in-flight work would leak entries in `activeRuns`, `suspendedRuns`, `backgroundTasks`, and `pendingSubAgentConfirmations`.

body:
## Summary Fixes the remaining VM expression engine test failures and adds dual-engine CI coverage. Brings the full `packages/workflow` test suite to **0 failures** with `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE=vm` and ensures both engines run on every test invocation. ### Fixes - **WHATWG percent-encoding**: VM-side `urlEncode` now encodes `!'()~` to match `URLSearchParams` output - **Lazy proxy `ownKeys`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor` traps**: `Object.keys()`, `Object.entries()`, `for...in`, and `JSON.stringify()` now work on proxy objects, including root proxies - **Cross-realm test assertions**: Relaxed assertions for typed arrays, `WeakMap`/`WeakSet`, `Intl`, `Math`, `Atomics`, `ArrayBuffer`, `SharedArrayBuffer`, `DataView` to test accessibility and behavior instead of cross-realm `toEqual` - **Process properties**: Added `process` as a lazy proxy in the VM isolate - **`renderExpression` complexity**: Extracted `mapVmError()` to bring method complexity below eslint limit ### Error propagation across isolate boundary Errors thrown inside the isolate or in host-side callbacks lose their class, name, and custom properties when crossing the V8 boundary. This PR adds a serialization pipeline that preserves them: ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph Host["Host - Node.js"] CB["Bridge callback
(getValueAtPath, etc.)"] SE["serializeError()"] RE["reconstructError()"] MAP["mapVmError()
in expression.ts"] end subgraph Isolate["V8 Isolate"] EXPR["Expression code"] E["E() handler
(swallows TypeError)"] PROXY["Lazy proxy
throwIfErrorSentinel()"] CATCH["Outer try-catch"] end CB -->|throws| SE SE -->|returns sentinel| PROXY PROXY -->|throws sentinel| E E -->|re-throws non-TypeError| CATCH EXPR -->|throws| E CATCH -->|returns sentinel via copy:true| RE RE -->|restores name + extra| MAP MAP -->|maps to ExpressionError| MAP ``` Key design decisions: - **Sentinels, not callbacks**: Errors are serialized into `{ __isError, name, message, stack, extra }` sentinel objects and returned as values. No callback round-trip needed. - **Single reconstruction point**: Errors are only reconstructed on the host in `reconstructError()`. title: fix(editor): Populate workflowDocumentStore in execution preview iframe
body:
## Summary

Two related bugs caused by the `workflowDocumentStore` migration where injected/computed store refs were `null`/`undefined` in certain contexts:

### 1. Input panel broken on execution preview (N8N-9831)
The `handleOpenExecution` post-message handler (used by the execution preview iframe) was not updating the `currentWorkflowDocumentStore` ref after initializing the workspace. After the NDV migration to `workflowDocumentStore` (PR #27158), `InputPanel.vue` reads nodes via the injected store ref — which stayed `null` in the execution preview iframe, causing the input panel to always show the "not connected" empty state.

**Fix:** Populate `currentWorkflowDocumentStore` after `openExecution()` completes, matching what the other two post-message code paths (`handleOpenWorkflow` and `handleOpenExecutionPreview`) already do via `importWorkflowExact`.

### 2. Demo/preview instance not rendering workflows correctly (ADO-4999)
In `initializeWorkspace`, connections were set via `workflowDocumentStore?.value?.setConnections()` — using a computed ref that evaluates to `undefined` when `workflowsStore.workflowId` is empty (which it is right after `resetWorkspace()`). The optional chaining silently skipped the call, leaving `workflowsStore.workflow.connections` empty. This caused AI agent nodes to render as squares with missing sub-connections in the demo/preview instance.

**Fix:** Use the already-available `initializedDocumentStore` direct reference (returned by `initState`) instead of the computed ref.

title: refactor: Implement task-based execution for instance AI and phased planning (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Refactors the instance AI runtime to extract orchestration logic from the CLI service into reusable packages, introduces a dependency-aware planned task system for multi-step builds, and adds three new frontend UI systems: structured questions, plan approval, and a task checklist.

### Backend: Runtime extraction & task-based execution

- **Extract generic runtime** from `instance-ai.service.ts` into `@n8n/instance-ai`:
  - `RunStateRegistry` — manages active/suspended/cancelled run lifecycle with confirmation timeout sweep
  - `BackgroundTaskManager` — spawns and tracks detached sub-agent tasks
  - `ResumableStreamExecutor` — unified stream consumption with suspend/resume HITL support
  - `StreamRunner` — thin wrapper for orchestrator-level manual-mode streaming
  - `AgentTreeSnapshotStorage` — persists agent trees for session restore
- **Planned task system** (`PlannedTaskService`, `PlannedTaskStorage`):
  - Dependency-aware task graph: tasks declare `deps` and execute in topological order
  - Plan tool creates the graph, emits a `tasks-update` for immediate UI visibility, then suspends for user approval before scheduling execution
  - Background task runners for each task kind: `build-workflow`, `manage-data-tables`, `research`, `delegate`
- **Workflow build loop** (`WorkflowTaskService`):
  - Build → verify → credential-fix → re-verify cycle with iteration logging
  - Sandbox-aware: works with ephemeral builder workspaces when available
- **Refactored sub-agent tools**: `delegate`, `build-workflow-agent`, `data-table-agent`, `research-agent` now use the shared `consumeStreamWithHitl` and `BackgroundTaskManager` instead of inline stream handling

### Backend: Questions & plan approval protocol

- **Refactored `ask-user` tool**: supports structured questions (single-select, multi-select, free-text) with options instead of free-text only. Each question renders in a paginated wizard with a built-in "Something else" input.
- **Plan tool suspend/resume**: the `plan` tool now suspends for user approval (`inputType: 'plan-review'`) before scheduling execution. Users can approve or request changes with feedback.
- **Extended confirmation protocol** (`@n8n/api-types`):
  - `inputType` enum: added `'questions'` and `'plan-review'`
  - `confirmationRequestPayload`: added `questions`, `introMessage`, `tasks` fields
  - `InstanceAiConfirmResponse`: added `answers` array
  - `InstanceAiConfirmRequestDto`: added `answers` validation
  - `ConfirmationData`: added `answers` field
  - `InstanceAiToolCallState.confirmation`: extended with new fields
  - `agent-run-reducer`: maps new fields from SSE events
  - `map-chunk.ts`: parses questions/tasks from tool suspend payloads
- **Full backend pipeline for answers**: DTO → controller → service → registry → resume data

### Frontend: New components

- **`InstanceAiQuestions.vue`**: Multi-step Q&A wizard with single-select (number badges), multi-select (checkboxes), free-text, pagination, keyboard navigation, "Something else" row. Adapted from AI builder's `PlanQuestionsMessage.vue`.
- **`PlanReviewPanel.vue`**: Single-card plan approval UI with accordion task list (expandable specs, dependency chips, kind icons), approve/request-changes footer. Renders inline in timeline — interactive while pending, read-only after approval.
- **`TaskChecklist.vue`**: Compact inline task status display (todo/in_progress/done/failed/cancelled icons).
- **`AnsweredQuestions.vue`**: Read-only Q&A pairs display after submission.

### Frontend: UI improvements

- **`AgentTimeline.vue`**: Renders questions, plan review, and task checklist inline instead of falling through to generic `InstanceAiToolCall`. Suppresses default rendering for pending questions/plan-review (handled by confirmation panel or inline).
- **`AgentNodeSection.vue`**: Redesigned delegate agent card — clean header with title/subtitle, human-readable tool labels row, collapsible "Delegation briefing" section, result/error footer.
- **`InstanceAiConfirmationPanel.vue`**: Added branches for `inputType === 'questions'` and `inputType === 'plan-review'`. Plan review excluded from confirmation panel (renders inline in timeline instead).
- **Confirmation panel exclusion**: plan-review tool calls filtered out of `pendingConfirmations` to avoid double rendering.

### Routing: Plan vs direct build

- Single workflow builds use `build-workflow-with-agent` directly (no plan/approval gate)
- Multi-step work (2+ tasks with dependencies) uses `plan` tool with approval
- `build-workflow-with-agent` added to orchestrator's tool set
- System prompt updated to guide the LLM on when to use each path

title: feat(editor): Replace restore/changes UI with inline version cards
body:
## Summary

Replaces the old inline "Restore version" links on user messages with dedicated **Version Card** components (`ChatVersionCard`) that appear between AI generations, showing node-level diffs.

Adds **non-destructive version restore**: when a user restores to an older version, messages after the restored version collapse into a `CollapsedMessagesGroup` instead of being deleted. The LLM thread is still truncated (backend), but the UI preserves the full history.

Key changes:

- **ChatVersionCard**: expandable card showing per-node diffs (added/modified/deleted), with restore, diff view, and history menu actions
- **CollapsedMessagesGroup**: collapsed region for messages after a restore point, with expand/collapse and "not visible to AI" note
- **Non-destructive restore flow**: `activeVersionCardId` and `resumeAfterRestoreMessageId` persisted to DB via new migration columns on `workflow_builder_session`
- **Post-modification versioning**: version cards use the post-modification workflow version (not the pre-modification revertVersionId), ensuring accurate diffs
- **Session reload parity**: version card IDs use `version-card-${userMessageId}` format consistently between live streaming and session reload
- **Collapsed-aware diffing**: `useReviewChanges` skips collapsed cards when finding predecessors for non-collapsed versions

### How to test

1. Open a workflow with the AI builder
2. Send 2-3 prompts that modify the workflow
3. Verify version cards appear between generations with correct node diffs
4. Click the `...` menu on an older version card → Restore
5. Confirm messages after the restored version collapse (with "X versions hidden" divider)
6. Send a new message — verify collapsed region stays, new messages appear after
7. Refresh the page — verify collapse state persists
8. Restore to the latest version — verify no collapse occurs (current conversation stays visible)

The Salesforce JWT API credential's **Private Key** field was rendered as a single-line password input, which strips newline characters when a PEM certificate is pasted. This caused JWT signing to always fail with `secretOrPrivateKey must be an asymmetric key when using RS256`.

title: fix(instance-ai): Scope project listing to only return projects the user can access (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug where the AI assistant (and MCP `search_projects` tool) listed **all users' personal projects** instead of only the current user's, causing confusing prompts like:

> "I see you have multiple personal projects. Which personal project is the MTG Card Bot currently in?"
> 1. "Jaakko Husso" 2. "Chat User" 3. "Member User"

### Root cause

`ProjectRepository.getAccessibleProjects()` and `getAccessibleProjectsAndCount()` used:

```sql
WHERE type = 'personal' OR projectRelations.userId = :userId
```

The first branch (`type = 'personal'`) matched **every** personal project in the instance regardless of ownership. Since every user already has a `projectRelation` to their own personal project (as `project:personalOwner`), the second branch already captures the user's own personal project — the first branch just adds everyone else's.

### Who uses these methods (and why it's a bug for all of them)

Three production callers rely on the fixed repository methods:

1. **`ProjectController.getAllProjects`** (`project.controller.ts`) — the `GET /projects` REST endpoint used by the UI sidebar and project pickers. Was returning other users' personal projects in the list even though the current user has no scopes on them and can't do anything with them.

2. **`InstanceAiAdapterService`** (`instance-ai.adapter.service.ts`) — calls `getAccessibleProjects` to determine which projects the user can work with. This was the main trigger for the bug — the AI saw all personal projects and asked "Which personal project?" on multi-user instances.

3. **MCP `search-projects` tool** (`search-projects.tool.ts`) — calls `getAccessibleProjectsAndCount` to search for projects the user can access. The tool's own description states its intent: *"Search for projects accessible to the current user. Use this to find a project ID before creating a workflow in a specific project."* It is explicitly scoped to `user.id` and meant to return only projects the user can work with — the buggy repository method was violating this contract by returning every personal project in the instance.

### Why this does NOT affect workflow transfers

Workflow transfer uses a **completely separate code path**. `WorkflowService.transferWorkflow()` validates the destination project via `projectService.getProjectWithScope()`, which checks whether the user has the `workflow:create` scope on that specific project — it never calls `getAccessibleProjects` or `getAccessibleProjectsAndCount`. Users don't have `workflow:create` on other users' personal projects, so transfers to foreign personal projects were never possible regardless of this bug.

### Fix

Remove the blanket `{ type: 'personal' }` clause from both repository methods. The user's own personal project is already returned via the `projectRelations.userId` join. Admin users are unaffected — they go through a separate `projectRepository.find()` code path that returns everything.

**Files changed:**
- `packages/@n8n/db/src/repositories/project.repository.ts` — Remove the `type = 'personal'` OR clause; switch from `LEFT JOIN` + `DISTINCT` to a simpler `INNER JOIN` (no duplicates possible now)
- `packages/cli/test/integration/database/repositories/project.repository.test.ts` — Update tests to assert the corrected behavior (member only sees own personal project)

## Related

- Linear: https://linear.app/n8n/issue/AI-2264
- Notion: https://www.notion.so/n8n/AI-sees-multiple-personal-projects-32d5b6e0c94f80eea0faf0f60dd58d69

title: fix(instance-ai): Use denylist for untestable triggers so polling triggers get verified
body:
## Summary

- Fixes a bug where `detectTriggerType()` used a **whitelist** of testable triggers (`manualTrigger`, `executeWorkflowTrigger`), causing all other triggers — including `scheduleTrigger` — to be classified as `trigger_only`, which **skips verification entirely**
- This led to the agent claiming it would "mock and verify" credentials but never actually running verification for schedule-based workflows
- Flips to a **denylist** of truly untestable triggers (`webhook`, `formTrigger`, `mcpTrigger`, `chatTrigger`) so polling/schedule triggers correctly go through verification

### Why denylist over whitelist

- The untestable set is smaller and more stable (only triggers needing an external request)
- Better failure mode: with a whitelist, forgetting a trigger silently skips verification; with a denylist, forgetting a trigger attempts verification and fails visibly

Ref: https://www.notion.so/n8n/Says-it-will-mock-creds-and-then-doesn-t-32c5b6e0c94f8037af0fc427e7ad8f85

## Test plan

- [ ] Build a workflow with a schedule trigger + mocked credentials → verify that verification runs instead of being skipped
- [ ] Build a workflow with a webhook trigger + mocked credentials → verify that verification is still skipped (trigger_only)
- [ ] Build a workflow with a manual trigger → verify that verification runs as before

title: fix(instance-ai): Remove normalizeWorkflowForSave expression wrapping (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

- Removes `normalizeWorkflowForSave()` which wrapped conditional parameters in expression format (e.g. `={{ "none" }}`) before saving AI-generated workflows
- The expression bypass in `displayParameter()` (`node-helpers.ts:431-433`) checks the **condition key's** value, not the parameter's own value — so the wrapping never actually prevented parameter stripping
- The wrapping caused the AI to learn and replicate invalid expression patterns (e.g. `={{ "none" }}` for `options`-type fields like ChatTrigger's `authentication`), making it struggle with fields that don't accept expressions

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify AI-built workflows with conditional parameters (e.g. ChatTrigger with `public: true` + `authentication`) save and activate correctly without expression wrapping
- [ ] Verify AI no longer generates `={{ "value" }}` patterns for options-type fields

title: fix: await publisher.publishCommand in multi-main workflow activation/deactivation
body:
In multi-main mode, follower instances were publishing Redis commands with `void` (fire-and-forget), causing Redis-level errors to be silently swallowed and returning success to the caller before the publish completed.

## Changes

- **`add()` method** — `await` the `add-webhooks-triggers-and-pollers` publish so Redis errors propagate to the caller instead of being discarded
- **`remove()` method** — same fix for `remove-triggers-and-pollers` for consistency

```diff
- void this.publisher.publishCommand({
+ await this.publisher.publishCommand({
      command: 'add-webhooks-triggers-and-pollers',
      payload: { workflowId, activeVersionId: dbWorkflow.activeVersionId, activationMode },
  });
```

`publishCommand` is already `async`, so no signature changes are needed. This does not guarantee the leader has finished processing the command — it only ensures the Redis publish itself doesn't fail silently.

title: feat(core): Prune instance_ai_workflow_snapshots table
body:
## Summary

This PR contains change to unmerged migration. This is fine and we decided in favor of this over a new migration.

`instance_ai_workflow_snapshots` table snapshots are pretty large. We were never cleaning up suspended "agentic-loop" and "workflowExecution" snapshots even after they are resumed, Mastra takes care of some of these snapshots automatically but not these.

I initially added compression to make those snapshots smaller, but since that comes with its own CPU and memory cost I scrapped that, the proper solution is to not let that table grow uncontrollably - cleaning up after resuming executions once they are no longer needed with `cleanupMastraSnapshots` should help a lot here and make the compression unnecessary.

I also added a daily cleanup that removes any snapshots that might be left orphaned, perhaps due to instance crashes or other similar reasons.

Added explicit status field on the table so that we can query these rows by status without parsing the snapshot, currently not that relevant but helps on the list query that Mastra can make (we weren't respecting all the args mastra could set there). This means that once merged we need to clean our dev dbs and run this migration again.

title: feat(Jira Node): Add OAuth2 (3LO) support
body:
## Summary

Adds OAuth2 Authorization Code (3LO) support to the Jira node and Jira Trigger node as a new `Cloud (OAuth2)` auth option, alongside the existing Cloud (API token), Server, and Server PAT modes.

### Changes

- **New credential** `JiraSoftwareCloudOAuth2Api` — extends `oAuth2Api`, uses Atlassian's auth service (`auth.atlassian.com`), includes `audience=api.atlassian.com&prompt=consent` query params, and supports optional custom scopes
- **CloudId resolution** — OAuth2 tokens are scoped for `api.atlassian.com`, so API calls go through `https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/{cloudId}/rest/...`; the cloudId is auto-discovered from the Atlassian `accessible-resources` endpoint using the user-supplied domain as a discriminator, and cached in memory for the life of the process
- **Node + Trigger** — new `Cloud (OAuth2)` option added to the `jiraVersion` parameter in both `Jira.node.ts` and `JiraTrigger.node.ts`
- **Constants** — `jiraSoftwareCloudOAuth2Api` added to `GENERIC_OAUTH2_CREDENTIALS_WITH_EDITABLE_SCOPE` to preserve custom scopes on reconnect
- **Tests** — credential OAuth2 flow tests, GenericFunctions credential routing tests (with accessible-resources mock), and node-level routing test

### How to test

1. Create a `Jira SW Cloud OAuth2 API` credential with your Atlassian site URL and OAuth2 app client ID/secret
2. Select `Cloud (OAuth2)` in the Jira node's _Jira Version_ dropdown
3. Connect the credential and run any Jira operation — API calls should succeed against `api.atlassian.com`

title: fix(agent Node): Add `guardrailsInput` fallback in auto mode and improve prompt validation
body: ## Summary Fixes two related issues in `getPromptInputByType` in `utils/helpers.ts`: 1. **Guardrails → AI Agent integration broken** (#27417): When a Guardrails node is connected to an AI Agent node, the agent throws "No prompt specified" because `auto` mode only looked for `chatInput` but the Guardrails node outputs `guardrailsInput`. The `guardrails` prompt type that previously handled this was removed from the UI in v3.1 without a migration path, leaving users with no working option. 2. **null prompt input not caught**: `evaluateExpression` returns `null` at runtime when the referenced field doesn't exist. The previous check only tested `=== undefined`, causing `null` to slip through silently and produce a confusing, unhelpful error message. ### Root Cause ```typescript // BEFORE — only checks undefined, misses null entirely if (input === undefined) { ... } // BEFORE — auto mode only looks for chatInput, ignores guardrailsInput input = ctx.evaluateExpression('{{ $json["chatInput"] }}', i) as string; ``` ### Changes **`utils/helpers.ts`** - Add `guardrailsInput` fallback in `auto` mode — if `chatInput` is null/undefined, automatically checks `guardrailsInput` next. `chatInput` and `guardrailsInput` are mutually exclusive in practice since the Guardrails node drops all incoming fields and only outputs `guardrailsInput` - Catch both `null` and `undefined` in prompt validation - Silently cast `number` and `boolean` primitives to string - Hard reject `object` and `array` types with a clear error message - Reject empty and whitespace-only strings - Add explicit `: string` return type — no more `as string` casts hiding runtime nulls - Improve all error messages to be generic and actionable - Add `itemIndex` to all `NodeOperationError` throws - Extract `isExpressionBased` const to avoid duplicating the condition - Add backwards compatibility comment for deprecated `guardrails` mode **`utils/descriptions.ts`** - Rename `auto` option from `"Connected Chat Trigger Node"` to `"Auto-detect from connected node"` — more accurate and future-proof - Update `auto` option description to mention both `chatInput` and `guardrailsInput` - Update `builderHint` to mention both Chat Trigger and Guardrails node - Update `textFromPreviousNode` default to `={{ $json.chatInput ?? $json.guardrailsInput }}` so the prompt field shows the correct resolved value regardless of which node is connected upstream - Apply same description updates to `promptTypeOptionsDeprecated` for consistency **`utils/tests/helpers.test.ts`** - Added 38 new tests for `getPromptInputByType` across 7 groups: - Happy path including `guardrailsInput` fallback - `null`/`undefined` inputs - Invalid type inputs - Empty/whitespace strings - Error message content - itemIndex correctness - Correct method called per promptType ### How to Test **Scenario 1 — Guardrails → AI Agent (the main fix)** 1. Create: `Manual Trigger → Guardrails → AI Agent → any Chat Model` 2. Guardrails: Operation = Sanitize, any text 3. AI Agent: Leave "Source for Prompt" on default (auto) 4. **Before:** "No prompt specified" 5. **After:** Works correctly ✅ **Scenario 2 — Chat Trigger → AI Agent (existing behavior)** 1. Create: `Chat Trigger → AI Agent → any Chat Model` 2. Run via chat widget 3. **Before and after:** Works correctly ✅ **Scenario 3 — Manual Trigger with no input** 1. Create: `Manual Trigger → AI Agent → any Chat Model` 2. Leave prompt on auto 3. **Before:** Confusing error mentioning internal field names 4. **After:** Clear actionable error message ✅ --- ### Canvas ### AI Agent Node ### Chat Model --- ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts closes #27417 Linear Reference: [GHC-7418](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/GHC-7418) related #27342 ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. - [ ] Docs updated or follow-up ticket created. - [x] Tests included. - [ ] PR Labeled with `Backport to Beta`, `Backport to Stable`, or `Backport to v1`

title: feat(core): Add RoleMappingRule entity and database tables
body:
## Summary

Adds the database layer for **role mapping rules**: rules map an expression to a target role, scoped by **type** and ordered by **`order`** (lower = higher priority; first match wins). A rule can apply to **multiple projects** via a join table.

**Schema**
- `role_mapping_rule`: `id` (UUID, PK), `expression` (text), `role`, `type`, `order` (integer); indexes on `role` and on `(type, order)`.
- `role_mapping_rule_project`: composite PK `(roleMappingRuleId, projectId)`; FKs to `role_mapping_rule` and `project` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`; index on `projectId`.

**Application**
- New TypeORM entity `RoleMappingRule` with `@ManyToMany` to `Project` and `@JoinTable` on `role_mapping_rule_project`.
- Inverse `@ManyToMany` on `Project.roleMappingRules`.
- UUIDs for rule IDs are generated in `@BeforeInsert` with `randomUUID()` (no DB default), consistent with `@n8n/db` guidance.

**Migrations**
- Common migration `1772800000000-CreateRoleMappingRuleTable` registered for **PostgreSQL and SQLite**.

**How to test**
1. Run migrations against a dev DB (`n8n start` or your usual migration path).
2. Confirm tables exist: `role_mapping_rule`, `role_mapping_rule_project`.
3. Optional: persist a `RoleMappingRule` with `projects` loaded/saved via TypeORM and verify join rows.

title: feat(instance-ai): Add setup-workflow tool with full node setup UI (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Implements the **backend-first workflow setup architecture** ([RFC](https://www.notion.so/n8n/Backend-first-workflow-setup-architecture-32c5b6e0c94f80a6a0a9c36b5b60d460)) for Instance AI.

Today's workflow setup is coupled to the canvas editor — credential discovery, parameter validation, and trigger testing all live in browser stores. This means setup can only happen when the user is staring at the canvas. The AI agent, operating from the chat sidebar, can't reach any of it.

This PR inverts control: **the backend owns analysis and mutation; the frontend is a passive renderer.** The result is a surface-agnostic setup contract that any client can drive — including the ones we're building next.

### Why this architecture matters

The setup tool communicates through a **structured `SetupRequest` contract** over a **suspend/resume state machine**. A surface only needs to render the data and send back user selections — it never needs to understand node types or credential schemas.

| Transport | Suspend becomes… | Resume becomes… |
|-----------|-------------------|-----------------|
| **SSE** (web editor) | Event on the stream | POST to chat endpoint |
| **CLI** | Printed prompt | stdin response |
| **MCP** | Tool suspend semantics | Tool resume call |

This means the same tool — zero modifications — can power workflow setup from a CLI session, an MCP server, or a mobile client. The contract is the interface; the transport is pluggable.

### What's in this PR

**Backend: analysis, resolution, and atomic apply**
- `SetupWorkflowService.analyzeWorkflow()` — DFS-based execution-order analysis with `CredentialCache` for cross-node deduplication
- `SetupWorkflowService.applyNodeChanges()` — single load-mutate-save cycle (no partial-success window)
- `InstanceAiAdapterService` gains `getParameterIssues()`, `getNodeCredentialTypes()`, and `isTestable()` — the same `NodeHelpers` logic the builder runs client-side, now available server-side
- Suspend/resume via Mastra tool mechanism — no new endpoints
- Unified orchestration: system prompt, verification verdict, and server guidance all converge on `setup-workflow`

**Frontend: render the contract, collect user input**
- `InstanceAiWorkflowSetup.vue` — card-scoped credential selections, HTTP URL grouping, auto-advance, inline parameter editing via `ParameterInputList`, first-trigger-only completion gating
- Reuses `NodeCredentials` (standalone mode) with `projectId` threading for project-scoped credential creation
- Server-authoritative canvas updates: waits for tool-result SSE before mutating the canvas
- Await-based confirmation: reverts UI on POST failure so the user always has a retry surface
- `InstanceAiCredentialSetup.vue` refactored to share the same UX patterns

**Tests: 30 focused tests** covering service analysis, tool state machine, apply/rollback semantics, and `needsAction` computation.

### Parity with the builder's setup panel

All setup rules from the existing builder panel are ported to the backend:

| Rule | How |
|------|-----|
| Non-testable credential skip | `credentialService.isTestable()` |
| First-trigger-only completion | `isFirstTrigger` flag from DFS sort |
| Disabled-node filtering | `node.disabled` check in `buildSetupRequests()` |
| Execution-order card sorting | DFS from triggers with position tiebreak |
| HTTP URL grouping | Same `groupCredentialsByType()` logic |
| Card-scoped selections | Selections keyed by card ID |
| Project-scoped credential creation | `projectId` threaded end-to-end |
| Atomic apply | Single load-mutate-save (not per-node) |

### Deliberate scope cuts

- **Webhook listening state** — requires streaming execution model; triggers run as one-shot
- **Full SSE reconciliation** — canvas reflects user selections + POST confirmation; server-side type coercion not fed back yet
- **In-memory suspend state** — process restart loses rollback guarantee (durable persistence is follow-up)

See the [RFC § Limitations & Next Steps](https://www.notion.so/n8n/Backend-first-workflow-setup-architecture-32c5b6e0c94f80a6a0a9c36b5b60d460) for the full gap analysis across surfaces.

body:
## Summary
Add plan-based execution to the Instance AI agent: a structured planning phase with user approval, phased background execution, and a dedicated plan/task UI.

### What this PR adds

**Planning system** — The orchestrator can now create multi-phase plans with `create-plan`, gather requirements via `ask-plan-questions`, and wait for user approval via `request-plan-approval`. After approval, phases execute as background tasks with deterministic state transitions managed by the workflow loop controller.

**Plan tools (8 new orchestration tools):**
- `create-plan` / `update-plan` / `approve-plan` / `request-plan-approval`
- `ask-plan-questions` — structured clarification Q&A before planning
- `update-phase-status` / `block-phase-with-question`
- `list-background-tasks` / `get-background-task` — orchestrator can query running tasks

**NDJSON thread streaming** — Replaces the SSE/event-bus transport with a long-running NDJSON stream per thread (`GET /stream/:threadId`). The stream opens once, delivers a sync frame with historical state, then streams delta events for the lifetime of the connection. Handles reconnect with frame replay.

**Durable task runs** — Background tasks (workflow builds, research, data-table ops) are now persisted as `InstanceAiTaskRun` records with typed outcomes, enabling the plan execution engine to track progress across phases and resume after interruptions.

**Plan & task UI:**
- `InstanceAiPlanPanel` — displays the current plan with phase timeline, status badges, and blocker cards
- `InstanceAiPlanTimeline` — visual phase-by-phase progress with artifacts and verification state
- `InstanceAiTaskPanel` — shows background task runs grouped by message, with real-time status

**Workflow loop enhancements:**
- `patchAttempts` state tracking — targeted node patches before escalating to full rebuild
- `patch` action type — allows single-node fixes without rebuilding the entire workflow
- `failed` terminal state with 3-strike verification budget
- `hasRepeatedRepair()` — prevents infinite patch loops for the same failure signature

**Agent run reducer** — Shared pure reducer (`agent-run-reducer.ts`) for building agent tree state from events, used by both frontend (live rendering) and backend (snapshot building). Handles plan events (`plan-created`, `plan-updated`, `phase-status-updated`, etc.) and task events.

title: perf(core): Cache authenticated user to avoid DB query on every request
body:
## Summary

Implement an in-memory TTL cache for `AuthService.validateToken()` to eliminate the redundant database query that runs on **every single authenticated API request**.

Previously, every request performed a full `UserRepository.findOne()` with a `relations: ['role']` join, even for the same user making back-to-back requests. The existing code had a TODO comment acknowledging this:

```typescript
// TODO: Use an in-memory ttl-cache to cache the User object for upto a minute
```

This PR implements exactly that — a `Map<string, CachedUser>` with a 60-second TTL, keyed by user ID. The cache uses the JWT hash as a staleness check, so any password change, email change, or MFA update immediately invalidates the cached entry (the JWT hash is derived from these fields).

### How it works

1. On first request, the user is fetched from DB and cached with the JWT hash + expiry
2. Subsequent requests within the TTL window skip the DB query entirely if the JWT hash matches
3. If the user changes their password/email/MFA, the JWT hash changes and the cache entry is bypassed
4. Disabled users are checked on every cache hit to ensure immediate lockout
5. Cache entries expire after 60 seconds, forcing a fresh DB lookup

### Benchmark results

Measured locally with n8n running on SQLite, Node.js 22.22.1. Each test sends sequential HTTP requests with a valid auth cookie.

#### Sequential requests (single client)

| Endpoint | Before (avg) | After (avg) | Improvement |
|----------|-------------|------------|-------------|
| `GET /rest/settings` | 8.1ms | 3.9ms | **52%** |
| `GET /rest/credentials` | 10.0ms | 4.2ms | **58%** |
| `GET /rest/executions` | 11.7ms | 6.9ms | **41%** |
| `GET /rest/workflows` | 14.5ms | 10.1ms | **30%** |
| `GET /rest/workflows/:id` | 14.6ms | 11.1ms | **24%** |

#### Concurrent requests (20 parallel)

|--------|--------|-------|-------------|
| Wall time | 265ms | 179ms | **32%** |

title: fix(cli): support sticky dist-tags for community packages
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes community package installation and updates for npm `dist-tags` such as `beta` and `next`, while intentionally continuing to reject semver ranges and non-registry package specs.

The original bug was that n8n treated every `name@...` suffix as if it had to be a strict semver version. That meant valid npm selectors like `n8n-nodes-imap@beta` were rejected before n8n ever reached the registry. The failure was reproducible both when the selector was embedded in the package name and when it was passed separately as the `version` field. In practice, this prevented installing community nodes from release channels, even though npm itself supports them.

The implementation replaces the previous semver-only validation with `npm-package-arg`, which is the parser npm itself uses for install specs. However, the fix does **not** simply “remove validation”. During investigation, that turned out to be unsafe: npm specs can also represent aliases, git repositories, tarball URLs, `file:` references, and local directories. Allowing arbitrary npm specs here would widen the install surface beyond registry-backed community packages. To avoid that, the new validation layer explicitly allows only:
- plain package names
- exact registry versions
- registry `dist-tags`

It explicitly rejects:
- semver ranges
- `npm:` aliases
- git specs
- tarball URLs
- `file:` specs
- local directory specs
- malformed selectors

The second part of the fix is making `dist-tag` installs sticky. Installing `n8n-nodes-foo@beta` should not behave like “resolve beta once, then forget it ever came from beta”. If we only stored the resolved version, later update checks would silently fall back to `latest`, which is the wrong channel. To fix that, this PR adds a nullable `requestedDistTag` field to `installed_packages`. n8n still stores the exact installed version as before, but now also remembers the original channel when the install came from a non-`latest` tag.

That storage model is deliberate. The exact version remains the source of truth for what is currently installed and for deterministic verification. The stored tag is only the selector used for future updates. This keeps installation deterministic while preserving channel semantics.

The install/update flow now resolves a tag to an exact version before download. That resolved version is then used for:
- checksum verification
- `npm pack`
- package loading
- pubsub update payloads

This is important for correctness in multi-instance setups. If one instance resolves `beta` to `1.2.3-beta.4`, every instance in the cluster must install that same artifact for the same operation. At the same time, secondaries must not lose the fact that the package is tag-tracked. For that reason, the pubsub payload now carries the exact resolved version **and** the original requested tag when one exists. Secondaries install the exact version, but keep the dependency selector in their local `nodesDownloadDir/package.json` as `beta`, so future `npm outdated` checks continue following the beta channel.

Update-check behavior was also adjusted. For regular installs, n8n keeps the existing behavior and compares against `latest`. For tag-tracked installs, n8n now uses npm’s `wanted` field instead. This matters because `latest` answers the stable channel question, while `wanted` answers the question “what would npm install for the dependency spec currently in package.json”. For a dependency pinned to `beta`, `wanted` is the correct channel-aware target. The code also avoids false positives by only marking an update as available when the chosen target version is actually greater than the installed version.

Update execution follows the same rule. If a package has `requestedDistTag` and the user clicks update without specifying an explicit version, n8n reuses the stored tag. That means `beta` keeps updating against `beta`. Exact-version installs still behave as before. Verified/checksum-based flows remain exact-version-based and are not widened.

A related cleanup in this PR is that uninstall now removes the package entry from the local `nodesDownloadDir/package.json`. This keeps the dependency spec file aligned with the real installed state and avoids stale selectors affecting `npm outdated`.

I explicitly did **not** add semver range support in this PR. During analysis, ranges turned out to need different long-term semantics from tags. A tag is a named channel and maps naturally to a sticky selector such as `beta`. A range such as `^1.2.0` would also need to be stored and preserved to behave correctly over time, but it raises a broader product and implementation question: should n8n treat ranges as sticky user intent, and how should that interact with UI messaging, update display, checksum verification, and restoration of missing packages? That is solvable, but it is a separate scope from the bug at hand. Supporting tags without ranges keeps this fix safe, focused, and easy to reason about.

From a root-cause perspective, the bug came from three coupled assumptions:
1. `name@selector` was assumed to mean `name@exact-semver`.
2. validation was duplicated across controller/service paths.
3. update logic assumed every install should eventually compare against `latest`.

This PR addresses all three:
- parsing is npm-spec-aware instead of semver-only
- validation is centralized around a stricter allowlist
- update behavior now respects the original install channel

Files changed include the controller, service, npm utility helpers, persistence layer, migration registration, and test suites. A local type declaration for `npm-package-arg` was added because the package does not ship TypeScript declarations in this repo setup.

title: fix(nodes-base): implement S3 bucket delete operation and fix related issues
body:
## Summary

Fixes #27396

Three issues were found and fixed in the S3 node:

### 1. `bucket > delete` operation not implemented

The **Delete** operation was defined in `BucketDescription.ts` and visible in the UI, but the execution block was **never implemented** in `S3.node.ts`. When triggered, it silently returned `success` with 0 output items in ~2ms — without making any HTTP request.

**Fix:** Added the missing `if (operation === 'delete')` block inside `if (resource === 'bucket')`.

```typescript
//https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_DeleteBucket.html
if (operation === 'delete') {
  const name = this.getNodeParameter('name', i) as string;
  await s3ApiRequestSOAP.call(this, `${name}`, 'DELETE', '');
  const executionData = this.helpers.constructExecutionMetaData(
    this.helpers.returnJsonArray({ success: true }),
    { itemData: { item: i } },
  );
  returnData.push(...executionData);
}
```

### 2. `s3ApiRequestSOAP` silently swallows errors on empty responses

In `GenericFunctions.ts`, the `s3ApiRequestSOAP` function had a `catch (error) { return error }` pattern. Any S3 operation returning a non-XML response (e.g. `HTTP 204 No Content`) would cause `parseString` to throw, which was silently caught and **returned as data** instead of being re-thrown. This masked real failures.

**Fix:** Empty responses (`HTTP 204`) now return `undefined` early. Parse errors are re-thrown correctly.

### 3. `destinationPath` in file copy requires undocumented leading slash

The `file > copy` operation parses `destinationPath` assuming it starts with `/` (using `split('/')[1]` to extract the bucket name). However, the UI field description does not mention this requirement, unlike `sourcePath` which explicitly states *"should start with (/)"*. Without the leading slash, the bucket name resolves to the file key, causing a `"resource not found"` error.

**Fix:** Normalize `destinationPath` to always start with `/` before parsing, making it resilient to both `bucket/key` and `/bucket/key` formats.

## Test plan

- [ ] Create a bucket via S3 node (`bucket > create`) ✅
- [ ] Delete a bucket via S3 node (`bucket > delete`) — previously broken, now fixed
- [ ] Copy a file with `destinationPath` without leading slash — previously broken, now fixed
- [ ] Verify existing operations (upload, download, getAll, search, folder ops) are unaffected

## Notes

- Verified against MinIO (S3-compatible). `DELETE /{bucket}` returns `HTTP 204 No Content`, which was the root cause of the silent failure in `s3ApiRequestSOAP`.
- The same `BucketDescription.ts` is shared with the AWS S3 node — that node should be checked for the same missing `delete` implementation.

## Summary
- **Cache tool instances**: Caches builder tool instances (search, get, suggest) on `WorkflowBuilderToolsService` so they are created once and reused across invocations instead of being recreated on every MCP tool call
- **Cache tool results**: Adds result caching for all three discovery tools (`searchNodes`, `getNodeTypes`, `getSuggestedNodes`) so repeated queries return cached results instantly

title: feat(calendly): Migrate Trigger to V2 API with HMAC Security and Versioned Architecture
body:
## Summary
This PR modernizes the Calendly Trigger node by migrating it to the **Calendly V2 API** and introducing critical security enhancements. To ensure zero breaking changes for existing workflows, this implements a **Versioned Node Architecture**.

* **Version 1 (Legacy):** Preserved as a sandbox using the `api/v1` endpoints and legacy `X-TOKEN` authentication to prevent breaking existing user setups.
* **Version 2 (Modern):** The new default, utilizing `api.calendly.com`, supporting both OAuth2 and Personal Access Tokens (PAT) via `Bearer` auth, and implementing mandatory webhook security features.

## Key Changes

###  Security & Authentication
* **Webhook Signature Verification:** Added HMAC-SHA256 signature verification. Users can now provide a `webhookSigningKey` in their credentials to guarantee incoming requests originate strictly from Calendly.
* **Replay Attack Protection:** Implemented a 5-minute timestamp validation window. The node extracts the `t` parameter from the signature header and rejects requests older than 300 seconds.
* **OAuth2 Scopes Update:** Updated the default scopes for `CalendlyOAuth2Api` to include all required permissions for current node functionality: `user:read`, `bookings:read`, `bookings:manage`, `webhooks:read`, and `webhooks:write`.
* **PAT Authentication Fix:** Resolved the issue where V2 rejected `X-TOKEN` headers. The credentials file now dynamically routes to `Authorization: Bearer` for V2 requests while maintaining legacy headers for V1.

###  Architecture & UX
* **Versioned Architecture:** Refactored the node using the `HttpRequest` injection pattern (`VersionedNodeType`). 
* **Identity Resolution:** Added an automatic pre-flight call to `/users/me` in V2 to automatically resolve `user` and `organization` URIs.
* **Robust Error Handling:** Improved 401/403 error messages to be highly descriptive, specifically guiding users on signature mismatches, stale timestamps, or missing `user:read`/`organization` scopes.
* **UI Enhancements:** Added a Notice Node for Organization-level scopes to warn users about required Admin/Owner permissions, and clarified the `webhookSigningKey` tooltip.

title: fix(core): Expand variables.value column from varchar(255) to TEXT
body:
## Summary

Add a PostgreSQL migration to expand the `variables.value` column from `varchar(255)` to `TEXT`.

The original `CreateVariables` migration (1677501636754) created the column as `varchar(255)`, but the entity definition uses `@Column('text')` and the documented limit is 1,000 characters. PostgreSQL enforces the `varchar(255)` constraint, causing `value too long for type character varying(255)` errors for all self-hosted PostgreSQL users since v0.225.0.

SQLite is unaffected because it does not enforce varchar length limits, and the recent `AddProjectIdToVariableTable` migration already recreated the SQLite table with `TEXT` columns.

title: fix(core): Send client_id and client_secret in body for OAuth2 PKCE flow
body:
## Summary

When OAuth2 PKCE grant type was used with "body" authentication, `client_id` and `client_secret` were not included in the token exchange request body (client authentication was done via header). This caused failures for APIs (e.g. Mercado Livre, SoundCloud) that require these parameters during PKCE flow.

The fix unifies the PKCE and body-auth logic so that `code_verifier` is added when PKCE is selected, and `client_id`/`client_secret` are added to the body when body authentication is selected — both can now apply together.

### Token exchange behavior by configuration

| Grant Type | Auth Method | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Authorization Code | Header | `client_id`/`client_secret` in `Authorization: Basic` header | No change |
| Authorization Code | Body | `client_id`/`client_secret` in request body | No change |
| PKCE | Header | `code_verifier` in body, `client_id`/`client_secret` in `Authorization: Basic` header | No change |
| **PKCE** | **Body** | **Only `code_verifier` in body; `client_id`/`client_secret` sent via header instead of body (bug)** | **`code_verifier`, `client_id`, and `client_secret` all sent in request body** |

title: fix(Google Drive Node): properly route failed file downloads to error…
body:
## 🐛 Bug Fix: Google Drive Node Silent Failure on Download Error

**Resolves:** #27312

### 📝 Description

This PR fixes a critical routing bug in the Google Drive `Download` operation. 

Previously, if a file download failed (e.g., 404 Not Found) and the user had **"Continue on error (using error output)"** enabled, the node would mutate the original item but fail to push it to the `returnData` array. This resulted in the node outputting an empty array, causing the workflow to silently succeed and stop, completely bypassing the intended Error Path.

### 🛠️ The Fix

Updated the `catch` block in `packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/Drive/v2/actions/router.ts`. 
Instead of mutating `items[i]`, the logic now safely creates a shallow copy of the item, appends the error message to the `json` property, and explicitly pushes it to the `returnData` array. This ensures the execution engine correctly routes the failed item to the error output branch.

---

### 🎥 Visual Proof
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a70e5aec-1304-479a-8f4d-b59a392b0914

### 🧪 How to Test

1. Add a **Google Drive** node and set it to **Download File**.
2. Enter a fake/invalid File ID (e.g., `invalid_file_id_12345`).
3. In the node settings, set **On Error** to `Continue (using error output)`.
4. Connect a NoOp node to the Error output branch.
5. Execute the workflow.

title: fix(core): Fix execution history when flow includes wait node
body:
## Summary

Re-applies the fix from #23146 (which was reverted in #25610 due to PostgreSQL timezone issues) with a corrected approach.

**Original bug:** When a workflow with a Wait node resumes, `setRunning()` overwrites the original `startedAt` timestamp with the current time, causing wrong execution duration and sort order in execution history.

**Why the original fix broke PostgreSQL:** PR #23146 used raw SQL `COALESCE(startedAt, :startedAt)` with `DateUtils.mixedDateToUtcDatetimeString()`, which produces timezone-ambiguous date strings. On PostgreSQL with `timestamptz` columns, these strings were interpreted using the session timezone instead of UTC, causing 1-hour offsets (or even negative durations) for non-UTC users.

**This fix:** Uses a transaction with standard TypeORM `findOneBy` + `update` methods instead of raw SQL. TypeORM handles date serialization correctly per database driver (SQLite and PostgreSQL), eliminating the timezone mismatch entirely.

### How to test

1. Create a workflow: Webhook → Wait (resume by webhook) → Edit Fields
2. Trigger the webhook to start execution
3. Execution enters "waiting" state — note the `startedAt` time
4. Resume the execution via the wait webhook
5. Verify `startedAt` remains unchanged (not overwritten with resume time)

Sample workflow is also provided in the [Linear ticket](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/CAT-1854/execution-history-incorrect-when-flow-includes-wait-node).

title: fix(HTTP Request Node): Fail on non-2xx status codes during pagination with "other" completion
body:
## Summary

When the HTTP Request node uses pagination with **"Pagination Complete When" set to "Other"**, non-2xx HTTP responses were silently accepted as valid data if the user's completion expression happened to evaluate to `true` on the error response. This caused the node to succeed instead of failing, even when "Never Error" was not enabled.

**Root cause:** The `continueExpression` for "other" pagination mode was solely based on the user's completion expression. When a non-2xx response satisfied that expression (e.g., `$response.statusCode === 404` returning `true`), pagination stopped normally without triggering the existing non-2xx error handling in `requestWithAuthenticationPaginated`.

**Fix:** The `continueExpression` now includes a non-2xx status check when `neverError` is `false`, ensuring the existing error path in the core pagination helper is always triggered for error responses. When `neverError` is `true`, the behavior is unchanged — non-2xx responses are returned as data.

**How to test:**
1. Create an HTTP Request node with pagination → "Pagination Complete When" = "Other"
2. Point it at an API that returns a non-2xx status during pagination
3. Without "Never Error": the node should fail with the HTTP error
4. With "Never Error": the node should return the response as data

body:
## Summary

When navigating to the Security & Policies settings page, the Personal Space sharing and publishing toggles would visually animate from OFF to ON, creating the impression that the user had changed settings.

**Root cause:** `useAsyncState` initializes `state` as `undefined`, so the computed getters (`personalSpaceSharing ?? false`, `personalSpacePublishing ?? false`) default to `false` before the API resolves. The `ElSwitch` would render as OFF, then animate to ON once data loaded. The existing `:loading` prop only shows a spinner — it doesn't suppress the transition animation.

**Fix:** Use `v-if="state !== undefined"` on the licensed switches so they don't render until data is available, with a disabled loading placeholder in the `v-else` branch. Also fixed the unlicensed fallback switches which were hardcoded to `false` instead of reflecting the actual setting value (relevant for instances that were licensed, had the feature enabled, then downgraded).

body:
## Summary

When executing a single node on the canvas where an upstream node previously errored, retrying shows "Node was not executed" instead of re-running the errored node.

**Root cause:** The `isDirty()` function in `find-start-nodes.ts` had an unimplemented error check (`// TODO: implement` with `const hasAnError = false`). **Fix:** Implement the error check — nodes whose run data contains errors are now marked as dirty, so they are re-executed on retry instead of being skipped.

title: fix(AI Agent Node): Extract tool name correctly for MCP tool calls
body:
Fix Gemini looping when using MCP Client tools in an AI Agent workflow.

  When the MCP Client node (a toolkit) exposes sub-tools, `createEngineRequests` correctly stores the actual MCP tool name (e.g., `list_tickets`) in
  `action.input.tool`. However, `resolveToolName` in `buildSteps.ts` was ignoring this and returning `nodeNameToToolName("MCP Client")` → `"MCP_Client"`
   instead.

  This wrong name was embedded in the `AIMessage` that forms the `{agent_scratchpad}` on every subsequent agent turn. Gemini validates function call
  names against its registered function declarations strictly. On the next turn it would attempt to call `"MCP_Client"` — a name not registered as a
  tool — causing `createEngineRequests` to return an empty actions array. With no tools to execute, the agent was immediately reinvoked with the same
  context, generating the same invalid tool call again. This repeated until the 10-iteration limit was hit.

  OpenAI/Azure OpenAI are more lenient about tool name mismatches in history, which is why they worked fine.

  **Fix:** `resolveToolName` now checks `action.input.tool` (the original MCP sub-tool name stored by `createEngineRequests` for toolkit tools) before
  falling back to the node name. Precedence:
  1. HITL tool name (unchanged)
  2. `input.tool` — the actual registered tool name for toolkit tools (new)
  3. `nodeNameToToolName(nodeName)` — fallback for standalone tools

title: fix(core): Resolve $().item expressions in partial executions
body:
## Summary

When using `$('NodeName').item` in the expression editor after a partial execution, the expression would fail with *"Can't get data for expression"* even though the referenced node had been executed successfully.

**Root cause:** `.item` uses paired item resolution which requires `connectionInputData` (the active node's input) to trace items back through the chain. In a partial execution where the active node hasn't run, `connectionInputData` is empty — even though the referenced node's data is available in `runData`.

**Fix:** When `connectionInputData` is empty and no pinned data exists, fall back to reading directly from the referenced node's `runData`. This matches what `first()`/`last()`/`all()` already do. The fallback only activates in the UI preview path — during real execution, `connectionInputData` is always populated before expressions are evaluated.

title: perf(core): Optimize execution deletions for throughput
body:
## Summary

When saving successful or failed executions is disabled, for each completed execution we do a synchronous hard-delete on the hot path, which at high throughput becomes a bottleneck, plus adds dead tuple churn and so vacuum pressure.

This PR adds `ExecutionPersistence.deleteUnsaved` so that, when pruning is enabled, we soft-delete each production execution with a backdated `deletedAt` (bypassing the grace period meant for manual executions) so the execution is immediately eligible for the next pruning hard-delete batch. When pruning is disabled, we fall back to immediate hard-delete so executions do not accumulate indefinitely.

body:
## Summary

In multi-main queue mode with `N8N_MINIMIZE_EXECUTION_DATA_FETCHING` enabled, evaluation test runs were failing because the worker returned lightweight job result summaries instead of full execution data. The evaluation test runner needs complete execution data (including `runData`) to compare outputs and compute metrics.

This PR introduces a `forceFullExecutionData` property on `IWorkflowExecutionDataProcess` that, when set to `true`, forces the main process to fetch full execution data from the DB regardless of the `N8N_MINIMIZE_EXECUTION_DATA_FETCHING` environment variable. Both `runTestCase` and `runDatasetTrigger` in the test runner service now set this flag.

### How to test
1. Enable queue mode with `N8N_MINIMIZE_EXECUTION_DATA_FETCHING=true`
2. Run an evaluation test suite

**Before:** Test data was automatically pinned to nodes after workflow generation, hiding validation issues and confusing users with "pin data" jargon.

**After:** Users see a "Follow-ups" section with clear actions:
- **Execute with mock data** — pins deferred test data and executes the workflow
- **Execute with my configured data** — disabled until credentials are configured
- After execution: **Unpin test data** and **Execute and refine** follow-ups appear

### Key changes

- **Deferred pin data** — Pin data from AI generation is stored but not applied until user explicitly chooses (`builder.store.ts`, `useWorkflowUpdate.ts`)
- **Follow-up actions UI** — Pre-execution and post-execution follow-up sections in `ExecuteMessage.vue`
- **Shared `QuickReplyType`** — Typed enum in `@n8n/api-types` used across FE/BE for quick reply actions
- **Store-only quick reply** — Backend stores "Execute with mock data" message in session history without triggering AI generation (`session-manager.service.ts`, `ai-workflow-builder-agent.service.ts`)
- **Silent test data re-executions** — Successful re-executions with test data skip sending to AI to avoid confusing responses
- **`useExecutionWatcher` composable** — Extracted shared one-shot execution watcher
- **`markStateDirty` on pin data apply** — Ensures pin data is saved to DB before execution (fixes webhook registration failures)

### Feature flag

All changes are gated by the existing `code-pin-data` PostHog experiment variant. Users not in this variant see no behavior changes.

### Known limitations (future work)

- Backend prompt changes to tailor AI responses to mock data context
- "Pinning mock data to nodes" thinking group progress indicator
- `showExecuteMessage` doesn't render after page reload (pre-existing issue)

When workflow settings (like `errorWorkflow`) were updated via the [WorkflowSettings](cci:2://file:///d:/dist/n8n/packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/Interface.ts:418:0-428:1) modal, the backend and the `workflowDocumentStore` were updated correctly. title: Fix/data table routing 404
body:
### **What this PR does:**
This PR fixes a routing bug that causes a 404 error when users attempt to create a new Data Table from a workflow opened via the main Overview page.

**The Problem:**
When a workflow is opened or created from the "Overview" page, the route does not contain the `?projectId=` query parameter. Because `ResourceLocator.vue` previously relied solely on `projectsStore.currentProjectId` (which hydrates from the route) to build the `allowNewResource` URL, it resulted in a malformed URL with an empty ID (`/projects//datatables/new`).

**The Solution:**
Updated the URL replacement logic in `ResourceLocator.vue` to include a robust fallback chain. If `projectsStore.currentProjectId` is undefined, it now gracefully falls back to the workflow's state: `workflowsStore.workflow?.homeProject?.id` or `projectsStore.personalProject?.id`.

### **How to test this PR:**
1. Start on the main **Home / Overview** page.
2. Perform a hard refresh to clear any existing Pinia state.
3. Open an existing workflow directly from the Overview list (do not navigate through the 'Projects' tab).
4. Add an **n8n Data Tables** node and set the operation to **Insert row**.
5. Click the **"Create new data table"** link.
6. *Expected Result:* You are successfully redirected to `/projects/{projectId}/datatables/new` instead of a 404 page.
