## Summary

When using Currents orchestration (pwc-p), rerunning a single failed machine (e.g., clicking "Rerun failed jobs" on machine 7) causes all tests to be rerun instead of just the tests that failed on that machine.

Root cause: With orchestration, tests are dynamically assigned by Currents rather than deterministically sharded. When a single machine restarts, Currents treats it as part of a new orchestration run.

Revert PRs [#22747](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/22747) and [#23139](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/23139) to restore deterministic sharding behavior until orchestration rerun logic is properly fixed.

title: fix(Chat Trigger Node): Fix file upload with streaming in public chat
body:
## Summary
Fixes file uploads failing with "Failed to parse request body" error when streaming is enabled in public/hosted chat mode. The hosted chat template was setting `Content-Type: application/json` in webhookConfig headers, which overwrote the browser's automatic `multipart/form-data` Content-Type when uploading files via FormData.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d43d3fe-e828-41cb-bd04-4cb6a2dcb0b1


## Changes

- Remove hardcoded `Content-Type: application/json` from hosted chat webhookConfig in `templates.ts`
- Strip Content-Type header in `sendWithFiles` when sending FormData, allowing the browser to set the correct multipart boundary
- Add regression test to verify Content-Type is excluded for file uploads while preserving other custom headers

## Testing

- Added unit test that sets Content-Type in webhookConfig, uploads a file, and verifies Content-Type is stripped from the request
- Manually tested file upload with streaming enabled in hosted chat mode

title: fix(API): Fixes how toJsonSchema creates dependant allOf checks when multiple fields depend on same field
body:
## Summary
Fixed Public API credential creation failing for credentials with conditional field requirements (e.g., JWT Auth).

## Problem
Creating JWT Auth credentials via Public API failed with schema validation errors because the `toJsonSchema` function incorrectly grouped all properties depending on the same field into a single conditional, regardless of their specific trigger values.

**Example:** When `keyType: 'pemKey'`, it incorrectly required `secret`, `privateKey`, AND `publicKey` instead of just `privateKey` and `publicKey`.

## Solution
Changed the dependency key from just the field name to `fieldName:value` combination to create separate conditionals for each unique field+value pair.

## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.

This PR adds expression resolution support for credential resolver configurations in the dynamic credentials system. It allows users to use n8n expressions (like $execution.id, $vars.*, $secrets.*) within credential resolver configs.

 ### Key Changes

New **ResolverConfigExpressionService** (packages/cli/src/modules/dynamic-credentials.ee/services/resolver-config-expression.service.ts)
  - Handles resolving expressions in resolver configs at runtime and validation time
  - Supports $execution, $vars, and $secrets expressions

Type-safe resolver configuration
  - Changed CredentialResolverConfiguration from Record<string, unknown> to INodeParameters for proper type checking when executing expression resolutions
  - Added isNodeParameters type guard in packages/workflow for validating config format

Updated credential resolution flow
  - resolveIfNeeded now receives additionalData, mode, and canUseExternalSecrets instead of separate executionContext and workflowSettings
  - This provides full context needed for expression resolution

title: fix(editor): Fix missing closing parenthesis in Google Auth button CSS url()
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a CSS syntax error in the Google Auth button component where the closing parenthesis was missing from all `url()` function calls. This bug caused the "Sign in with Google" button to be invisible until the user hovered over it.
**What was wrong:**
- The CSS `url()` functions were missing closing parentheses in all four background image CSS variables
- This caused the background images to fail loading in the normal state
- The button only appeared on hover because some browsers attempted to render the `:hover` state image
**What changed:**
- Added missing closing parentheses `)` to all four `url()` function calls in the `googleAuthButtons` object
**Before:**
'--google-auth-btn--color--background--normal': `url(${baseUrl}static/google-auth/normal${type}`
After:
'--google-auth-btn--color--background--normal': `url(${baseUrl}static/google-auth/normal${type})`
Testing:
- ✅ ESLint passes
- ✅ The Google Auth button now displays correctly on page load
- ✅ All button states (normal, focus, pressed, disabled) work as expected

title: refactor(ai-builder): Improve pairwise evaluation architecture and LangSmith integration (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Refactors the pairwise evaluation system to improve code readability and fix LangSmith trace visibility issues. The original 965-line monolithic `pairwise-runner.ts` has been decomposed into focused,
single-responsibility modules under a new `evaluations/pairwise/` directory. Additionally, this PR fixes a critical issue where nested LLM runs (generations and judge evaluations) were not appearing in
the LangSmith dashboard due to incorrect traceable wrapper placement.

## Changes

### LangSmith Trace Visibility Fixes

Nested traceable calls within LangSmith's evaluator context were either causing 403 errors or not appearing in the trace hierarchy. The solution involved:

- Moving all LLM work (workflow generation + judge evaluations) into the target function rather than the evaluator
- Wrapping each generation and judge call with `traceable()` to ensure proper parent-child relationships in traces
- Pre-computing all metrics in the target and passing them as feedback, so the evaluator simply extracts and returns them
- Adding `experiment_name` and `evaluating_generation` metadata to traces for better filtering and debugging

### Code Organization

Reorganized from a single large file into `evaluations/pairwise/` with clear module boundaries:

- `runner.ts` - High-level orchestration for both local and LangSmith modes
- `generator.ts` - Workflow generation, creates the LangSmith target function
- `judge-chain.ts` - Single LLM judge implementation
- `judge-panel.ts` - Multi-judge execution and majority vote aggregation
- `metrics-builder.ts` - Constructs LangSmith-compatible metrics
- `types.ts` - Type definitions and guards

### Code Quality Improvements

- Extract magic strings and defaults into `constants.ts`
- Refactor `createAgent()` and others to use options object pattern
- Add input validation and defensive checks
- Remove duplicate `EvalCriteria` type definition
- Replace scattered `console.log` calls with logger utility

### New Functionality

- `N8N_EVALS_DISABLED_NODES` env var to exclude specific node types during evaluation

title: feat(core): expand tilde (~) to default allowed directory in file paths
body:
## Problem

Currently, when using file operation nodes (Read/Write Files from Disk, Read Binary File, etc.), users must specify the full path to files in the allowed directory. The default allowed directory is `~/.n8n-files`, which is a non-trivial path that users need to remember and type for every file operation.

For example, to write a file, users must specify:
- `~/.n8n-files/myfile.txt` (full path)
- Or `/home/user/.n8n-files/myfile.txt` (absolute path)

This creates a major inconvenience for file operations, as users cannot use the simpler `~/myfile.txt` syntax that would be more intuitive.

## Solution

This PR modifies the `resolvePath` function to expand `~` to the default allowed directory (`~/.n8n-files`) or the first configured allowed path if `N8N_RESTRICT_FILE_ACCESS_TO` is set.

Now users can use:
- `~/myfile.txt` → resolves to `~/.n8n-files/myfile.txt`
- `~` → resolves to `~/.n8n-files` directory

## Changes

1. **Core change**: Modified `resolvePath()` in `file-system-helper-functions.ts` to expand `~` before path resolution
2. **Documentation**: Updated node descriptions for all file operation nodes to document the `~` expansion behavior:
   - Read/Write Files from Disk
   - Read Binary File
   - Write Binary File
   - Read Binary Files

## Behavior

- If `N8N_RESTRICT_FILE_ACCESS_TO` is configured, `~` expands to the first allowed path
- If restrictions are disabled (empty string), `~` still expands to `~/.n8n-files`
- Backward compatible: Previously `~` didn't work correctly, so this fixes and improves the behavior

## Testing

- `~/test.txt` should resolve to `~/.n8n-files/test.txt`
- `~` should resolve to `~/.n8n-files` directory
- Works with configured allowed paths via `N8N_RESTRICT_FILE_ACCESS_TO`

body:
## Summary

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/71310cc2-dca0-4efa-bcc5-f0e31e5bcad4


<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

## Flow Diagrams

New User Message Flow:

1. User types message
2. Frontend saves workflow → gets versionId
3. Frontend sends message to /ai/build with versionId in payload
4. Backend stores versionId in message metadata (additional_kwargs)
5. AI processes and responds
6. (No version save after response - already saved before)

Session Loading Flow:

1. Frontend calls /ai/sessions to get messages
2. Extract versionIds from messages with additional_kwargs.versionId
3. Call POST /workflow-history/workflow/:id/versions with versionIds
4. Backend returns only existing versions
5. Frontend filters out messages referencing non-existent versions
6. Display version cards only for existing versions

Restore Flow:

1. User clicks restore on version card (version card is derived from user message with versionId)
2. Show RestoreVersionConfirm dialog
3. On confirm:
   a. restore workflow version using workflow history feature
   b. Backend finds user message with this messageId in metadata, removes that message AND all messages after it
   c. Frontend truncates local messages similarly

body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

This PR solves this problem:
- In multi main setup, when an instance changes external secret configuration (add, changes, delete a provider), it saves it to the db and pushes a pubsub event
- other instance listen to this event, but reload only the provider that were already in cache
- this means that all new providers were not reloaded at added to the provider cache of leader instances

The solution:
- on pubsub event listener, reloads settings from the db
- reload new and existing providers configuration
- disconnect and remove old providers from cache

title: fix(core): Resolve file path correctly when serving node icons from N8N_CUSTOM_EXTENSIONS
body:
## Summary - [Fixes NODE-3843](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/NODE-3843/community-issue-bug-custom-node-icon-path-includes-absolute-container) 

Fix node icons not loading when using "N8N_CUSTOM_EXTENSIONS" to load custom nodes from directories other than "/home/node/.n8n/custom".

```bash
# Test docker image with PR fixes
docker pull ghcr.io/n8n-io/n8n:branch-resolve-filePath-correctly-when-serving-node-icons
# For amd64 architectures
docker pull --platform linux/amd64 ghcr.io/n8n-io/n8n:branch-resolve-filePath-correctly-when-serving-node-icons
````

### Related Github Issues

* [Bug: Custom Node icon path includes absolute container path (/icons/CUSTOM//home/… Icon Not Loading/Broken #21360](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/21360)
* [When placing custom nodes into the ~/.n8n/custom folder, the node icon cannot be displayed. #22452](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/22452)
## Icon Resolution for Custom Nodes

### Context

Resolves the node icon file path when loaded from `/icons/${packageName}/${iconPath}`.

### Problem

Using `N8N_CUSTOM_EXTENSIONS`, nodes can be loaded from any directory outside of `CWD='$N8N_USER_FOLDER/.n8n/'`.

Custom nodes are loaded by `custom-directory-loader.ts` using an absolute path, different from the default `package-directory-loader.ts`. The icon loading logic for custom nodes seems a bit broken, because icons are resolved by absolute paths encoded in URLs.

**Examples when served from `/icons/${packageName}/${iconPath}`:**
- `/icons/CUSTOM//home/node/.n8n-custom`
- `/icons/CUSTOM/C:/User/name/.n8n-custom`

### Implementation

`resolveIcon()` has a special `path.resolve()` strategy for custom nodes considering:
- An absolute Linux file path is encoded in the URL using `//`
- `//` in URLs can be normalized to `/` by proxies, load balancers, etc.
- A Windows file path starts with drive letters like `C:` not `/`

### Future Improvements

> [!NOTE]
> Instead of fixing the broken custom node loading strategy in `resolveIcon()`, make `custom-directory-loader.ts` also use relative paths. Besides having different icon loading strategies, encoding an absolute path in URLs seems a security risk.

title: fix: Fix checksum hashing when WebCrypto is unavailable
body:
## Summary

We've been experiencing problems with calling WebCrypto `crypto.subtle` in insecure contexts (http). To make sure the fix is a proper one, I moved all `calculateWorkflowChecksum` calls to the server, as we need to update it anyway when the data is updated, so it makes sense to not call it on the client. At the same time, I updated the function to fall back to a pure-JS SHA-256 when WebCrypto is unavailable.

To test this:
1. Start the app locally (HTTP).
`N8N_SECURE_COOKIE=false pnpm dev`
2. Find your LAN IP (e.g. `ifconfig | grep "inet " | grep -v 127.0.0.1`).
3. Open `http://<LAN_IP>:<port>` (e.g. `http://192.168.1.23:5678`)
4. See no error anymore

Describe what the PR does and how to test.

This PR adds the possibility to create / edit credential resolvers. To do that, users have to open the workflow settings, and they will see a new "Credential Resolver" setting, for them to pick a resolver.   - Two tabs: Configuration and Details

- WorkflowSettings integration
  - Dropdown to select resolver for workflow
  - "New" button to create resolvers
  - "Edit" button when resolver selected
- Handles deletion: reloads list and resets selection if needed
- Default value is empty string ("") for no selection

### Technical notes

title: feat(core): Make n8n workflows on Chat require streaming response mode (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Chat will initially ship with just `streaming`  response mode support, and before we've been forcing the workflows to be run in this response mode, which has led to some confusion.

Instead of forcing the response mode to `streaming` make the `streaming` mode a requirement, making it so that the agent can't be used on Chat unless the correct streaming mode is selected.

To not make this clunky to use make it so that if the `availableInChat` toggle is enabled the available Response Mode options change to only `streaming`, and the default changes. Since `availableInChat` is a new field in 1.4 version of the node this shouldn't cause regressions, as the field is default: false.

Also make it possible to have `streaming` response mode in non public workflows, and improve Chat error handling on 400 errors, displaying the error text on the error toast.

title: feat(Google Vertex Node): Add Application Default Credentials (ADC) authentication support
body:
## Summary

This PR adds Application Default Credentials (ADC) authentication support for Google Vertex AI nodes, enabling seamless authentication when running n8n in Google Cloud environments (GKE, Cloud Run, Compute Engine) or when using the `gcloud` CLI locally.

### Changes:
- Add new `googleApiAdcApi` credential type for ADC authentication
- Add authentication selector to both **Google Vertex Chat Model** and **Embeddings Google Vertex** nodes
- Support project ID configuration via:
  - Node parameter override
  - Credential configuration
  - Auto-detection from ADC environment
- Extract shared Google Cloud regions to a reusable module (`packages/nodes-base/credentials/common/google/regions.ts`)
- Add comprehensive unit tests for both authentication methods
- Add documentation for ADC setup and usage

### How to Test:
1. Create a new Google Vertex Chat Model or Embeddings Google Vertex node
2. Select "Application Default Credentials (ADC)" as the authentication method
3. Configure the ADC credential (optionally specify region and project ID)
4. If running locally, ensure you've run `gcloud auth application-default login`
5. If running in GCP, the node should automatically use the attached service account

**Before:**
Only Service Account JSON key authentication was supported

**After:**
Users can choose between Service Account or ADC authentication

title: feat: Add AWS CLI profile authentication support
body: - Add authentication type selector to AWS credentials (Access Keys vs Profile) - Support AWS CLI profile names (default and custom profiles) - Use native AWS SDK fromNodeProviderChain for credential resolution - Maintain full backwards compatibility with existing access key auth - Available for Bedrock and all AWS nodes in N8N ## Summary This PR adds support for authenticating with AWS using AWS CLI profiles (from `~/.aws/credentials` and `~/.aws/config`), in addition to the existing access key authentication. ### Why This Change? - **More secure for local development**: No need to copy/paste access keys into n8n - **Follows AWS best practices**: AWS recommends using profiles and temporary credentials - **Supports all AWS credential types**: IAM users, IAM roles, SSO, temporary credentials, etc. - **Easier for users**: Users who already have AWS CLI configured can immediately use n8n without additional setup - **Better for teams**: Team members can use their individual AWS profiles without sharing credentials ### Changes Made 1. **AWS Credentials (`Aws.credentials.ts`)**: Added "Authentication Type" selector with Access Keys (default) and AWS Profile options 2. **Types (`types.ts`)**: Extended `AwsIamCredentialsType` with `authenticationType` and `awsProfile` fields 3. **Bedrock Node (`LmChatAwsBedrock.node.ts`)**: Updated to handle profile-based authentication 4. **Dependencies**: Added `@aws-sdk/credential-providers` to both `nodes-base` and `nodes-langchain` packages ### How to Use 1. Go to **Settings** → **Credentials** → **Add Credential** → **AWS (IAM)** 2. Select **Authentication Type** → **AWS Profile** 3. Enter your AWS profile name (e.g., "default" or custom profile) 4. Select your AWS region 5. Use with any AWS node (Bedrock, S3, Lambda, etc.) ### Backwards Compatibility ✅ 100% backwards compatible - existing credentials continue to work unchanged (default type: "Access Keys") ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts Related to #21568 - This PR adds AWS CLI profile authentication support, addressing part of the request for better AWS credential chain support. ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. body: ## Summary ## 🐛 Bug Fix: Manually Defining Array Fields in Edit Fields Node This PR addresses a bug where users could not correctly define an **Array** type field within the **Edit Fields** node using string input. fixes: #22586 --- ### 📝 Bug Description When a user defined a field as type `Array` in the **Edit Fields** node and provided a list of values in any of the below fashion user use to get error as code was not able to parse it correctly * apples,bananas,pears * "apples","bananas","pears" * apples, bananas, pears * [apples, bananas, pears] **Affected n8n version:** 1.121.3 (and potentially earlier versions) ### 🚀 Solution This fix introduces logic to correctly detect when the chosen field type is `Array` and attempts to parse the input string into a structured array. It now successfully handles various common array string formats, including: * Simple comma-separated values (e.g., `apples, bananas, pears`) * Quoted comma-separated values (e.g., `"apples", "bananas", "pears"`) * Bracketed array notation (e.g., `[apples, bananas, pears]` or `["apples", "bananas", "pears"]`) The output is now consistently a proper JSON array, making the manual array definition functional as intended. --- ### 🧪 Steps to Verify (How to Test) 1. Start a new workflow and add an **Edit Fields (Set)** node. 2. In the "Mode" section, keep **Manual Mapping (default)**. 3. Configure the new field, (click add field): * **Field Name:** `fruits` * **Field Type (from dropdown):** `Array` * **Value:** Enter a comma-separated list, e.g., `apples, bananas, pears` 4. Run the workflow. 5. Inspect the output data from the **Edit Fields** node. **✅ Expected Result:** The output should contain the field `fruits` as a proper array structure: ```json { "fruits": [ "apples", "bananas", "pears" ] } ``` few of the working screen-shot are below ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. title: fix(core): Update migration that activate workflows with executeWorkflowTrigger
body:
## Summary

Fixes the `ActivateExecuteWorkflowTriggerWorkflows` migration to properly handle all valid Execute Workflow Trigger configurations, including:
- Version 1 nodes with empty parameters
- Version 1.1 nodes with missing `type` fields in workflowInputs (which default to "string")

## Root cause

The migration logic was too strict in validating Execute Workflow Trigger nodes:

1. **Version 1 nodes**: These nodes have no `inputSource` parameter and use empty `parameters: {}`. The migration was not recognizing empty parameters as valid, failing to activate workflows with v1 Execute Workflow Trigger nodes.

2. **Version 1.1 nodes with missing types**: The Execute Workflow Trigger v1.1 has a default type of "string" for workflow inputs. When users don't explicitly set a type, it's not included in the JSON. The migration's `hasValidWorkflowInputs()` validation required the `type` field to exist, incorrectly rejecting valid configurations.

## Changes

### Migration ([1763048000000-ActivateExecuteWorkflowTriggerWorkflows.ts](packages/@n8n/db/src/migrations/common/1763048000000-ActivateExecuteWorkflowTriggerWorkflows.ts))

1. **Version 1 support** (lines 99-102): Added check for empty or missing parameters object. If `!params || Object.keys(params).length === 0`, the workflow is considered valid and will be activated.

2. **Version 1.1 missing type support** (lines 195-196): Updated `hasValidWorkflowInputs()` to treat missing `type` field as valid:
   ```typescript
   // type is optional (defaults to 'string' in version 1.1)
   (!('type' in value) || (typeof value.type === 'string' && value.type.length > 0))

title: fix: Remove SystemCredentials source check during AWS role assume
body:
## Summary

This removes the 'source === "environment"' check done during the role assume for AWS SystemCredentials.

In every case of the SystemCredentials usage for AWS, it is supposed to assume the role required during credential setup (with the given externalId as well). The previous conditional would only do that assume if it was via environment. This left out the (recently added) pod, container, and instance sources, and those would return the system credentials instead (unintended, I think, and a **potential security risk**). These sources should act the same way.

I added a test using one of the other sources, and red-green tested. I've also tested this "in practice" along with my other PR (#22316) in our environment.

## Summary

```
SystemError [ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR]: A system error occurred: uv_os_homedir returned ENOENT (no such file or directory)

title: fix(cli): register webhooks when activating workflow via REST API
body:
## Summary

When activating a workflow via REST API (POST /rest/workflows/{id}/activate), webhooks are not being registered because `shouldAddWebhooks()` in `ActiveWorkflowManager` only returns `true` for `init` and `leadershipChange` activation modes, not for `activate`.

## Fix

Added `activate` to the list of activation modes that trigger webhook registration in `shouldAddWebhooks()` method.

**Before:**
```typescript
if (['init', 'leadershipChange'].includes(activationMode)) return true;
```

**After:**
```typescript
if (['init', 'leadershipChange', 'activate'].includes(activationMode)) return true;
```

## Testing

Tested manually on a development build:
1. Created a workflow with a webhook node
2. Activated it via REST API: `POST /rest/workflows/{id}/activate`
3. Verified the webhook responds with 200 OK and "Workflow was started"

Fixes #21614

title: fix(editor): Bind color-scheme to app theme setting
body:
## Summary
Fixes `light-dark()` CSS function resolving based on OS preference instead of n8n's theme setting.

**Problem**
When a user sets n8n to "light" theme while their OS is in dark mode (or vice versa), canvas elements using `light-dark()` would display with the wrong colors because `color-scheme: light dark` on `:root` defers to OS preference.

**Solution**
Bind `color-scheme` explicitly to the `data-theme` attribute on `body`, so `light-dark()` always resolves to match the app's actual theme.

title: feat: Allow running Playwright e2e tests using Vite dev server (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

This pull request enhances the Playwright end-to-end testing setup to support running tests against separate backend and frontend servers, improving flexibility for local development and CI environments. The changes introduce new environment variables, update test fixtures and configuration, and improve documentation to clarify usage. The most important changes are:

**Support for Separate Backend and Frontend URLs:**

- Added support for `N8N_BASE_URL` (backend) and `N8N_EDITOR_URL` (frontend) environment variables, allowing tests to target different URLs for API calls and browser navigation. This enables workflows where the backend and frontend run on different ports or servers. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e5aaab3c5c13c70972ee90cc2fcd798b1c4068f0f8c51d13d03bd172300d8ea7R16-R71) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-65e68182f93e2b59bebff120b20fc48d71a7faae92ca25835955272906a81701R8-R24)

- Updated test fixtures (`base.ts`) to provide `backendUrl` and `frontendUrl` to tests, ensuring API requests and browser navigation go to the correct endpoints. The `n8nPage` class now receives an API helper instance that uses the backend URL. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d7ca8512459a7d82e638d2cf6c092fecd9e1e20e25ac6fcd1f44a72a3ac7a514R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d7ca8512459a7d82e638d2cf6c092fecd9e1e20e25ac6fcd1f44a72a3ac7a514R26-R27) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d7ca8512459a7d82e638d2cf6c092fecd9e1e20e25ac6fcd1f44a72a3ac7a514L93-R99) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-d7ca8512459a7d82e638d2cf6c092fecd9e1e20e25ac6fcd1f44a72a3ac7a514R126-R151) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-d7ca8512459a7d82e638d2cf6c092fecd9e1e20e25ac6fcd1f44a72a3ac7a514L141-R166) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-d7ca8512459a7d82e638d2cf6c092fecd9e1e20e25ac6fcd1f44a72a3ac7a514L152-R198) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-d7ca8512459a7d82e638d2cf6c092fecd9e1e20e25ac6fcd1f44a72a3ac7a514L188-R217) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-aef4ce1281e9d08fd3dd293e59b117256e6cda894f9ac9fb1356329311b88d34L123-R125)

**Configuration and Command Updates:**

- Modified Playwright configuration and project setup to use the new URL helpers, ensuring the correct URLs are used for web server startup and test execution. Added a new `dev` script for local development with separate backend/frontend, and a `dev:fe:e2e` script for frontend-only e2e development. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b4fa4d93cdd8f7fdd4e3234a206d26484c68ea593284f449dc3015cd767f0604L10-R13) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b4fa4d93cdd8f7fdd4e3234a206d26484c68ea593284f449dc3015cd767f0604R40-R44) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b4fa4d93cdd8f7fdd4e3234a206d26484c68ea593284f449dc3015cd767f0604L51-R66) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-aef2c13acdeca77c6adbad9648e66222dcc3c0668d88be8943028afeff3d60d6R4-R5) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-aef2c13acdeca77c6adbad9648e66222dcc3c0668d88be8943028afeff3d60d6L34-R36) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-aef2c13acdeca77c6adbad9648e66222dcc3c0668d88be8943028afeff3d60d6L46-R55) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-c31bf53740e93c047301d7add64686430a3bd7bf41efd5307fd9536313002cddR5-R8) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-7ae45ad102eab3b6d7e7896acd08c427a9b25b346470d7bc6507b6481575d519R24)

title: fix(editor): Don't create duplicate placeholder nodes on agent failure
body:
## Summary
Fixes an issue where AI Agent nodes appeared duplicated in the execution logs view when the agent execution finished with an error.

When the full AI Agent execution fails or doesn't complete, the agent node itself is NOT in the execution's `runData`, but its child nodes (LLM, tools, etc.) ARE present. Each child node independently tried to insert the parent AI Agent as a placeholder node, resulting in the agent appearing multiple times in the logs tree.

- Added deduplication logic in `createLogTreeRec` to track and filter duplicate placeholder entries (nodes without actual task data)
- Updated `mergeStartData` to better handle duplicate runs by checking for exact matches (same executionIndex AND startTime) to prevent duplicates from AI agent cases
- Added comprehensive test coverage for the duplication scenario

title: feat(core): Add resolvable fields to credential entity
body:
## Summary

This PR adds fields on the CredentialEntity to support dynamic credential resolution:
- **resolverId**: varchar foreign key (nullable) linking to a credential resolver
- **isResolvable**: boolean to determine whether to try and resolve the credentials at runtime
- **resolvableAllowFallback**: boolean to determine whether credentials should fallback to static credential data if the resolver fails

### Design Decisions

**TypeORM Relationship**: We intentionally omit the `@ManyToOne` decorator because the linked entity is defined in the dynamic credentials module. TypeORM treats `resolverId` as a regular text field while the database handles foreign key constraints. This approach is acceptable since we don't need to load `credential.resolver` via TypeORM—the credential module can independently query the resolver repository with the resolver ID.

**Field Independence**: `isResolvable` can be `true` even when `resolverId` is `null`. This handles cases where the resolver is configured at a higher level in the hierarchy (workflow/project/instance) rather than on the individual credential. This also allows customers to "disable" the resolving mechanism temporarily (e.g., for debugging) while keeping the resolver ID reference.

**Fallback Behavior**: `resolvableAllowFallback` only falls back to static credential data, not to alternative resolvers. The fallback path for credentials goes from the most specific resolver (on the credential) to the least specific (on the workflow, project, or instance). The last possible option is to allow fallback to the static credential data. This supports edge cases like LLM credentials where some users might not have personal credentials and can fall back to a company key.

### Migration Safety

The migration includes `transaction = false` for SQLite to prevent [data loss from SQLite foreign key quirk](https://n8nio.slack.com/archives/C035KBDA917/p1764321309535179?thread_ts=1764258843.340829&cid=C035KBDA917) when dropping foreign keys.

title: feat(ai-builder): Add multi-judge pairwise evals and local mode (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Adds a hierarchical scoring system with multi-judge consensus to the pairwise evaluation pipeline. The new approach uses multiple LLM judges per evaluation and aggregates results via majority vote, reducing variance from LLM non-determinism. Also introduces local evaluation mode for testing prompts without requiring a LangSmith setup.

## Changes

### Scoring System

Evaluation now uses a 3-level hierarchy:

1. Each criteria (do/don't rule) → binary pass/fail
2. Each judge aggregates criteria → `primaryPass` (true only if ALL pass) + `diagnosticScore` (passes/total)
3. Multiple judges aggregate via majority vote → final PASS/FAIL

Example with 3 judges evaluating 5 criteria each:
- Judge 1: 5/5 pass → `primaryPass=true`, `diagnosticScore=1.0`
- Judge 2: 4/5 pass → `primaryPass=false`, `diagnosticScore=0.8`
- Judge 3: 5/5 pass → `primaryPass=true`, `diagnosticScore=1.0`
- Result: 2/3 judges passed → PASS, avg diagnostic = 0.93

### Metrics Reported to LangSmith

| Metric | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `pairwise_primary` | 0 or 1 based on majority vote |
| `pairwise_diagnostic` | Average diagnostic score across judges (0-1) |
| `pairwise_judges_passed` | Count of judges with `primaryPass=true` |
| `pairwise_total_violations` | Sum of violations across all judges |
| `pairwise_total_passes` | Sum of passes across all judges |

### CLI Flags

Common flags (both modes):
| Flag | Description | Default |
|------|-------------|---------|
| `--judges <n>` | LLM judges per evaluation | 3 |
| `--verbose`, `-v` | Show judge details and timing | false |

LangSmith mode:
| Flag | Description | Default |
|------|-------------|---------|
| `--notion-id <id>` | Filter to single example by metadata | all |
| `--repetitions <n>` | Workflow generations per prompt | 1 |
| `--name <name>` | Custom experiment name | `pairwise-evals` |

Local mode (no LangSmith required):
| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--prompt <text>` | Prompt to generate workflow from |
| `--dos <rules>` | Newline-separated "do" rules |
| `--donts <rules>` | Newline-separated "don't" rules |

### Other Changes

- Move judge execution inside the generator for better parallelism with LangSmith's concurrent workflow generation
- Add `utils/logger.ts` for consistent colored output with verbose mode support

## Testing

```bash
# Local evaluation with 5 judges
pnpm eval:pairwise --prompt "Create a Slack workflow" --dos "Use Slack node" --judges 5 --verbose

# Single dataset example
pnpm eval:pairwise --notion-id <id> --judges 5 --verbose

# Full dataset
pnpm eval:pairwise --repetitions 3 --judges 3
```

title: fix(editor-ui): correctly parse cURL content-type with parameters (#22699)
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes an issue where importing a cURL command with a `Content-Type` header containing parameters (e.g., `application/json; charset=UTF-8`) resulted in incorrect parsing of the body.

Previously, the import logic used a strict equality check against supported content types. This caused headers like `application/json; charset=UTF-8` to be treated as unknown/raw, leading to the body being parsed incorrectly (specifically, it would incorrectly use the first key of the JSON object as the body content).

The fix involves stripping any parameters (everything after `;`) from the `Content-Type` header before validating it against the supported types.

**How to test:**

1. Open a new HTTP node.
2. Click on "Import cURL".
3. Paste the following command:
   ```bash
   curl --request POST \
     --url https://example.com/api \
     --header 'content-type: application/json; charset=UTF-8' \
     --data '{"userId":"123","active":false,"visited":false}'
   ```
4. Verify that the Body Parameters are correctly parsed as JSON key-value pairs (`userId`, `active`, `visited`) instead of the body being set to just `"userId"`.

## Summary
Moves to use `process.constrainedMemory` instead of `os.totalmem()` for determinig total available memory. title: fix(core): Prevent execution data from being overwritten on manual workflow resume
body:
## Summary

Fixes issue where manual workflow executions would lose trigger outputs (e.g., from form triggers) when resumed after waiting for webhook/form submission.

**Root cause:** Execution data initialization logic in `WorkflowRunner.run()` ran unconditionally for every manual execution in queue mode. When a workflow resumed after waiting, this would overwrite the existing execution data that contained the trigger outputs.

**Solution:** Move queue mode offloading logic from `WorkflowRunner` to `WorkflowExecutionService` to ensure execution data is initialized only once at workflow start, not when resuming from a wait state.

This issue was introduced with this refactor: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/22219

title: chore(ai-builder): Add workflow naming, compaction, and session cleanup to multi-agent  (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

This PR is a follow-up to the multi-agent architecture refactor, bringing several nice-to-have features from the legacy single-agent implementation (`workflow-builder-agent.ts`) to the new multi-agent architecture (`multi-agent-workflow-subgraphs.ts`).
Key additions include automatic workflow naming from the first user message, conversation compaction via `/compact` and `/clear` commands, and auto-compaction when context exceeds token limits. The PR also adds comprehensive Switch node support and Structured Output Parser discovery improvements.

## Changes

### Workflow Naming & Session Management
- Auto-generate workflow name from first user message on empty. workflows
- Add `/compact` command to summarize conversation history while preserving context
- Add `/clear` command to start fresh conversation with cleaned state
- Implement auto-compaction when token threshold is exceeded (default 40K tokens)
- Add `previousSummary` state field for context preservation after compaction

### Switch Node & Structured Output Parser Improvements (Multi-Agent Regression Fixes)

In the legacy single-agent architecture, the agent could iteratively refine node configurations:
1. Add nodes → 2. Connect (possibly wrong IO config) → 3. Configure to fix IO → 4. Reconnect → 5. Pass

With the multi-agent architecture, builder and configurator subgraphs run more sequentially, so the builder needs to get input/output parameters right on the first shot. These additions give the builder better upfront knowledge:

**Switch Node:**
- Add Switch node guide and examples for the configurator
- Add switch node pattern documentation for builder subgraph (how to set up `rules.values[]` for correct output count)
- Include dynamic output detection for Switch nodes in discovery

**Structured Output Parser:**

After a change in #22213, which prevents credentials from being saved if there are missing required fields, MCP OAuth2 credentials broke. ---

> [!WARNING]
> Some dependencies could not be looked up. Check the Dependency Dashboard for more information.

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2025-66414](https://redirect.github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/security/advisories/GHSA-w48q-cv73-mx4w)

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) TypeScript SDK does not enable DNS rebinding protection by default for HTTP-based servers. When an HTTP-based MCP server is run on localhost without authentication with `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` or `SSEServerTransport` and has not enabled `enableDnsRebindingProtection`, a malicious website could exploit DNS rebinding to bypass same-origin policy restrictions and send requests to the local MCP server. This could allow an attacker to invoke tools or access resources exposed by the MCP server on behalf of the user in those limited circumstances.

Note that running HTTP-based MCP servers locally without authentication is not recommended per MCP security best practices. This issue does not affect servers using stdio transport.

Servers created via `createMcpExpressApp()` now have this protection enabled by default when binding to localhost. Users with custom Express configurations are advised to update to version `1.24.0` and apply the exported `hostHeaderValidation()` middleware when running an unauthenticated server on localhost.

title: fix(core): Fix workflow statistics constraint
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

This PR modifies the workflow_statistics table to preserve statistics when workflows are deleted, instead of cascading deletes.

### The problem
Currently, the on delete cascade on the workflow statistics `workflowId` field means than when a workflow is deleted, the linked statistics are deleted too. This goes against the purpose of the statistics, which is to be an always increasing cumulative number (especially used for licensing quotas)

### Key Changes:

- Schema Changes:
  - Added auto-incrementing id as new primary key (required for nullable FK)
  - Removed FK constraint of workflow ID, to allow orphaned statistics linking to non existent workflow (deleted workflow).  This is to ease debugging the number (on top of having the workflow name)
  - Added workflowName column to add more readable information to the statistics, especially on workflow deletion
  - Changed count and rootCount from INT to BIGINT for large cumulative values
  - Added unique index on (workflowId, name)
- Tests Added/Updated:
  - Migration tests verifying behavior
  - Integration tests verifying workflowName population

title: fix(core): Make sub-workflows with waits return correct data to parents
body:
## Summary

Fixes parent workflows receiving incorrect data from child workflows that contain Wait nodes. Parents now receive data from the child's **last node** after the wait completes.

Also fixes a race condition where multiple child executions (in "run once for each item" mode) could resume the same parent execution multiple times.

## Related Linear Issues
- https://linear.app/n8n/issue/CAT-1801/subworkflow-doesnt-return-correct-data-after-waiting
- https://linear.app/n8n/issue/PAY-2720/community-issue-calling-a-sub-workflow-with-a-wait-by-webhook-node

## Related GitHub Issues
- https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/13135
- https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/15556

## Breaking Change

This is a **breaking change** for v2 release. The behavior changes from returning no data to returning data after the wait completes, which is the expected behavior but differs from historical functionality.

## Changes Made

### Core Fix
1. **New helper function** `updateParentExecutionWithChildResults()` in `workflow-helpers.ts`
   - Updates parent's `nodeExecutionStack[0].data` with child's final output
   - Applied in both execution paths: time-based waits (WaitTracker) and webhook-based waits (WebhookHelpers)

### Race Condition Fix
2. **Atomic status updates** in `ExecutionRepository.updateExistingExecution()`
   - Added optional `requireStatus` parameter
   - Uses WHERE clause: `WHERE id = ? AND status = ?` for atomic check-and-update
   - Returns boolean indicating success/failure

3. **Exception handling** for concurrent resume attempts
   - New `ExecutionAlreadyResumingError` exception
   - `ActiveExecutions.add()` throws when another process already resumed execution
   - `WaitTracker.startExecution()` catches and handles gracefully

## How It Works

**Before (Buggy Behavior)**:
1. Child hits Wait node → Parent received no data from the sub-execution
2. Child completes after wait → Parent again received no data from the sub-execution
3. Result: Parent gets wrong data (the input of the "Execute workflow" node)

**After (Fixed Behavior)**:
1. Child hits Wait node → Parent pauses
2. Child completes after wait → Updates parent's execution data in DB
3. Parent resumes → Execute Workflow node returns updated data

**Race Condition Prevention**:
- Multiple children try to resume parent → Only first succeeds (atomic DB update)
- Others get `ExecutionAlreadyResumingError` → Caught and handled
- Parent executes only once with correct data

**E2E Test (1)**:
- `packages/testing/playwright/tests/ui/subworkflow-wait.spec.ts`
  - Full flow with real workflows and webhook triggers
  - Verifies parent receives `'child - after'` not `'child - before'`

## Review Notes

- This fixes long-standing community issue with 30+ comments
- Promise.race semantics maintained (parent resumes on first child completion)
- Race condition in "run once for each item" mode is documented and acceptable
- No performance impact - single additional DB query per child completion

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2024-51999](https://redirect.github.com/expressjs/express/security/advisories/GHSA-pj86-cfqh-vqx6)

## Withdrawn Advisory
This advisory has been withdrawn because it describes a correctness bug, not a vulnerability with real security impact. This link is maintained to preserve external references.

## Original Description

### Impact

when using the extended query parser in express (`'query parser': 'extended'`), the `request.query` object inherits all object prototype properties, but these properties can be overwritten by query string parameter keys that match the property names

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> the extended query parser is the default in express 4; this was changed in express 5 which by default uses the simple query parser

### Patches

the issue has been patched to ensure `request.query` is a plain object so `request.query` no longer has object prototype properties. this brings the default behavior of extended query parsing in line with express's default simple query parser

### Workaround

this only impacts users using extended query parsing (`'query parser': 'extended'`), which is the default in express 4, but not express 5.  all users are encouraged to upgrade to the patched versions, but can otherwise work around this issue:

#### provide `qs` directly and specify `plainObjects: true`

```js
app.set('query parser',
  function (str) {
    return qs.parse(str, {
      plainObjects: true
  });
});
```

title: fix(core): During partial execution don't include loop as start node if the loop isn't closed
body:
## Summary

In partial executions, while searching for the start nodes, if we see a Loop node we check the output at index 0 (the `done` output). If there's no data, we treat the whole loop as needing to be re-run.

However, some Loop nodes don't actually represent a loop in the graph e.g., while a workflow is under development. In this case we want to check the `loop` output (index 1) to determine whether it should be included as a start node.

title: feat(ai-builder): Using templates to improve generation
body: ### Summary This PR addresses what we set out to test in ticket https://linear.app/n8n/issue/AI-1673 - we wanted to see what we could do to improve generation using templates. This work has proven to improve generation by 5-10% based on evaluation scores - I've also provided some concrete examples where the generation has proven to have some extra nuance that allows the workflows to actually function correctly. This PR also addresses: https://linear.app/n8n/issue/AI-1756/feature-add-template-ids-chosen-to-telemetry Adding telemetry around this new feature of the workflow builder. The templates are currently retrieved using just free text search from the templates API. We sort them by recency and relevancy to search. The workflow builder agent generally carries out 2-3 queries for templates, each returning a maximum of 5 templates (to avoid getting too irrelevant). This also only uses free templates. title: Security Hardening: Enhanced Access Controls and Resource Protection
body:
## Overview

This PR introduces three critical security hardening features designed to enhance enterprise security compliance and protect against resource exhaustion attacks. These features provide administrators with granular control over workflow and credential sharing, as well as schedule interval enforcement.

## Security Features

### 1. Workflow Sharing Control (`N8N_DISABLE_WORKFLOW_SHARING`)

**Purpose**: Allows organizations to disable workflow sharing and transfer functionality to meet enterprise security compliance requirements.

**Implementation**:
- Added `disableSharing` property to `WorkflowsConfig` (default: `false`)
- Integrated sharing checks in workflow share and transfer endpoints (`/workflows/:id/share` and `/workflows/:id/transfer`)
- Returns `400 Bad Request` with clear error messages when sharing is disabled

**Usage**:
```bash
N8N_DISABLE_WORKFLOW_SHARING=true
```

### 2. Credential Sharing Control (`N8N_DISABLE_CREDENTIAL_SHARING`)

**Purpose**: Enables organizations to disable credential sharing functionality for enhanced security posture and compliance.

**Implementation**:
- Added `disableSharing` property to `CredentialsConfig` (default: `false`)
- Added sharing validation to credential share endpoint (`/credentials/:id/share`)
- Returns `400 Bad Request` with descriptive error message when sharing is disabled

**Usage**:
```bash
N8N_DISABLE_CREDENTIAL_SHARING=true
```

### 3. Minimum Schedule Interval Enforcement (`N8N_MIN_SCHEDULE_INTERVAL_SECONDS`)

**Purpose**: Prevents resource exhaustion attacks by enforcing a minimum interval between workflow schedule executions.

**Implementation**:
- Added `minScheduleIntervalSeconds` property to `WorkflowsConfig` (default: `300` seconds / 5 minutes)
- Created `ScheduleValidationService` to validate schedule intervals across all trigger types:
  - Seconds-based intervals
  - Minutes-based intervals
  - Hours-based intervals
  - Days-based intervals
  - Weeks-based intervals
  - Months-based intervals
  - Cron expressions
- Integrated validation into `ActiveWorkflowManager` during workflow activation
- Comprehensive error handling with clear error messages indicating minimum allowed interval

**Usage**:
```bash
N8N_MIN_SCHEDULE_INTERVAL_SECONDS=300  # Default: 300 seconds (5 minutes)
```

**Validation**:
- Validates all schedule trigger types before workflow activation
- Calculates minimum interval for cron expressions dynamically
- Throws `ApplicationError` with descriptive messages when intervals are too short

## Technical Details

### Files Changed

**Configuration**:
- `packages/@n8n/config/src/configs/workflows.config.ts` - Added workflow sharing and schedule interval configs
- `packages/@n8n/config/src/configs/credentials.config.ts` - Added credential sharing config
- `packages/@n8n/config/test/config.test.ts` - Updated tests

**Core Services**:
- `packages/core/src/validation/schedule-validation.service.ts` - New service for schedule validation
- `packages/core/src/validation/index.ts` - Export schedule validation service
- `packages/core/src/index.ts` - Export validation module

**Controllers**:
- `packages/cli/src/workflows/workflows.controller.ts` - Added sharing checks to share/transfer endpoints
- `packages/cli/src/credentials/credentials.controller.ts` - Added sharing check to share endpoint
- `packages/cli/src/active-workflow-manager.ts` - Integrated schedule validation during activation

## Security Benefits

1. **Access Control**: Prevents unauthorized sharing of workflows and credentials, reducing the risk of sensitive data exposure
2. **Resource Protection**: Mitigates denial-of-service attacks by preventing overly frequent schedule executions
3. **Compliance**: Enables organizations to meet enterprise security requirements and audit standards
4. **Defense in Depth**: Adds multiple layers of security controls that can be configured independently

## Backward Compatibility

All features are opt-in via environment variables and default to permissive behavior (`false` for sharing controls, `300` seconds for minimum interval). Existing workflows and configurations will continue to function without changes unless these security features are explicitly enabled.

## Testing

- Configuration tests updated to include new properties
- Schedule validation service includes comprehensive interval calculation for all trigger types
- Error handling tested for all validation scenarios

## Migration Notes

No migration required. These features are additive and can be enabled gradually:
1. Set environment variables as needed
2. Restart n8n instance
3. Existing workflows will be validated on next activation if `N8N_MIN_SCHEDULE_INTERVAL_SECONDS` is set

title: fix(core, editor): Move single webhook trigger check to the backend
body:
## Summary

Improve the handling of single webhook triggers by moving the check to the backend and filtering based on reachability.

There are certain triggers that can't be activated for testing if the workflow is active in production. Today, the frontend detects if one of these triggers exists in the workflow, and shows an error if you try to do a manual run while the workflow is active.

However, if you're attempting to do a manual run to a destination that isn't connected to the single webhook trigger (or a manual run from a specific trigger), then it doesn't matter that the single webhook trigger _exists_, because it doesn't actually need to be activated for the test run. So in this change we move the check to the backend, at the point where we are actually about to register the test webhook. If the single webhook trigger is _actually_ going to be registered, only then do we throw an error.

New behaviour: https://www.loom.com/share/cb6c658ad6304de3b19f393c29b57433

title: test(ai-builder): Add pairwise evaluations (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

This PR adds pairwise evaluation support to the AI Workflow Builder evaluation framework. Pairwise evaluation provides a simpler, criteria-based approach to workflow assessment, evaluating generated workflows against custom "do" and "don't" rules defined in a LangSmith dataset.

### Key Features

- **Criteria-based evaluation**: Workflows are evaluated against a checklist of dos and don'ts rather than complex multi-metric scoring
- **LangSmith integration**: Full integration with LangSmith for dataset management and experiment tracking
- **Configurable example limits**: New `EVAL_MAX_EXAMPLES` env variable to limit evaluation runs (useful for testing)
- **Simple scoring**: Pass/fail scoring based on criteria compliance (passes / total rules)

### Changes

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `evaluations/chains/pairwise-evaluator.ts` | Core pairwise evaluation logic with LLM-based criteria checking |
| `evaluations/chains/pairwise-evaluator.test.ts` | Unit tests for the pairwise evaluator |
| `evaluations/langsmith/pairwise-runner.ts` | LangSmith runner for pairwise evaluation experiments |
| `evaluations/index.ts` | Added pairwise evaluation entry point |
| `evaluations/README.md` | Documentation for pairwise evaluation |
| `package.json` | Added `eval:pairwise` npm script |

### Dataset Format

The pairwise evaluation expects a LangSmith dataset with examples in this format:

```json
{
  "inputs": {
    "prompt": "Build an automation that...",
    "evals": {
      "dos": "Use HTTP Request node for API calls\nInclude error handling",
      "donts": "Don't use deprecated nodes\nDon't hardcode credentials"
    }
  }
}
```

### Usage

```bash
# Run pairwise evaluation
pnpm eval:pairwise

# Limit to specific number of examples
EVAL_MAX_EXAMPLES=2 pnpm eval:pairwise

# Use custom dataset
LANGSMITH_DATASET_NAME=my-dataset pnpm eval:pairwise
```

### Metrics Reported to LangSmith

- `pairwise_score`: Overall pass rate (0-1)
- `pairwise_passed_count`: Number of criteria that passed
- `pairwise_failed_count`: Number of criteria violated

Each result includes detailed comments with violations and passes along with justifications.

This release fixes a regression for cases where the `ignore` option is used with a string ([#​403](https://redirect.github.com/mrmlnc/fast-glob/issues/403), [#​404](https://redirect.github.com/mrmlnc/fast-glob/issues/404)).

The public interface of this package does not support a string as the value for the [`ignore` option](https://redirect.github.com/mrmlnc/fast-glob#ignore) since 2018 year ([release](https://redirect.github.com/mrmlnc/fast-glob/releases/tag/2.0.0)).

So, in the next major release, we will reintroduce method implementations that do not involve strings in the `ignore` option.

### [`v3.3.0`](https://redirect.github.com/mrmlnc/fast-glob/releases/tag/3.3.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/mrmlnc/fast-glob/compare/3.2.12...3.3.0)

> **Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/mrmlnc/fast-glob/compare/3.2.12...3.3.0>

##### 🚀 Improvements

**Method aliases**

New methods (`glob`, `globSync`, `globStream`) have been added in addition to the current methods (default import, `sync`, `stream`), which eliminate the need to rename the method when importing. In addition, an `async` alias has been added for the default import, which makes it possible to use this packet with ESM.

**Method to convert paths to globs**

A new method (`convertPathToPattern`) has been added in this release to convert a path to a pattern. The primary goal is to enable users to avoid processing Windows paths in each location where this package is used by utilities from third-party packages.

See more details in the [pull request](https://redirect.github.com/mrmlnc/fast-glob/pull/392).

##### 🐛 Bug fixes

- In the past, we mishandled patterns that contained slashes when the `baseNameMatch` option was enabled, which went against the documented behavior. ([#​312](https://redirect.github.com/mrmlnc/fast-glob/issues/312))
- Several problems with matching patterns that contain brace expansion have been resolved.  The primary issue solved is when the pattern has duplicate slashes after it is expanded ([#​394](https://redirect.github.com/mrmlnc/fast-glob/issues/394)), or the `micromatch` package does not correctly generate a regular expression ([#​365](https://redirect.github.com/mrmlnc/fast-glob/issues/365)).
- All negative patterns will now have the `dot` option enabled when matching paths. Previously, the `!**/*` patterns did not exclude hidden files (start with a dot). ([#​343](https://redirect.github.com/mrmlnc/fast-glob/issues/343))
- The issue that led to duplicates in the results when overlapping or duplicate patterns were present among the patterns has been fixed. At the moment, we are only talking about leading dot. Other cases are not included. For example, running with the patterns `['./file.md', 'file.md', '*']` will now only include `file.md` once in the results. ([#​190](https://redirect.github.com/mrmlnc/fast-glob/issues/190))

title: fix(editor): Avoid clearing EULA license key when closing dialog
body:
## Summary

## Summary

This PR fixes the issue that the "Download current role settings csv"  does not show up if you have done the following two changes in two steps:
- change user role provisioning setting
- enable single sign on

title: fix(MCP Client Node): Fix selecting PKCE auth flow for some servers and request scopes from `scopes_requested` during DCR
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

### Description

This PR includes fixes for 2 issues that were discovered when trying to connect to a single MCP server using OAuth2 with Dynamic Client Registration 

#### PKCE flow fix
During DCR, there is a process of selecting which auth flow to use to obtain the token. Previously, PKCE was selected when `code_challenge_methods_supported` includes `S256` and `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported` includes `none`. However, some servers expect PKCE to be used even if there is `S256` in `code_challenge_methods_supported` and `none` is not present in `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported`. This PR accounts for this

#### Scopes fix
During DCR, server metadata _may_ include `scopes_supported` which has a list of available scopes that can be requested by the client. Previously, this was ignored which caused n8n to request only `openid` scope. Because of missing scopes some MCP servers couldn't be used. This PR fixes this and request all scopes that are in `scopes_supported` when obtaining the token

**Note**: we are planning to allow users to manually request whatever scopes they would like when connecting to an MCP server, which would be more flexible

### Testing
MCP server to test with: `https://mcp.semilattice.ai` (this is the server with which the issues were discovered)

title: refactor(editor): Refactor NDV parameter list implementation and performance (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

This refactor optimizes how NDV parameters are rendered by removing redundant reactive work and caching everything upfront using a throttled watcher. I also optimized shouldDisplayNodeParameter to run in O(n) instead of O(n²), which should result in a nice speed-up for nodes with many parameters. Before doing any changes, I added extensive tests to ensure that the refactor preserves the current output and behavior.

Values are not cached because CodeMirror is incompatible with throttled values. The cursor jumps as soon as the throttled watcher updates the parameter value.

### Performance (node with ~20 parameters)
- Before: ~95 template function calls total, ~15 calls per render
- After: 7 template function calls, 1 throttled watcher, 1 ref, all data except parameter value is pre-computed
- Overall: ~80% less render-time work → should be roughly 2-4x faster updates, plus throttling

### Additional Benefits

1. **Better Reactivity Control**: Throttling prevents excessive updates during rapid parameter changes
2. **Simpler Template Logic**: Template is now purely declarative with no function calls
3. **Easier Debugging**: Pre-computed data structure makes it easy to inspect what's being rendered
4. **Type Safety**: `ParameterComputedData` interface provides strong typing for template usage

### Testing
Before attempting the refactoring, added comprehensive test cases for `ParameterInputList.vue` and `shouldDisplayNodeParameter` to ensure backwards compatibility with old behaviour.

title: feat(core): Chat only users (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Create new instance role `global:chatUser`, aka `Chat user` which has only Chat related permissions.

Unlike regular users this user also only gets (new) `project:personalOwnerViewer` project role to their personal project, which only allows them viewer access on their own personal project, so they won't be able to create workflows/credentials/dataTables etc under their personal project either. Having this project role still signals project ownership, and this role shouldn't be normally assignable. _(They don't really need the viewer access either and we could lock that up even more, but having viewer access simplified UI support as we've been assuming all users would be able to do at least certain things.)_

If user attempts to access /home pages on the UI they get redirected back to /home/chat, and they're only supposed to interract with chat / settings pages. This isn't rock solid, and as users still have viewer access on their personal project they could land on workflows under their personal project with viewer rights - but that doesn't seem like a big deal as our usual access control anyways restricts what they can do, and they shouldn't have workflows.

If the user is later upgraded from `Chat user` to other roles they regain the usual `project:personalOwner` project role on their personal project. One of the reasons `project:personalOwnerViewer` role exists is this - otherwise we would lose track of who actually owns the personal project if we just made the users `project:viewer` on it.

Also made bunch of UI side tweaks to skip requests the user won't be able to do / not error due to the abnormal access rights.

An alternative approach could be to introduce a new column on `project` to track the owner/creator, perhaps named `creatorId` and use that to retain the ownership information of personal projects while the user would just have `project:viewer` on it. Commit implementing that https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/diff/cha-66-chat-only-users...cha-66-chat-only-users-2 here.

title: Fix (ERPNext Node): double URL encoding docType causing 404 errors with spaces
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a double URL encoding bug in the ERPNext node that caused 404 errors when using docTypes with spaces (e.g., "Service Product") in combination with filters. 

**The Problem:**
When a docType name contained spaces, it was being encoded twice:
1. First in `getDocTypes()` with `encodeURI()`
2. Then again by the HTTP library when sending the request

This resulted in filters containing `Service%2520Product` instead of `Service%20Product`, causing ERPNext/Frappe to fail with a "DocType not found" error.

**The Fix:**
Removed the manual `encodeURI()` call in the `getDocTypes()` method (line 87).  The HTTP library automatically handles URL encoding for both path parameters and query parameters, so manual encoding is unnecessary and causes double-encoding.

**Before:**
```typescript
return { name, value: encodeURI(name) };
```

**After:**
```typescript
return { name, value: name };
```

**How to Test:**
1. Set up an ERPNext instance with a DocType that contains spaces in its name (e.g., "Service Product")
2. Use the ERPNext node's "Get All" operation
3. Select the DocType with spaces
4. Add a filter (e.g., field: "enabled", operator: "=", value: "1")
5. Execute the workflow
6. Verify it returns results instead of a 404 error

title: feat(ai-builder): Implement Core Subgraph Infrastructure
body:
## Summary
This PR refactors the AI workflow builder from a single monolithic agent into a multi-agent system with specialized subgraphs. Each subgraph handles one phase of workflow building, coordinated by a supervisor.

## Problem

The single-agent approach has limitations:
- One agent must handle discovery, building, and configuration in a single context
- Long prompt with all instructions leads to context dilution
- Difficult to iterate on individual phases independently
- No clear separation between structural and parameter changes

## Solution

Split into four specialized agents, each with focused responsibilities:

```
User Request
     │
     ▼
┌─────────────┐
│  Supervisor │ ─── Routes based on intent
└─────────────┘
     │
     ├──► Discovery ─── Find relevant nodes
     │         │
     │         ▼
     ├──► Builder ───── Create structure
     │         │
     │         ▼
     └──► Configurator ─ Set parameters
              │
              ▼
┌─────────────┐
│  Responder  │ ─── Synthesize response
└─────────────┘
     │
     ▼
User Response
```

## Architecture

### Supervisor Agent

Routes user requests to the appropriate subgraph based on intent:

| User Intent | Route To |
|-------------|----------|
| Question or chat | Responder |
| New workflow or new node types | Discovery |
| Connect/disconnect existing nodes | Builder |
| Change parameter values | Configurator |

The supervisor only runs once at the start. After that, routing is deterministic: discovery → builder → configurator → responder.

### Discovery Subgraph

**Purpose**: Find n8n nodes relevant to the user's request.

**Tools**: `search_nodes`, `get_node_details`, `get_best_practices`, `submit_discovery_results`

**Process**:
1. Retrieve best practices for identified workflow patterns
2. Search for nodes matching user requirements
3. Get details for promising candidates
4. Submit structured results with connection-affecting parameters

**Output**: List of nodes with `{nodeName, version, reasoning, connectionChangingParameters}`

The connection-changing parameters are critical—they tell the Builder which parameters affect what inputs/outputs a node has (e.g., Vector Store's `mode` parameter changes whether it accepts documents or queries).

### Builder Subgraph

**Purpose**: Create workflow structure using discovery results.

**Tools**: `add_nodes`, `connect_nodes`, `remove_node`, `remove_connection`, `validate_structure`

**Process**:
1. Create all nodes from discovery results
2. Connect nodes following n8n connection rules
3. Validate structure (trigger present, connections valid)
4. Report what was built

**Key prompt sections**:
- Workflow Configuration node placement (after trigger)
- AI sub-node connection patterns (models/tools/memory → agent)
- RAG workflow patterns (embeddings/loaders → vector store)
- Connection type mapping (main, ai_languageModel, ai_tool, etc.)

The Builder must call `validate_structure` before finishing to catch missing triggers or invalid connections.

### Configurator Subgraph

**Purpose**: Set parameters on all nodes after structure exists.

**Tools**: `update_node_parameters`, `get_node_parameter`, `validate_configuration`

**Process**:
1. Configure each node with appropriate parameters
2. Handle special cases ($fromAI, webhooks, credentials)
3. Validate configuration (prompts present, valid $fromAI usage)
4. Report setup instructions for user

**Special handling**:
- `$fromAI('key', 'description', 'type')` expressions for AI tool nodes
- Instance URL injection for webhook/chat trigger nodes
- Credential placeholders for authenticated services

The Configurator must call `validate_configuration` before finishing.

### Responder Agent

**Purpose**: Synthesize user-facing response from coordination log.

**No tools**—just a prompt that receives context about what was discovered, built, and configured, then generates a coherent response.

**Output format**:
- Summary of what was built
- Brief explanation of the workflow
- Setup instructions (credentials, webhooks, etc.)
- Prompt for adjustments

## State Management

### Parent Graph State

Shared state that coordinates between subgraphs:

```typescript
{
  messages: BaseMessage[]        // User conversation
  workflowJSON: SimpleWorkflow   // Current workflow
  workflowContext: {...}         // Execution data/schema
  nextPhase: string              // Routing decision
  discoveryContext: {...}        // Nodes found, best practices
  workflowOperations: [...]      // Pending operations
  coordinationLog: [...]         // Phase completion records
}
```

### Coordination Log

Tracks subgraph completion for deterministic routing:

```typescript
{
  phase: 'discovery' | 'builder' | 'configurator',
  status: 'completed' | 'error',
  timestamp: number,
  summary: string,
  output?: string,  // Setup instructions from configurator
  metadata: {...}   // Phase-specific data
}
```

After each subgraph completes, `getNextPhaseFromLog()` determines the next step without LLM involvement.

### Subgraph Isolation

Each subgraph has its own internal state:
- `DiscoverySubgraphState`: userRequest, nodesFound, bestPractices
- `BuilderSubgraphState`: workflowJSON, discoveryContext, workflowOperations
- `ConfiguratorSubgraphState`: workflowJSON, instanceUrl, workflowOperations

State transforms at boundaries:
- `transformInput()`: Extract what subgraph needs from parent state
- `transformOutput()`: Return results to update parent state

## Streaming

### Event Formats

Parent graph events (legacy):
```
[streamMode, data]
```

Subgraph events (new):
```
[namespace[], streamMode, data]
// namespace like ['builder_subgraph:612f4bc3-...']
```

### Filtering

Internal subgraph messages are filtered—users only see:
- Tool progress events (real-time feedback)
- Workflow updates (canvas changes)
- Responder output (final response)

Messages from discovery/builder/configurator agents are suppressed.

## Feature Flag

```typescript
new WorkflowBuilderAgent({
  enableMultiAgent: true,  // Use multi-agent architecture
  // ... other config
});
```

title: feat(Anthropic Node): Add prompt caching support
body:
## Summary

This PR implements Anthropic's prompt caching functionality for the Anthropic Vendor Node, enabling up to 90% cost reduction and improved latency for workflows with repeated system prompts.

### What this PR does:
- Adds an "Enable Prompt Caching" toggle in the Anthropic node options (defaults to OFF for backward compatibility)
- Transforms system messages to array format with `cache_control` markers when caching is enabled
- Registers the `prompt-caching-2024-07-31` beta header with the Anthropic API
- Maintains full backward compatibility - existing workflows continue to work unchanged

### How to test:
1. Create a workflow with an Anthropic node (Vendor node, "Send a Message" action)
2. Add a system message of at least 1024 tokens (~768 words or ~3000 characters)
   - Example long system message provided in testing
3. In Options, toggle "Enable Prompt Caching" to ON
4. Execute the workflow 3 times:
   - **First execution**: Check response usage field for `cache_creation_input_tokens` > 0
   - **Second execution**: Check for `cache_read_input_tokens` > 0 (90% cost savings!)
   - **Third execution**: Verify cache is still being read

**Note**: System messages must be at least 1024 tokens for Anthropic to activate caching. Shorter messages will show cache fields as 0.

### Example response with caching enabled:
```json
"usage": {
  "input_tokens": 15,
  "cache_read_input_tokens": 1098,
  "output_tokens": 281
}
```

title: feat(editor): Add workflow auto-save functionality
body:
Auto-Save Feature for n8n Workflows

Overview

This feature adds automatic workflow saving to n8n, helping users avoid losing work by periodically saving dirty workflows in the background.

How It Works

  • Workflows are automatically saved every 60 seconds when changes are detected
  • Auto-save only triggers for existing workflows (not new unsaved ones)
  • Users can toggle the feature on/off in Settings → Personal
  • A visual indicator shows when auto-save is in progress

Safety Guards

Auto-save will not run when:

  • Workflow is currently executing
  • Workflow is already being saved
  • Branch is in read-only mode (source control)
  • Workflow is archived
  • User lacks update permissions

Files Modified

File | Purpose -- | -- useAutosave.ts | Core composable with timer and save logic SaveButton.vue | UI indicator for auto-save state WorkflowDetails.vue | Integration with workflow header SettingsPersonalView.vue | Toggle in user settings user-settings.schema.ts | Schema for autosaveEnabled interfaces.ts | TypeScript interface update en.json | i18n translations

Usage

  1. Open any existing workflow
  2. Make changes (workflow becomes "dirty")
  3. Wait 60 seconds - workflow saves automatically
  4. To disable: Settings → Personal → Toggle "Auto-save workflows"

title: feat(nodes-langchain): Add token usage tracking and cost calculation …
body:
## Summary
This PR implements automatic token usage tracking and real-time cost calculation for AI Agent nodes, addressing a highly requested community feature with 20+ active members requesting this functionality.

### What it does
AI Agent nodes now automatically track and report:
- Token usage from LLM calls (prompt tokens, completion tokens, total tokens)
- Estimated costs in USD based on current model pricing
- Model name for transparency
- Accuracy indicator (actual vs estimated tokens)

### How it works
- **AgentTokenTracker** - A LangChain callback handler that captures token usage from all LLM calls automatically
- **ModelPricingService** - Fetches up-to-date pricing from LiteLLM CDN with fallback pricing for 15+ common models
- **Token Accumulation** - Automatically accumulates tokens across multi-turn conversations with tool calls

### Output Example
```json
{
  "output": "I found 3 relevant documents for you...",
  "tokenUsage": {
    "promptTokens": 320,
    "completionTokens": 180,
    "totalTokens": 500,
    "isEstimate": false,
    "estimatedCost": 0.000705,
    "modelName": "gpt-4o-mini"
  }
}
```

### Use Cases Enabled
- **Cost tracking per customer** - Track LLM costs for usage-based billing
- **Budget management** - Set alerts when costs exceed thresholds
- **Prompt optimization** - Identify expensive workflows and optimize prompts
- **Model comparison** - Compare costs across different LLM providers
- **Enterprise compliance** - Audit trails and cost allocation

### How to test
1. Create a new AI Agent node (Tools Agent V3)
2. Configure with any LLM provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google)
3. Add a simple prompt like "What is 2+2?"
4. Execute the workflow
5. Check the output - you should see `tokenUsage` field with all tracking data

**Supported Models:**
- **OpenAI**: GPT-4, GPT-4 Turbo, GPT-4o, GPT-4o Mini, GPT-3.5 Turbo
- **Anthropic**: Claude 3 Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, Claude 3.5 Sonnet
- **Google**: Gemini Pro, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Gemini 1.5 Flash
- Plus any model in the [LiteLLM database](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/main/model_prices_and_context_window.json)

- Community request: https://community.n8n.io/t/retrieve-llm-token-usage-in-ai-agents/68714

  - [x] 26 unit tests for ModelPricingService
  - [x] 7 unit tests for AgentTokenTracker
  - [x] Integration tests for token tracking in agent execution
  - [x] All 1560 tests passing ✅

## Implementation Details

### Files Changed:
- `AgentTokenTracker.ts` - LangChain callback handler for token capture
- `modelPricing.ts` - Pricing service with CDN integration and fallback data
- `types.ts` - Extended AgentResult and RequestResponseMetadata types
- `buildResponseMetadata.ts` - Token accumulation across iterations
- `prepareItemContext.ts` - TokenTracker initialization
- `runAgent.ts` - Cost calculation integration
- Comprehensive test files for all new components

### Key Features:
- ✅ **Backward compatible** - existing workflows unaffected
- ✅ **Type safe** - full TypeScript support
- ✅ **Provider agnostic** - works with all LLM providers
- ✅ **Performance optimized** - 24-hour pricing cache
- ✅ **Gracefully handles unknown models** (returns null cost)
- ✅ **Supports both streaming and non-streaming modes**

### Pricing Data Source
- **Primary**: jsDelivr CDN (fast, cached, no rate limits)
- **Backup**: Embedded pricing for 15 common models (~5KB)
- **Data freshness**: Pricing cached for 24 hours, LiteLLM updates daily
- **Why CDN?**: 8x faster than raw GitHub, no rate limit issues, 99.99% uptime

title: fix(EmailSend Node): Support binary data expressions in attachments
body:
Fixes #20832

Users can now use expressions like ={{ $('NodeName').item.binary.data }} in the attachments parameter, in addition to the existing comma-separated string format.

Changes:
- Enhanced attachment processing to handle string, IBinaryData object, or array
- Updated EmailSendOptions type to accept string | IBinaryData | IBinaryData[]
- Added comprehensive unit tests (12 tests) covering backward compatibility and new expression functionality
- Maintained full backward compatibility with existing workflows

## Summary

Fixes a bug where users cannot use expressions to reference binary data from other nodes in the EmailSend node's attachments parameter. Previously, only comma-separated string property names were supported (e.g., `"data, file1"`). Now users can also use expressions like `={{ $('Read File').item.binary.data }}` to dynamically reference binary data.

### What changed
- Enhanced attachment processing to detect and handle both string and object/array inputs
- Updated type definitions to accept `string | IBinaryData | IBinaryData[]`
- Added comprehensive unit tests (12 tests) covering all scenarios
- Fully backward compatible - existing workflows continue to work unchanged

### How to test
1. Create a workflow with a node that outputs binary data (e.g., "Read/Write Files from Disk")
2. Add an EmailSend node
3. In the attachments field, use an expression: `={{ $('Read/Write Files from Disk').item.binary.data }}`
4. Execute the workflow
5. Verify that the email is sent with the attachment

**Before this fix:** Attachment would not be sent (expression resolved to object, code expected string)  
**After this fix:** Attachment is correctly attached to the email

### Test Coverage
- ✅ Backward compatibility with string property names (`"data"`, `"data, file1, file2"`)
- ✅ Expression-resolved IBinaryData objects
- ✅ Arrays of binary data objects
- ✅ All email formats (HTML, text, both)
