title: refactor(core): Switch to multiprocessing pipes in native Python runner
body:
## Summary The Python pipe buffer for `multiprocessing.Queue` is limited to 64 KB, so currently the Python runner sends back via the queue only metadata pointing to a shared memory segment containing the result of the task: ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant RunnerProcess as Runner process participant Queue as Queue participant TaskSubprocess as Task subprocess participant SharedMemory as Shared memory RunnerProcess->>Queue: Create queue RunnerProcess->>TaskSubprocess: Start task subprocess via forkserver TaskSubprocess->>TaskSubprocess: Execute user code TaskSubprocess->>TaskSubprocess: Serialize result to JSON TaskSubprocess->>SharedMemory: Allocate shared memory SharedMemory->>SharedMemory: Create /dev/shm/abc123
⚠️ Visible to other processes TaskSubprocess->>SharedMemory: Write JSON result TaskSubprocess->>Queue: Send back metadata
shm_name + shm_size TaskSubprocess->>SharedMemory: Close handle for shared memory Queue->>RunnerProcess: Relay JSON metadata RunnerProcess->>RunnerProcess: Parse JSON metadata RunnerProcess-->>SharedMemory: Open segment by name and read JSON result RunnerProcess->>RunnerProcess: Parse JSON result RunnerProcess->>SharedMemory: Close handle for shared memory RunnerProcess->>SharedMemory: Delete shared memory RunnerProcess->>RunnerProcess: Send result to broker ``` We'd like to make this result invisible to other processes. Hence in this PR, we switch to multiprocessing pipes for direct IPC between runner process and task subprocess. To prevent deadlock with large payloads that exceed the pipe buffer, we spawn a reader thread to run concurrently with the taks subprocess, consuming data as it becomes available. The pipe connections use private FDs not discoverable by other processes. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant RunnerProcess as Runner process participant Pipe as Pipe participant TaskSubprocess as Task subprocess participant ReaderThread as Reader thread RunnerProcess->>Pipe: Create read and write
pipe handles RunnerProcess->>ReaderThread: Spawn reader thread RunnerProcess->>TaskSubprocess: Start task subprocess via forkserver RunnerProcess->>Pipe: Close parent's write handle ReaderThread-->>Pipe: Block on read TaskSubprocess->>TaskSubprocess: Execute user code TaskSubprocess->>TaskSubprocess: Serialize result to JSON TaskSubprocess->>TaskSubprocess: Include result in msg TaskSubprocess->>Pipe: Write msg length TaskSubprocess->>Pipe: Write JSON msg Note over Pipe: ✓ Not discoverable TaskSubprocess->>Pipe: Close child's write handle Pipe-->>ReaderThread: Data available ReaderThread-->>Pipe: Read msg length ReaderThread-->>Pipe: Read exact msg bytes ReaderThread->>ReaderThread: Parse msg ReaderThread->>ReaderThread: Store msg in shared list RunnerProcess->>RunnerProcess: Wait for subprocess to exit RunnerProcess->>RunnerProcess: Wait for reader thread to join RunnerProcess->>RunnerProcess: Get result from shared list RunnerProcess->>RunnerProcess: Send result to broker ``` Notes: - Used a unidirectional `multiprocessing.Pipe` instead of `os.pipe` because with `forkserver` the subprocess is not forked directly from the parent but from the `forkserver` process. This means that with `os.pipe` + `forkserver` FDs are not automatically inherited by the subprocess, leaving the child with no access to the write end. `multiprocessing.Pipe()` passes FDs. ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts https://linear.app/n8n/issue/CAT-1663 ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. title: feat(core): Use active version instead of current version (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

This PR decouples the active version from the current version of the workflow:

- Add a foreign (nullable) key `activeVersionId` to the workflow entity
    - It does not currently replace the `active` flag, but we will tackle this as tech debt later.
- Automatic executions now always run the populated active version of the workflow. Manual executions still use the data that is sent.
- Update public API endpoints with keeping the current behavior
    - Update `activeVersion` with the current version when updating and activating workflows
    - Return `activeVersion` for GET endpoints (it'll be the same as the current version until user starts using V2 endpoints)
    - Remove `excludePinnedData` from activate endpoint (it was unused and using "GET" type was semantically incorrect)
- Update the logic to always first add a record to workflow history and only then update the workflow entity, so that `activeVersion` is set once along with the workflow entity update

### Active Version Usage

These are now using the active workflow version:

1. Workflow Activation [`active-workflow-manager.ts` - [add](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/4ea2757df67519c0b7e1de19a35c55d74ed93266/packages/cli/src/active-workflow-manager.ts#L540)]
    - When activating workflows, the system now uses `activeVersion` nodes and connections instead of current version.
2. Webhook Cleanup [`active-workflow-manager.ts` - [clearWebhooks](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/4ea2757df67519c0b7e1de19a35c55d74ed93266/packages/cli/src/active-workflow-manager.ts#L248)]
    - When deactivating workflows and removing webhooks, the system now uses `activeVersion` to properly identify and clean up the correct webhooks.
3. Activation Error Handling [`active-workflow-manager.ts` - [activateWorkflow](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/4ea2757df67519c0b7e1de19a35c55d74ed93266/packages/cli/src/active-workflow-manager.ts#L462)]
    - When workflow activation fails and throws an error workflow needs to execute, it now uses `activeVersion` instead of current version.
4. Production Webhook Execution [`live-webhooks.ts` - [executeWebhook](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/8527e4b6f1b35472ac472e5c3857cb0e072acb0a/packages/cli/src/webhooks/live-webhooks.ts#L71)]

### What I tested and how

- For public endpoints, I created workflows with an HTTP Request node that sends a payload to activate or update another workflow.

Problem
n8n was not detecting HTTP proxy environment variables on Windows PowerShell, causing connections to external services (like Notion) to fail when behind a proxy.

**#User Issue:**
No proxy activity in proxy software
No "Installing global HTTP proxy agents" debug message
Connection to Notion failed

**#Root Cause**
The [hasProxyEnvironmentVariables()](vscode-file://vscode-app/c:/Users/akcho/AppData/Local/Programs/Microsoft%20VS%20Code/resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) function in [http-proxy.ts](vscode-file://vscode-app/c:/Users/akcho/AppData/Local/Programs/Microsoft%20VS%20Code/resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) only checked for uppercase environment variables ([HTTP_PROXY](vscode-file://vscode-app/c:/Users/akcho/AppData/Local/Programs/Microsoft%20VS%20Code/resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html), [HTTPS_PROXY](vscode-file://vscode-app/c:/Users/akcho/AppData/Local/Programs/Microsoft%20VS%20Code/resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html), [ALL_PROXY](vscode-file://vscode-app/c:/Users/akcho/AppData/Local/Programs/Microsoft%20VS%20Code/resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html)), but Windows PowerShell and Unix systems commonly use lowercase variants ([http_proxy](vscode-file://vscode-app/c:/Users/akcho/AppData/Local/Programs/Microsoft%20VS%20Code/resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html), [https_proxy](vscode-file://vscode-app/c:/Users/akcho/AppData/Local/Programs/Microsoft%20VS%20Code/resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html), [all_proxy](vscode-file://vscode-app/c:/Users/akcho/AppData/Local/Programs/Microsoft%20VS%20Code/resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html)).

**#Solution**
Modified [http-proxy.ts](vscode-file://vscode-app/c:/Users/akcho/AppData/Local/Programs/Microsoft%20VS%20Code/resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) to check both uppercase and lowercase environment variables:

Change 1: Detection Logic

```javascript
function hasProxyEnvironmentVariables(): boolean {
    return Boolean(
        process.env.HTTP_PROXY ??
            process.env.http_proxy ??
            process.env.HTTPS_PROXY ??
            process.env.https_proxy ??
            process.env.ALL_PROXY ??
            process.env.all_proxy,
    );
}
``` 
Change 2: Debug Logging
```javascript
LoggerProxy.debug('Installing global HTTP proxy agents', {
    HTTP_PROXY: process.env.HTTP_PROXY ?? process.env.http_proxy,
    HTTPS_PROXY: process.env.HTTPS_PROXY ?? process.env.https_proxy,
    NO_PROXY: process.env.NO_PROXY ?? process.env.no_proxy,
    ALL_PROXY: process.env.ALL_PROXY ?? process.env.all_proxy,
});
```

✅ Compatible with Windows, Linux, and macOS

title: #Http proxy env case sensitive(#21199)
body:
#**Fix HTTP Proxy Environment Variable Detection on Windows**
**#The Issue(#21199)**
n8n was not detecting HTTP proxy environment variables on Windows when set through PowerShell. Users who set $env:http_proxy and $env:https_proxy found that n8n ignored these settings and failed to route traffic through their proxy server. The debug logs showed no "Installing global HTTP proxy agents" message, confirming the proxy wasn't being recognized.

**#Root Cause**
The problem was in the [hasProxyEnvironmentVariables()](vscode-file://vscode-app/c:/Users/akcho/AppData/Local/Programs/Microsoft%20VS%20Code/resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) function in [http-proxy.ts](vscode-file://vscode-app/c:/Users/akcho/AppData/Local/Programs/Microsoft%20VS%20Code/resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html). It only checked for uppercase environment variable names:

However, Windows PowerShell (and many Unix-like systems) commonly use lowercase variable names. When users set $env:http_proxy="http://127.0.0.1:7890" in PowerShell, n8n couldn't detect it because the function only looked for the uppercase version.

**#How I Fixed It**
Modified the [hasProxyEnvironmentVariables()](vscode-file://vscode-app/c:/Users/akcho/AppData/Local/Programs/Microsoft%20VS%20Code/resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) function to check both uppercase and lowercase variants using the nullish coalescing operator (??):

`return Boolean(
    process.env.HTTP_PROXY ??
        process.env.http_proxy ??
        process.env.HTTPS_PROXY ??
        process.env.https_proxy ??
        process.env.ALL_PROXY ??
        process.env.all_proxy,
);`


**#Testing**

Test 3: No proxy variables ✓ Returns false correctly
Result: All tests passed
2. Build Test:
Exit code: 0 - No compilation errors

Final Outcome
✅ n8n now correctly detects proxy environment variables on Windows PowerShell
✅ Maintains backward compatibility with existing uppercase variables
✅ Works across all platforms (Windows, Linux, macOS)
✅ No breaking changes - purely additive fix
✅ Minimal code change - only the detection logic modified

title: Chat memory cleanup
body:
#### **Fix Memory Node Session Persistence Issue** #21186

#**Description**

This PR fixes a bug where the Memory node (Simple Memory) was keeping old conversation data after users refreshed or reset their chat sessions. Users were seeing their AI respond with context from previous conversations even after starting a new session.

#**The Problem**

The Memory node uses a singleton pattern to cache conversation buffers. These buffers were being kept in memory for 1 hour before cleanup. When users clicked "refresh" in the chat UI and started a new conversation, the old buffer was still there and got reused, causing the LLM to have access to messages from the previous session.

#**What Changed**

Changed the cleanup threshold in [MemoryBufferWindow.node.ts](vscode-file://vscode-app/c:/Users/akcho/AppData/Local/Programs/Microsoft%20VS%20Code/resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.html) from 1 hour to 5 minutes.

Before:

`const oneHourAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 60 * 60 * 1000);`
After:

`const thirtySecondsAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 5*60 * 1000);`

**#Why 5 Minutes**
When a user refreshes their chat session and takes a break, the old memory is cleaned up within a reasonable timeframe
Active conversations where users pause to think or type longer responses (up to 5 minutes) still work normally
Balances cleanup of stale sessions with real-world conversation patterns where users may need time to compose thoughtful responses
Prevents memory buildup from abandoned sessions while protecting legitimate active conversations


Build passes successfully with no errors.

This PR fixes a TypeScript compiler complaint (TS7022) in the DateRangePicker component by adding an explicit type annotation for the slots variable.

What I changed:

In DateRangePicker.vue
Imported type Slots from vue.
Annotated slots as const slots: Slots = useSlots();.

Solves: 
Status: Open.
#21187 

Why:

TypeScript raised TS7022: "'slots' implicitly has type 'any' because it does not have a type annotation and is referenced directly or indirectly in its own initializer."
Adding the explicit Slots type restores proper typing for slots, improves IDE autocompletion, and prevents strict type-checking failures (for example under noImplicitAny). 

Notes:

This change is low-risk and purely improves typing; no functional behavior was modified.
Unit tests for DateRangePicker are present and should continue passing.

title: Add S3 Storage Support for Execution Data
body:
## Summary
This PR implements S3 storage support for non-binary workflow execution data, allowing execution data to be stored in S3 with gzip compression instead of PostgreSQL. This provides significant storage cost savings while maintaining backward compatibility.

### Description
#### Problem
Currently, all workflow execution data is stored in PostgreSQL, which can lead to:
High database storage costs for large execution datasets
Database performance degradation with large execution data
Limited scalability for high-volume workflows

#### Solution
This PR introduces a hybrid storage approach that allows execution data to be stored in S3 with gzip compression, similar to how binary data is already handled.

### Implementation Details
#### Configuration
New environment variable: 
1. N8N_EXECUTION_DATA_MODE (default: database, options: database | s3)

#### Database Changes
1. Added s3Key column to execution_data table (nullable string)
2. Added storageMode column to execution_data table (enum: database | s3)
3. Made the existing data column nullable for S3 mode
4. Created migrations for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite

#### Usage
1. To enable S3 storage for execution data:
2. Set environment variable: N8N_EXECUTION_DATA_MODE=s3
3. Ensure S3 configuration is set up (reuses existing binary data S3 config)
4. Run database migrations to add new columns
5. New executions will automatically use S3 storage

#### Migration Strategy
1. Existing Data: Remains in PostgreSQL unchanged
2. New Data: Uses S3 when N8N_EXECUTION_DATA_MODE=s3 is configured
3. Transparent: No changes needed to existing workflows or API endpoints

title: fix(ai-builder): Auto-generate names only for workflows with default names
body:
## Summary

Improve workflow name generation logic in AI workflow builder to only auto-generate names for empty workflows with default naming patterns (e.g., "My workflow", "My workflow 1").

## Changes
- Extracted `shouldModifyState` as a pure, testable export. This moves the routing logic out of the workflow graph into a standalone function that determines the next node: agent, compact_messages, delete_messages, create_workflow_name, or auto_compact_messages.

- Enhanced the workflow name generation condition to check both:
  - Workflow has zero nodes (`nodes?.length === 0`)
  - Workflow name matches default pattern `/^My workflow( \d+)?$/` or is undefined

This ensures names are only auto-generated for truly new, empty workflows with default names, and won't be generated for workflows that already have nodes or custom names.

### Testing
Added 17 unit tests for `shouldModifyState` covering command handling, workflow name generation logic with nodes condition, and auto-compact behavior.

title: feat(redis): add cluster mode support and refactor client connection …
body:
This pull request adds support for connecting to Redis clusters in addition to standalone Redis instances, enhancing the flexibility and scalability of Redis integrations. The changes introduce a new "Cluster Mode" option in credentials, update the connection logic to handle both modes, and refactor code to use a unified client type for both standalone and cluster connections.

**Redis Cluster Support and Credential Enhancements:**

* Added a `clusterMode` boolean option to the Redis credentials (`Redis.credentials.ts`), allowing users to specify whether to connect to a Redis Cluster or a standalone instance. The host field now clarifies that, in cluster mode, any node in the cluster can be provided. The database selection option is hidden when cluster mode is enabled. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f75e3993f1415e76f121b541058008022f847cad1ceaf8fa1bd1f23a5cdefa2bR8-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f75e3993f1415e76f121b541058008022f847cad1ceaf8fa1bd1f23a5cdefa2bR36-R37) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f75e3993f1415e76f121b541058008022f847cad1ceaf8fa1bd1f23a5cdefa2bR49-R53)
* Updated the Redis credential type definitions to include `clusterMode` and introduced new types (`RedisClusterClient`, `RedisClientType`) to support both cluster and standalone clients.

**Connection Logic and Utility Refactoring:**

* Refactored the `setupRedisClient` function to create either a standalone or cluster client based on the `clusterMode` flag. The function now uses `createCluster` for cluster mode, handling initial node discovery and TLS options.
* Simplified and unified the connection test logic to work for both standalone and cluster modes by connecting directly and removing redundant error handling and timeouts.

**Node and Trigger Adaptations:**

* Updated the main Redis node (`Redis.node.ts`) and Redis trigger node (`RedisTrigger.node.ts`) to use the new unified client type, ensuring all Redis operations (including pub/sub, key management, and data manipulation) work seamlessly with both standalone and cluster clients. All Redis commands are now executed through a type-cast `anyClient` for compatibility. title: feat(Slack Node): Include slack message in send and wait operation of Slack node
body: ## Summary When the "Send and Wait" operation of Slack node is used, the original message that is posted on Slack is currently not accessible. This enhancement would solve several problems: 1. It would eliminate the need to use separate nodes to track message information 2. It would allow for more complete message lifecycle management within a single workflow 3. It would make it easier to build workflows that require referencing both the original message and the response 4. title: feat(ai-builder): Properly separate system and user prompts in AI nodes
body:
## Summary


The AI workflow builder tends to put all instructions (system-level role definitions, task descriptions, AND dynamic user context) into a single `text`/user message field in AI nodes. This makes prompts:
- Hard to maintain (changing behavior requires editing data references)
- Not reusable (static instructions mixed with dynamic data)
- Against AI prompt engineering best practices

**Example of the problem:**
```json
{
  "text": "=You are an orchestrator agent that coordinates specialized agents. Your task is to: 1) Call Research Agent Tool 2) Call Fact-Check Agent Tool. The research topic is: {{ $json.researchTopic }}"
}
```
## Solution

Implemented guidance and validation to ensure AI nodes properly separate:
- **System Message**: Static role, capabilities, task descriptions, behavioral instructions
- **User Message/Text**: Dynamic user input, context variables, data references

**After the fix:**
```json
{
  "text": "=The research topic is: {{ $json.researchTopic }}",
  "options": {
    "systemMessage": "You are an orchestrator agent that coordinates specialized agents.\n\nYour task is to:\n1. Call the Research Agent Tool to gather information\n2. Call the Fact-Check Agent Tool to verify findings\n3. Call the Report Writer Agent Tool to create a report\n4. Return ONLY the final result"
  }
}
```

Clean separation: static instructions in system message, dynamic data in text field.

## Key Changes

### 1. Multi-Node Support
The solution applies to **all AI nodes with system message support**:
- **AI Agent**: `options.systemMessage` + `text`
- **LLM Chain**: `messages.messageValues[]` (system role) + `text`
- **Anthropic**: `options.system` + `messages.values[]`
- **OpenAI**: `messages.values[]` (role: system vs user)

### 2. Updated Main Agent Prompt
**File**: `packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/tools/prompts/main-agent.prompt.ts`

Added `<system_message_configuration>` section with:
- Explanation of system message vs user prompt
- Node-specific field mappings
- Examples showing WRONG vs RIGHT patterns
- **Special emphasis on AI Agent Tools (sub-agents)**: Must configure BOTH system message AND text field with `$fromAI()`

### 3. Generic Detection in Parameter Updater
**File**: `packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/chains/prompts/prompt-builder.ts`

Added `hasSystemMessageParameters()` method that detects nodes with system message support by checking for:
- `options.systemMessage` (AI Agent)
- `options.system` (Anthropic)
- `messages` parameter (OpenAI, LLM Chain)

### 4. New Parameter Guide
**File**: `packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/chains/prompts/parameter-types/system-message.ts`

Created `SYSTEM_MESSAGE_GUIDE` with:
- Multi-node field mappings
- Practical examples for different use cases
- Guidance for both main agents and sub-agents

### 5. Programmatic Evaluation
**File**: `packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/evaluations/programmatic/evaluators/agent-prompt.ts`

- Enhanced evaluator to flag violations

title: Fix: Clarify 403 Forbidden error message to include validation errors
body:
### Description

This PR updates the generic error message displayed for HTTP 403 (Forbidden) responses.

### Why is this change needed?

The previous error message was:
`"Forbidden - perhaps check your credentials?"`

This message was misleading because it *only* suggested an authentication or permissions issue. However, our application also returns a 403 status code for certain request validation failures (e.g., when a user submits text that exceeds the maximum allowed length).

This caused confusion, as users were led to believe they had a credential problem when the actual issue was with the content of their request.

### What did this change do?

I've updated the error string to be more comprehensive and guide the user toward both potential causes.

**Old Message:**
`"Forbidden - perhaps check your credentials?"`

**New Message:**
`"Forbidden. Access denied. This may be due to insufficient permissions or a request validation error (e.g., text length)."`

This new message now correctly informs the user that a 403 can be triggered by *either* a permissions issue or a data validation rule, improving the user experience and reducing troubleshooting time.

title: Fix NIM incompatibility with empty content
body:
## Summary

### Problem
n8n AI Agents fail when using NVIDIA's OpenAI-compatible API (and potentially other strict APIs) with tool calling enabled. The workflow fails with a `400 Bad Request` error after the LLM decides to call a tool.

**Root Cause:** When LangChain creates an `AIMessage` with `tool_calls`, it sets the `content` field to an empty string `""`. While OpenAI's API accepts this, NVIDIA's API strictly validates and requires `content` to have at least 1 character, returning:
```
"String should have at least 1 character"
```

### Solution
This PR adds two fixes:

1. **HTTP-level content fix in `LmChatOpenAi.node.ts`**: Intercepts fetch requests and replaces empty `content: ""` with a single space `content: " "` in assistant messages that contain `tool_calls`. This happens at the HTTP level, ensuring compatibility regardless of which LangChain method is invoked.

2. **Proper message formatting in `N8nLlmTracing.ts`**: Adds `handleChatModelStart` method to correctly process `BaseMessage[][]` from LangChain's chat models, ensuring messages are logged as structured objects rather than concatenated strings.

### Testing
1. Set up an AI Agent (v2.2+) with NVIDIA API endpoint
2. Add an HTTP Request Tool to the agent
3. Execute workflow that triggers tool calling
4. **Before fix**: Fails with 400 error
5. **After fix**: Successfully completes with tool calls

**Example curl to test directly:**
```bash
# ❌ Fails with empty content
curl -X POST "https://<nvidia-endpoint>/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <api-key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "nvidia/llama-3-3-nemotron-super-49b-v1-5",
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": "",
        "tool_calls": [
          {
            "id": "test",
            "type": "function",
            "function": {
              "name": "test",
              "arguments": "{}"
            }
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "role": "tool",
        "content": "result",
        "tool_call_id": "test"
      }
    ]
  }'

# ✅ Works with space in content
curl -X POST "https://<nvidia-endpoint>/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <api-key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "nvidia/llama-3-3-nemotron-super-49b-v1-5",
    "messages": [
      {
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": " ",
        "tool_calls": [
          {
            "id": "test",
            "type": "function",
            "function": {
              "name": "test",
              "arguments": "{}"
            }
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "role": "tool",
        "content": "result",
        "tool_call_id": "test"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

### Files Changed
- `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/llms/LMChatOpenAi/LmChatOpenAi.node.ts` - HTTP-level content fix
- `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/llms/N8nLlmTracing.ts` - Message formatting fix
- `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/llms/N8nNonEstimatingTracing.ts` - Message formatting fix
- `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/agents/Agent/agents/ToolsAgent/common.ts` - Helper functions
- `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/agents/Agent/agents/ToolsAgent/V2/execute.ts` - Apply fix in agent execution
- `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/agents/Agent/agents/ToolsAgent/V3/execute.ts` - Apply fix in agent execution

title: feat(API): Add optional projectId parameter to credential creation
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

Previously, [credentials created via the Public API](https://docs.n8n.io/api/api-reference/#tag/credential/post/credentials) were always saved to the user's personal project.
This change adds an optional projectId parameter to the POST /credentials endpoint, allowing credentials to be created in any project where the user has credential:create permission.

The implementation follows [the pattern used in the REST API credential creation endpoint](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/a2efb1fe7e0a8963ac68f82d96a4027ad77b0598/packages/cli/src/credentials/credentials.service.ts#L397-L454).
If projectId is not provided, the credential is saved to the user's personal project, maintaining backward compatibility.

title: feat(Anthropic Chat Model Node): Add automatic prompt caching for system messages
body:
## Summary

  Enables Anthropic's prompt caching feature for all system messages when using the Anthropic Chat Model node. This automatically adds `cache_control` markers to system prompts, reducing costs by up to 90% and latency by up to 85%
  for repeated calls.

  ## Changes

  - Wraps ChatAnthropic model's `invoke` method to inject `cache_control` into system messages
  - No user configuration required - works automatically
  - Added comprehensive unit tests (9 test cases, 386 lines)

  ## Benefits

  - **90% cost reduction** on cached input tokens (cache reads are 10x cheaper than regular input)
  - **85% latency reduction** for repeated calls with the same system prompt
  - **Zero configuration** - automatically enabled for all Anthropic workflows
  - **Universal benefit** - helps AI Agent nodes with large system prompts, multi-turn conversations, and any workflow with static system messages

  ## Technical Details

  **Cache Implementation:**
  - Type: ephemeral (5-minute TTL, refreshed on each use)
  - Minimum: 1024 tokens for Sonnet/Opus, 2048 for Haiku models
  - Compatible with all Claude models (Opus 4.1, Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, etc.)
  - No beta header required (prompt caching is GA since December 2024)

  **Code Example:**
  ```typescript
  // Automatically converts:
  new SystemMessage("You are a helpful assistant")

  // To:
  {
    type: 'text',
    text: 'You are a helpful assistant',
    cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' }
  }

  Testing

  - Added promptCaching.test.ts with 9 comprehensive test cases
  - Covers: string content, array content, multiple messages, edge cases
  - Follows testing patterns from PR #20253 and #20484
  - All tests use proper mocking and assertion patterns

  Related

  - Closes #13231 (community request for system prompt caching)
  - Related to PR #20484 (AI Workflow Builder uses similar caching strategy)
  - Anthropic docs: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/prompt-caching

  Checklist

  - Code follows n8n style guide
  - TypeScript compliance (no ts-ignore)
  - Comprehensive tests included
  - Small, focused PR (single feature)
  - Proper commit message format
  - No breaking changes

title: feat(core): Add programmatic workflow validation in AI workflow builder
body:
## Summary

This PR adds programmatic workflow validation capabilities to the AI workflow builder agent. The validation system runs automated checks against workflows to detect critical issues and provide feedback to the AI agent.

### Key Changes

1. **New `validate_workflow` tool** - Allows the AI agent to validate workflows programmatically during the building process
2. **Programmatic evaluation** - Extracted and modularized evaluation logic:
  - Checks providing list of violations, now used both in `validate_workflow` tool and as part of evaluation process (moved to `src/`)
  - Calculating scores (left in `evaluations/`)
3. **Expression context refactoring** - Refactored expression evaluation context initialization
4. **Connections resolution** - Now uses expression evaluation instead of temporary `Function` constructor approach used before
5. **Prompt changes** - Instruct main agent to run validation after making changes to the workflow

### How it works

The agent can now call `validate_workflow()` after making changes to ensure the workflow is valid. The tool:
- Runs all programmatic checks against the current workflow
- Returns errors for critical or major violations
- This helps the agent to self-correct issues before finalizing workflows

title: feat(core): Support stopping AI message generation on chat hub (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

This PR adds endpoint for stopping AI message generation by `messageId` + `sessionId` on the backend.  The execution is cancelled and stops immediately, and the code handling the execution marks it as cancelled.

To support this we now save AI messages in `"running"` state (renamed from pending) as soon as they're created, with empty contents. This links the message to the execution, and this way we can find it with messageId + sessionId and stop it.

This solution lacks the capability to save the partial message - the partially generated response isn't available on the execution data. I'm considering some hacky way to observer the streamed messages that execution engine is sending to the FE on the backend, but I'll explore that in a followup.

On the UI I made the send button change to a stop button while streaming is in progress. On cancel the stream reports an error, so I made UI to not do that if there's no streaming message anymore - essentially ignoring any errors that happen after we stop streaming.

title: feat(core): Limit chat history context window length with a map of limits (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Add a map of context window size limits by model and use that map to trim chat history context window to sizes that fit the models we use. If the limit is set to `0` or if the mapping is missing for the model used no trimming is applied, meaning that eventually the conversation will break once user hits these limits.

The trimming is done by a new mechanism on tools agent node that I added.

This trimming is quick when context window is small, but might take like ~300ms on large context window - better than erroring though.

This seems like a bit of a pain to maintain, but realistically our users will probably only hit this on the models with small context windows, all modern models seem to have plenty large limits.

Later on maybe we want this value to be configurable by conversation - I think the billing by these LLM providers is also by input token, and large context window burns tokens.

title: #18883: Wordpress - Add automatic fallback for non-pretty permalinks
body:
## Summary

The WordPress node now automatically handles both pretty and non-pretty permalink configurations. When a request to `/wp-json/` returns a 404 error, the node automatically retries using the `/?rest_route=` format, which works universally across all WordPress permalink settings.

**Before**: WordPress node only worked with pretty permalinks enabled (requires mod_rewrite/nginx configuration)

**After**: WordPress node works with any permalink configuration automatically - no user configuration needed

### Testing

1. **With pretty permalinks**: Configure WordPress credentials with pretty permalinks enabled → Request succeeds using `/wp-json/wp/v2/...`

2. **With plain permalinks**: Configure WordPress credentials with plain permalinks → Initial `/wp-json/` request fails with 404 → Automatically retries with `/?rest_route=/wp/v2/...` → Request succeeds

3. **Edge cases**: Trailing slashes normalized correctly, non-404 errors don't retry, proper error messages when both formats fail

title: refactor(ai-builder): Refactor prompt caching evals
body: ## Summary This PR consolidated prompt caching metrics into main evaluation flows (CLI and LangSmith), removes redundant cache-quality testing infrastructure, and eliminated cost calculations to support dynamic model usage. ## Changes ### 1. Security: Removed Vulnerable File Logger Deleted `evaluations/utils/cache-logger.ts` which had several issues: - Path traversal vulnerability in constructor where `testCaseId` parameter was used unsanitized in file path construction - Buffered all log entries in memory until manual `flush()`, causing potential memory pressure - Per-message cache stats were only used by a single specialized script ### 2. Consolidated Cache Metrics into Main Evaluation Flows Cache stats were already being captured but only displayed when running the specialized `test-cache-quality.ts` script. Now cache statistics are displayed by default in all evaluation runs. #### CLI Runner (`cli/runner.ts`, `cli/display.ts`) - Added `--repetitions N` flag for cache warming analysis - Added `displayCacheStatistics()` call to show cache metrics after every run - When `repetitions > 1`: - Runs all tests N times sequentially - Displays cache hit rate progression after each repetition - Shows final aggregated results from last repetition #### LangSmith Runner (`langsmith/evaluator.ts`, `langsmith/runner.ts`) Fixed bug where field mapping used wrong source key (`cache_create_input_tokens` instead of `cache_creation_input_tokens`). This caused cache creation tokens to always be `undefined`, resulting in incorrectly calculated cache hit rates Added new LangSmith metrics: - `totalPromptTokens`: Sum of all input token types (addresses confusion about low input token counts) - `cacheHitRate`: Calculated cache hit rate as percentage (0-1 scale) with descriptive comment Cleaned up verbose console logging. #### Display Enhancements (`utils/evaluation-reporter.ts`) Enhanced `displayCacheStatistics()` to show aggregate table with total tokens and overall cache hit rate, plus a per-test breakdown showing individual cache performance for each test case. Hit rates are color-coded: green for >60%, yellow for 30-60%, and red for <30%. Also removed `results` parameter from `displaySummaryTable()` since it's no longer needed. ### 3. Removed Cost Calculations Models will be dynamic (not just Anthropic Claude), making hardcoded pricing misleading. Removed: - `PRICING` constants with Anthropic-specific pricing - `calculateCostSavings()` function - `calculateCacheEffectiveness()` function (combined hit rate + cost savings) - `estimatedCostSavings` field from `CacheStatistics` interface - "Cost Savings" columns from CLI tables and markdown reports - Cost calculation tests from `cache-analyzer.test.ts` ### 4. Deleted Redundant Cache Eval Deleted `evaluations/test-cache-quality.ts` (381 lines). This specialized script is now unnecessary because cache metrics are displayed in standard evaluation runs, the `--repetitions` flag enables cache warming analysis in both modes, and per-test breakdown provides equivalent insight without additional tooling. Also removed the `eval:cache` npm script from `package.json`. ### 5. Unified CLI Arguments Both CLI and LangSmith modes now support `--repetitions N` flag via `index.ts`. Previously only LangSmith had this support. ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts ## Review / Merge checklist - [ ] PR title and summary are descriptive. This adds unnecessary noise to debug logs when developers are trying to debug n8n itself, not the telemetry libraries.

For chatbots, always make sure the chatbot has access to relevant data from the rest of the workflow, if the user requests a workflow that collects data and then wishes to chat with it as well. 2. For forms, always store the raw form response somewhere for administration purposes. 3. Consider memory limitations during data extraction. 4. How to build multi-step forms. 5. For scraping, recommend using scraping providers like Apify rather than attempting to scrape sites directly and breaking ToS. There are many other best practices which can all be found as markdown in the best practices directory of the tools. Categorisation is based on the following list: https://linear.app/n8n/issue/AI-1559/feature-prompt-categorization-prioritise-techniques, prioritisation of the techniques can also be seen here. ## Technical This has been implemented as two tools: 1. ` categorize-prompt.tool.ts` - this attempts to pick the applicable techniques involved in the prompt and provides a confidence (confidence is not currently used, but helps for evaluation) 2. `get-best-practices.tool.ts` - this tool provides documentation based on a provided list of techniques. A new evaluator has also been added `best-practices-evaluator.ts` which categorizes the prompt, fetches applicable best practices and then attempts to assess whether the generated workflow follows these practices. This is quite difficult to do as best practices can be subjective, I think evaluating against a gold sample in future could be a good method of capturing and evaluating the subjective nature. I have also created a new style of test for the categorization chain, `chains/test/integration/prompt-categorization.integration.test.ts` - this test can be used to run the categorization chain by itself against a real model. It is *not* evaluating the quality of its output but instead confirming that it roughly conforms to expectations. ## Examples Below is an example of a prompt that was performing poorly before best practices, around forms (info capturing on [Notion](https://www.notion.so/n8n/Fails-at-multi-step-forms-24e5b6e0c94f800ebadbc8577fee63b4?source=copy_link)) Before: After: In the before, we can see that it doesn't create a multi-step form as requested and it disconnects the notion information from the workflow. In the second example, there is multiple form nodes, it has disabled n8n attribution as per best practices and the notion information for building the forms is correctly connected. ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. title: fix(benchmark): Autodiscover runners container
body:
## Summary

We have multiple benchmarking docker composes where the n8n container defines its dependencies and we start them all up by [starting up only n8n](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/a4264f077dfc412a4571e7fab5165411449c5ec0/packages/%40n8n/benchmark/scripts/run-for-n8n-setup.mjs#L86). 

But exceptionally, setups may have 1+ runners containers that depend on n8n (not the other way round), so the benchmarking docker composes are not starting up runners containers, breaking benchmarks that rely on Code nodes.

This fix auto-discovers runners containers and starts them up as well, if needed.

Tested via:

```sh
pnpm benchmark-locally \
	--n8nTag=1.115.3 \
	--scenarioFilter js-code-node \ # or py-code-node
	--runDir /tmp/n8n-data \
	postgres # or scaling-single-main, etc.
```

Notes: 
- If you don't pass in an n8n tag, you'll fall back to `latest` and get an error saying that there's no `latest` tag for the runners image. I addressed this at #20802 but we need to wait until next Monday for it to become available.
- This relies on the new `--scenarioFilter` flag which I added yesterday at #20804 which is now in `ghcr.io/n8n-io/n8n-benchmark:latest` so make sure to pull this first.
- I fixed worker initialization at #20495 so if you happen to test below 1.115.1 it's expected that benchmarks for scaling setups will fail.

## Summary

Two fixes for task stopping:

- When canceling a running task, we call `stop_process()` which contains `process.join(timeout=1)` which blocks the event loop for up to 1 second. Follow-up to #19740

title: Fix data table unresponsive with large string cells
body: ## Summary This PR fixes a critical bug where the Data Tables UI becomes unresponsive and breaks layout when a single string cell contains a very large value (e.g., ~1.6–2 MB HTML content). The solution implements bounded, safe rendering for string cells: * **Truncation**: Large string values (over 1000 characters) are truncated to 300 characters in the table cell, with an ellipsis and a "View full" button. * **Full View Modal**: A new `ViewFullStringModal` allows users to view the complete, scrollable content of large strings without affecting table layout or performance. * **HTML Escaping**: All string content is now rendered as escaped text (never as HTML markup) to prevent XSS vulnerabilities and layout issues. * **Layout Stability**: CSS is applied to cap cell height and prevent overflow, ensuring the table remains responsive and all rows are visible. * **Editor Behavior**: The large text editor (`.ag-large-text-input`) now has a `max-height` and `overflow-y: auto` to prevent it from expanding indefinitely. **To test**: 1. Create a Data Table with a string column. 2. Insert a very large string (e.g., >1.7 MB, like an entire HTML 404 page or ~6,500 lines) into a cell. 3. Open the table with pagination in a Chrome-based browser. 4. Verify that: * The table remains responsive. * All rows are visible, and headers/pagination are clickable. * The large string cell displays truncated text with a "View full" button. * Clicking "View full" opens a modal displaying the full, scrollable content as plain text. * The copy-to-clipboard functionality in the modal works. * Editing a large string in-cell opens a fixed-height, scrollable textarea. ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts closes https://linear.app/n8n/issue/ADO-4256 ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. - [ ] [Docs updated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs) or follow-up ticket created. - [x] Tests included. - [ ] PR Labeled with `release/backport` (if the PR is an urgent fix that needs to be backported) ---

title: fix(nodes-base): SendGrid credentials test uses /scopes instead of marketing endpoint to avoid false 403 (credentials without Marketing scope)
body:
Summary

Change SendGrid credentials test endpoint from /marketing/contacts to /scopes to avoid false 403 for API keys without Marketing Campaigns scope.

Problem
- The current credential test hits /marketing/contacts, which requires Marketing permissions. Many SendGrid API keys are scoped only for Mail Send, so the test returns 403 and n8n displays a misleading credentials error.

Change details
- Updated file: packages/nodes-base/credentials/SendGridApi.credentials.ts
- Changed test.request.url from /marketing/contacts to /scopes
- Authorization header remains Bearer <apiKey> via existing credentials config
- No runtime changes to SendGrid node requests or behavior

Rationale
- /scopes is a minimal, safe endpoint that returns the API key scopes and is accessible with any valid API key, independent of Marketing Campaigns scope. This avoids false negatives during credential testing.

Reproduction (before)
1) Create a SendGrid API key without Marketing Campaigns permissions (e.g., Mail Send only).
2) Configure SendGrid credentials in n8n and click Test.
3) Result: 403 Forbidden → n8n shows "Forbidden - perhaps check your credentials?" despite a valid key.

Expected (after)
- Testing the same credentials should succeed because /scopes doesn’t require Marketing permissions.

Testing
- Lint passes locally via pre-commit hook.
- Manual check: GET https://api.sendgrid.com/v3/scopes with a Bearer key returns 200 with scopes for valid keys.

Impact
- No breaking changes.
- Only the credential test endpoint is adjusted; actual node operations (Mail/Marketing) remain unchanged and still require appropriate SendGrid scopes at execution time.

Docs
- No docs changes needed. Existing docs remain accurate; this reduces confusion in the credentials test.

Checklist
- [x] Small, focused PR
- [x] Lint/format pass
- [x] Clear rationale and testing notes
- [ ] Additional automated tests (not applicable here; behavior unchanged at runtime)

## Summary
Fixes the issue where editing a cell in the Data Table only updates the edited field, leaving dependent columns like `updated_at` stale until page reload.

After a cell value change:
- Calls `updateRow` with the new data.
- Immediately fetches the full updated row via `fetchRowById` to get server-generated fields (e.g., new `updatedAt` timestamp).
- Replaces the local row in `rowData` with the fresh data.
- Triggers `setGridData` to refresh the AG Grid view.

This ensures the UI reflects backend changes without requiring a full page reload.

title: fix(core): Prevent duplicate nodeExecuteBefore events for agent nodes
body:
## Summary

Fixes agent nodes showing stuck spinner in the UI due to duplicate `nodeExecuteBefore` events. 

**Problem**: When AI agent nodes pause execution to run tool nodes and then resume with tool results, they were emitting `nodeExecuteBefore` twice (initial + resume) but `nodeExecuteAfter` only once. This caused the frontend's execution tracking queue to become unbalanced, leaving spinners stuck in "executing" state.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9abc831c-0e68-499c-9286-6abf4903a3a1



**Solution**: Skip the `nodeExecuteBefore` hook when an agent node resumes execution after tool completion by setting and checking a `nodeWasResumed` metadata flag.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3377fbef-2a94-4c13-ab8c-aaf9fc0e12b0




**Key changes**:
- Added `nodeWasResumed` flag to `ITaskMetadata` interface (optional for backward compatibility)
- Modified `handleRequest()` in `requests-response.ts` to set `nodeWasResumed: true` when re-scheduling agent node
- Updated `workflow-execute.ts` to skip `nodeExecuteBefore` hook if `nodeWasResumed` is true
- Added test verifying correct 1:1 pairing of before/after events
- Added JSDoc for both `nodeWasResumed` and `preserveSourceOverwrite` properties

title: fix(ai-builder): Assistant side panel open without blocking calls
body:
## Summary

With the addition of the empty state to the builder side panel the opening of the panel had to be blocking. Since we load the messages when the panel opens we needed to know if there were messages to decide whether or not to show the empty state. This did however mean that the opening of the panel was blocking and could lead to some lag, it felt somewhat unpleasant.

To solve this, we now have a call to check if there are any messages currently for a workflow (endpoint POST `/sessions/metadata`) that occurs when the canvas/workflow loads. This means that we can open the panel immediately as we know whether or not we need to open the empty state already - messages can load in once they are available.

Ticket: https://linear.app/n8n/issue/AI-1525/t2w-add-loading-state-to-builder-side-panel

title: fix(core): Retain source overwrite in paired items in tool executions
body:
## Summary

  This PR fixes an issue with paired item data lineage in AI tool executions by conditionally preserving sourceOverwrite metadata when tools are
  invoked by agents.

## Changes

### Core Changes

  - packages/core/src/execution-engine/workflow-execute.ts: Added conditional logic to preserve sourceOverwrite in paired items when
  preserveSourceOverwrite metadata flag is set
  - packages/core/src/execution-engine/requests-response.ts: Enhanced tool execution setup to:
    - Propagate sourceOverwrite from parent node to tool input
    - Add preserveSourceOverwrite: true metadata flag for tool executions
    - Properly track parent node ancestry chain (previousNode, previousNodeOutput, previousNodeRun)

### Type Changes

  - packages/workflow/src/interfaces.ts: Added preserveSourceOverwrite?: boolean field to metadata interface

### Testing

  - packages/core/src/execution-engine/__tests__/workflow-execute-process-process-run-execution-data.test.ts:
    - Added comprehensive test coverage for sourceOverwrite preservation in tool execution scenarios (DataNode → AgentNode → ToolNode)
    - Added test for sourceOverwrite behavior in loop scenarios
    - Simplified and cleaned up test assertions (removed ~50+ lines of verbose comments)

## Problem Solved

  When AI agents invoke tools, the tools need to access data from nodes that executed before the agent (e.g., a Data node). Previously, the paired
  item chain would break at the agent node, preventing tools from resolving expressions like $('DataNode').item.json.field.

  This PR ensures that sourceOverwrite is conditionally preserved for tool executions (identified by the preserveSourceOverwrite metadata flag),
  allowing tools to traverse the full ancestry chain back to pre-agent nodes while avoiding incorrect retention in other scenarios like loops.

title: fix(core): Proxy all HTTP traffic instead of only axios
body:
## Summary

Implements HTTP proxy support for all Node.js HTTP traffic using `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`, and `NO_PROXY` environment variables.

**Previous implementation**: Proxy support was limited to n8n's request utilities (`httpRequest`) and axios requests via interceptors.

**This PR**: Extends proxy support to all native Node.js `http`/`https` requests by configuring global agents, including third-party libraries like `rss-parser` used by the RSS Read node.

- Configures global `http.globalAgent` and `https.globalAgent` with proxy support
- Respects standard proxy environment variables and `NO_PROXY` exclusions

### Limitations

Some requests may still bypass the proxy:
- Libraries using alternative HTTP clients (e.g., `undici`)
- Libraries explicitly overriding the default agent

### Testing

1. Set up local proxy (e.g., tinyproxy)
2. Test with various combinations of `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`
3. Verify RSS Read node and other HTTP-dependent nodes respect proxy settings
4. Confirm `NO_PROXY` patterns work correctly

title: fix(Postgres Node): Correct UPSERT parameterization to avoid duplicate placeholders
body: ## Summary This PR fixes malformed SQL generation in the Postgres v2 upsert operation. The previous implementation reused the same placeholder index for different purposes, producing invalid parameterized queries that could cause protocol errors. ## Problem The upsert builder generated queries like: ```sql INSERT INTO $1:name.$2:name($4:name) VALUES($4:csv) ON CONFLICT ($3:name) DO UPDATE SET ... ``` **Issues:** 1. **Duplicate parameter index**: `$4` was used both as `:name` (for column identifiers) and `:csv` (for values), violating pg-promise formatting rules 2. **Non-sequential numbering**: Placeholders appeared out of order ($1, $2, $4, $3) 3. **Inconsistent column ordering** This resulted in "invalid message format" or protocol errors in certain environments. ## Solution The fix ensures: - **Unique placeholders**: Each parameter gets a distinct index - `$3:name` → column identifiers - `$4:csv` → row values - `$5:name`, `$6:name`, ... → conflict columns and SET pairs - **Sequential ordering**: Parameters are numbered in logical order (1, 2, 3, 4, ...) - **Deterministic column order**: Matching columns appear first, then remaining columns **After:** ```sql INSERT INTO $1:name.$2:name($3:name) VALUES($4:csv) ON CONFLICT ($5:name, $6:name) DO UPDATE SET $7:name = $8, $9:name = $10 RETURNING ... ``` ## Changes - Updated `packages/nodes-base/nodes/Postgres/v2/actions/database/upsert.operation.ts` - Modified parameter array construction to maintain unique, sequential indices - Ensured compliance with pg-promise formatting semantics (`:name` for identifiers, `:csv` for value lists) - Updated test expectations in `packages/nodes-base/nodes/Postgres/v2/test/operations.test.ts` ## Testing - ✅ All existing tests pass with updated expectations (using pnpm test) - ✅ Verified correct placeholder numbering and separation - ✅ Confirmed deterministic column ordering - ✅ "Match on all columns" correctly generates `DO NOTHING` with proper conflict list ## Related Issues Fixes #20122 (malformed parameterization in Postgres upsert) ## Backward Compatibility - No changes to MySQL or SQLite code paths - Upsert semantics (`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE/DO NOTHING`) remain unchanged - Query results are identical; only internal SQL generation is corrected ### Corrected SQL Query (from logs) ### Working n8n Workflow:

## Summary

The AI workflow builder now receives all expressions from workflow nodes along with their resolved values. This helps the agent detect when expressions aren't resolving properly, even when execution appears successful.

  - Trims values to 200 characters max
  - Groups by node name

- **useAIAssistantHelpers.test.ts** - Added 10 tests using mocked `resolveExpression`

- **ai.controller.ts** - Pass `expressionValues` through to workflow builder service
- **workflow-builder-agent.ts** - Updated `ChatPayload` interface with `expressionValues`

{

}

title: fix(core): Fix broker websocket connection closure on runner heartbeat failure
body:
## Summary

Came across [this high-frequency report](https://n8nio.sentry.io/issues/6386727022) on Sentry.

When the broker detects a runner heartbeat failure, the broker is currently sending status code 1005 in a ws close frame, which is causing the `ws` library to throw.

But [RFC 6455](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455) says:

>1005 is a reserved value and MUST NOT be set as a status code in a Close control frame by an endpoint.  It is designated for use in applications expecting a status code to indicate that no status code was actually present.

So 1005 is a used to represent the absence of a status code. It's never sent over the wire, only exists at the application layer to distinguish between "no code sent" vs "code n sent"

Hence this PR switches to `CloseProtocolError` on heartbeat failure. From my reading of the RFC, heartbeat failure is a protocol violation error:

>1002 indicates that an endpoint is terminating the connection due to a protocol error. [...] Upon receipt of a Ping frame, an endpoint MUST send a Pong frame in response, unless it already received a Close frame.

title: Fix: Prevent workflow crash caused by missing fields in execution data
body:
## Summary

This PR prevents a runtime calculation error that can occur when ```ctx.runData.startedAt``` is missing.
In production, this issue caused a TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getTime') when the system attempted to process incomplete run data (in my case, during initialization, but it can happen at any point where unfinished executions are recovered or processed).

Previously, the condition only verified ```ctx.runData.stoppedAt```, which allowed ```startedAt``` to be ```null``` and led to the crash.
The fix adds a safeguard to ensure both values are defined before calculating runtime:

```ts
if (ctx.runData.stoppedAt && ctx.runData.startedAt) {
///
```

title: fix(core): Solve intermittent typeorm-related build errors for `QueryDeepPartialEntity`
body:
## Summary

My understanding is that these [intermittent typeorm-related build errors](https://gist.github.com/ivov/ecc7606837a388b853b4209a90a6bc3b) have two causes:

### 1. Infinite recursion due to circular types

TypeScript hits the recursion depth limit when resolving types for entities in a circular type relationship, namely for `QueryDeepPartialEntity` which types the arg to the `insert`, `upsert`, `update` methods on entities and transaction managers. This infinite recursion issue was solved [here](https://github.com/n8n-io/typeorm/pull/28). (Another approach would have been adding [`Relation<T>`](https://github.com/n8n-io/typeorm/blob/0f1567dd8fa1b6a2db4608441364c171d2ee0aa7/src/common/RelationType.ts) everywhere, but it looks easy to forget to use. Our entities currently use this type only ever once.) This PR removes all the now unneeded type exemptions that we had in place.

### 2. Excessively deep type instantiation

TypeScript fails to resolve entity types for `QueryDeepPartialEntity` because our entity field types are part of a massive type hierarchy. This is solved in this PR using `ISimplifiedPinData` for `ExecutionData.workflowData` to cut short a type hierarchy that would otherwise contain the whole of `INodeExecutionData`. Practically speaking, we rarely if ever need access to deeply nested properties inside the pindata inside the workflow that is inside execution data, so this is reasonably safe. But simplifying pindata is a workaround; the root fix is interrogating all the types that we use for all entity fields, e.g. it's unclear why we have `WorkflowEntity`, `IWorkflowDb` and `IWorkflowBase`, but that overhaul would be a big effort beyond the scope of this PR. Notice also that `ISimplifiedPinData` exists and is [already in use](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/9d4db4b658fb0d2632db97a0de68a919b9dfd54f/packages/%40n8n/db/src/entities/workflow-entity.ts#L98) before this PR, likely because this issue has come up before.

I tested this PR by running `pnpm reset` and then making harmless changes in various backend packages and rebuilding the monorepo multiple times, with no build errors.

title: fix: Chat side panel open/close behaviour and builder state accuracy (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Issues discussed in detail and video of some of these problems shown in issue: https://linear.app/n8n/issue/AI-1515/bug-t2w-side-panel-behaviour-closing-in-overview-toggling-correctly

There were a couple of core issues which I kept coming across when working on the blank states changes, primarily around the fact that the `assistant.store.ts` and the `builder.store.ts` both independently stored state around whether the chat panel is open or not - therefore I created a new store which could handle this information independently and look after keeping the assistant and builder stores accurate.

This allows for a single location the chat panel is opened from, with options for opening the builder or the assistant. The state has been broken out into another very small store (literally just the state) so that the builder and assistant stores can utilise the state without encountering cyclic issues. The chat panel store needs to access the builder/assistant stores to reset and update state when they are opening.

This fixes a few issues that were encountered:
1. The panel not toggling correctly, previous to this PR there were scenarios were toggling the chat panel between ask/build would mean that it couldn't be toggled closed, as the stores had independent state about whether it was open and its hard to know which store to call to close it.
2. The panel staying open in locations it is not allowed - the assistant can be open in a few more views than the builder, the builder is restricted to the editable canvas; because of this the builder could sometimes end up open in places that it wasn't intended to be open as the assistant state is keeping it open.
3. Builder state getting carried over into other canvases, due to the assistant staying open the builder state wasn't always correctly updated, the new chat panel store keeps track of the route and can reset the builder store state if entering a new canvas.
4. Hiding the toggle for ask/build when the panel is open in a view that should not have access to the build chat - while the new chat panel store will close the builder if it is opened somewhere it is not meant to be, it is a weird UX to click the toggle and have the panel close.

Finally, I have moved a lot of the logic that pertains to the assistant/builder panel into the features directory, as some of the builder logic had already been moved there and it seems like a good location to contain everything related to the assistant/builder chat experience.

This PR adds real-time streaming of execution progress information via Server-Sent Events (SSE), with a focus on AI agent transparency and tool call visibility.
**Key Changes:**
- **Tool Call Streaming**: AI agents now emit `tool-call-start` and `tool-call-end` chunks when invoking tools, providing real-time visibility into agent actions
- **Node Execution Streaming**: All nodes emit `node-execute-before` and `node-execute-after` chunks, enabling detailed workflow execution tracking
- **Workflow Lifecycle Chunks**: Workflow execution now emits `begin` and `end` chunks to clearly mark execution boundaries
- **Enhanced Metadata**: Chunks now include `nodeType` in addition to `nodeId` and `nodeName` for better context
- **Flexible Metadata Structure**: Metadata fields are now optional where appropriate, allowing different chunk types to include relevant information

**What This Enables:**
- Users can see which tools AI agents are calling in real-time without opening the n8n UI
- Custom UIs can display live agent reasoning and tool usage
- Better debugging of agentic workflows through transparency
- Improved UX for customer-facing AI applications built with n8n

title: fix(core): Fix worker setup completion
body:
## Summary

At #20219 I added an `await` when registering the job processing handler on the worker, in the understanding that the `Promise` returned by `Queue.prototype.process` represents registration completion, based on the [type definition](https://github.com/OptimalBits/bull/blob/489c6ab8466c1db122f92af3ddef12eacc54179e/index.d.ts#L583-L602).

This understanding was incorrect, as `Queue.prototype.process` triggers a chain of calls: `Queue.prototype.start` →  `Queue.prototype.run` → `Queue.prototype.processJobs` → `Queue.prototype._processJobOnNextTick` which eventually resolves [here](https://github.com/OptimalBits/bull/blob/489c6ab8466c1db122f92af3ddef12eacc54179e/lib/queue.js#L1140) only when the queue is closing, which means the `Promise` returned by `Queue.prototype.process` is intended for shutdown logic, not for registration completion.

This PR reverts the change at #20219.

title: feat(ai-builder): Optimize Anthropic prompt caching with 4-breakpoint strategy
body:
## Summary

Implements an optimized prompt caching strategy for the AI Workflow Builder using Anthropic's prompt caching feature. This reduces API costs while maintaining full functionality.

### Why This Change?

The AI Workflow Builder makes repeated API calls with similar conversation context. Without prompt caching, we were paying full price for reprocessing the same system prompts, node type schemas, and conversation history on every request. This resulted in unnecessarily high API costs, especially for longer conversations.

### What's Changed?

**Core Optimization (4-breakpoint caching strategy):**
- Implements maximum 4 cache breakpoints per Anthropic's API limits
- Cache breakpoint 1: System message (agent instructions and node schemas)
- Cache breakpoint 2: Previous conversation summary (when auto-compact is enabled)
- Cache breakpoint 3: Second-to-last message (previous turn's context)
- Cache breakpoint 4: Last message (current workflow state)

**Dynamic workflow context injection:**
- Workflow JSON, execution data, and node schemas are now injected dynamically into messages
- Previous messages have workflow context stripped to enable prefix matching for cache hits
- Auto-compact threshold increased from 20K to 180K tokens to allow better cache utilization

**Evaluation Framework:**
- Comprehensive testing suite to measure cache hit rates and cost savings
- Per-message cache statistics logging with visual indicators
- Cost calculation engine using Claude Sonnet 4 pricing model
- Environment-based configuration for different test scenarios

### Results

Empirical testing shows:
- **Cache hit rates: 80-85%** across typical workflow builder conversations
- **Measurable savings: $8.25** across 30 test runs in validation

### Testing

Run cache quality tests:
```bash
cd packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee
export N8N_AI_ANTHROPIC_KEY="your-api-key"
export CACHE_TEST_USE_BASIC_CASES=true
export CACHE_TEST_ITERATIONS=3
pnpm eval:cache
```

View detailed logs:
```bash
cat results/cache-logs/iteration-N/test-id.log
cat results/cache-quality-results-*.json
```

### Technical Details

**Files Changed:**
- `constants.ts` - Increased auto-compact threshold to 180K tokens
- `main-agent.prompt.ts` - Removed static workflow context from system message
- `workflow-builder-agent.ts` - Core caching implementation with dynamic context injection
- `evaluations/` - Complete testing framework for cache quality measurement

**Key Implementation Pattern:**
1. Strip workflow context from previous messages to enable prefix matching
2. Inject fresh workflow context only into the last message
3. Add cache breakpoints at strategic conversation boundaries
4. Use ephemeral cache control (5-minute TTL) for cost efficiency

title: fix: use chat_input field for HumanMessage content instead of content
body:
## Description
Fixed message mapping in chat history to correctly extract text content from HumanMessage objects.

## Problem
HumanMessage objects store their text content in `kwargs.chat_input`, while AIMessage objects use `kwargs.content`. The previous implementation only checked `kwargs.content` for all message types, causing human messages to display as undefined.

## Solution
Added conditional logic to check message type and extract text from the appropriate field:
- `HumanMessage`: use `kwargs.chat_input`
- `AIMessage`: use `kwargs.content`

## Changes
- Updated message mapping logic to handle different content field locations based on message type

## Proof - API Response Payload
The chat API returns messages with different structures for HumanMessage vs AIMessage:

title: ci: Fail release build on node popularity data fetch error
body:
## Summary

Node popularity data is being used to enhance node search ranking. It is fetched during the build process by the script `fetch-node-popularity.mjs`. When fetching up-to-date popularity data fails, fallback search ranking will be used, as this is not critical and we don't want to unnecessarily block CI pipelines and local dev builds when popularity data is unavailable for some reason.

Though, we want to make sure that **release builds** contain up-to-date popularity data.

This PR adds env variable that controls if the `fetch-node-popularity.mjs` script should fail in case of a fetch error, or silently ignore it.

  This PR adds support for configuring n8n's Source Control feature via environment variables, enabling easier deployment in containerized environments where configuration through environment variables is
  preferred over database settings.

  ### New Environment Variables

  - `N8N_SOURCECONTROL_REPOSITORY_URL` - Git repository URL (supports both SSH and HTTPS)
  - `N8N_SOURCECONTROL_HTTPS_USERNAME` - Username for HTTPS authentication
  - `N8N_SOURCECONTROL_HTTPS_PASSWORD` - Password or Personal Access Token for HTTPS authentication
  - `N8N_SOURCECONTROL_BRANCH_NAME` - Git branch name (defaults to 'main')
  - `N8N_SOURCECONTROL_BRANCH_READONLY` - Whether the branch should be read-only (defaults to false)

  ### Behavior

  - Environment variables are only used when **no database configuration exists**
  - Database settings take priority over environment variables once configured through the UI
  - When HTTPS credentials are provided via env vars, the connection type is automatically set to HTTPS
  - Source control is automatically initialized on startup when credentials are provided
  - SSH key loading is skipped when using HTTPS to avoid unnecessary errors

  ### Example Usage

  ```bash
  N8N_SOURCECONTROL_REPOSITORY_URL=https://github.com/user/repo.git \
  N8N_SOURCECONTROL_HTTPS_USERNAME=myusername \
  N8N_SOURCECONTROL_HTTPS_PASSWORD=ghp_myPersonalAccessToken \
  N8N_SOURCECONTROL_BRANCH_NAME=main \
  pnpm start

  Testing

  1. Start n8n with the environment variables set (ensure no existing source control configuration in database)
  2. Verify source control settings appear in UI under Settings > Source Control
  3. Verify connection type is set to HTTPS
  4. Verify repository operations (pull/push) work correctly
  5. Modify settings through UI and restart - verify database settings take precedence over env vars

title: fix(frontend): add timezone-aware UI date formatting (formatDateForUI) — fixes #20330
body:
…fixes #20330

# Summary :-

Adds `formatDateForUI`, a timezone-aware UI date formatter used by the frontend.  
If a `timeZone` (IANA) is provided, the function uses `Intl.DateTimeFormat` to render the date and time in that zone (e.g. `Asia/Beirut`). When no timezone is provided the code falls back to the existing `dateformat` behavior to remain backwards-compatible.

This fixes the display mismatch where stored UTC timestamps were being shown in the wrong local time in the UI.

# How to test its working :-

1. Run the frontend (or compile the single file) and call `formatDateForUI('2025-10-02T14:00:00Z', 'Asia/Beirut')`.
   - Expected: date `Oct 2` and time `5:00 PM` (Beirut)
2. Call without a timezone to ensure legacy behavior is unchanged:
   - `formatDateForUI('2025-10-02T14:00:00Z')` should use the existing formatting (no TZ conversion).
3. Try invalid/empty inputs: `null`, `''`, `invalid-string` — should return safe results (`{date:'', time:''}` or `Invalid Date` as appropriate).

title: fix(Slack Node): Prevent invalid array arg on team join
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a bug in the Slack Trigger node where `team_join` events with "Resolve IDs" enabled would fail with a Slack API error `invalid_array_arg`.

**Root Cause:**  
The `team_join` event payload from Slack includes a full user object at `event.user` (per [Slack's documentation](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/events/team_join/)). However, when "Resolve IDs" was enabled, the code attempted to pass this entire object to `getUserInfo()`, which expects a string user ID, causing the API error.

**Fix:**  
Added a specific branch for `team_join` events in the "Resolve IDs" logic. When the event type is `team_join`, we now extract the user's `name` property directly from the existing `event.user` object instead of making an unnecessary API call (that breaks) to `getUserInfo()`. 

**Testing:**  
- Edited test to test `team_join` event handling with `resolveIds` enabled

title: fix(form): Form Completion Page Redirect Not Working
body:
**Summary**
This PR fixes a bug where the Form Completion Page redirect did not work correctly. When a workflow was configured to redirect after form submission, users would see “Redirecting to [URL]” but the browser never navigated to the target URL.

**Problem:**
The Form node’s redirect functionality was failing when configured to redirect users after form submission. Users would see *“Redirecting to [URL]”* but the actual redirect would not occur.

**Root Cause:**
The `Content-Security-Policy` header was using the `sandbox` directive **without** `allow-same-origin`, which caused:

* The page to have `Origin: null` instead of the actual origin
* POST requests from the completion page to be treated as cross-site requests
* CORS errors blocking the request needed to trigger the redirect
* Silent failure of the redirect functionality

**Solution:**
Added `allow-same-origin` to the CSP sandbox directive in `formCompletionUtils.ts`.

Before:

```ts
const SANDBOX_CSP =
	'sandbox allow-downloads allow-forms allow-modals ...';
```

After:

```ts
const SANDBOX_CSP =
	'sandbox allow-same-origin allow-downloads allow-forms allow-modals ...';
```

**Impact:**

* ✅ Form completion redirects now work correctly
* ✅ No security degradation (`allow-same-origin` is safe for this use case)
* ✅ Fixes both development and production environments
* ✅ Works with all redirect types (URL redirect, show text, return binary)

**Testing:**
Reproduction steps before fix:

1. Create a workflow with *Form Trigger → Form → Form (completion node)*
2. Configure completion node with **Redirect to URL** option
3. Submit the form
4. Redirect fails (stuck on "Redirecting to..." page)

After fix:

* Same steps as above
* Form now successfully redirects to the configured URL

**Headers Changed:**

Before:

```
Origin: null
Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site
```

After:

```
Origin: http://localhost:5678
Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin
```

**Files Changed:**

* `packages/nodes-base/nodes/Form/utils/formCompletionUtils.ts`

title: fix(core): Only resume waiting parent workflows
body:
## Summary
When a sub-workflow completes after waiting, only resume the parent workflow if it was actually intended to be resumed.

Today when a child workflow resumes after waiting, we also set the parent workflow to be resumed once the child completes. This assumes that the parent is waiting, but this is a bad assumption:
1. If the parent was configured to not wait for the child, then the parent might already be completed. This throws an error. See attached ticket for more details.
2. If the parent was configured to not wait but had a _later_ Wait node, this is also a bug - we'll resume it when it shouldn't be resumed.

This change passes a flag to explicitly indicate whether the parent was configured to wait for the child. Only in that case should we resume the parent as soon as the child finishes.

Note: I tried simpler approaches like just explicitly checking whether the parent was waiting. This could resolve case 1 above, but didn't solve case 2. IMO the whole flow around waiting and resuming is somewhat convoluted, and would be tackled in a larger refactor.

title: fix(editor): Fix execution state race condition in AI Builder (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Fixes a race condition in the AI Builder's workflow execution watcher where the execution state was incorrectly reported as "running" even after the workflow finished executing.

## Root Cause

The execution watcher in `ExecuteMessage.vue` was monitoring `isWorkflowRunning` to detect when a workflow execution completes. However, there was a race condition where:

1. `isWorkflowRunning` would change to `false`
2. But `workflowExecutionData.status` was still `"running"` (not yet updated)

This caused the component to emit the `workflowExecuted` event while the execution state was still showing as "running", leading to incorrect state reporting in the AI Builder.

## Changes

### ExecuteMessage.vue
- Changed execution watcher to monitor `workflowExecutionData.status` directly instead of `isWorkflowRunning`
- Now only emits completion event when status is not `'running'` or `'waiting'`

### ExecuteMessage.test.ts
- Updated all tests to mock `workflowExecutionData.status` instead of `isWorkflowRunning`
- Added proper async handling with `flushPromises()` to account for async watcher callbacks

title: fix(core): Only resume the parent workflow if its actually waiting
body:
## Summary
Only resume the parent workflow if it's actually waiting.

Otherwise we get an error from the wait tracker that the workflow has already finished.

For some context: when we run a sub-workflow, the parent can be configured to block or not on the child. If the parent blocks, it remains running; until the child workflow goes into `waiting`, at which point we also put the parent into `waiting`. Therefore when the child wakes up we have to wake up the parent as well. **However** if the parent was configured not to block, then it was never waiting in the first place, and it never needed to be resumed.

Manually tested in two cases:
- The sub-workflow uses a webhook wait. Verify that there's no error when the webhook is called.
- The sub-workflow uses a 66-second wait. Verify that there's no error when the sub-workflow finishes. NOTE: 66s because for short waits under 65s we simply remain `running`. See the Wait node impl for the explanation.

title: fix(core): Check all outputs for chat triggers, first output only for webhooks
body:
## Summary

We recently changed how we extract the last node's response. Before it checked only the first main output to extract the response (e.g. for webhook or chat triggers with "lastNode" mode). Now it searches through all main outputs to find the first one with data.

This might introduce unwanted changes into existing webhook workflows.

We decided to keep this new behavior for chat triggers, but go back to the old behavior for webhooks.

**The difference:**

Chat triggers: Check all main outputs of the last executed node and use the first output that has data to extract the reply
Webhooks: Only check the very first output (like it used to work)

**How we're fixing it:**

This PR adds a new flag `checkAllMainOutputs` that controls which behavior to use based on whether the workflow was started by a webhook or a chat trigger.
