### form-data uses unsafe random function in form-data for choosing boundary
[CVE-2025-7783](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-7783) / [GHSA-fjxv-7rqg-78g4](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-fjxv-7rqg-78g4)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary

form-data uses `Math.random()` to select a boundary value for multipart form-encoded data. This can lead to a security issue if an attacker:
1. can observe other values produced by Math.random in the target application, and
2. can control one field of a request made using form-data

Because the values of Math.random() are pseudo-random and predictable (see: https://blog.securityevaluators.com/hacking-the-javascript-lottery-80cc437e3b7f), an attacker who can observe a few sequential values can determine the state of the PRNG and predict future values, includes those used to generate form-data's boundary value. The allows the attacker to craft a value that contains a boundary value, allowing them to inject additional parameters into the request.

This is largely the same vulnerability as was [recently found in `undici`](https://hackerone.com/reports/2913312) by [`parrot409`](https://hackerone.com/parrot409?type=user) -- I'm not affiliated with that researcher but want to give credit where credit is due! My PoC is largely based on their work.

##### Details

The culprit is this line here: https://github.com/form-data/form-data/blob/426ba9ac440f95d1998dac9a5cd8d738043b048f/lib/form_data.js#L347

An attacker who is able to predict the output of Math.random() can predict this boundary value, and craft a payload that contains the boundary value, followed by another, fully attacker-controlled field. This is roughly equivalent to any sort of improper escaping vulnerability, with the caveat that the attacker must find a way to observe other Math.random() values generated by the application to solve for the state of the PRNG. However, Math.random() is used in all sorts of places that might be visible to an attacker (including by form-data itself, if the attacker can arrange for the vulnerable application to make a request to an attacker-controlled server using form-data, such as a user-controlled webhook -- the attacker could observe the boundary values from those requests to observe the Math.random() outputs). A common example would be a `x-request-id` header added by the server. These sorts of headers are often used for distributed tracing, to correlate errors across the frontend and backend. `Math.random()` is a fine place to get these sorts of IDs (in fact, [opentelemetry uses Math.random for this purpose](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js/blob/2053f0d3a44631ade77ea04f656056a2c8a2ae76/packages/opentelemetry-sdk-trace-base/src/platform/node/RandomIdGenerator.ts#L22))

##### PoC

PoC here: https://github.com/benweissmann/CVE-2025-7783-poc

Instructions are in that repo. It's based on the PoC from https://hackerone.com/reports/2913312 but simplified somewhat; the vulnerable application has a more direct side-channel from which to observe Math.random() values (a separate endpoint that happens to include a randomly-generated request ID). 

##### Impact

For an application to be vulnerable, it must:
- Use `form-data` to send data including user-controlled data to some other system. The attacker must be able to do something malicious by adding extra parameters (that were not intended to be user-controlled) to this request. Depending on the target system's handling of repeated parameters, the attacker might be able to overwrite values in addition to appending values (some multipart form handlers deal with repeats by overwriting values instead of representing them as an array)
- Reveal values of Math.random(). It's easiest if the attacker can observe multiple sequential values, but more complex math could recover the PRNG state to some degree of confidence with non-sequential values. 

If an application is vulnerable, this allows an attacker to make arbitrary requests to internal systems.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: Unknown
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:H/SI:H/SA:N`

## Summary

When an instance recovers after a workflow crash, we track the number of executions affected using the pulse telemetry event.

To test this locally 

- Temporarily remove the prod check [here](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/packages/cli/src/crash-journal.ts#L24) 
- Reduce the frequency of the pulse event [here](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/packages/cli/src/telemetry/index.ts#L91)
- Create a new source in rudderstack and add the key [here](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/packages/%40n8n/config/src/configs/diagnostics.config.ts#L22)
- Set up a triggered workflow that runs every second (to ensure we have a bunch of workflows in queue) 
- When you have a few workflows in queue, kill the local server
- create the file `crash.journal` in your local `.n8n` directory 
- start the server again. 
- You should see the crashed workflows metric in rudderstack

title: fix(core): Support MCP server when offloading is enabled
body:
## Summary

Typically nothing should execute on main in queue mode with offloading enabled, so main should not need access to a runner. But it turns out that the MCP Server Trigger runs tools _from within the trigger itself_, which means that a main does need access to a runner if the MCP Server Trigger calls a Code node.

No context on why the MCP Server Trigger is set up like this - it strikes me any actual execution from a trigger (tool invocation or otherwise) should be enqueued and main should remain a producer. But rearchitecting this feature would be a dedicated effort, so for now we restore the runner on main even when offloading is enabled.

To test:
1. Create a workflow with an MCP server trigger and connect a Call n8n Workflow tool. Activate it.
2. Create a subworkflow with a Code node and configure the first workflow to call the second one.
3. Start a main in queue mode with `N8N_RUNNERS_MODE=internal` and `OFFLOAD_MANUAL_EXECUTIONS_TO_WORKERS=true`.
4. [Configure](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-langchain.mcptrigger/#integrating-with-claude-desktop) Claude Desktop to call the production webhook URL of the MCP Server Trigger.
5. Prompt Claude to call the n8n workflow.

title: fix(Discord Node): Prevent redundant URL wrapping for embed images in JSON mode
body: ## Summary ### Problem The Discord node's `prepareEmbeds` function always wraps the `image` field value in a `{url: ...}` object. This works correctly for "Enter Fields" mode where users input plain URL strings that need to be converted to Discord's required format. However, when using "Raw JSON" mode with properly formatted Discord embed objects `{image: {url: "..."}}`, the function incorrectly wraps them again, creating invalid nested structures `{image: {url: {url: "..."}}}`, causing Discord API errors. ### Solution This PR added type checking to only wrap string URLs into objects. When the `image` value is already an object from Raw JSON input, it's preserved as it is. This maintains compatibility with both input modes: strings from UI fields get wrapped, while pre-formatted objects from Raw JSON pass through unchanged. ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts Closes #16921 ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. title: feat(ModelSelector): Add predefined selection strategies and enhance custom rule handling
body:
## Summary

Adds a new selection mode to `Model Selector`:
- Default: **Custom Condition** (existing behavior).
- New: **Predefined Strategy → First Non-Failing Model**: automatically tries connected models in order until one succeeds, via `withFallbacks(...)`.

Also:
- UI: “Add Rule” → “Add Selection”, with “Custom Condition” as the default group.
- Backward compatible: existing `rules.rule` continue to work as custom conditions.
- Tracing preserved: selected and fallback models receive `N8nNonEstimatingTracing` and respect `N8nLlmTracing` parent run index.

How to test manually:
1. Connect 2+ LLM models to `Model Selector`.
2. In `Rules`, choose “Predefined Strategy → First Non-Failing Model”.
3. Feed downstream into a chain/agent node.
4. Make the first model fail (e.g., invalid credentials or intentionally bad config) and observe it falls back to the next model without failing the node.

Unit tests included:
- `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/ModelSelector/test/ModelSelector.node.test.ts`
  - Custom/legacy rule selection works and prioritizes custom.
  - Predefined strategy returns a model composed with fallbacks and is used when custom doesn’t match.
  - Validations (no rules, invalid indices), callback injection, and multi-rule evaluation.

title: fix(core): Integer overflow in insights runtime calculation
body:
## Summary

Fixes integer overflow in insights runtime calculation that causes database insertion failures for long-running workflows.

**Root Cause:**
Runtime values calculated from `ctx.runData.stoppedAt.getTime() - ctx.runData.startedAt.getTime()` can exceed PostgreSQL INTEGER limit (2,147,483,647), causing database insertion to fail for workflows running longer than ~35 minutes.

**Solution:**
- Move `MIN_RUNTIME` and `MAX_RUNTIME` constants to module level for better performance
- Replace magic number with `2 ** 31 - 1` for clarity (PostgreSQL signed 32-bit INTEGER max)
- Add value clamping to safely handle runtime values outside valid range
- Include warning log when clamping occurs for debugging purposes

**Code Changes:**
```typescript
// Before:
const value = ctx.runData.stoppedAt.getTime() - ctx.runData.startedAt.getTime();

// After:
const runtimeMs = ctx.runData.stoppedAt.getTime() - ctx.runData.startedAt.getTime();
if (runtimeMs < MIN_RUNTIME || runtimeMs > MAX_RUNTIME) {
    this.logger.warn(`Invalid runtime detected: ${runtimeMs}ms, clamping to safe range`,);
}
const value = Math.min(Math.max(runtimeMs, MIN_RUNTIME), MAX_RUNTIME);
```

**Impact:**
- ✅ Prevents insights service crashes for long-running workflows
- ✅ Maintains backward compatibility - no breaking changes
- ✅ Zero risk of regression - only adds safety bounds
- ✅ Production-ready fix for enterprise environments

**Testing:**

title: fix(frontend): ensure consistent timezone handling in date formatters
body:
## Problem

This PR fixes a timezone inconsistency issue where execution times were displayed differently in the execution list (left sidebar) and execution details (right panel). Users reported an 8-hour time difference between these two displays.

**Example of the issue:**
- Left sidebar (execution list): Aug 7, 14:52:28
- Right panel (execution details): 2025-08-07 22:53

## Root Cause

The inconsistency was caused by different timezone handling approaches:

1. **ExecutionsTime component** (left sidebar): Used `new Date(props.startTime).getTime()` which respects the browser's local timezone
2. **convertToDisplayDate function** (right panel): Used `dateformat(fullDate, mask)` directly, which could interpret the input differently depending on the data format

## Solution

Ensured all date formatting functions consistently convert input to proper `Date` objects before formatting:

- Modified `convertToDisplayDate()` and `convertToDisplayDateComponents()` to create `Date` objects first
- Updated `toDayMonth()` and `toTime()` functions for consistency
- Applied the same fix to `typesUtils.ts` date formatters

## Changes Made

### `packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/utils/formatters/dateFormatter.ts`
- Added `const date = new Date(fullDate);` before all `dateformat()` calls
- Fixed variable naming conflicts (renamed destructured `date` to `dateStr`)
- Added explanatory comments

### `packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/utils/typesUtils.ts`
- Applied the same Date object conversion pattern
- Ensures consistency across the entire codebase

## Testing

Tested the fix with various date inputs to ensure:
- No behavioral changes for existing functionality
- Consistent timezone handling across all date formatters
- Proper handling of Date objects, strings, and numbers

## Impact

- ✅ Fixes timezone display inconsistency
- ✅ Maintains backward compatibility
- ✅ No breaking changes
- ✅ Improves user experience by showing consistent times

This fix ensures that execution times are displayed consistently throughout the n8n interface, respecting the user's local timezone settings.

title: feat(ReadWriteFile): Add createDirectory function and integrate into write operation
body:
# feat(ReadWriteFile): Add createDirectory function and integrate into write operation

## Summary
<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

This PR adds a new `createDirectory` helper function to the file system utilities and integrates it into the ReadWriteFile node's write operation. The enhancement allows users to automatically create directories when writing files, preventing failures when the target directory doesn't exist.

### Key Changes:
- **New `createDirectory` helper function** that:
  - Creates directories recursively using `mkdir` with `{ recursive: true }`
  - Intelligently handles both file paths and directory paths
  - Distinguishes between files (with extensions) and directories
  - Properly handles edge cases like hidden files (`.env`, `.gitignore`) and files with multiple extensions (`.tar.gz`)
  - Respects existing file path security restrictions
  
- **ReadWriteFile node enhancement**:
  - Added new "Create Directory if Not Exists" option (boolean, default: false)
  - When enabled, automatically creates the target directory before writing the file
  - Maintains backward compatibility with existing workflows

### Testing:
1. Create a ReadWriteFile node with write operation
2. Enable the "Create Directory if Not Exists" option
3. Set a file path in a non-existent directory (e.g., `/tmp/new/nested/path/file.txt`)
4. Execute the node - it should successfully create the directory structure and write the file
5. Verify that security restrictions still apply (blocked paths should still be rejected)

title: fix(Reranker Cohere Node): Add 'Top N' parameter to control document return count
body:
## Summary

Currently Reranker Cohere always return 3 items from the reranker node no matter how many times it received in input. This is very annoying and makes the whole node useless in many cases.
Imagine that we received 20 items from the vector store and want to rerank them and take 10 best items, but we can't do it because Reranker always returns no more than 3 items.

This is happening because we don't pass `topN` parameter to the `@langchain/cohere`'s `CohereRerank` constructor. Which leads to setting this value to 3. See here: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchainjs/blob/6e972e4004c794918910f940d000956922523cbd/libs/langchain-cohere/src/rerank.ts#L16

It closes #16428 and described here https://community.n8n.io/t/vector-store-rerank-results-always-limited-to-3/139552

Therefore I've added a new parameter to the node which allows to pass the value further to the Langchain library.

title: feat: Evaluation framework for AI Workflow Builder
body:
## Summary

This PR implements an evaluation framework to test and measure the AI Workflow Builder's ability to generate correct n8n workflows from natural language prompts.

## Implementation

### Architecture
The evaluation system is organized into distinct modules:

- **Core evaluation engine** (`/core`): Handles test execution, environment setup, and agent initialization
- **CLI runner** (`/cli`): Provides local evaluation with progress tracking and detailed reporting
- **Langsmith integration** (`/langsmith`): Enables dataset-based evaluation with experiment tracking
- **LLM chains** (`/chains`): Implements test case generation and workflow evaluation using AI
- **Type definitions** (`/types`): Zod schemas and TypeScript types for validation
- **Utilities** (`/utils`): Metrics calculation, report generation, and helper functions

### Key Components

#### Test Runner
The test runner orchestrates the evaluation process for each test case:

1. **Workflow Generation**: Creates a dedicated WorkflowBuilderAgent instance per test to avoid state conflicts. The agent receives a natural language prompt and generates a workflow through its chat interface.

2. **State Extraction**: After generation, retrieves the agent's state containing the workflow JSON. Validates the state structure using type guards to ensure the workflow is properly formed.

3. **LLM-based Evaluation**: Passes the generated workflow along with the original prompt to a separate LLM evaluator. The evaluator analyzes the workflow against the prompt requirements and n8n best practices, returning structured scores and violations for each category.

4. **Error Recovery**: Failed generations or evaluations return a zero-score result with error details, allowing the test suite to continue running and report partial results.

5. **Parallel Execution**: Uses p-limit to control concurrency, running multiple tests simultaneously while preventing resource exhaustion. Each test runs in isolation with its own agent instance.

#### Evaluation Metrics
Evaluates workflows across five weighted categories:
- **Functionality** (30%): Correctness of node selection and goal achievement
- **Connections** (25%): Proper node connections and data flow
- **Expressions** (20%): n8n expression syntax and data path validity
- **Node Configuration** (15%): Required parameters and field population
- **Structural Similarity** (10%): Comparison with reference workflows when available

#### Violation Severity System
- Critical violations: -40 to -50 points (workflow-breaking issues)
- Major violations: -15 to -25 points (significant functionality problems)
- Minor violations: -5 to -15 points (inefficiencies or style issues)

### Execution Modes

#### CLI Mode
```bash
pnpm run eval                           # Run with default test cases
pnpm run eval:generate  # Include AI-generated test cases
EVALUATION_CONCURRENCY=10 pnpm run eval # Custom concurrency limit
```

Outputs:
- Real-time progress bar with test status
- Markdown report: `results/evaluation-report-[timestamp].md`
- JSON results: `results/evaluation-results-[timestamp].json`

#### Langsmith Mode
```bash
pnpm run eval:langsmith
```

Features:
- Dataset validation with fallback to listing available datasets
- Experiment tracking with metadata (model name, evaluation type)
- Structured result storage in Langsmith dashboard

### Configuration

#### Required Files
- `nodes.json`: Contains n8n node type definitions required for the AI agent to generate valid workflows. The evaluation framework validates its presence and provides clear error messages if missing.

#### Environment Variables
- `N8N_AI_ANTHROPIC_KEY`: Required for LLM access
- `LANGSMITH_API_KEY`: Required for Langsmith evaluation
- `USE_LANGSMITH_EVAL`: Switches to Langsmith mode
- `LANGSMITH_DATASET_NAME`: Override default dataset
- `EVALUATION_CONCURRENCY`: Parallel test execution limit (default: 5)
- `GENERATE_TEST_CASES`: Enable dynamic test case generation

title: feat: Add global repository search to GitHub node
body:
# Add Global Repository Search to GitHub Node

## Description
This PR adds a new "Search" resource to the GitHub node that allows users to search repositories globally across all of GitHub using the GitHub Search API.

## Changes Made

### Core Implementation
- **Added "Search" resource** to the GitHub node resource options
- **Added "Search Repositories" operation** with comprehensive parameters:
  - `query`: Search query string (supports GitHub search syntax)
  - `sort`: Sort options (best-match, stars, forks, help-wanted-issues, updated)
  - `order`: Sort order (asc/desc)
  - `returnAll`: Boolean to control pagination
  - `limit`: Maximum results when returnAll is false
- **Added execution logic** to call GitHub's `/search/repositories` API endpoint
- **Updated parameter visibility** to hide owner/repository fields for global search

### Testing
- **Unit Tests**: Created `GithubSearch.test.ts` with 6 comprehensive test cases
- **Workflow Tests**: Created `GithubSearchWorkflow.json` for workflow testing
- **Test Coverage**: Tests cover basic queries, returnAll functionality, different sort options, user filters, organization filters, and error handling

## Use Cases
This feature enables users to:
- Search for repositories by language, stars, forks, etc.
- Filter by user or organization: `user:facebook react`
- Find trending repositories: `language:javascript stars:>1000`
- Discover projects by topic: `org:microsoft language:typescript`
- Search for help-wanted repositories: `help-wanted-issues:>5`

## API Compatibility
- Uses official GitHub Search API (`/search/repositories`)
- Supports all GitHub search syntax and filters
- Handles pagination correctly with `returnAll` parameter
- Maintains existing authentication methods (Access Token/OAuth2)

## Testing
All tests pass:
```bash
- search repositories with basic query
-search repositories with returnAll enabled  
- handle search with different sort options
- handle search with user filter
- handle search with organization filter
- handle API errors gracefully
```

## Breaking Changes
None. This is a purely additive feature that doesn't affect existing functionality.

title: fix(editor): Prevent cursor from jumping in the focus panel (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

When typing quickly in the focus panel input, the cursor would unexpectedly jump to the end of the text. This was caused by the use of a debounce wrapper around `valueChanged`, which introduced asynchronous updates, which triggered Vue to re-evaluate `resolvedParameter.value` and re-bind it to the input, causing the DOM to reset the cursor position.

- Remove `debounce()` from `valueChanged` to ensure updates happen synchronously and predictably.
- Introduce a local ref (`inputValue`) as a stable intermediary between user input and the reactive `resolvedParameter.value` to avoid directly binding the input to a recomputed value that may change identity on every render.

title: fix(core): Prevent re-entry during workflow activation
body:
## Summary

We have a [guarantee](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/f3ef0a713c1f63015b8aee55b1b9dd7bcea21f54/packages/cli/src/active-workflow-manager.ts#L96-L99) that an instance is a leader or a follower by the time we reach workflow activation, but there is a race condition where workflow activation is triggered in reaction to a leadership acquisition while regular workflow activation on bootup is ongoing.

Workflow activation logic ideally should be atomic, possibly by queuing activations, but that is a larger refactor that will need to be its own dedicated effort. For now this PR prevents re-entry to protect against the race condition.

title: fix(core): Handle Redis cache prefix on cluster mode
body: ## Summary Fixes Redis cluster prefix handling for cache service to ensure proper hash tagging in cluster mode. **Problem**: When using Redis cluster mode (`QUEUE_BULL_REDIS_CLUSTER_NODES`), the cache service was incorrectly constructing key prefixes as `{n8n:cache:}` which includes the trailing colon inside the hash tag braces. **Solution**: Modified the cache service to construct cluster prefixes as `{n8n:cache}:` where only the meaningful hash tag part is wrapped in braces, and the final colon is placed outside. **Why this matters**: - In Redis cluster mode, hash tags `{}` determine which slot keys are placed in - All keys with the same hash tag go to the same Redis node - This ensures atomic operations across related cache keys work correctly - Follows Redis cluster best practices and Bull.js recommendations **Changes**: - Updated `CacheService.init()` to separate hash tag construction from final prefix - Maintains backward compatibility for non-cluster Redis deployments **Testing**: - Existing cache functionality tests continue to pass - No changes to memory cache behavior ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. body:
# feat(langchain): add OpenAI-compatible Reranker node

## Summary

This PR adds a new **Reranker OpenAI** node that enables document reranking using OpenAI-compatible APIs. The node improves the relevance of documents retrieved from vector stores by reordering them based on their semantic similarity to a given query.

## Features

### 🎯 Core Functionality
- **Document Reranking**: Reorders documents by relevance using OpenAI-compatible reranking APIs
- **Configurable Top N**: Allows users to specify the maximum number of documents to return
- **Seamless Integration**: Works with existing Vector Store nodes through the `ai_reranker` connection type
- **Multiple API Support**: Compatible with OpenAI, SiliconFlow, and other OpenAI-compatible services

### 🔧 Technical Implementation
- **API Compatibility**: Supports the standard `/v1/rerank` endpoint format
- **Proper Error Handling**: Graceful handling of API errors and network issues
- **Metadata Preservation**: Maintains original document metadata while adding relevance scores
- **Performance Optimization**: Limits API calls to specified Top N value

### 🧪 Quality Assurance
- **Comprehensive Tests**: 15 unit tests covering all functionality
- **Documentation**: Complete node and credential documentation with examples
- **Example Workflows**: Ready-to-use RAG workflow example

## API Compatibility

The node supports any service implementing the OpenAI reranking API format:

```bash
POST /v1/rerank
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <api-key>

{
  "model": "rerank-model-name",
  "query": "user query",
  "documents": ["doc1", "doc2", "..."],
  "top_n": 3
}
```

### Supported Services
- **OpenAI**: When reranking APIs become available
- **SiliconFlow**: `Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-8B`, `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3`
- **Custom APIs**: Any OpenAI-compatible reranking service

## Usage Example

### Basic RAG Workflow
```
Chat Trigger → AI Agent ← Vector Store (Top K: 10, Use Reranker: ✓)
                ↑              ↑
        Language Model    Reranker OpenAI (Top N: 3)
                              ↑
                        Embeddings Model
```

1. **Vector Store** retrieves 10 similar documents
2. **Reranker** reorders and returns top 3 most relevant documents
3. **AI Agent** uses the 3 best documents to generate responses

## Files Added

### Core Implementation
- `nodes/rerankers/RerankerOpenAI/RerankerOpenAI.node.ts` - Main node implementation
- `nodes/rerankers/RerankerOpenAI/openai.svg` - Node icon
- `credentials/OpenAIApi.credentials.ts` - Enhanced credentials with configurable base URL

### Documentation
- `nodes/rerankers/RerankerOpenAI/RerankerOpenAI.node.md` - Node documentation
- `credentials/OpenAIApi.credentials.md` - Credentials documentation
- `nodes/rerankers/RerankerOpenAI/examples/README.md` - Usage examples

### Tests
- `nodes/rerankers/RerankerOpenAI/__tests__/RerankerOpenAI.node.test.ts` - Node tests
- `nodes/rerankers/RerankerOpenAI/__tests__/OpenAIRerank.test.ts` - Core functionality tests

### Examples
- `nodes/rerankers/RerankerOpenAI/examples/basic-rag-workflow.json` - Complete RAG workflow

## Benefits

### 🎯 Improved Relevance
- **Better Search Results**: Reranking significantly improves document relevance
- **Semantic Understanding**: Uses advanced models to understand query-document relationships
- **Quality over Quantity**: Returns fewer but more relevant documents

### 💰 Cost Efficiency
- **Reduced Token Usage**: Only processes the most relevant documents in downstream tasks
- **Configurable Limits**: Users can balance quality vs. cost with Top N parameter
- **Efficient API Usage**: Minimizes unnecessary API calls

### 🔧 Developer Experience
- **Easy Integration**: Drop-in replacement for existing vector search workflows
- **Flexible Configuration**: Supports various models and API endpoints
- **Comprehensive Documentation**: Clear setup instructions and examples

## Testing

All tests pass successfully:
```
Test Suites: 2 passed, 2 total
Tests:       15 passed, 15 total
```

### Test Coverage
- ✅ Node configuration and properties
- ✅ Credential handling and validation
- ✅ API request formatting and error handling
- ✅ Document reranking and metadata preservation
- ✅ Top N limiting and edge cases

## Breaking Changes

None. This is a new feature that doesn't affect existing functionality.

## Migration Guide

Not applicable - this is a new node.

## Related Issues

This addresses the need for improved document relevance in RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) workflows, a common request in the n8n community.

title: fix(core): Populate MCP endpoints in frontend settings
body: ## Summary This PR resolves a bug where the `N8N_ENDPOINT_MCP` and `N8N_ENDPOINT_MCP_TEST` environment variables were not being correctly passed to the frontend when n8n is deployed behind a proxy. This resulted in nodes like "MCP Trigger" displaying broken URLs. The fix ensures that these endpoint settings are properly loaded into the frontend's `rootStore` during initialization, making their behavior consistent with other endpoints like webhooks and forms. ### How to test: 1. Set up an n8n instance with environment variables to simulate a proxy (e.g., `WEBHOOK_URL="http://localhost/"`, `N8N_ENDPOINT_MCP_TEST="n8n/mcp-test"`). 2. In the UI, create a new workflow and add an "MCP Trigger" node. 3. Check the "Test URL" displayed in the node's properties panel. - **Before fix:** The URL is broken (e.g., `http://localhost/mcp-test/`). - **After fix:** The URL renders correctly with the full path (e.g., `http://localhost/n8n/mcp-test/`). title: fix(Reranker Cohere Node): Add 'Top N' parameter to control document return count
body:
## Summary

Currently Reranker Cohere always return 3 items from the reranker node no matter how many times it received in input. This is very annoying and makes the whole node useless in many cases.
Imagine that we received 20 items from the vector store and want to rerank them and take 10 best items, but we can't do it because Reranker always returns no more than 3 items.

This is happening because we don't pass `topN` parameter to the `@langchain/cohere`'s `CohereRerank` constructor. Which leads to setting this value to 3. See here: https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchainjs/blob/6e972e4004c794918910f940d000956922523cbd/libs/langchain-cohere/src/rerank.ts#L16

It closes #16428 and described here https://community.n8n.io/t/vector-store-rerank-results-always-limited-to-3/139552

Therefore I've added a new parameter to the node which allows to pass the value further to the Langchain library.

title: build(docker): Allow environment variable override for Docker platform choice
body:
# Pull Request Description

## Summary

This PR adds support for cross-platform Docker builds in the `dockerize-n8n.mjs` script by allowing environment variable override of the target platform. This enables building Docker images for different architectures (e.g., amd64) even when running on different host architectures (e.g., ARM64).

### Problem
Currently, the `dockerize-n8n.mjs` script automatically detects the host architecture and builds Docker images for that platform only. This prevents cross-platform builds, which are essential for:
- Building amd64 images on ARM64 machines (Apple Silicon Macs)
- CI/CD pipelines that need to target specific platforms
- Deployment scenarios requiring platform-specific images

### Solution
Add environment variable support to override the platform detection:
- Introduce `DOCKER_PLATFORM` environment variable
- Maintain backward compatibility with existing behavior
- Allow explicit platform specification for cross-platform builds

## Changes

### Modified Files
- `scripts/dockerize-n8n.mjs`: Updated `getDockerPlatform()` function to support environment variable override

### Code Changes
```javascript
function getDockerPlatform() {
	// Allow environment variable override for cross-platform builds
	if (process.env.DOCKER_PLATFORM) {
		return process.env.DOCKER_PLATFORM;
	}

	const arch = os.arch();
	const dockerArch = {
		x64: 'amd64',
		arm64: 'arm64',
	}[arch];

	if (!dockerArch) {
		throw new Error(`Unsupported architecture: ${arch}. Only x64 and arm64 are supported.`);
	}

	return `linux/${dockerArch}`;
}
```

## Usage Examples

### Build for amd64 on ARM64 machine
```bash
DOCKER_PLATFORM=linux/amd64 pnpm run build:docker
```

### Build for ARM64 on x64 machine
```bash
DOCKER_PLATFORM=linux/arm64 pnpm run build:docker
```

### Use with custom image name and platform
```bash
IMAGE_BASE_NAME="my-registry/n8n" IMAGE_TAG="v1.0.0" DOCKER_PLATFORM="linux/amd64" pnpm run build:docker
```

## Testing

### Manual Testing Performed
The functionality has been manually tested to ensure it works correctly:

1. **Native build** (no environment variable):
   ```bash
   pnpm run build:docker
   # Should build for host architecture
   ```

2. **Cross-platform build**:
   ```bash
   DOCKER_PLATFORM=linux/amd64 pnpm run build:docker
   # Should build for amd64 regardless of host
   ```

3. **Verify image architecture**:
   ```bash
   docker image inspect n8nio/n8n:local --format '{{.Architecture}}'
   # Should return the target architecture
   ```

### Note on Automated Tests
This change modifies a build script (`dockerize-n8n.mjs`) that doesn't currently have automated tests. The n8n project doesn't have existing unit tests for build scripts, and this change is minimal and focused. The functionality has been manually verified to work correctly and maintain backward compatibility.

## Benefits

1. **Cross-platform compatibility**: Build images for any supported platform
2. **CI/CD flexibility**: Support for multi-architecture builds in pipelines
3. **Developer experience**: Better support for ARM64 developers building for x64 deployments
4. **Backward compatibility**: No breaking changes to existing workflows

## Related Issues

None

## Review / Merge checklist

- [x] Code changes are minimal and focused
- [x] Backward compatibility is maintained
- [x] Manual testing has been performed
- [x] No breaking changes introduced

## Notes

- This is a non-breaking change that maintains full backward compatibility
- The feature is opt-in through environment variables
- No additional dependencies are required
- Follows existing code patterns and conventions
- Manual testing has been performed to verify functionality

title: feat(Ollama Credentials): Add optional API key support to Ollama credentials (Openwebui proxy)
body:
## Summary
Adds optional API key authentication to Ollama credentials to support [OpenWebUI](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui) integration.

**Background:**
Many users deploy Ollama with OpenWebUI to provide a public chat interface for their models. OpenWebUI acts as a proxy for Ollama and provides features like user management, conversation history, and web access. However, when OpenWebUI proxies Ollama requests, it requires Bearer token authentication.

Currently, n8n's Ollama integration cannot authenticate with [OpenWebUI-proxied](https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/api-endpoints/#-ollama-api-proxy-support) instances, limiting users to direct Ollama connections only.

**Changes:**
- **Added optional `apiKey` field** to Ollama credentials.
- **Implemented Bearer token authentication** when API key is provided  
- **Maintains full backward compatibility** - existing workflows continue working unchanged
- **Improved test endpoint** from `/` to `/api/tags` for more reliable connection validation

**Testing:**
✅ **Without API key**: Direct Ollama connection works as before  
✅ **With API key**: OpenWebUI-proxied Ollama connection authenticates successfully  
✅ **Connection test**: Updated endpoint properly validates Ollama availability

title: fix(core): Fix getting webhook methods from path only when dynamic webhook path
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

Currently, when a webhook is dynamic (has a param in its path - e.g /path/:id), has a CORS wildcard setup, and the user calls the webhook from a browser on a different domain, the getWebhookMethods fails (both on test and live webhooks). That's because for now, the getWebhookMethods only try to find webhooks that exactly match the path, and thus dynamic path are not matched

This PR suggests to use the same method we use to find dynamic webhook from path in the getWebhookMethods, but extend it to search for all http methods. This should be safe because if the path is dynamic, the webhook id is in the path and unique.

## Summary

This PR introduces a workflow suggested actions feature that helps users discover important workflow configuration options. The feature displays contextual suggestions in the workflow header to improve discoverability of AI evaluations, error workflow setup, and time tracking.

### Key Features

- **Workflow Suggested Actions Component**: A new bell icon in the workflow header that shows relevant suggestions based on workflow state
- **Smart Detection**: Automatically detects when a workflow could benefit from:

  - Error workflow configuration (for active workflows without error handling)
  - Time saved tracking (for measuring automation impact)
- **First Activation Trigger**: Automatically opens suggestions when a workflow is activated for the first time
- **Persistent Preferences**: Users can dismiss suggestions, and their choices are remembered via IndexedDB
- **Centralized Cache Management**: New `useWorkflowsCache` composable for managing workflow-related cache operations

title: docs: Update issue template
body:
## Summary
Updates the template used in product to closer match what we use on GitHub now.

## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts


## Review / Merge checklist

- [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. ([conventions](../blob/master/.github/pull_request_title_conventions.md)) <!--
   **Remember, the title automatically goes into the changelog.
   Use `(no-changelog)` otherwise.**
-->
- [ ] [Docs updated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs) or follow-up ticket created.
- [ ] Tests included. <!--
   A bug is not considered fixed, unless a test is added to prevent it from happening again.
   A feature is not complete without tests.
-->
- [ ] PR Labeled with `release/backport` (if the PR is an urgent fix that needs to be backported)

title: perf(core): Introduce decorator to report slow method calls
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a way to create timing method decorators. This way we can e.g. decorate DB queries to log a warning when they exceed a duration threshold, using our existing `winston` logging.

```
09:23:11.214   warn    Slow database query { "method": "WorkflowRepository.getMany", "durationMs": 453, "thresholdMs": 100, "params": "[hidden]", "file": "timed.js", "function": "descriptor.value" }
```

For DB queries, this decorator differs from [query logging](https://typeorm.io/docs/advanced-topics/logging) in `typeorm` in that this decorator works at repository method level rather than SQL query level, this decorator supports structured logs rather than free-form logs in `typeorm`, and this is enabled by default and configurable per method and only for decorated queries.

In future we should decorate all critical queries, setting individual thresholds.

title: fix(GithubTrigger Node): Correctly access httpCode from error object
body:
## Summary

Fixes a runtime crash in the GitHub Trigger node when re‑activating a workflow whose webhook was manually deleted on GitHub.  
Instead of trying to read `error.cause.httpCode` (which is undefined), this change reads `error.httpCode` directly.  

**How to test**  
1. Start n8n with a tunnel:  `./packages/cli/bin/n8n start --tunnel`
2. Create a workflow with a GitHub Trigger node pointed at a repo you control, and activate it.  
3. In GitHub, go to **Settings » Webhooks** for that repo and delete the webhook n8n created.  
4. In n8n, deactivate then reactivate the workflow.  
5. Before this PR you’d see a crash (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'httpCode')`); after, activation succeeds without errors.

body:
## Summary
This PR addresses streaming functionality issues and improves the chat plugin architecture. The changes enable streaming in manual execution mode, handle empty streaming responses, and refactor the chat plugin for better maintainability.

- Removed the condition that prevented streaming from working in manual execution mode. The `sendChunk` handler is now registered regardless of execution mode. @schrothbn Do you recall the reason for this condition by any chance? 🤔

title: fix(editor): Fix canvas layouting when tab is not active
body:
## Summary

The canvas layout function in `useCanvasLayout.ts` fails when the browser tab is not active(for example when triggered during AI workflow generation). This occurs because Vue Flow cannot calculate node dimensions when DOM elements are not visible.

When a tab is inactive:
- DOM elements have zero dimensions or are not rendered
- Vue Flow's `node.dimensions` property becomes undefined or contains invalid values
- The layout function attempts to destructure `dimensions: { width, height }` without checking if dimensions exist

## Solution

Added a fallback mechanism that calculates node dimensions when Vue Flow dimensions are unavailable:

1. Created `getNodeDimensions` helper function that:
   - Checks if `node.dimensions` exists and contains valid width/height values
   - Falls back to `calculateNodeSize` based on node properties (type, input/output counts)
   - Returns default dimensions as a last resort

2. Updated `createDagreGraph` and `boundingBoxFromCanvasNode` functions to use the safe dimension getter

3. The dimension calculation logic considers:
   - Node render type (configuration, configurable, default)
   - Number of main inputs/outputs
   - Number of non-main connections

title: fix(core): Fetching schema files in Docker
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

Fix fetching schema files in Docker

When building a Docker image, the schema files are placed in a path that has a dotfile (folder): `.pnpm`  \
Example: `/usr/local/lib/node_modules/n8n/node_modules/.pnpm/n8n-nodes-base@file+packages+nodes-base_@aws-sdk+credential-providers@3.808.0_asn1.js@5_1af219c3f47f2a1223ec4ccec249a974/node_modules/n8n-nodes-base/dist/nodes/Slack/__schema__/v2.3.0/message/post.json`. This usually doesn't happen during local development

You need to explicitly allow dotfiles when sending the schema file, otherwise Express throws a `NotFoundError`. This causes the endpoint to return 404 when trying to fetch the schema file

title: fix(WhatsApp): Replace currency-codes with local ISOCountryCodes utility
body:
## Summary
Fixes TypeScript import error in WhatsApp MessagesDescription.ts by replacing external `currency-codes` dependency with the local `ISOCountryCodes` utility for consistency with the n8n codebase.

## Problem
- TypeScript error: "Cannot find module 'currency-codes' or its corresponding type declarations"
- WhatsApp node was using external `currency-codes` package while other n8n nodes use the local `@utils/ISOCountryCodes` utility
- Inconsistent dependency management across the codebase

## Changes
- **Removed:** `import countryCodes from 'currency-codes'`
- **Added:** `import { isoCountryCodes } from '@utils/ISOCountryCodes'`
- **Updated currency mapping:**
  - From: `countryCodes.data.map(({ code, currency }) => ({ name: \`${code} - ${currency}\`, value: code }))`
  - To: `isoCountryCodes.map(({ alpha2, name }) => ({ name: \`${alpha2} - ${name}\`, value: alpha2 }))`

## Benefits
- ✅ Eliminates external dependency requirement
- ✅ Follows established n8n patterns (consistent with other nodes)
- ✅ Fixes TypeScript compilation error
- ✅ Uses ISO country codes instead of currency codes (more appropriate for country selection)
- ✅ No breaking changes for end users

- [x] Code consistency improvement

title: Implement trello webhook signature verification
body:
## Summary

# What this fixes
- Trello webhook signature verification was not implemented, making webhooks insecure
- Webhook validation failed when callback URL in payload differed from node configuration

# Changes
- Implemented HMAC SHA1 signature verification per Trello's documentation
- Uses callback URL from webhook payload with fallback to node's configured URL  
- Ensures webhooks are accepted when no OAuth secret is configured

# Why we extract URL from webhook payload
Trello signs webhooks using the exact callback URL that was stored during webhook registration:
signature = HMAC_SHA1(requestBody + storedCallbackURL, secret)

The stored URL can differ from the node's current URL due to:
- Development workflow changes (`/webhook-test/` vs `/webhook/`)
- Environment differences (dev vs prod)
- Node configuration changes after webhook registration

Our solution prioritizes the `callbackURL` from Trello's payload (the one Trello used to sign) with fallback to the node's configured URL, ensuring signature validation always uses the same URL Trello used to generate the signature.

# Security Impact
- Prevents unauthorized webhook requests from triggering workflows
- Validates all incoming Trello webhooks against configured OAuth secret

# Testing
- Verified signature validation works with actual Trello webhook payloads
- Confirmed fallback URL logic handles both test and production scenarios

title: fix(core): Remove non-included nodes regardless of the package when using NODES_INCLUDE
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

Fix an issue when using `NODES_INCLUDE` environment variable. Non-included nodes should be removed, but that doesn't happen for nodes from other packages

For example: 
- `NODES_INCLUDE='["n8n-nodes-base.manualTrigger"]'` will include the manual trigger and all nodes from `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain`
- `NODES_INCLUDE='["n8n-nodes-base.manualTrigger", "@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.agent"]'` will include only the manual trigger and the AI agent. Other AI nodes are filtered out because there is an AI node in `NODES_INCLUDE`

This also happens with installed community nodes, as those are separate packages

This is due to the fact that [`PackageDirectoryLoader` filters out](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/101004390bf5cdf5f67675dcfccb551f71ea4b70/packages/core/src/nodes-loader/package-directory-loader.ts#L29) any nodes from other packages, so if no nodes are included from the current package, it's the same as setting `NODES_INCLUDE='[]'` which doesn't do anything (for that package)

This PR fixes this by checking if there are nodes in `NODES_INCLUDE` before they are filtered by package

title: feat(editor): AI workflow builder front-end (no-changelog)
body:
# AI Workflow Builder: Frontend Integration (Part 3/3)

## Overview

This PR completes the AI Workflow Builder integration by implementing the frontend components that connect to the new agent-based architecture.

## Key Changes

### 1. Message Type Refactoring and Harmonization

**Files**: 
- `packages/frontend/@n8n/design-system/src/types/assistant.ts`
- `packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/types/assistant.types.ts`

The message type system has been completely restructured to align with the agent architecture:
- Consolidated message types into a unified `ChatUI` namespace
- Added new message types: `ToolMessage` for real-time tool execution feedback
- Introduced `WorkflowUpdatedMessage` for canvas state synchronization
- Removed deprecated message types that were specific to the old chain-based system

### 2. Simplified State Management and Canvas Integration

**Files**: 
- `packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/stores/builder.store.ts`
- `packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/components/AskAssistant/Agent/AskAssistantBuild.vue`

The builder store has been refactored with clear separation of concerns:
- **Store responsibilities**: Message state, session management, workflow data preparation
- **Component responsibilities**: Canvas updates via event bus, telemetry tracking
- Improved error recovery with retry handlers that preserve context
- Reactive computed properties for filtered message lists (tool and workflow messages)

Key implementation details:
- `applyWorkflowUpdate()` prepares workflow data and preserves existing node positions
- `AskAssistantBuild.vue` watches for workflow messages and triggers canvas updates
- Position preservation ensures existing nodes don't jump during updates
- New nodes are flagged for automatic layout recompute

### 3. Enhanced Message Processing

**File**: `packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/composables/useBuilderMessages.ts`

New composable for message handling:
- **Tool Message Deduplication**: Prevents duplicate tool messages by tracking `toolCallId`
- **Rating Logic**: Shows ratings only after workflow updates complete
- **Thinking State Management**: Handles assistant "thinking" messages gracefully
- **Progressive Updates**: Merges tool message updates incrementally

### 4. Real-time Canvas Updates and Tidy Up Integration

**Files**:
- `packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/views/NodeView.vue`
- `packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/composables/useCanvasOperations.ts`
- `packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/stores/builder.store.ts`

Canvas integration improvements:
- Direct workflow JSON updates from builder messages
- Automatic "Tidy Up" feature for newly added nodes
- Position preservation for existing nodes during updates


### 5. Design System Chat Components

**Location**: `packages/frontend/@n8n/design-system/src/components/AskAssistantChat/`

The design system now includes a comprehensive set of chat components for the AI assistant:

#### Message Components Architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[MessageWrapper] --> B[BaseMessage]
    B --> C[TextMessage]
    B --> D[ToolMessage]
    B --> E[BlockMessage]
    B --> F[CodeDiffMessage]
    B --> G[ErrorMessage]
    B --> H[EventMessage]
```

title: feat: AI Workflow Builder core (no-changelog)
body:
# AI Workflow Builder: Core Agent Architecture Refactoring (Part 1/3) ## Overview This PR introduces fundamental architectural changes to the AI Workflow Builder, refactoring from a sequential chain-based approach to a flexible agent-based architecture. This is the first of three PRs that need to be merged to fully implement the new system. ## Architecture Overview The new architecture centers around a LangGraph state machine that orchestrates tool execution and state management: ```mermaid graph TD START([User Message]) --> AGENT[Agent
Decides Actions] AGENT --> TOOLS{Tools Needed?} TOOLS -->|Yes| PARALLEL[Execute Tools
in Parallel] TOOLS -->|No| RESPOND[Generate Response] PARALLEL --> OPS[Collect Operations] OPS --> PROCESS[Process Operations
Update Workflow] PROCESS --> AGENT RESPOND --> END([Stream to Frontend]) style AGENT fill:#e3f2fd style PARALLEL fill:#fff3e0 style PROCESS fill:#f3e5f5 ``` ## Key Changes ### 1. Core Agent Implementation The refactoring replaces sequential chain execution with a stateful LangGraph agent that: - Executes multiple tools in parallel for better performance - Maintains conversation state across interactions - Handles iterative workflow building through a feedback loop - Recovers gracefully from errors without losing context **Implementation**: `packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/workflow-builder-agent.ts` ### 2. Tool System Implementation Six specialized tools replace the previous chain components: - **`node-search`**: Fuzzy search across available node types - **`node-details`**: Retrieve detailed parameter schemas for nodes - **`add-node`**: Add nodes with intelligent positioning and naming - **`connect-nodes`**: Create connections with proper output handling - **`remove-node`**: Safely remove nodes and their connections - **`update-node-parameters`**: Configure node parameters using dedicated LLM chain Tools execute in parallel when possible, improving response times for complex operations. ### 3. State Management and Operations Queue The system uses an operations queue pattern to ensure atomic state updates: - **State Management**: `packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/workflow-state.ts` - **Operations Processing**: `packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/utils/operations-processor.ts` Key features: - Tools return operations instead of directly mutating state - Operations accumulate from parallel tool execution - Processing applies operations atomically in correct order - Enables future undo/redo capabilities ### 4. Message Streaming and Real-time Updates The streaming architecture provides real-time feedback: - **Stream Processor**: `packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/utils/stream-processor.ts` - **Progress Tracking**: `packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/tools/helpers/progress.ts` Stream modes: - `updates`: State changes and agent messages - `custom`: Tool execution progress ### 5. Session Management Conversation persistence through LangGraph's MemorySaver: - Thread format: `workflow-{workflowId}-user-{userId}` - Commands: `/clear` (reset session), `/compact` (summarize conversation) - Automatic session restoration on reconnection ### 6. Supporting Chains Three chains enhance the agent's capabilities: 1. **Parameter Updater**: Dynamic prompt assembly for node configuration based on natural language array of instructions 2. **Conversation Compact**: Reduces conversation size while preserving context 3. **Planner**: Legacy chain kept for future enhancements ### 7. Error Handling Error handling maintains conversation flow: - Structured error types (ValidationError, NodeTypeNotFoundError) - Tool-level error isolation prevents cascade failures - Errors returned as messages for graceful degradation ## Technical Deep Dive ### 1. LangGraph Agent State Machine The agent orchestrates all operations through a state machine: ```mermaid graph TD START([Start]) --> CHECK{Check Command} CHECK -->|"/clear"| DELETE[delete_messages] CHECK -->|"/compact"| COMPACT[compact_messages] CHECK -->|"regular message"| AGENT[agent] AGENT --> DECIDE{Has Tool Calls?} DECIDE -->|Yes| TOOLS[tools
Parallel Execution] DECIDE -->|No| END([End]) TOOLS --> PROCESS[process_operations
Apply Mutations] PROCESS --> AGENT DELETE --> END COMPACT --> END style AGENT fill:#e3f2fd style TOOLS fill:#fff3e0 style PROCESS fill:#f3e5f5 style DELETE fill:#ffebee style COMPACT fill:#e8f5e9 ``` **State Flow Details:** - **agent**: Calls LLM with available tools, decides next actions - **tools**: Executes multiple tools in parallel for efficiency - **process_operations**: Applies accumulated operations to workflow - **delete_messages**: Clears conversation history - **compact_messages**: Summarizes long conversations - See: `packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/workflow-builder-agent.ts` ### 2. State Mutations Through Operations Queue The system ensures atomic state updates through an operations queue pattern: ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> ToolExecution: Tools Execute state ToolExecution { [*] --> Parallel Parallel --> Tool1: add_nodes Parallel --> Tool2: connect_nodes Parallel --> Tool3: update_parameters Tool1 --> Op1: Returns Operations Tool2 --> Op2: Returns Operations Tool3 --> Op3: Returns Operations } ToolExecution --> OperationsQueue: Collect All Operations state OperationsQueue { Queue: Operations Array Queue --> Reducer: operationsReducer Reducer --> Merged: Merged Operations } OperationsQueue --> ProcessNode: process_operations state ProcessNode { Apply: applyOperations() Apply --> Clear: addNodes Clear --> Update: removeNode Update --> Connect: updateNode Connect --> Merge: mergeConnections } ProcessNode --> WorkflowJSON: Updated Workflow ProcessNode --> ClearQueue: operations = null WorkflowJSON --> [*] ``` **Key Concepts:** - Tools return operations, not direct mutations - Operations queue accumulates changes from parallel tool execution - Reducer handles special cases (clear operations, append logic) - Process node applies all operations atomically - Operations cleared after successful processing - See: `packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/workflow-state.ts` - See: `packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/utils/operations-processor.ts` ### 3. Stream Processing and Real-time Updates The system provides real-time feedback through streaming: ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph Tool Execution T1[Tool Invoked] --> PR[Progress Reporter] PR --> E1[Starting...] PR --> E2[Validating node type...] PR --> E3[Creating connections...] PR --> E4[Success/Error] end subgraph Stream Processing E1 --> CE[Custom Events] E2 --> CE E3 --> CE E4 --> CE CE --> SP[Stream Processor] SP --> MODE{Stream Mode?} MODE -->|updates| AU[Agent Updates] MODE -->|custom| TP[Tool Progress] AU --> AM[Agent Messages] AU --> WU[Workflow Updates] TP --> TM[Tool Messages] end subgraph Frontend Display AM --> Chat[Chat UI] TM --> Tool[Tool Status UI] WU --> Canvas[Workflow Canvas] end style PR fill:#e8f5e9 style SP fill:#fff3e0 style MODE fill:#ffebee ``` **Implementation Flow:** 1. Tools report progress via `progressReporter.progress()` 2. Progress events stream as custom events 3. Stream processor routes events based on type 4. Frontend receives typed messages for UI updates 5. Tool messages show real-time execution status - See: `packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/utils/stream-processor.ts` - See: `packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/tools/helpers/progress.ts` ### 4. Parameter Update Chain and Prompt Caching The parameter update chain dynamically assembles prompts with caching for efficiency: ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph Cached Components BASE[Base Instructions
Expression Rules] NODE[Node Parameters Definitions] EXAMPLES[Relevant Configuration
Examples] end subgraph Dynamic Assembly REQ[User Request] --> ANALYZE[Analyze Node Type] ANALYZE --> BUILD[Build Prompt] BASE --> BUILD NODE --> BUILD EXAMPLES --> BUILD BUILD --> CACHE{Cached?} CACHE -->|Yes| FAST[Reduced Tokens] CACHE -->|No| FULL[Full Token Cost] end FAST --> LLM[LLM Processing] FULL --> LLM LLM --> OUTPUT[Updated Parameters] style BASE fill:#e8f5e9 style NODE fill:#e8f5e9 style EXAMPLES fill:#e8f5e9 ``` **Key Features:** - Anthropic prompt caching reduces token costs - Node-specific prompts for HTTP, If, Database nodes - Dynamic example selection based on context - Structured output for reliable parsing - See: `packages/@n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/chains/parameter-updater.ts` ## Integration Points ### Service Layer Integration - `packages/cli/src/services/ai-workflow-builder.service.ts`: Manages AI builder lifecycle - Handles LLM provider configuration (OpenAI/Anthropic) - Integrates with AI Assistant Client for enterprise deployments ### API Controller - `packages/cli/src/controllers/ai.controller.ts`: Streaming endpoint - JSON Lines format with custom delimiter: `⧉⇋⇋➽⌑⧉§§\n` - Rate limiting: 100 requests per window ### Frontend State Management - Builder store processes streaming messages - Real-time canvas synchronization - Tool execution visualization ## Review / Merge checklist - [ ] PR title and summary are descriptive. title: fix(Slack Node): Fix timestamp handling in history filters
body:
## Summary

The code was incorrectly converting latest and oldest filter timestamps from strings to Unix epoch seconds using `new Date().getTime() / 1000`.

As can be understood from the API documentation, the `latest` and `oldest` fields are expected to be strings of UNIX time including milliseconds.
Also, the same timestamp format is used for input and output in other Slack APIs.

In n8n, to allow the output of other Slack nodes to be used as input directly, this value should be treated as a string.

[https://api.slack.com/methods/conversations.history](https://api.slack.com/methods/conversations.history)

This change may potentially break the behavior of workflows that are functioning in existing use cases.
I suspect that the existing code may not be working as expected, but caution should be exercised just in case.

body:
# fix: prevent browser crash when deleting HTTP Request node body parameters (fixes #17384)

// Fix: Prevent crash when deleting array item by checking bounds and making a copy to avoid Vue reactivity issues

## Summary

This PR fixes a critical browser crash that occurs when users try to delete body parameters in the HTTP Request node. The crash affects n8n cloud users and happens in multiple browsers (Chrome and others).

**Root Cause:** The crash occurs in the `updateParameterByPath` function when directly mutating Vue reactive arrays using `splice()` without proper bounds checking or Vue reactivity handling.

**Solution:** Added bounds checking and created shallow array copies before mutation to prevent Vue reactivity conflicts.

**Testing:** 
- ✅ Tested deleting single body parameter
- ✅ Tested deleting multiple body parameters  
- ✅ Verified no browser crashes occur
- ✅ Confirmed parameter deletion works correctly

## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts

- **Fixes #17384** - HTTP Request node browser crash when deleting body parameters
- **Linear ticket:** GHC-3145

## Review / Merge checklist

- [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. ([conventions](../blob/master/.github/pull_request_title_conventions.md))
- [x] [Docs updated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs) or follow-up ticket created. *(No docs needed - internal bugfix)*
- [x] Tests included. *(Manual testing completed - this is a UI crash fix)*
- [ ] PR Labeled with `release/backport` (if the PR is an urgent fix that needs to be backported) *(Reviewer decision)*

## Technical Details

**Before (crashes browser):**
```typescript
data.splice(parseInt(index, 10), 1);
```

**After (safe):**
```typescript
const idx = parseInt(index, 10);
if (idx >= 0 && idx < data.length) {
    const newData = data.slice(); // make a shallow copy for Vue reactivity
    newData.splice(idx, 1);
    set(nodeParameters as object, path, newData);
}
```

## Impact

- **Low risk** - Only affects array deletion logic
- **High value** - Fixes critical browser crash issue
- **Backward compatible** - No breaking changes

## Summary

This PR migrates workflow tests from the `execute-batch` command to Playwright, introducing schema-based validation that detects API breaking changes while avoiding false positives from dynamic values.

- **Schema validation**: Detects structural changes (field renames, type changes) instead of value differences

```bash
# Run tests
pnpm test:workflows
```

title: refactor: Add SVG loader for Storybook and bump version
body:
## Summary
- Adds `vite-svg-loader` to properly handle SVG imports in Storybook (when loading custom SVG icons in `frontend/@n8n/design-system/src/components/N8nIcon/icons.ts`)
- Updates Sass to v1.71.1 for better compatibility with Vite/Storybook dependencies

## Changes
- **package.json**: Bumped Sass from v1.64.1 to v1.71.1
- **vite.config.mts**: Added SVG loader configuration 
- **pnpm-lock.yaml**: Updated dependencies

### Sass Upgrade Reasoning
The Sass upgrade from v1.64.1 to v1.71.1 was necessary due to compatibility issues with our current Vite and Storybook dependencies. The older Sass version (1.64.1) was causing build conflicts and preventing proper module resolution in the updated build toolchain.

While v1.71.1 resolves these compatibility issues and allows the build to work correctly, it introduces deprecation warnings that we'll need to address before Dart Sass 3.0.0:

1. **`@import` deprecations**: All `@import` rules need to be migrated to `@use` and `@forward`
   - Affects multiple components (N8nButton, N8nAlert, N8nLink, etc.)
   - Sass provides an automated migrator: https://sass-lang.com/d/import

2. **Global built-in function deprecations**: Functions like `unquote()` need to be namespaced
   - Need to replace `unquote()` with `string.unquote()`
   - Commonly used in Button.scss for dynamic property values

These warnings shouldn't affect current functionality but will become breaking changes in Dart Sass 3.0.0. Use [N8N-8707](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/N8N-8707) for follow-up

- **Cloud SQL**: PostgreSQLデータベース（自動バックアップ、HA対応）
- **Artifact Registry**: Dockerイメージの安全な保存・管理
- **Secret Manager**: データベースパスワードとn8n暗号化キーの管理
- **IAM**: 最小権限の原則に基づくセキュリティ設定

### デプロイメント構成

#### Staging環境
- **プロジェクト**: n8n-stg-466014
- **リソース**: 小規模（1CPU/1Gi、インスタンス0-3台）
- **PostgreSQL**: db-f1-micro、10GB、削除保護無効
- **用途**: 開発・テスト環境

#### Production環境
- **プロジェクト**: n8n-prd-466015
- **リソース**: 大規模（4CPU/4Gi、インスタンス2-20台）
- **PostgreSQL**: db-n1-standard-2、100GB、Regional HA、削除保護有効
- **用途**: 本番運用環境

### セキュリティ機能
- Secret Managerによる機密情報の暗号化保存
- サービスアカウントベースの最小権限アクセス
- ネットワークレベルのアクセス制御
- 削除保護による重要データの保護
- 包括的な監査ログ設定

- [ ] Staging環境でのTerraform apply実行確認
- [ ] Production環境でのTerraform apply実行確認
- [ ] Secret Manager設定の動作確認
- [ ] GitHub ActionsによるDockerイメージビルド確認
- [ ] Cloud Runサービスの正常起動確認
- [ ] PostgreSQLデータベース接続確認
- [ ] n8nアプリケーションの基本動作確認

### 実行手順

#### Secret Manager設定
```bash
# Staging環境
gcloud config set project n8n-stg-466014
gcloud secrets create n8n-stg-db-password --data-file=-
gcloud secrets create n8n-stg-encryption-key --data-file=-
```

```bash
terraform apply -var-file="environments/stg/terraform.tfvars"
```

title: feat(Microsoft Teams Node): Add support for government cloud tenants
body:
## Summary

This PR adds configurable Microsoft Graph API base URL support to the Microsoft Teams node, allowing users to connect to government cloud tenants (GCC/DoD) that use different Graph API endpoints.

**Changes made:**
- Added `baseUrl` field to `MicrosoftOAuth2Api` credentials with default value `https://graph.microsoft.com`
- Modified `microsoftApiRequest` function in Teams v2 transport to use the configurable base URL
- Maintains backward compatibility with existing public cloud tenants

**Testing:**
1. Create Microsoft Teams credentials with custom base URL (e.g., `https://graph.microsoft.us` for GCC)
2. Use Microsoft Teams node to list channels or send messages
3. Verify successful connection to government cloud tenants

**Before:** Hardcoded `https://graph.microsoft.com` caused "401 - InvalidCloudInstance" errors for GCC/DoD tenants
**After:** Configurable base URL supports all Microsoft Graph instances including government clouds

## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts

Fixes [#17283](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/17283) - Microsoft Teams node fails with "401 - InvalidCloudInstance" for GCC/DoD tenants

title: feat(Telegram): Add JSON keyboard support for inline and reply keyboards
body:
## Summary

This PR enhances the **Telegram node** in n8n by introducing support for **raw JSON input** for **Inline** and **Reply Keyboards**. This feature allows users to switch from the visual keyboard builder to directly providing button configurations as JSON — enabling dynamic and advanced use cases.

### Key Improvements:

* New `Specify Keyboard` option:

  * `Using Fields Below` (default) — continue using the graphical interface
  * `Using JSON` — directly input Telegram-compatible JSON array of buttons
* Supports advanced button types:

  * Inline: `callback_data`, `url`, `switch_inline_query`, etc.
  * Reply: `request_contact`, `request_location`, `web_app`, etc.
* **Dynamic expressions** are supported for the JSON input
* Simplified input: only the `button array` is required
* Fully **backward-compatible** with existing Telegram workflows

### How to Test:

1. In the Telegram node:

   * Set **Reply Markup** to `Inline Keyboard` or `Reply Keyboard`
   * Choose `Using JSON` under **Specify Keyboard**
   * Paste valid button array JSON, e.g.:

**Inline Keyboard JSON Example**:

```json
[
  [
    {"text": "✅ Approve", "callback_data": "approve"},
    {"text": "❌ Reject", "callback_data": "reject"}
  ],
  [
    {"text": "📄 View Details", "url": "https://example.com/details"}
  ]
]
```

**Reply Keyboard JSON Example**:

```json
[
  [
    {"text": "📱 Share Contact", "request_contact": true},
    {"text": "📍 Share Location", "request_location": true}
  ],
  [
    {"text": "🌐 Open Web App", "web_app": {"url": "https://example.com"}}
  ],
  [
    {"text": "🔙 Back to Menu"}
  ]
]
```

> Other keyboard options (like `resize_keyboard`, `selective`, etc.) remain configurable in the UI section.

---

title: ci: Automate base image + sbom + attestation
body:
Replaces manual workflow dispatch with automated CI based on Dockerfile changes.

The new workflow triggers on pushes to the `master` branch when the base Dockerfile is modified. It builds and pushes multi-platform images with Node.js versions 20, 22, and 24 to both GitHub Container Registry and Docker Hub.

The base images will also now be published with the extra tags for the git commit sha, this will allow us to pin to those versions.

Also enables provenance and SBOM generation for the main Docker build push workflow.

## Summary

This PR adds SBOM and provenance attestations to our Docker images for improved supply chain security and license compliance.
Changes

Added sbom: true and provenance: true to all Docker build actions
Updated base image workflow to build on Dockerfile changes with immutable tags
Both n8n-base and n8n images now include attestation

### Check base image attestations
docker buildx imagetools inspect n8nio/base:20 --format "{{json .}}" | jq

#### Check main image attestations  
docker buildx imagetools inspect n8nio/n8n:latest --format "{{json .}}" | jq

### Look for these attestation types in the output:
 - "application/vnd.in-toto+json" entries
 - Predicates: "https://spdx.dev/Document" (SBOM)
 - Predicates: "https://slsa.dev/provenance/v0.2" (Provenance)

body: ## Summary https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a076c6a-9194-4a33-bfc6-b24a5a9531e9 On current <=4.6 versions of the Google Sheets Node `n8n-nodes-base.googleSheets` it isn't possible to update cells' value back to empty using the `Update Row` or `Append or Update Row` operations, like one would expect. This PR makes that possible by adding a new optional type option to Resouce Mapper Component (RMC), currently named `allowEmptyValues`. If node wishes to use `resourceMapper` but still accept empty strings as valid values (instead of skipping them) the node can opt in to this behaviour by enabling the flag on its property definition. title: Feature: Graphql websocket mode
body:
## Summary

Added WebSocket support to the GraphQL node to enable real-time GraphQL subscriptions. This enhancement allows users to connect to GraphQL servers that support WebSocket subscriptions, such as Mythic C2 servers (Offensive Security), for real-time data streaming.

### Key Features Added:
- **Connection Mode Selection**: Choose between HTTP (existing) and WebSocket (new) modes
- **WebSocket Protocol Support**: Supports `graphql-transport-ws`, `graphql-ws`, and legacy `graphql` protocols
- **Real-time Subscriptions**: Subscribe to GraphQL subscriptions for live data updates
- **Comprehensive Configuration**: WebSocket URL, timeouts, SSL settings, headers, variables, and operation names
- **Error Handling**: Robust error handling for different GraphQL WebSocket protocols and connection issues

### Testing:
1. Set Connection Mode to "WebSocket"
2. Configure WebSocket URL (e.g., `wss://your-server/graphql`)
3. Select appropriate subprotocol (default: `graphql-transport-ws`)
4. Enter GraphQL subscription query and variables
5. Execute to receive real-time subscription data

The implementation maintains full backward compatibility with existing HTTP functionality.

title: feat: Proxy all RudderStack frontend telemetry events through the backend
body:
## Summary

To prevent RudderStack or any other third-party service in front of their servers from seeing the user’s IP address, we are now proxying frontend telemetry events through our backend. This ensures that third-party services only receive the server’s IP address instead of the user’s, which is classified as personally identifiable information (PII).

## Background

The [initial approach](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/17088) was to remove the RudderStack SDK from the frontend and send telemetry data directly. However, the SDK handles important tasks like collecting browser, operating system, and device information. Reimplementing this logic manually would introduce complexity and potential inaccuracies.

## Implementation

We kept the RudderStack SDK on the frontend but configured it to send events to our backend instead of directly to RudderStack. The backend then proxies these events to RudderStack. This preserves the benefits of the SDK while protecting user IP addresses.

## How to test

1. Create a FE source in RudderStack
2. Copy the write key and replace the in the diagnostic configuration [here](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/bd6d9542539fb167c0119e571522173ec1aff2e0/packages/%40n8n/config/src/configs/diagnostics.config.ts#L22).
3. Go to the source in RudderStack and start live events.
4. Start n8n and start seeing the events coming in.

title: fix(core): Make our file reads more robust (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

I investigated Aikido's AI findings of our potentially weak points for file inclusion attacks. While I couldn't find anything actually exploitable lets adjust our code a bit, protecting us in future against potentially leaking files via these file operations if an attacker was somehow able to inject relative paths as file names, or perhaps via a malicious nodes icon files.

`safeJoinPath` can be used instead of `path.join` if you want to ensure the joined path doesn't escape the parent path you're joining to, and combining that with `isContainedWithin` allows us to ensure the created file paths don't escape the folders we intend to work within. To make these helpers available everywhere on the backend they are located in `@n8n/backend-common` and `isContainedWithin` was moved there.

title: chore: Fix hot reload for nodes-langchain package (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the hot reload functionality for the `@n8n/nodes-langchain` package during development. The main issues were:
1. The watch mode in the dev script was hanging due to chained commands
2. Hot reload was not working properly with chokidar v4
3. Credential lookup errors were occurring during the reload process

## Changes

### 1. Updated chokidar implementation for v4 compatibility
- Chokidar v4 [removed glob support](https://github.com/paulmillr/chokidar?tab=readme-ov-file#changelog), requiring a different approach
- Instead of watching glob patterns like `'**/*.json'`, we now watch directories and use the `ignored` function to filter files
- Added proper file filtering based on loader type (lazy-loaded vs regular packages)

### 2. Fixed tsup watch mode hanging issue
- Created a cross-platform post-build script (`post-build.js`) to replace chained shell commands
- The script runs all necessary post-build tasks (tsc-alias, copy files, generate metadata)

### 3. Improved hot reload reliability
- Watch the correct directory (`dist` for lazy-loaded packages)
- Only trigger reload on file changes and additions (not removals) to prevent issues during build
- Add 1sec delay to nodemon when started via watch to prevent issues 5678 port still being used because it was shutting-down

### 4. Update tsup watch configuration
- Explicitly watch specific directories: `nodes`, `credentials`, `utils`, `types`
- This ensures file changes are properly detected as just `entry` wasn't triggering recompile

title: perf(core): Improvements to GET `/workflows` endpoint
body:
## Summary

1. When filtering by tags load into memory all workflow data (including the pin data) which can be quite large, causing a a temporary memory spike.

title: fix(AWS Bedrock Chat Model Node): Do not show issues for arbitrary model names
body:
## Summary

It's possible to specify valid AWS Bedrock model name using expression (e.g. you can specify the inference profile instead of on demand model, like `arn:aws:bedrock:eu-central-1:218116993570:inference-profile/eu.anthropic.claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219-v1:0`). Thus we don't want to show errors if the evaluated expression isn't in the list of models fetched from the AWS Bedrock endpoint.

The new optional property `allowArbitraryValues` was introduced, which disables this check for the parameter of type `options`.

It also address the related issue: when the `options` parameter is specified via expression, and expression is not evaluated, we should not show validation issue "value '' is not allowed".

title: fix(core): Fix license in test containers
body:
## Summary

Test containers activate the e2e controller, which [disables all license features](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/657e5a3b3a5184b9f1f6b6303faabb9feef0d70a/packages/cli/src/controllers/e2e.controller.ts#L79-L110), leading to all license features being disabled in test containers except multi-main. 

Assuming the e2e controller is unneeded in the test container stack, we should keep it disabled. This does not affect multi-main because it is [explicitly enabled](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/1a39ab62ac99bf0733dc0cef16b3bc74a1cc26d2/packages/testing/containers/n8n-test-container-creation.ts#L153) by the test containers.

title: fix(Execute Sub-workflow Node): Improve paired item handling for child workflows
body:
## Summary

When we execute a subworkflow and this subworkflows changes the order of the items not as the last step, the paired item link is broken, because the ExecuteWorkflow Node just relies on the PairedItem information from the items of the last node of the subworkflow. This introduces a simple backtracking, which does not cover all possible cases, that tries to trace the paired items through the subworkflow execution data. This also exposes a new method to nodes to get access to other workflow executions.

title: fix(n8n Form Node): Make customizing form custom styles possible on mobile screens and on form end redirect
body:
## Summary

We are taking n8n forms in use at the welcome personalization survey. To support that use case I've been building a form with custom styles that gets embedded on that page. This PR fixes some annoyances I've noticed:

- It wasn't possible to style the background using `var(--color-background)` and `var(--color-card-bg)` on mobile screens like one would expect
- It wasn't possible to apply custom styles to the redirect page that briefly shows up as the redirect happens

This PR fixes both of those annoyances. Default forms on mobile do exactly the same.
