title: perf(core): Eliminate unnecessary license server calls
body:
## Summary

Every visit to `/settings/usage` as the instance owner triggers a renewal call to the license server, which always fails if the instance is unlicensed:

```
08:58:52.860   error   Failed to renew license: renewal failed because current cert is not initialized { "stack": "Error:  renewal failed because current cert is not initialized\n    at T._renew (/Users/ivov/Development/n8n/node_modules/.pnpm/@n8n_io+license-sdk@2.22.0/node_modules/@n8n_io/license-sdk/src/LicenseManager.ts: 443: 13)\n    at T.renew (/Users/ivov/Development/n8n/node_modules/.pnpm/@n8n_io+license-sdk@2.22.0/node_modules/@n8n_io/license-sdk/src/LicenseManager.ts: 432: 17)\n    at License.renew (/Users/ivov/Development/n8n/packages/cli/src/license.ts: 193: 22)\n    at LicenseService.renewLicense (/Users/ivov/Development/n8n/packages/cli/src/license/license.service.ts: 124: 23)\n    at LicenseController.renewLicense (/Users/ivov/Development/n8n/packages/cli/src/license/license.controller.ts: 69: 29)\n    at handler (/Users/ivov/Development/n8n/packages/cli/src/controller.registry.ts: 78: 41)\n    at /Users/ivov/Development/n8n/packages/cli/src/response-helper.ts: 157: 23\n    at Layer.handleRequest (/Users/ivov/Development/n8n/node_modules/.pnpm/router@2.2.0/node_modules/router/lib/layer.js: 152: 17)\n    at next (/Users/ivov/Development/n8n/node_modules/.pnpm/router@2.2.0/node_modules/router/lib/route.js: 157: 13)\n    at /Users/ivov/Development/n8n/packages/cli/src/controller.registry.ts: 153: 4", "file": "license.service.js", "function": "mapErrorMessage" }
08:58:52.861   error   400 Failed to renew license: renewal failed because current cert is not initialized { "file": "response-helper.js", "function": "sendErrorResponse" }
```

This PR ensures that the BE does not forward pointless renewal requests to license server.

This change was made on the BE, because the client makes the renewal call [without having license data in the store](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/3b1483096625ead20803a320567f651df221137c/packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/views/SettingsUsageAndPlan.vue#L107-L112). Changing this on the FE would require a call to fetch license data from the license server to decide whether to renew, which would negate the benefit. No context on why the client is laid out like this - ideally in future we can optimize further if the FE can make sure to have license data by the time it mounts this component.

title: fix(editor): Reset dirty state on workflow activation only if its current workflow
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

Currently, whenever a workflow is activated, and whatever the workflow, a 'workflowActivated' event is broadcasted to all socket clients. 
This events is caught and used to reset the dirty state so that dirty state is set to false. This means that if workflow B is set as active on one client (one user on a browser), then another client on another browser, working on workflow A, will get the dirty state reset to false, even if they made changes to the workflow.

This PR checks that the workflow which has been activated is the one currently working on in the canvas.

title: fix(Slack Node): Change Slack ts and thread_ts type to string
body:
## Summary

Slack treats their message timestamp (`ts` and `thread_ts`) as `string`. Due to the timestamp property type is defined as `number` here, n8n makes Slack API calls with `number` instead, unless it is specifically converted to `string`.

Some related official documents:
* https://api.slack.com/methods/chat.postMessage#arg_thread_ts
* https://api.slack.com/methods/chat.update#arg_ts
* https://github.com/slackapi/node-slack-sdk/issues/780

In the case of replying to a thread, it's silently sent the message to the channel as a separate thread. It doesn't throw any errors.

The issue seems to be started since https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/commit/bbc103fc268f65b69a556d6e6e83435f04403bfe. It was `string`, but converted to `number` for FE validation purposes.

```ts
async webhook(ctx: IWebhookFunctions): Promise<IWebhookResponseData> {
  const proxy = await ctx.getWorkflowDataProxy(0)
  // I expect that this data will be added to execution logs as metadata
  // as per https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.executiondata/
  proxy.$execution.customData.setAll({
    sessionId: 'abc123',
    userId: 'user456'
  })

  // ...
}
```

Webhook nodes can now use the same execution data customization capabilities as other node types, providing consistency across the n8n execution engine while maintaining backward compatibility.

title: feat(core)!: Introduce insecure mode in task runner
body:
## Summary

Introduce insecure mode (i.e. no sandboxing) in the task runner, for compatibility with libraries like `pdf-lib` and `puppeteer`. The existing flag to disable prototype mutation is not enough to allow compatibility.

Notes:
- The `n8n-task-runners.json` config file is being used by the official image and also has the secure flags `--disallow-code-generation-from-strings` and `--disable-proto=delete` so I decided not to add `N8N_RUNNERS_INSECURE_MODE` as an allowed env. If a user is able to deploy a runner in external mode and wants to make it insecure, they will know to edit this config file.
- Since the `N8N_RUNNERS_ALLOW_PROTOTYPE_MUTATION` is not satisfying its goal of allowing compatibility, I decided this time it's worth outright replacing this flag rather than maintaining it for a long deprecation period. Let me know if you disagree.
- The implementations for run-once-for-all-items and run-once-for-each-item modes are very similar but not 100% identical, so I decided not to abstract them away. The deduplication does not seem worth the indirection.
- To share the `'secure' | 'insecure'` we'd have to extract this type to a common package like `@n8n/backend-common`, as `cli` conditionally imports `@n8n/task-runner` and the latter cannot import the former. But moving this out to a separate package does not seem worth it only to share a small union type.

title: feat(Cohere Chat Model Node): Add Cohere Chat Model node
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces support for Cohere Chat Models in n8n and fixes a streaming issue with the Tools Agent.

### 1. Add Cohere Chat Model Node

- **New Node**: Adds `LmChatCohere` node that integrates Cohere's chat models (Command, Command-R, etc.)
- **Credentials Enhancement**: Updates `CohereApi` credentials to support custom base URLs for enterprise/proxy configurations
- **Token Usage Tracking**: Implements a custom `tokensUsageParser` that correctly extracts token usage from Cohere's response format

### 2. Fix Tools Agent Streaming Issue

When creating a custom `RunnableSequence` for the Tools Agent, the `streamRunnable` property wasn't being properly passed to the `AgentExecutor`, causing potential streaming-related issues. To fix this, we cast the `RunnableSequence` to `AgentRunnableSequence` type and explicitly set `streamRunnable: false` and `singleAction: false` properties before passing to `AgentExecutor`

### 3. Update Token Usage Parser Interface
Modified the `TokensUsageParser` type from accepting `LLMResult['llmOutput']` to accepting the full `LLMResult` object Different LLM providers return token usage in different formats - some in `llmOutput`, others in `generations`

body:
## Summary

While working on #16834 I noticed every call to `getParentTypes` (e.g. via credentials testing) mutates the existing parents array, i.e. we keep appending credential types to the `extends` array of a credential type in memory. This is not currently causing a bug that I know of, but this is incorrect and unintended and might lead to unexpected behavior in future. Let's fix it before it does.

title: fix(core): Deduplicate credential types when lazyloading
body:
## Summary

For lazyloaded packages, we [load](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/0debbc3503246d44741cff846482f5aab5f84dc6/packages/core/src/nodes-loader/lazy-package-directory-loader.ts#L9-L13) all credentials types descriptions and locations from build artifacts - and later when we need a credential type, we [instantiate](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/0debbc3503246d44741cff846482f5aab5f84dc6/packages/core/src/nodes-loader/directory-loader.ts#L253-L256) it on demand from its class file location and cache the instance in memory.

But when we instantiate a credential type on demand, we also [push](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/0debbc3503246d44741cff846482f5aab5f84dc6/packages/core/src/nodes-loader/directory-loader.ts#L245) it to the collection of loaded credential types, which was already populated with all credentials descriptions. This likely was intended for eagerly loaded credentials types, but not for lazyloaded ones. Therefore, all lazyloaded credential types that are instantiated on demand end up duplicated in memory. Also, these copies are not 100% identical to credentials descriptions - these copies lack the `iconUrl` and `supportedNodes` properties added to credentials types during startup.

When we later happen to trigger credentials types to be [regenerated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/0debbc3503246d44741cff846482f5aab5f84dc6/packages/cli/src/services/frontend.service.ts#L55) (e.g. on community package install), these credential types polluted with duplicates are written to the static cache at `~/.cache/n8n/public/types/credentials.json`. See a sample cache [here](https://gist.github.com/ivov/6e5f57340984c4ec384f6b462bab361c) with ~60 duplicates, e.g.  `salesforceOAuth2Api` and `payPalApi`. 

The FE then fetches this polluted cache and loads it in the Pinia store [by credential type name](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/0debbc3503246d44741cff846482f5aab5f84dc6/packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/stores/credentials.store.ts#L218), so the duplicates overwrite the originals on the client side. As a result, the client stops requesting credentials icons because of the missing `iconUrl` and also loses track of some nodes-creds relations because of the missing `supportedNodes`.

Hence this PR stops us from loading lazyloaded credential types twice in memory. Lazyloaded node types are unaffected. In future we might want to enforce uniqueness with a map, and perhaps move away from having a monolithic cache for node and cred types.

title: feat(LangChain Nodes): Upgrade LangChain and improve proxy handling for LLM nodes
body:
## Summary

This PR upgrades the LangChain packages and improves proxy handling in the @n8n/nodes-langchain package to provide better enterprise proxy support, including NO_PROXY handling.

All LangChain packages have been upgraded to their latest versions, with OpenAI SDK upgraded from v4 to v5.

Breaking change in OpenAI v5: The httpAgent option was removed and replaced with fetchOptions.dispatcher, [requiring the use of undici's dispatcher interface](https://github.com/openai/openai-node?tab=readme-ov-file#configuring-proxies). 

To unify proxy logic with the core nodes (which rely on `getAgentWithProxy` from `requestHelperFunctions`), same `proxy-from-env` approach was used. It allows to respect `NO_PROXY` env variables, but requires `targetUrl` to determine the `proxyUrl`.

As LangChain models only allow providing proxy agent during initialization (and not dynamically) – baseUrls were used instead of targetUrl, which should reasonably cover at least domains specified in `NO_PROXY`.

For some LangChain models it's difficult to know even the domain in advance (e.g. AWS Bedrock Chat). In that case dummy target URL is used, so `NO_PROXY` would not be respected.

### Key Changes

1. Proxy Implementation

- Replaced manual environment variable checking with proxy-from-env package (same approach used in core package)

2. Environment Variable Priority

The new implementation respects the standard proxy environment variable behavior:
- For HTTPS URLs: Uses HTTPS_PROXY or https_proxy
- For HTTP URLs: Uses HTTP_PROXY or http_proxy
- Lowercase variables take precedence over uppercase (following curl/wget conventions) ‼️
- NO_PROXY/no_proxy is respected for excluding hosts from proxy ‼️
- No proxy will be used if target URL is not specified and only HTTP_PROXY environment variable is set ‼️

3. Target URL Handling

- Added optional targetUrl parameter to properly determine which proxy to use (and to handle `NO_PROXY`)
- When target URL is unknown (e.g., AWS Bedrock), uses a dummy URL as fallback
- This ensures proxy support even when the final destination isn't known in advance

### Package Updates

'@langchain/core': 0.3.61
'@langchain/openai': 0.5.16
'@langchain/anthropic': 0.3.23
'@langchain/community': 0.3.47
'langchain': 0.3.29

title: fix(Token Splitter Node): Prevent tiktoken blocking on repetitive content
body:
## Summary

js-tiktoken can block the Node.js process and consume excessive memory when processing texts with many sequentially repeating characters. This creates a DoS vulnerability where malicious actors could send payloads like 'a' repeated 100,000+ times to hang the process.

## Solution

Detect repetitive content before tiktoken processing and fall back to character-based token estimation:

1. **Detection**: `hasLongSequentialRepeat()` checks for 1000+ sequential character repeats
2. **Fallback**: Use character-based estimation (chars/token ratios) instead of tiktoken
3. **Scope**: Applied to both LLM tracing and text splitting operations

### Trade-offs

**Pros:**
- Prevents process blocking and memory exhaustion
- Minimal performance impact for normal text (early exit on detection)
- Maintains functionality with reduced accuracy for edge cases

**Cons:**
- Token counts are estimates for repetitive content (accuracy vs performance)
- Character-based splitting may not respect token boundaries perfectly


## Implementation Details

### Detection Algorithm
- Uses string iterator for O(1) memory complexity (vs O(n) with array conversion)
- Properly handles multi-byte Unicode characters (emojis, etc.)
- Threshold of 1000 characters balances security with legitimate use cases

### Token Estimation
- Simple character count divided by model-specific ratios (e.g., 4.0 for GPT-4)
- Trade-off: Less accurate but prevents blocking
- Character-based splitting maintains approximate chunk sizes

### Error Handling
- All functions validate inputs and return safe defaults
- Tiktoken failures gracefully fall back to estimation
- No exceptions thrown to callers

title: feat(editor): Add What's New notification callout
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a callout notification that shows up when new "What's new" articles are available. Clicking on the notification takes the user to the What's new modal. The modal can be dismissed, in which case it won't be shown on future page loads - unless new "What's new" items are added on the article.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cce3088b-b9d4-4243-8c6f-68e98e49817f

Also various other issues that were brought up on product review were addressed:

1. The text of the notification is read from a separate `calloutText` field.

2. We also made some last minute changes to the API that returns this data, and this PR makes those changes to the data model we expect. Also a bit of resliency to unexpected responses was added, but not much. Still, before this branch gets deployed we can't deploy the creators site backend changes to prod, else master would start failing. I'll take care of deploying that at the right time.

3. Also drop the use of DynamicScroller, and simplify the modal's overflows to make it look better on windows (and to not have double scrollbar). Scrolling to the correct item is now done with plain javascript.

4. The callout on what's new modal is only shown if there's a significant update available (>= 2 minors or security).

title: refactor(Structured Output Parser Node): Support schema via expression
body:
## Summary

Previously, output parsers were always fetched at index 0, causing all items in a batch to use the same parser configuration. Additionally, the input schema field had `noDataExpression: true`, preventing users from using n8n expressions to dynamically generate schemas based on input data.
This PR refactors the output parser resolution to support per-item configuration:

#### Changes:
1. **Modified `getOptionalOutputParser()` function**
   - Added optional `index` parameter (defaults to 0)
   - Parser retrieval now uses the provided index while configuration check remains at index 0

2. **Updated parser instantiation in nodes**
   - **ToolsAgent V2**: Moved parser creation inside the item processing loop
   - **ChainLLM**: Pass current `itemIndex` to `getOptionalOutputParser()`
   - Each item now gets its own parser instance based on its position

3. **Enabled expressions in schema field**
   - Changed `noDataExpression` from `true` to `false` in `buildInputSchemaField()`

title: fix(Google Sheets Node): Inconsistent Google Sheet Tool update behavior due to wrong type of row_number field
body:
## Summary

`row_number` field property used to match rows for the update operation in Google Sheet was `string`, but used as a number:
https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/f4d0b9f79609633f86a6126d060fdc1c13ca5ab9/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/Sheet/v2/helpers/GoogleSheet.ts#L610

Using the Google Sheet node's update operation as a tool for AI Agent ended up with incorrect tool schema (`row_number: string`). Also, when switching to expression mode to customize `$fromAi` parameters – it was possible to accidentally add a space after the `{{ $fromAi(...) }} `, which led to Google Sheet API error `Unable to parse range`

So the type for the field was changed to `number`.

title: refactor(core): Make instances more resilient to license sync issues
body:
## Summary

On license renewal...

- in scaling single-main mode, main messages workers and webhook-type instances to reload the license via pubsub, and
- in scaling multi-main mode, the leader main messages follower mains, workers, and webhook-type instances to reload the license via pubsub.

Since pubsub messages are ephemeral and not retried, any instance who for any reason missed the `reload-license` message will remain with a stale license in memory, until it receives a new `reload-license` message or until it restarts. A stale license in memory can lead to failing license runtime checks for an otherwise valid license.

This PR uses the license SDK's newly added [`onExpirySoon` callback](https://github.com/n8n-io/license-management/pull/149) to trigger a license reload when a non-leader (follower main, worker, webhook-type instance) is 2h away from license expiry, to account for any missed pubsub messages.

title: feat: Improve Aws Credential to allow Assumption of IAM Roles
body:
## Summary

This PR adds improvements to the AWS credential that address both security best practices and allows for advanced AWS access patterns, like enabling cross-account AWS access on behalf of the user's credentials, or the n8n server.

The current implementation only allows for IAM User Access Key / Secret Key (or temporary credentials that will need to be constantly refreshed). This pattern is against AWS's best practice recommendations to have workloads that assume an IAM Role rather than rely on long-lived credentials:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html#bp-workloads-use-roles
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-user.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_common-scenarios_third-party.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/v1/userguide/cli-configure-role.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com#cli-role-prepare

To address this, I've added a new feature to the AWS Credential. Once PR is reviewed and merged, I will gladly add documentation.

Summary:

1. Add a toggle for "Credential Type" which by default is the existing options for `IAM Access Key` and new option for `Assume IAM Role`

2. For Role Assumption: 

- the user must provide a Role ARN, an ExternalID (to address the "Confused Deputy" problem) and a Session Name
- the user can choose to "Use System Credentials for STS Call" if the n8n administrator has configured AWS credentials in the environment variables OR in an EC2/ECS/EKS role on the n8n server. The system creds must have permission to assume roles on behalf of any n8n users and should require an external id to be configured. (The system credentials will never be used for anything but `sts.AssumeRole` by this credential, users must not be allowed to use the system creds for workflows)
- the user can also choose to provide an Access Key & Secret Key that is used to perform the STS AssumeRole call if the administrator has not configured system AWS credentials. 

⚠️ Note about External ID: This should actually be something unique that n8n generates per-credential and displays to the user, and not something the user is able to configure. I couldn't figure out a way to make the credential editor do something like this though (generate a value that is used as part of the credential and display it read-only to the user). Instead, I've documented this deviation from best practice and suggest to the user that the External ID they generate on their own should be treated as a secret from any other users they don't trust within the same n8n instance. This is not ideal but is the best I can come up with.

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/apn/securely-using-external-id-for-accessing-aws-accounts-owned-by-others/

3. For IAM Access Key:

- the behavior is still the same and is backward compatible with existing AWS credentials
- I have created several unit tests that show existing credentials should continue working fine, but someone else might want to review too

![aws_credential](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/acec3b3b-56e5-4038-9601-73ae77288cd8)

title: feat(core): Add Support for Additional Body Properties in OAuth2 API Client Credentials Flow
body:
## Summary

Add support for sending additional body properties when using OAuth2 client credentials grant type with body authentication.

This enhancement allows users to include custom properties in the token request body when authenticating with OAuth2 services that require additional parameters beyond the standard client_id and client_secret.

This PR merely exposes it for use in the Generic OAuth2 API Credentials Configuration UI. The backend work to support additional body properties in the token request were done in previous MRs by other contributors:
- https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/15003
- https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/15335

This resolves a community pain point that was first expressed back in 2023: https://community.n8n.io/t/oauth2-options-and-troubleshooting/25374.

There are a number of APIs that use OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Flow which require additional properties in body during the token request (such as audience). Here are a few examples:
- [Pax8](https://devx.pax8.com/reference/createaccesstoken)
- [SPS Commerce](https://developercenter.spscommerce.com/#/docs/new-authentication-docs/machine2machine-applications)
- [Ory](https://www.ory.sh/docs/hydra/guides/audiences)

### Changes
- Add `sendAdditionalBodyProperties` boolean field to OAuth2Api credentials
- Add `additionalBodyProperties` JSON field for custom body parameters
- Update OAuth2 client initialization to include additional body properties when configured
- Display additional body properties field only when grant type is 'clientCredentials', authentication is 'body', and sendAdditionalBodyProperties is enabled

###  Testing
- Verified additional body properties are correctly parsed and included in token requests
- Confirmed field visibility logic works as expected with display options
- Tested with various JSON configurations for additional properties

title: Fix: Consistent Use of `testTimeout` in Jest Configurations
body:
The `testTimeout` property is used to define the maximum time a test can run before Jest considers it a failure. While some `jest.config.js` files define it (e.g., `packages\cli\jest.config.js` and `packages\@n8n\ai-workflow-builder\jest.config.js`), others do not. For consistency and to ensure tests do not run indefinitely, it is good practice to define a default `testTimeout` in the root `jest.config.js` so all packages inherit it.

Applied fixes:
--- a/jest.config.js
+++ b/jest.config.js
@@ -50,6 +50,7 @@
 	collectCoverage: isCoverageEnabled,
 	coverageReporters: ['text-summary', 'lcov', 'html-spa'],
 	workerIdleMemoryLimit: '1MB',
+	testTimeout: 5_000, // Default timeout for tests in milliseconds
 };

title: fix(core): Show correct error messages when nodes can't be used in an expression
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

Because partial executions trim the workflow down to only the nodes that connect the trigger and the destination node the `WorkflowDataProxy` can't differentiate between nodes that are not connected to the node referencing them and nodes that simply don't exist.

Take this workflow as an example:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8af741d3-74ae-4a9f-9a91-a25bf3f33d80)

For the orphaned node:
 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bc9e46f9-1418-4d2f-9a7c-7e3498b9fe1e

For the child node:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc387c18-79a1-4f07-8f56-9f0cebfeb0e3

For a missing node:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/893039e8-a1f2-4cc2-ae18-e85e1d371449

After evaluating different ways to fix this, including:
1. giving a more generic error during partial executions (e.g. "Error finding the referenced node. Make sure the node you referenced is spelled correctly and is a parent of this node.")
	* impacts UX
	* complicates the `WorkflowDataProxy`
2. threading the original workflow through to the `WorkflowDataProxy`, (e.g. adding an optional `originalWorkflow` property to the `Worfklow`)
	* complicates the `WorkflowDataProxy`
3. passing the original workflow to the `WorkflowExecute.processRunExecutionData` and relying on `runNodeFilter` to pass over disabled and unrelated nodes correctly
	* risk of introducing partial execution regressions

I chose the 3rd option as it may just work and retain the UX while avoiding complicating the `WorkflowDataProxy`.

## Summary

- Created local `tiktoken.ts` utility with bundled `cl100k_base.json` and `o200k_base.json` files
- Updated `N8nLlmTracing.ts` to use local tokenizer for LLM token counting
- Added custom `TokenTextSplitter` class since the original doesn't accept custom tokenizers
- Modified build process to copy JSON encoding files to dist folder
- Added `js-tiktoken` dependency for lightweight tokenization

title: feat(Code Node): Allow Preloading pyodide modules for Python Code Node
body:
## Summary

This PR serves to improve the functionality of the Code Node when using Python / Pyodide.

Add the `N8N_NODES_PYTHON_PACKAGES_PRELOAD` environment variable to the config. This is used to specify which Pyodide modules get preloaded in the VM since they cannot be lazy loaded due to lack of network access during Code Node runtime. Example `N8N_NODES_PYTHON_PACKAGES_PRELOAD=matplotlib,numpy` will preload these modules to the Pyodide environment.

This should not introduce any security concerns, packages are not retrieved from PyPI, they are precompiled for the WSM Pyodide environment and operate within the same sandbox.

https://pyodide.org/en/stable/usage/packages-in-pyodide.html#packages-in-pyodide

title: refactor(core): Move module logic to `@n8n/backend-common`
body:
## Summary

As part of the extensions project, we need to allow modules to import the utils at `packages/cli/test/integration/shared` for use in integration tests in modules, which means moving those utils to `@n8n/backend-test-utils`. 

And as a prerequisite for that move, we need to move the DB connection to `@n8n/db` so it can be shared with `cli` and `@n8n/backend-test-utils`. 

And as a prerequisite for that DB connection move, we need to move module logic to `@n8n/backend-common` so it can be shared with `cli` and `@n8n/backend-test-utils`. This is because `DbConnectionOptions` relies on `ModuleRegistry` to add a module's entities to the typeorm connection before it is established.

Hence this PR starts by moving module logic to `@n8n/backend-common`. 

Notes:
- This PR also moves modules hooks registration to `cli` to prevent a dep cycle between `@n8n/backend-common` and `n8n-core`.

title: feat(Sticky Note Node): Support YouTube video embeds on Sticky notes
body:
## Summary

Support embedding YouTube player on sticky notes by entering a custom markdown tag like

`@[youtube](<video_id>)`

for instance

```
## I'm a note 
**Double click** to edit me. [Guide](https://docs.n8n.io/workflows/sticky-notes/)

@[youtube](ZCuL2e4zC_4)
```

renders as 

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c02cb74c-fda5-4cb4-a9e3-369d79eba0af)

This will also be used as an enabler for `What's new` section articles.

I did consider using existing `markdown-it-video` plugin but that seemed long abandoned and had unnecessary functionality, and implementing a plugin for just YouTube ourselves wasn't that difficult.

To support the YouTube iframe on the rendered HTML a double sanitization had to be removed - Markdown content no longer passes through `sanitize-html` with `v-n8n-html`. The security implications need to be throughly considered, but `xss` should already prevent XSS attacks from happening.

title: feat(editor): Allow users to update verified nodes from the node settings panel
body:
## Summary

Allow users to update verified nodes from the node settings panel

This PR also does the following:
- Renames `activePackage` to `unverifiedNodesPackage` to discern between verified community node and unverified community nodes as unverified community nodes comes from Community Node store but verified community nodes comes from Node Types store
- Includes `semver` as dependency to differentiate between the currently installed version and version available in strapi. We already have this dependency installed in the root and we need to make it accessible to the FE
- Includes a notice for users who enable both verified and unverified nodes since we want to prevent them from installing verified nodes with versions we haven't vetted yet

To test with verified nodes and Verdaccio:
1. Cherry-pick `db80abc4fd7057554983f1cfd1ebb20e08f0081e`
2. Set `export N8N_UNVERIFIED_PACKAGES_ENABLED=false` and `export N8N_VERIFIED_PACKAGES_ENABLED=true`
3. Follow the instructions in the Verdaccio doc on Notion

To test with verified nodes and npm:
1. Set `export N8N_UNVERIFIED_PACKAGES_ENABLED=false` and `export N8N_VERIFIED_PACKAGES_ENABLED=true`

To test with verified and unverified nodes:
1. Set `export N8N_UNVERIFIED_PACKAGES_ENABLED=true` and `export N8N_VERIFIED_PACKAGES_ENABLED=true`

To test with unverified nodes only:
1. Set `export N8N_UNVERIFIED_PACKAGES_ENABLED=true` and `export N8N_VERIFIED_PACKAGES_ENABLED=false`

title: fix(Postgres Node): Handle comma-separated parameters in queries
body:
## Summary

## Problem
The Postgres Node's `stringToArray` function incorrectly splits query parameters at every comma, including commas inside quoted values. This breaks queries where parameters contain commas (e.g., `"Smith, John"` gets split into `"Smith"` and `" John"`), causing SQL execution errors.

## Solution
Enhanced the `stringToArray` function in `packages/nodes-base/nodes/Postgres/v2/helpers/utils.ts` to properly handle:
- Quoted values containing commas (both single and double quotes)
- Escaped quotes within quoted values  
- Mixed quoted and unquoted parameters
- Empty quoted values
- Proper whitespace trimming

The new implementation uses a state machine approach to track quote boundaries and only splits on commas outside of quoted contexts.

## Changes Made
- **Enhanced `stringToArray` function**: Replaced simple comma splitting with quote-aware parsing

## Test Coverage
Added extensive test cases in `utils.test.ts`:
- Basic comma-separated values
- Values with internal commas when quoted
- Mixed quoted/unquoted values  
- Escaped quotes handling
- Single and double quote support
- Empty quoted values
- Whitespace handling

title: feat(Airtable Node): Add field ID support for more resilient workflows
body:
# feat(Airtable Node): Add field ID support for more resilient workflows

- Add 'Use Field IDs' option for create/update/upsert operations
- Add 'Return Fields By Field ID' option for get/search operations
- Fetch field name to ID mappings from Airtable API
- Maintain backward compatibility with existing workflows
- Add comprehensive tests for field ID functionality

This makes workflows more robust when field names change in Airtable, as field IDs remain constant unlike field names.

## Summary

This PR adds support for using Airtable field IDs instead of field names in the Airtable node. This addresses a common pain point where workflows break when field names are changed in Airtable, since field IDs remain constant.

### Key Features:
1. **Use Field IDs** toggle for create/update/upsert operations - automatically converts field names to IDs
2. **Return Fields By Field ID** option for get/search operations - returns data with field IDs as keys
3. UI continues to display field names for easy configuration
4. Full backward compatibility - existing workflows work unchanged

### How to test:

1. **Create operation with field IDs:**
   - Add an Airtable node set to "Create" 
   - Configure your base and table
   - Map some fields using the column mapper
   - Enable the "Use Field IDs" toggle
   - Execute the workflow - fields will be sent using IDs instead of names

2. **Get operation with field IDs:**
   - Add an Airtable node set to "Get"
   - Configure base, table, and record ID
   - Enable "Return Fields By Field ID" option
   - Execute - the response will have field IDs as keys (e.g., `fld1234` instead of `Name`)

3. **Test resilience to field name changes:**
   - Create a workflow with "Use Field IDs" enabled
   - Change a field name in Airtable
   - Run the workflow again - it should still work correctly

### Screenshots:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6c86cfb-69f7-4adc-8220-c93abee23af3)

The new options appear prominently in the UI:

**For Create/Update operations:**
```
Base: [Your Base]
Table: [Your Table]  
Columns: [Field mappings]
☐ Use Field IDs  ← New toggle here
Options: [Other options]
```

**For Get/Search operations:**
```
Record ID: [ID]
☐ Return Fields By Field ID  ← New option here
Options: [Other options]
```

title: fix(client-oauth2): 👻 ensure client_credentials flow follows RFC 6749
body:
## Summary
This PR ensures that the OAuth2 client credentials flow strictly follows [RFC 6749](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc6749.txt) specifications, particularly section 4.4.3, which states that no refresh token should be included in the response.

## Changes Made
- Modified the [ClientOAuth2Token](https://github.com/uklok/n8n/blob/master/packages/%40n8n/client-oauth2/src/client-oauth2-token.ts) class to handle the client credentials flow without expecting a refresh token
- Updated the credentials flow implementation to properly handle token responses according to the spec
- Added type safety to distinguish between different grant types

## Testing
- [x] Verified that client credentials flow works without refresh tokens
- [x] Confirmed that token refresh attempts are made for client credentials grant type
- [x] Ensured backward compatibility with existing implementations

## Related Issues
- [Fixes: OAuth2 Client Credentials | Not refreshing expired tokens](https://community.n8n.io/t/oauth2-client-credentials-not-refreshing-expired-tokens/127129/6)
- [Ref: OAUTH Bearer Token Refresh Issue?](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/10199)

## Additional Context
According to RFC 6749 Section 4.4.3, the client credentials flow should not return a refresh token. This change ensures compliance with the specification while maintaining backward compatibility with existing code.

Note: I have touched the minimum amount of code to solve the issue and preserve current behavior. I assume a better solution could be set in place but this would cover both scenarios for now.

title: perf(core): Skip init for unlicensed modules
body:
## Summary

As part of the extensions project, we finally have a mechanism to stop loading into memory expensive features that are excluded from the user's license. This will benefit most cloud instances and self-hosters, as comparatively only very few instances have access to Enterprise features. On bootup we now load the entrypoints for all modules, register their DB entities, and initialize only free and licensed features that are enabled.

In future we could explore more optimizations like not loading entrypoints and entities at all, but the effort there is bigger and the benefit smaller, because entrypoints dynamically load dependencies and DB entities are unlikely to have any.

title: fix(core): Register transition handlers after modules init
body:
## Summary

At #15871 we moved module loading to the entrypoint, to allow modules to register their own DB entities before we establish the DB connection. But we missed that at this early stage the license has not initialized yet, i.e. `InstanceSettings.isMultiMain` still evaluates to `false` and so we fail to register the leadership transition handlers.

This PR moves transition handler registration back down to its [original position](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/14940/files#diff-9127350789432874069fb52007d0658e9bb7ea76ca4ee3ee038d9a968b5e5284R98) after modules initialize. Also removed an excess decorator left behind by a misresolved merge.

To test, start two mains, wind down the leader, and watch as the new leader starts all the decorated services: adding triggers and pollers, wait tracking, executions pruning, etc.

# Description
Backport of #29894 to `release-candidate/2.19.x`.

2.19.3 makes instances that are connected to a git repo via ssh crash on startup.

Motivated by https://n8nio.slack.com/archives/C069KJBJ8HE/p1778083726698099?thread_ts=1778083017.559409&cid=C069KJBJ8HE

## Checklist for the author (@konstantintieber ) to go through.

- [x] Review the backport changes
- [x] Fix possible conflicts
- [x] Merge to target branch

After this PR has been merged, it will be picked up in the next patch release for release track.

# Original description

## Summary

https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/29834 bumped `simple-git` to 3.36.0 which blocks `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` by default as a security hardening measure. This broke n8n startup when source control is configured with an SSH connection.                                                
                                                                                                                                                              
This PR adds `allowUnsafeSshCommand: true` to opt in to the `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` usage. This is safe because the SSH command is constructed internally from n8n-managed paths, not from user input.

Also adds a test assertion to catch this if the option is ever removed.

title: fix(ai-builder): Preserve collected planning context
body:
## Summary

Preserve planning context that was already collected before the planner sub-agent runs, i.e. what answers were already answered and what resources were already discovered so it doesn't ask for a credential name that it already knows of...

Example:
```
## Already-collected answers

- What should this workflow do?: Create a todo list for me based on discussions in Slack
- How often should it run?: Every morning
- Which Slack messages should it read?: All channels I'm a member of
- Where should the output go?: Email it to me
- Which model should it use?: Anthropic
- Credential selected for slackApi: Slack account (slackApi)
- Credential selected for anthropicApi: Anthropic account (anthropicApi)

## Already-discovered resources

- Credentials available: Slack account (slackApi), Anthropic account (anthropicApi)
- Data tables available: Personal todos, Team tasks
```

**Disclaimer:**  It's a bit disorganised, basically assembling the context by hand. https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/28666 in this (a bit orphaned) PR we improve these briefings by making them fully typed and in a central place... we should move that over the line and use the typed contract for this PR as well...

**What does it do checklist:**
- Adds prior `ask-user` answers plus credential and data table discovery results to the planner briefing as dedicated sections.
- Reads prior tool observations from the current message group when available, so planner follow-up runs can still see context collected earlier in that assistant turn.
- Records selected credential names/types from prior credential setup results when a matching credential list result is available.
- Shares tool-name constants with the tools that emit the observed events, reducing drift if tool IDs change.
- Tells the planner to trust already-collected briefing context and avoid re-asking for those choices.
- Avoids appending the same current user request twice when memory already returned it.

title: fix(ai-workflow-builder): Use OS path separator in MCP node-type path check
body:
## Summary

The MCP `get_node_types` tool fails on Windows with `Invalid path - path traversal detected` for every legitimate node ID, blocking the MCP workflow-building loop. Other MCP tools (`search_nodes`, `validate_workflow`, etc.) are unaffected.

### Root cause

The path-containment check in [code-builder-get.tool.ts:49](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/packages/%40n8n/ai-workflow-builder.ee/src/code-builder/tools/code-builder-get.tool.ts#L49) hardcodes `'/'` as the path separator:

```ts
return resolvedPath.startsWith(resolvedBase + '/') || resolvedPath === resolvedBase;
```

On Windows, `path.resolve()` returns paths with backslash separators (e.g. `C:\Users\foo\nodes\sub`). Comparing them against `resolvedBase + '/'` (e.g. `C:\Users\foo\nodes/`) always fails — every legitimate path gets flagged as path traversal.

n8n already has a canonical implementation of this check in [`@n8n/backend-common`](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/packages/%40n8n/backend-common/src/utils/path-util.ts#L8-L17) that correctly uses `path.sep`. This PR aligns the tool's local copy with that pattern.

### Fix

Replace the hardcoded `'/'` with `path.sep`. One-character behavioral change on Windows (`\\` instead of `/`), no observable change on POSIX (`sep` is `'/'` there).

### Test

`pnpm --filter @n8n/ai-workflow-builder test:unit code-builder-get` — 36/36 passing (35 existing + 1 new).

The new regression test simulates Windows `resolve` + `sep` behavior using `path.win32` since `path.resolve` on POSIX won't produce Windows-style paths. It asserts:
- `winChild.startsWith(winBase + path.win32.sep)` is `true` (the fix works)
- `winChild.startsWith(winBase + '/')` is `false` (documents the bug)

body:
## Summary

Adds the first runtime code to `@n8n/engine` (post-scaffold from CAT-2906): an HTTP server factory and an in-process e2e test harness.

- `createEngineServer()` — sync factory; builds an Express app exposing `GET /healthz` → `{ status: 'ok' }`. Returns `{ app }` (no I/O).
- `startEngineServer()` — async harness in `src/testing/`; calls the factory, listens on `127.0.0.1:0`, returns `{ url, stop }` (`stop` is a promisified `server.close()`).
- Smoke test (`*.e2e.test.ts`) hits real loopback HTTP via `supertest`.

### Deviations from the ticket

- **No separate `@n8n/engine-server` package.** Collapsed into `@n8n/engine` with a `src/server/` directory split. The package boundary was already flagged as provisional in the ticket, and there's no foreseeable consumer of the engine library independent of the server. Cheaper to evolve in-package and extract later if a real consumer appears.
- **Not wired into CI.** The smoke test runs only via the per-package `test:e2e` script; default `pnpm test` excludes `*.e2e.test.ts`. We can promote it once the harness has stabilised.

### How to test

\`\`\`bash
pnpm --filter=@n8n/engine test         # default, skips e2e
pnpm --filter=@n8n/engine test:e2e     # boots harness, hits /healthz

title: fix(core): Initialise encryption key proxy on worker and webhook instances
body:
## Summary

When `N8N_ENV_FEAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY_ROTATION=true`, the `EncryptionKeyManagerModule` was restricted to `main` instances only. As a result, `EncryptionKeyProxy.setProvider()` was never called on worker or webhook instances, so `isConfigured()` always returned `false` and those instances silently fell back to legacy CBC decryption — meaning they could not decrypt GCM-encrypted credentials.

This fix removes the `instanceTypes` restriction from the module so it loads on all instance types. Key creation (bootstrapping) is guarded to `main` only — workers and webhooks only wire up the provider so they can read existing keys from the database.

**Before:** Workers and webhook instances always used the legacy CBC path, failing to decrypt credentials encrypted with the active GCM DEK.

**After:** Workers and webhook instances initialise the key proxy on startup and correctly decrypt GCM-encrypted credentials using the existing DEKs in `deployment_key`.

### Changes

- `encryption-key-manager.module.ts` — removed `instanceTypes: ['main']` restriction; controller import guarded to `main` only
- `encryption-bootstrap.service.ts` — key creation (`bootstrapLegacyCbcKey` / `bootstrapGcmKey`) guarded to `main` only; `setProvider()` runs on all instance types

### How to test

1. Start n8n in queue mode with `N8N_ENV_FEAT_ENCRYPTION_KEY_ROTATION=true` (main + worker).
2. Create a credential via the main — confirm `credentials_entity.data` has a UUID prefix (GCM-encrypted).
3. Run a workflow on the worker that uses that credential — it should decrypt successfully.
4. Confirm worker logs show `Encryption key bootstrap complete`.
5. Confirm no new rows appear in `deployment_key` after the worker starts (key creation skipped).

title: fix(core): Filter WaitTracker to only poll waiting executions
body:
## Summary

`ExecutionRepository.getWaitingExecutions()` was filtering with `status != 'crashed'` instead of `status = 'waiting'`. This meant executions in terminal states (`error`, `success`, `canceled`) that retained a stale `waitTill` value — so-called zombie rows — were returned on every poll cycle.

For each zombie row, WaitTracker would compute a negative `setTimeout` delta (since `waitTill` was in the past), Node.js would emit a `TimeoutNegativeWarning`, the timer would fire in ~1ms, `startExecution()` would be called but blocked by the already-resuming guard, and the row would remain in the next poll — repeating every ~60s indefinitely.

Part of this fix was originally applied in #27066 but was dropped when that PR was reverted in #28538.

**Changes:**
- `getWaitingExecutions()`: `status: Not('crashed')` → `status: 'waiting'` — only executions explicitly in the waiting state should ever be resumed
- `markAsCrashed()`: clear `waitTill` when bulk-marking executions as crashed
- `cancelMany()`: clear `waitTill` when bulk-cancelling executions
- `stopBeforeRun()`: clear `waitTill` when cancelling before execution starts

**How to test:**

Couldn't actually reproduce the issue, but the query changes are actually valid here. Seeking [further STR here](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/29370#issuecomment-4388791895).

Manually seed a zombie row and confirm the old query returns it while the new one doesn't:

```sql
-- Create zombie: status=error with stale waitTill (simulates the bug)
UPDATE execution_entity SET status='error', "waitTill" = NOW() - INTERVAL '1 hour' WHERE id = <id>;

-- Old query (buggy) — returns the zombie:
SELECT id, status, "waitTill" FROM execution_entity
WHERE "waitTill" <= NOW() + INTERVAL '70 seconds'
  AND status != 'crashed';

-- New query (fixed) — returns nothing:
SELECT id, status, "waitTill" FROM execution_entity
WHERE "waitTill" <= NOW() + INTERVAL '70 seconds'
  AND status = 'waiting';
```

With the fix in place and a zombie row seeded, the WaitTracker poll logs stay silent. Without it, you see the repeating `TimeoutNegativeWarning` + "already being resumed" loop every ~60s.

title: ci: Apply SafeChain @n8n/* exclusion to all setup-nodejs steps
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #29881. That PR added `SAFE_CHAIN_MINIMUM_PACKAGE_AGE_EXCLUSIONS: '@n8n/*'` directly on the `Install Dependencies` step's `env:` block, so the exclusion was scoped to that single step. Steps that run later in the same job — most importantly the publish steps in `release-publish.yml` — never saw the variable, and SafeChain 1.5.1 kept hiding recently-published `@n8n/*` versions from them.

That hiding broke `pnpm publish -r`. pnpm decides whether to skip a package by asking the registry which versions exist; with the freshly-published version filtered out, pnpm thought the version was new, called `PUT`, and npm rejected the duplicate upload:

```
npm error code E403
npm error 403 403 Forbidden - PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/@n8n%2fdesign-system
        - You cannot publish over the previously published versions: 2.20.0.
```

This PR moves the exclusion into a `\$GITHUB_ENV` export co-located with the SafeChain install, so it propagates to every subsequent step in the calling job — install, build, and publish — through a single source of truth. Same exclusion scope (`@n8n/*`) as #29881.

## Test plan

The failure repros on the `release/2.20.2` pipeline:
- ✅ Successful run on 2.19.3 (SafeChain 1.4.1, no minimum-age filter): https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/actions/runs/25430054993/job/74593767500
- ❌ Failed run on 2.20.2 (SafeChain 1.5.1): https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/actions/runs/25432157412/job/74601019718

After this change the publish steps inherit the exclusion and pnpm's "skip already-published" check sees the existing version and short-circuits, matching pre-1.5.1 behavior.

title: fix(core): Add ESLint rule to prevent error instances in toThrow assertions
body:
## Summary

Adds a new ESLint rule `n8n-local-rules/no-error-instance-in-to-throw` that prevents passing error instances to `.toThrow()` in test assertions.

**Problem:** Passing `new Error(...)` to `.toThrow()` causes flaky tests because Jest compares error instances by reference, not by message content. This is especially unreliable with custom error classes like `NodeOperationError` that take extra constructor arguments.

**Solution:** The rule flags `.toThrow(new SomeError(...))` and requires splitting into two assertions:
```typescript
// Before (flaky)
await expect(promise).rejects.toThrow(new BadRequestError('Token is required'));

// After (reliable)
const promise = controller.acceptInvitation(req);
await expect(promise).rejects.toThrow(BadRequestError);
```

title: feat(ai): Export AI agent traces via OpenTelemetry
body:
## PR: feat(ai): Export AI agent traces via OpenTelemetry

### Problem

When `N8N_OTEL_ENABLED=true`, only `workflow.execute` and `node.execute` spans are exported. The internal operations of AI agent nodes (LLM calls, tool invocations, chain reasoning steps) are invisible to OTEL — they only go to LangSmith/LangFuse via LangChain callbacks. Self-hosted users who rely on OTEL for observability have no way to trace what's happening inside their AI agents.

### Solution

Adds an `OtelAiCallbackHandler` — a LangChain `BaseCallbackHandler` that creates OTEL child spans for AI operations. When OTEL is enabled and a node is executing (active span exists), the handler is automatically included in the LangChain callback chain alongside any existing callbacks (like LangSmith).

### Span Hierarchy (After)

```
workflow.execute
  └─ node.execute (AI Agent)
       ├─ ai.chain.call (AgentExecutor)
       │    ├─ ai.llm.call (gpt-4)          ← NEW
       │    ├─ ai.tool.call (calculator)     ← NEW
       │    ├─ ai.llm.call (gpt-4)          ← NEW
       │    └─ ai.retriever.call (pinecone)  ← NEW
       └─ ...
```

### Span Types & Attributes

| Span | Key Attributes |
|------|---------------|
| `ai.llm.call` | `gen_ai.system`, `gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.request.temperature`, `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens` |
| `ai.tool.call` | `n8n.ai.tool.name`, `n8n.ai.tool.input.length`, `n8n.ai.tool.output.length` |
| `ai.chain.call` | `n8n.ai.chain.type` |
| `ai.retriever.call` | `n8n.ai.retriever.type`, `n8n.ai.retriever.query.length`, `n8n.ai.retriever.document_count` |

### Configuration

| Env Var | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `N8N_OTEL_TRACES_INCLUDE_AI_SPANS` | `true` | Opt-out flag to disable AI spans while keeping workflow/node spans |

### Design Decisions

- **Zero overhead when OTEL is disabled**: Uses `trace.getActiveSpan()` to detect OTEL presence. When no SDK is registered, the OTEL API returns no-op objects — no handler is created, no performance impact.
- **Proper parent-child nesting**: Uses `parentRunId` from LangChain callbacks to build correct span hierarchy (e.g., tool calls nested under the LLM call that invoked them).
- **Non-breaking**: Existing LangSmith/LangFuse tracing continues to work unchanged. The OTEL handler runs alongside other callbacks.
- **Follows OTEL semantic conventions**: Uses `gen_ai.*` attribute namespace per the [OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/).


### Files Changed

| File | Status | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/utils/otel-ai-callback-handler.ts` | NEW | Core OTEL-LangChain bridge|
| `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/utils/otel-ai-callback-handler.test.ts` | NEW | 18 unit tests for the handler |
| `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/utils/tracing.ts` | MODIFIED | Integrates OTEL handler when active span detected |
| `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/utils/tracing.test.ts` | MODIFIED | 3 new OTEL integration tests |
| `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/package.json` | MODIFIED | Added `@opentelemetry/api` dep + test devDeps |
| `packages/cli/src/modules/otel/otel.config.ts` | MODIFIED | Added `N8N_OTEL_TRACES_INCLUDE_AI_SPANS` config flag |
| `packages/cli/src/modules/otel/otel.module.ts` | MODIFIED | Exposes `includeAiSpans` in module context |
| `packages/workflow/src/interfaces.ts` | MODIFIED | Added `includeAiSpans?: boolean` to otel interface |

- All 26 existing tracing tests pass
- All 65 OTEL module tests pass
- Manually verified with Jaeger: AI spans appear nested correctly under node spans

Extends the previous HTTP Request Node `url` expression handling fix from #21101 to older node versions.

body:
## Summary

Make the URL the single source of truth for the active thread id by splitting the monolithic \`InstanceAiView.vue\` (~960 lines) into a layout shell + two route-children leaf views.

### Layout shell — \`InstanceAiView.vue\` (~150 lines)

- Sidebar (collapse state via \`useSessionStorage\`, resize, transition, in-sidebar collapse via \`InstanceAiThreadList\`'s \`@collapse\`)
- \`<RouterView />\` for the leaves
- Page-level lifecycle: \`loadThreads\`, \`fetchCredits\`, credits push listener, gateway setup
- \`onUnmounted\`: \`closeSSE\`, \`stopCreditsPushListener\`, \`stopGatewayPushListener\` (only fires when leaving the namespace, not on empty↔thread)
- \`onBeforeRouteLeave\`: reset sidebar to collapsed when leaving the chat namespace
- \`provide(SidebarStateKey, { collapsed, toggle })\` so leaves can render the collapsed-mode toggle in their own header

### Empty leaf — \`InstanceAiEmptyView.vue\` (\`/instance-ai\`)

- Header (sidebar toggle when collapsed + credits + settings)
- Empty state UI (suggestions, centered input, status bar, credit warning banner)
- On mount: \`store.clearCurrentThread()\` — fresh placeholder UUID, SSE closed, state reset
- Submit: \`sendMessage\` then \`router.replace({ name: INSTANCE_AI_THREAD_VIEW, params: { threadId } })\` once the thread is persisted. The in-flight stream survives the navigation because the store's single runtime stays mounted across leaf swaps.

### Thread leaf — \`InstanceAiThreadView.vue\` (\`/instance-ai/:threadId\`)

- Full chat UI: header (sidebar toggle, thread title, reconnect indicator, credits/settings/debug/artifacts), message list with scroll management, floating input, preview panel
- Watches \`props.threadId\` with \`immediate: true\`:
  - already on this thread → reconnect SSE if disconnected
  - known thread → \`switchThread\`
  - unknown thread → wait for \`loadThreads\` (idempotent) then validate; redirect to empty if still unknown
- \`onUnmounted\`: cleanup observers, execution tracking (SSE close stays in the layout)

### Shared chrome

Both leaves consume two reusable pieces so the duplicated header / banner code from the initial split is gone:

- \`components/InstanceAiViewHeader.vue\` — sidebar toggle (when collapsed) + credits dropdown + settings button + read-only callout, with \`title\` and \`actions\` slots for leaf-specific bits (Thread fills both; Empty fills neither). Owns the global \`.sidebar-toggle-fade-*\` keyframes — single source of truth.
- \`composables/useCreditWarningBanner.ts\` — owns the \`dismissed\` ref + watch that resets dismissal on transition into low-credits + \`visible\` computed. Takes \`MaybeRefOrGetter<boolean>\` so the composable doesn't depend on the store; leaves call it as \`useCreditWarningBanner(isLowCredits)\` after \`storeToRefs\`.

### Module descriptor

Reorganised into nested routes:
- Parent \`/instance-ai\` → \`InstanceAiView\` (layout)
- Child \`''\` → \`InstanceAiEmptyView\` (named \`INSTANCE_AI_VIEW\`)
- Child \`':threadId'\` → \`InstanceAiThreadView\` (named \`INSTANCE_AI_THREAD_VIEW\`)

### Why

- Eliminates the \`currentThreadId = uuidv4()\` placeholder hack — the URL is the only source of truth for which thread is active.
- Sets up clean per-route lifecycle (each leaf owns its own concerns).
- Prerequisite for future per-thread runtimes (\`Map<threadId, ThreadRuntime>\` + provide/inject), which is where consumer churn happens — that's a follow-up PR, not this one. Components stay on \`store.X\` here.

title: fix(ai-builder): Use expiring Computer Use setup tokens (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the Computer Use setup-command flow around the short-lived pairing token.

Security rationale:
- The setup command contains temporary pairing material that is copied into a local terminal and can outlive the immediate setup moment in local user environments.
- That credential should stay short-lived, single-use, and scoped only to initial pairing.
- The setup-command endpoint should not return an existing long-lived `sess_*` session key, because session keys are the durable credential for an already paired Computer Use daemon.

What changes:
- `POST /instance-ai/gateway/create-link` now returns setup-token expiry metadata: `expiresAt` and `ttlSeconds`.
- The Computer Use setup UI shows when the setup token expires and refreshes the command before copying if the previous token has expired.
- Setup command generation now stays on the `gw_*` pairing-token path and does not return an existing active `sess_*` session key.

What was already true / preserved:
- Setup tokens are short-lived and single-use. Expired setup tokens cannot be consumed for pairing.
- Already paired Computer Use sessions continue using their session key and have no time-based expiry. They remain valid until explicit disconnect/revocation, while the server-side session state exists.
- This PR does not add session rotation, daily re-pairing, or timed session expiry.

User impact:
- Users can see that a setup command is time-limited.
- If they copy after expiry, the UI gets a fresh setup command first.
- A running paired Computer Use daemon/service is not invalidated just because the original setup token expired.

| Area | Previous behavior | New behavior | Example fixed | Why this matters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MCP server names | External/browser MCP configs were passed to the MCP client as configured. | Server names must be safe identifiers before connection setup; unsafe configs are skipped and logged. | A configured server named `bad server` or `constructor` is skipped before client setup. | Treats MCP connection metadata as untrusted input and avoids unsafe keys in internal maps. |
| MCP tool names | External, browser, and local gateway tools were merged with only limited exact-name filtering. | Tool names must be safe identifiers, must not collide after normalization, and must not overlap with domain/orchestration tools. Unsafe or conflicting tools are skipped and logged. | `search_files` and `search-files` are treated as the same claim; `custom_workflows` is rejected because it claims a reserved suffix. | Prevents MCP-provided names from ambiguously overlapping with trusted Instance AI tools. |
| Toolset composition | Local gateway tools were added inside domain tool construction, making ownership/filtering harder to reason about. | MCP tools are collected centrally in `createInstanceAgent`, then added separately to orchestration context and orchestrator toolsets. | Local gateway tools go through the same validation path before being exposed to the orchestrator or sub-agents. | Keeps the trust boundary in one place, so MCP tools cannot bypass shared validation through a different construction path. |
| MCP schemas | Schema sanitization handled provider-incompatible nulls but had no budget around oversized or unsupported shapes. | Input/output schemas are bounded by depth, node, property, and union limits. Unsupported Zod shapes cause only the offending tool to be skipped. | A tool with 251 input properties or a schema deeper than 32 levels is skipped while other tools continue loading. | Bounds work done on MCP-provided schemas and avoids accepting shapes the provider/tooling cannot safely represent. |
| Local gateway schemas | Raw gateway JSON schemas were converted before size checks. | Gateway JSON schemas are checked before tool construction, then sanitized after conversion. | An oversized local gateway schema is rejected before JSON Schema to Zod conversion. | Applies resource limits before expensive conversion work and keeps local gateway behavior aligned with external MCP behavior. |
| Gateway resource decisions | Resource-decision options were treated as arbitrary strings through the suspend payload, frontend, and confirmation DTO. | The daemon wire payload is parsed as strings, then narrowed to `denyOnce`, `allowOnce`, and `allowForSession`; unsupported options are filtered/rejected. | A daemon option like `alwaysAllow` is not rendered in the confirmation UI and is rejected by the confirmation DTO. | Keeps persistent permission semantics owned by settings/product flows instead of accepting arbitrary daemon-provided actions. |

### Supported MCP identifier contract

- Starts with a letter
- Contains only letters, numbers, `_`, or `-`
- Has a maximum length of 64 characters
- Does not use Unicode compatibility-normalized variants
- Does not use unsafe object keys after lowercasing (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype`)
- Does not collide after normalization, e.g. `search-files`, `search_files`, and `SearchFiles` are treated as the same claim
- Does not claim a reserved domain/orchestration tool name, including reserved suffixes such as `custom_workflows`

### Schema bounds

| Bound | Limit |
| --- | ---: |
| Maximum depth | 32 |
| Maximum total nodes | 1,000 |
| Maximum properties on one object | 250 |
| Maximum union options | 100 |

Unsupported schemas are skipped at the tool level and logged with source, tool name, path, and limit details.

### Review notes

- Name validation is shared across external MCP, browser MCP, and local gateway MCP.
- Valid MCP tools continue to be loaded; invalid tools are skipped instead of failing the whole agent setup.
- Resource confirmation remains limited to once/per-session choices. Persistent permission modes stay settings-owned.

title: feat(core): Add JSON Schema for .node.json codex files
body:
## Summary

Adds the canonical zod schema for `.node.json` (codex) files to `n8n-workflow`, generates JSON Schema artifacts at build time, and ships them with the published package. Foundation slice for the codex-schema effort ([CE-1012](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/CE-1012)); on its own it ships a published schema community node authors can consume via jsDelivr for IDE intellisense.

### What this PR ships

- **`packages/workflow/src/codex-file-schema.ts`** — single source-of-truth zod schemas. Two profiles:
  - `nodeCodexFileSchema` — base profile, allows `subcategories`
  - `communityNodeCodexFileSchema` = `nodeCodexFileSchema.omit({ subcategories: true })`
  - `NODE_FIELD_REGEX` enforcing `[@scope/]package-name.nodeType` shape. Cross-package validation (matching the prefix against the consumer's `package.json` name) lives in the eslint plugin (CE-743) and the runtime loader (CE-1014).
  - All fields carry `.describe()` annotations that propagate to per-property `description` in the JSON Schema for IDE hover help.
- **`CodexData`** is now `z.infer<typeof codexBodySchema>` — the hand-written type was removed; existing `import type { CodexData }` paths continue to resolve.
- **`packages/workflow/scripts/generate-codex-schemas.ts`** — `tsx` build script using `zod-to-json-schema`. Self-verifies by comparing regenerated content to the on-disk file; writes the new content + exits non-zero on drift, so `pnpm build` itself fails when committed schemas are stale. No CI step required, no git dependency.
- **`packages/workflow/schemas/{node,community-node}-codex-file.schema.json`** — generated artifacts. `draft-07`, `additionalProperties: false`, `$id` set to the jsDelivr `@latest` URL. Included in the `files` field so they ship with the npm package.
- **`packages/workflow/README.md`** — distribution guidance (`@latest` URL recommended, `@<exact>` for pinning) and semver discipline (breaking schema changes require a major bump of `n8n-workflow`).
- **30 fixture-based unit tests** covering missing-required, unknown top-level fields (`details`/`aliases` typo), malformed `node` regex, malformed URL, base profile accepts `subcategories`, community profile rejects it, unknown `resources` keys, regex shape acceptance and rejection.

### Decisions documented in the slice

- **JSON Schema draft-07**, the most widely-supported draft in VS Code's JSON LSP and what SchemaStore recommends. zod-to-json-schema doesn't support 2020-12 yet; Biome is the only major project on 2020-12 in the comparison set we surveyed.
- **`additionalProperties: false`** pervasively, via zod `.strict()`. Catches typos like `categores`/`details`/`aliases` from day one — these are the actual bugs in the existing built-in `.node.json` files this effort is unblocking.
- **jsDelivr distribution** with `@latest` recommended URL — zero-infra, tracks npm releases. Other projects use their own domain (Biome, Renovate, Turborepo) or SchemaStore (tsconfig, package.json, eslint); jsDelivr is a pragmatic interim, and the `$id` field can be updated in a future major if hosting moves.
- **Inline refs** (no `$defs`) for flatter editor error messages.
- Schema changes are public API and follow semver — breaking schema changes require a major bump of `n8n-workflow`.

### How to test

```bash
pnpm --filter n8n-workflow build       # regenerates + drift-checks + compiles
pnpm --filter n8n-workflow test        # runs all tests including the 30 new ones
pnpm --filter n8n-workflow lint
pnpm --filter n8n-workflow typecheck
cd packages/workflow && npm pack --dry-run  # confirms schemas/*.json ship in the tarball
```

**Drift detection**: edit a field in `packages/workflow/src/codex-file-schema.ts` and run `pnpm --filter n8n-workflow generate-schemas`. The generator updates `schemas/*.json` and exits non-zero. Re-run after committing → exits zero. `pnpm build` behaves the same way.

### Out of scope (covered by sibling slices)

- Eslint rule changes — [CE-743](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/CE-743)
- Runtime validation in `directory-loader.ts`, cleanup of `details`/`aliases` in built-in files, workspace `.vscode/settings.json` — [CE-1014](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/CE-1014)
- `@n8n/node-cli` template `$schema` integration — [CE-1015](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/CE-1015)
- SchemaStore registration — [CE-1016](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/CE-1016)

title: fix(core): Lint package.json in community node tooling (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Both `@n8n/scan-community-package` and `@n8n/node-cli` were silently skipping every `@n8n/eslint-plugin-community-nodes` rule that gates on `context.filename.endsWith('package.json')`:

- `no-overrides-field`
- `valid-peer-dependencies`
- `package-name-convention`
- `require-community-node-keyword`
- `ai-node-package-json`
- `no-runtime-dependencies`
- `no-forbidden-lifecycle-scripts`
- partial: `icon-validation` (its package.json reads)

Two independent root causes for the same symptom:

1. **Scanner** (`@n8n/scan-community-package`): the file glob was `**/*.js` only, so ESLint never received `package.json`. Even if it had, the default `espree` parser can't parse a top-level JSON object literal, and the recommended flat-config didn't register a JSON-capable parser.
2. **node-cli** (`@n8n/node-cli`): the community-nodes recommended config was wired into a `**/*.ts`-scoped `extends:` block. ESLint never matched `package.json` against that block, so all the package.json-targeting rules loaded but never fired.

Net effect for both: scanner reported "passed all security checks" and node-cli's `lint` exited green even when a package contained obvious violations.

### Changes

**`@n8n/scan-community-package`:**
- `scanner.mjs`: glob `['**/*.js', '**/*.json']` (with `package-lock.json` ignored), register `@typescript-eslint/parser` for `**/*.json`, export `analyzePackage` for testing.
- `package.json`: add `@typescript-eslint/parser` dep, vitest setup.
- New `scanner.test.mjs`: 4 regression tests (overrides field caught, lifecycle scripts caught, clean package passes, empty package returns passed).

**`@n8n/node-cli`:**
- `configs/eslint.ts`: extract `communityNodesRecommended` into a local; apply it via `extends:` in the existing `package.json` block in addition to the `**/*.ts` block. The recommended config's rules self-gate on filename, so applying it to both file groups is safe.
- New `configs/eslint.test.ts`: 3 regression tests that load the actual `config` / `configWithoutCloudSupport` exports, run ESLint against fixture `package.json` files, and assert that `no-overrides-field` and `no-forbidden-lifecycle-scripts` actually report.

### Verification

- Scanner: `pnpm test` → 4/4 pass.
- node-cli: `pnpm test` → 114/114 pass (3 new); `pnpm typecheck` clean; `pnpm lint` clean.
- Plugin: `pnpm test` → 403/403 still pass (no plugin changes).
- **Confirmed regression value:** stashing the `eslint.ts` fix causes all 3 new node-cli tests to fail; restoring it makes them pass.

### End-to-end evidence against the package from the ticket

Side-by-side run of the published broken scanner vs. this branch, both pointed at `@crono-one/n8n-nodes-crono-public-api@1.4.1` (the package that surfaced the bug in CE-1022):

```
$ npx @n8n/scan-community-package@0.17.0 @crono-one/n8n-nodes-crono-public-api@1.4.1
✅ Package @crono-one/n8n-nodes-crono-public-api@1.4.1 has passed all security checks
```

```
$ node packages/@n8n/scan-community-package/scanner/cli.mjs \
       @crono-one/n8n-nodes-crono-public-api@1.4.1

❌ Package @crono-one/n8n-nodes-crono-public-api@1.4.1 has failed security checks
Reason: ESLint violations found

Details:

…/@crono-one/n8n-nodes-crono-public-api-1.4.1/dist/package.json
  80:5  error  The "overrides" field is not allowed in community node packages.
              Dependency overrides can introduce incompatible versions of shared
              libraries into the n8n runtime and cause conflicts with other nodes
              @n8n/community-nodes/no-overrides-field

…/@crono-one/n8n-nodes-crono-public-api-1.4.1/package.json
  80:2  error  The "overrides" field is not allowed in community node packages…
              @n8n/community-nodes/no-overrides-field

✖ 2 problems (2 errors, 0 warnings)
```

Bonus: the broader `**/*.json` glob also catches the package's `dist/package.json`, which carries the same `overrides` field shipped twice in the tarball.

### How to test

```bash
# scanner regression test
cd packages/@n8n/scan-community-package && pnpm test

# node-cli regression test
cd packages/@n8n/node-cli && pnpm test eslint.test
```

Or end-to-end against the package mentioned in the ticket:

```bash
# After this fix, the scanner should now flag the overrides field.
node packages/@n8n/scan-community-package/scanner/cli.mjs @crono-one/n8n-nodes-crono-public-api
```

title: fix(core): Preserve AxiosHeaders instance when applying OpenAI vendor defaults
body:
## Summary

`applyVendorHeaders` was rebuilding `config.headers` as a plain object with a spread (`{ ...vendorDefaults, ...callerHeaders }`), which discarded the `AxiosHeaders` instance that axios expects on `InternalAxiosRequestConfig`. This caused downstream failures when the interceptor tried to call `config.headers.setContentType()` on the mutated plain object.

The fix uses `headers.set(defaults, false)` instead, which:

- preserves the `AxiosHeaders` prototype so the interceptor stays re-runnable,
- merges vendor defaults without overwriting caller-provided headers (`false` = do not overwrite).

The function is typed with `InternalAxiosRequestConfig` since `headers` is guaranteed to be an `AxiosHeaders` instance at the interceptor stage.

### How to test

1. Configure an HTTP Request node targeting `https://api.openai.com/...` with caller-provided headers (e.g. `Authorization: Bearer <key>`).
2. Execute the workflow and verify the request succeeds and caller headers are preserved.

body:
## Summary

Adds a new ESLint rule `@n8n/community-nodes/cred-class-oauth2-naming` that enforces consistent `OAuth2` naming on credential classes implementing `ICredentialType`.

A credential is detected as OAuth2 if **any** of the following are true:
- the class name contains `OAuth2`
- the class TypeScript-extends a base whose name contains `OAuth2`
- the `extends` class field references an OAuth2 credential (e.g. `extends = ['oAuth2Api']`)
- the `name` or `displayName` field contains `OAuth2`

When detected, all of the following must contain `OAuth2`:
- class name (must end with `OAuth2Api`) — auto-fixable
- `name` field
- `displayName` field

This consolidates three rules from the legacy `eslint-plugin-n8n-nodes-base` plugin (`cred-class-name-missing-oauth2-suffix`, `cred-class-field-name-missing-oauth2`, `cred-class-field-display-name-missing-oauth2`) into a single conceptual check, and is more lenient on detection (any of class name / extends / hint) to reduce false negatives on subclasses.

### How to test

```bash
cd packages/@n8n/eslint-plugin-community-nodes
pnpm test cred-class-oauth2-naming.test.ts
pnpm typecheck
pnpm build:docs
pnpm lint:docs
```

title: fix(core): Preserve node positions on AI workflow updates
body: ## Summary When AI tools (MCP and the instance-ai deep agent) updated an existing workflow, server-side `layoutWorkflowJSON` re-ran the Dagre layout from scratch over the parsed result. For content-only edits this caused sticky notes to drift over different nodes than the user originally placed them on: This PR removes the temporary `layoutWorkflowJSON` post-processing in favor of the SDK's native `toJSON({ tidyUp: true })`, which already respects explicit `config.position`. Positions roundtrip through SDK code via `parseWorkflowCodeToBuilder` → `builder.toJSON({ tidyUp: true })`, so the layout step becomes a no-op for fully positioned workflows. Also extends `calculateNodePositionsDagre` with two improvements that make mixed positioned/unpositioned workflows lay out cleanly: - Seed Dagre with explicit `x,y` so newly added nodes anchor to existing positioned neighbors. - Reanchor sticky notes using explicit positions (not Dagre's guess) for already-positioned covered nodes. Replaces #28902. Net result: smaller surface — no `preservePositions` flag, no `LayoutableWorkflowJSON`/`LayoutableNodeJSON` types, no server-side post-processing layer. Layout is owned by the SDK. ### How to test 1. Use an MCP client or the instance-ai deep agent to update a workflow that already has manually positioned nodes and a sticky note. 2. Change content only — for example update a sticky note's text or a node parameter — without asking for a relayout. 3. Confirm content changes apply, existing positioned nodes stay put, and sticky notes remain anchored over the same nodes. 4. Confirm that brand-new workflows or newly added nodes still receive automatic Dagre layout. ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts Closes [ADO-5104](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/ADO-5104/bug-sticky-note-position-is-always-changed-when-updated-through-layout) ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] I have seen this code, I have run this code, and I take responsibility for this code. - [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. - [ ] [Docs updated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs) or follow-up ticket created. - [x] Tests included. - [ ] PR Labeled with `Backport to Beta`, `Backport to Stable`, or `Backport to v1` (if the PR is an urgent fix that needs to be backported)

title: fix(Google Cloud Storage Node): Fix large file upload and add Project RLC
body:
## Summary
### Fix: Large binary file upload (resumable upload)

The first Object → Create execution was broken for large files because the binary stream was consumed in full before being uploaded.

This PR fixes it by:
- Implementing **resumable upload** (GCS resumable upload protocol) for streaming binary data
- Chunking the stream into 8 MB pieces using `processStreamInChunks`
- Handling empty files (`contentLength === 0`) as a `Buffer.alloc(0)` to avoid a hanging stream read
- Falling back to standard multipart upload for non-streaming (Buffer) content — behaviour unchanged for small/text content

### Improvement: Project ID RLC (node v1.1)

Replaces the plain-text `projectId` string field on Bucket → Create / Get Many with a **Resource Locator Component**, allowing users to select their GCP project from a searchable list (fetched via Cloud Resource Manager API) or enter the ID manually. Node v1 behaviour is preserved.

**How to test:**
1. Upload a large binary file (>8 MB) via Object → Create — should succeed without errors
2. On a v1.1 node, Bucket → Create: the Project field should show a searchable dropdown of GCP projects
