title: fix(editor): Make sure trimmed placeholder never reaches backend
body:
## Summary

The backend sends a "trimmed" placeholder (`{ [TRIMMED_TASK_DATA_CONNECTIONS_KEY]: true }`) for larger amounts of execution data. The FE shows a loading spinner if it finds that placeholder anywhere in the data. That placeholder is meant to be transient. 
Two flows could persist it as pinned data, which then round-trips through subsequent runs and corrupts the workflow's stored state. Once corrupted, the affected execution data would never load in the frontend, even for unaffected nodes.

This PR closes both leaks:

- **`usePinnedData.setData`**: refuse to pin any input that contains the trimmed marker. Surfaces a toast and emits a `Ndv data pinning failure` telemetry event with `error_type: 'trimmed-data'`.
- **`useExecutionDebugging.applyExecutionData`** (the "Copy to editor" flow): skip nodes whose run data carries the marker so we don't pin a placeholder when restoring a debug execution.
- **`RunData.vue`**: when execution is in a terminal state (`success` / `error` / `canceled` / `crashed`) but the data still contains the placeholder, swap the indefinite spinner for a "Pinned data on this node is corrupted and can't be displayed." message. If the corruption is on the current node's `pinData`, render an **Unpin data** button so the user can recover without DB surgery.

## Summary

Adds the LLM-as-judge grader (`graders/llm.ts`) to the computer-use eval
harness. Trace-level graders verify the agent called the right tools but
can't read English; this grader closes the gap. Auto-appended to every
scenario by the runner.

> **Stacked on #29797.** This PR targets the
> `feat/instance-ai-computer-use-eval` branch, which ships the
> deterministic harness alone. Review #29797 first; once it merges,
> GitHub will auto-retarget this PR to master.

### What this adds

- `evaluations/computer-use/graders/llm.ts` — the grader. Builds a
  prompt from the user's request, the agent's final text, and a
  compact tool-call summary. Asks a small/cheap LLM (Haiku 4.5 by
  default) "did the assistant succeed?". Parses the verdict via the
  shared `parseJudgeVerdict` helper from #29800.
- `LlmTaskCompletedGrader` interface in `types.ts` — supports
  optional `criteria`, `model`, `timeoutMs`.
- Auto-append in `cli.ts withDefaultGraders` so every scenario gets
  it for free; explicit `llm.taskCompleted` entries in scenario JSON
  override (used by M.1, M.3, M.5 to teach the judge adversarial
  scoring rules).
- Dispatch case + `userPrompt`/`scenarioCategory` plumbing in
  `applyGrader` / `runGraders`.
- 11-test suite covering verdict parsing, prompt construction
  (category/criteria/finalText injection, truncation at 8 000 chars,
  tool-call summarisation with footer), agent error and timeout
  handling.
- README docs.

### Why a separate PR

The deterministic harness in #29797 is reviewable on its own — it
runs scenarios end-to-end and scores them mechanically. The LLM judge
is the qualitative layer on top: it adds runtime cost (one Anthropic
call per scenario), introduces a new dependency on an API key during
eval runs, and has its own failure modes (timeouts, unparseable
verdicts) worth reviewing in isolation.

This PR's diff is ~250 counted lines — fits cleanly under the 1 000-line
size limit.

## How to test

After #29797 lands, this branch rebases onto master automatically:

```bash
cd packages/@n8n/instance-ai
pnpm typecheck
pnpm lint
pnpm test
```

End-to-end (smallest scenario, no browser needed):

```bash
pnpm eval:computer-use -- --only 6.1
```

The judge runs against Haiku unless overridden; ensure
`N8N_INSTANCE_AI_MODEL_API_KEY` (or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) is set.

title: feat(ai-builder): Speeds up Instance AI eval by parallelizing iterations and trimming mock handler (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

Two small, independent perf wins for `pnpm eval:instance-ai` (the harness that builds + verifies workflows end-to-end against real providers). 

🥇 **Combined effect: **728s → ~165s wall-clock (−77%) at unchanged quality** (`pass@k=0.60` median, 0 mock-issue, 0 framework-failure).**

### Commit 1:`perf(instance-ai eval): parallelize iteration loop in runDirectLoop`

Iterations passed via `--iterations N` previously ran sequentially: build a workflow (~120s), run scenarios (~80s), repeat. With three iterations against a single test case, that was ~450s of pure sequential build wall-clock no matter how fast the rest of the pipeline ran.

Iterations are independent (separate threadIds, separate workflow IDs); the only shared mutable lane state is `claimedWorkflowIds`, a `Set` whose `add`/`has` are single-threaded-safe between awaits in JS. Replaced the sequential `for` with `Promise.all(Array.from({length: iterations}, ...))`. **728s → ~210s (−71%).**

### Commit 2: `perf(instance-ai eval): simplify mock-handler`

The eval mock-handler exposed two tools (`lookup_api_docs`, `get_node_config`) and the system prompt instructed the agent to call both before generating each mock response — i.e. two extra LLM round-trips per mock call, ~60+ avoidable round-trips per scenario iteration. Both inputs are already known at call time:
- `get_node_config` returned what the user prompt already inlined under `## Node Configuration`.
- `lookup_api_docs` fetched Context7 docs (module-cached after the first call regardless).

Pre-fetched api-docs once and inlined them, dropped both tools, trimmed `MOCK_SYSTEM_PROMPT` 47% (672 → 353 tokens). **~210s → ~165s (−21% additional).**

## How this PR came about — autoresearch experiment

This wasn't hand-tuned. We ran an *autoresearch* loop (Karpathy-style "tweak → benchmark → keep/revert") against the eval harness using pi-autoresearch

- **Setup**: dedicated worktree, driver script that reads a session brief (files in scope, files out of scope, "tried" log), proposes a code change, runs `pnpm eval:instance-ai`, parses the result, ranks against running best.
- **Primary metric**: `total_s` (eval wall-clock), `bestDirection: lower` — declared up front, no human in the loop deciding what "better" meant.
- **Guardrails** (had to all pass for a trial to be promoted to "keep"):
  - Quality didn't regress: `pass@k ≥ 0.60`, `0 mock_issue`, `0 framework_failure`.
  - Pre-commit hook ran `pnpm typecheck` + `pnpm lint` + unit tests on every iteration. Run #5 was rejected as `checks_failed` (lint config broke) even though it was a 214s win — exactly what the hook is for.
- **Budget caps**: `maxIterations: 50`, ~$2–5/turn against a filtered subset (`--filter contact-form --iterations 3`). Total session burn ~$50, ran 39 trials.
- **Methodology shift halfway**: switched from single-run to **median-of-3** per iteration once we noticed a ±30s noise floor driven by Anthropic agent variance. The "best ever" 159s under single-run turned out to be a 2.7σ lucky outlier — honest steady-state was ~169s.

### What we tried and discarded
Per-scenario mock memoization, single-flight on cache, mock-handler→Haiku, verifier timeout shortening, sub-agent grace tuning, lane-setup parallelization, prompt trims on Phase 1 and verifier — all within noise or actively worse.

### Surprising findings
- **The n8n AI proxy is a perf asset, not just an auth gateway.** Bypassing it to direct Anthropic was *+26% slower* — proxy connection pooling beats whatever caching the direct path could unlock.
- **Anthropic ephemeral prompt caching is a no-op through the proxy** (`cache: true` on `createEvalAgent` does nothing until `N8N_AI_ASSISTANT_BASE_URL` is unset). Two independent experiments confirmed.
- **Build dropouts under parallelism are inherent.** 1-of-3 stochastic build failures persist regardless of stagger / concurrency cap / poll interval tweaks.... parallel layout still wins on wall-clock even when 1 iter drops.


## How to test

```bash
cd packages/@n8n/instance-ai
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... pnpm eval:instance-ai --filter contact-form --iterations 3
```

Expected: wall-clock ~160–180s (vs. ~728s on master) with `pass@k=0.60` and `mock_issue=0`. For a stricter signal, run 3× and take the median.

title: fix(editor): Prevent node renaming to restricted JS method names
body:
## Summary

## Problem
Renaming nodes to JavaScript built-in method names like "toString", "hasOwnProperty", "valueOf", etc. breaks workflow functionality. This occurs because these names conflict with Object.prototype methods when nodes are stored and accessed as object properties.

## Solution
Adds validation in `Workflow.renameNode()` to block restricted names:
- Validates against a list of JS object built-in method names
- Allows names containing restricted words as substrings (e.g., "myToString" is permitted)
- Throws `UserError` with message listing all restricted names
- Implements error handling in `useCanvasOperations` to display toast messages when renaming fails

## Alternative Approach Considered
Initially attempted to fix this by replacing all `object.hasOwnProperty(key)` calls with `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(object, key)` throughout the codebase (see commit cc976c2235e0bec1284ce037937250efd928e86f). While this approach would technically allow reserved names to be used, it was deemed too risky due to:
- Extensive changes required across multiple files
- Uncertainty about all the places where node names are used for object property access
- Potential for introducing subtle bugs in edge cases
- Risk of missing some usage patterns

title: fix(core): Prevent queue starvation from subworkflow executions
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #16094

Since workers enqueue subworkflow executions like any other job, we risk a scenario where a high volume of incoming jobs that require subworkflow calls can lead to queue starvation, i.e. workers enqueuing child executions but never getting to them, bringing processing to a halt. This change protects against this by prioritizing subworkflow executions over webhook and regular executions.

For cases where users want to freely write plain text without worrying about special characters, "HTML" is not an ideal workaround as it contains its own set of special characters to take note of and escape.

Reference:
https://t.me/grammyjs/288130
https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#html-style

## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts

Potentially related issues include: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/13376

Where recommendations of "HTML" parse_mode may work on a case-by-case basis, it does not always work as HTML also has its own set of characters it must escape.

title: fix: Run evaluations as full manual executions in queue mode
body:
## Summary

When running evaluation in queue mode (1 worker) and single main, will run into this error.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/719f7a78-42f3-422a-bfaf-f8da28763d98)
Because it's running a partial execution, instead of full manual execution.

Why? Here in `runManually`, because `data.runData` is `undefined`, the execution is running as a  partial execution.
https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/aa407350bbf14e0b6a76ad386ab6f211a9e4a77b/packages/cli/src/manual-execution.service.ts#L115

This fix ensures that evaluations always run as full executions even in queue mode.
Also passing pin data, which is needed here in order to ensure the dataset data is passed correctly in queue mode.

title: feat: Add Outgrow trigger node
body:
Description
The Outgrow Trigger node enables n8n workflows to automatically receive data whenever an Outgrow calculator is submitted. This creates powerful automation possibilities for lead capture, form submissions, and interactive content engagements.

Value Proposition
Real-time lead capture: Immediately process calculator/form submissions

Seamless integrations: Connect Outgrow data to 200+ n8n apps

No-code automation: Marketing/sales teams can build workflows without developers

Features
🕒 Configurable polling: Checks for new submissions at custom intervals (default: 5 mins)

🔍 Calculator selection: Dynamically loads available calculators from connected account

📊 Rich data output: Returns complete submission details of calculator.

✅ Duplicate prevention: Smart tracking of processed submissions

Authentication
🔑 API Key Authentication:

Requires Outgrow API key from [Account Settings](https://app.outgrow.co/settings/api)

Supports multiple account connections

Operations
poll: On New Submission
Triggers when new calculator submission is detected

manual: Fetch Submissions
Immediately retrieves recent submissions (for testing/workflow debugging)

Test Cases
Scenario 1: New Lead Capture

Configure node with valid API credentials

Select calculator from dropdown

Set polling interval to 15 minutes

Submit test form on Outgrow calculator

Expected result:

Workflow triggers within 15 minutes

Output contains all form fields

Execution data shows in n8n UI

Scenario 2: Invalid API Key
Enter incorrect API key in credentials

Execute node manually

Expected result:

Node returns clear authentication error

Error appears in execution log

Workflow shows failed status

title: feat(Keboola): Add support for table uploads via Storage API
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces a new **Keboola node** to the `n8n workflow editor`. It allows users to upload data to Keboola Storage API via a CSV upload, followed by table import or creation logic.

This includes:

- Support for upload operation on table resource.
- Smart creation of buckets and tables if they do not exist.
- Handling both full and incremental import modes.
- Parameter support for bucket name, table name, primary keys, and import mode.
- Clean and type-safe implementation using Zod validation.
- Integration of a custom credentials screen for `keboolaApiToken`.

### How to test

- Install the Keboola node in a `local n8n` instance.
- In a workflow:
    - Set the operation to Upload.
    - Provide: bucket stage (in/out), bucket name, table name, optional primary keys, and import mode.
    - Provide valid credentials using Keboola API Token (see note below).
    - Execute the workflow with input items. 

### Credentials

This node uses a new credential type: `Keboola API Token`, including:

- `stack` (region-specific base URL)
- `apiToken` (Storage API token)

> Note: Credentials are tested automatically during setup.

### Additional Information

- Node versioning and V1/ structure follows the style of the HubSpot node.
- All parameters are grouped under a clear UI schema.
- Includes workflow-based tests and unit test coverage for utility functions and validation.

### Documentation

Related documentation PR: [n8n-io/n8n-docs#3288](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs/pull/3288)
The documentation is being added to the external [n8n.io/docs](https://docs.n8n.io/) site.

→ Placeholder links for the docs have already been included in Keboola.node.json.

> 📌 Until the documentation is officially published:
> You can create a free test project using the [Keboola Project Wizard](https://connection.us-east4.gcp.keboola.com/wizard).
> Or reach out to radek.tomasek@keboola.com for help with test credentials or setting up a sandbox project for QA and review.

title: fix(core): Don't swallow connection errors when fetching credentials
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

We have had multiple reports of executions failing, because the credential could not be found:
`Credential with ID "305" does not exist for type "googleBigQueryOAuth2Api".`
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/59a48864-5ca2-4f8b-8400-88a645b8cc5c)


Sometimes these have been false positives, because the error thrown by TypeORM was actually a connection error that we just ignore.
This PR first checks if the error thrown is an `EntityNotFoundError` before replacing it with a `CredentialNotFoundError`. 
If it's any other error it will be re-thrown so that user reports contain the correct error when they report this. (most of the time it's [this](https://github.com/brianc/node-postgres/blob/03642abec1c09337fa9cfb4b7ce5543b086c6437/packages/pg-pool/index.js#L262), but we can't be sure because we're hiding it).

When returning the dataset from the Evaluation Trigger Node, a limit of `maxRows` is applied defaulting to 1000 rows.
In addition, filters can be applied to the dataset. 
The current implementation uses `row?.json?.row_number` to apply the limit which leads to rows being lost if there is a filter that would include rows after `maxRows`. 
We fix this by simplifying and instead of filtering based on `row_number` simply slicing the filtered result.

title: Draft: feat(Todoist): implement pagination for task listing
body:
## Summary

This PR implements pagination for the Todoist task listing integration.

Previously, all tasks were fetched in a single request, which could cause issues with performance and reliability for users with a large number of tasks. This update introduces support for paginated requests to handle task retrieval more efficiently.

**Key changes:**
- Added support for `page` and `page_size` parameters in task listing API calls.
- Replaced the single API request with looped paginated requests.
- Implemented proper termination conditions to avoid over-fetching or infinite loops.
- Optimized memory usage by processing tasks in chunks instead of loading all at once.
- Fixed a potential infinite loop when `returnAll` was true and the API response didn’t change.

To test:
- Use the Todoist node with a large number of tasks and observe performance improvements.
- Confirm that pagination works with both `returnAll` and `limit` options.
- Ensure that task data is correctly retrieved without duplication or missing entries.

## Summary

This PR introduces streaming support for the OpenAI Chat Completion endpoint, allowing the node to return response chunks in real time as they are generated by the API.

This enhancement significantly improves the user experience for interactive workflows by providing immediate feedback.

Key changes include:

  - Making the core OpenAI node visible in the UI (`hidden: false`).
  - Adding a new boolean parameter, **`Enable Streaming`**, to the Chat Completion operation.

4.  Execute the node. You should see the output items being generated one by one as the response streams in.

title: fix(core): Prevent worker from recovering finished executions
body:
## Summary

Crash recovery has [plenty of known issues](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/CAT-581/bug-crash-handling-functionality-is-broken-main-mode#comment-d542017d) but I found a fundamental one.

Consider this scenario:

- Main enqueues a job for execution 1 whose workflow has an error-handling workflow
- Worker A picks up job, runs execution 1, which throws, finishing with `error` status
- Worker A enqueues job for execution 2, for the error-handling workflow
- Worker B picks up job, runs execution 2 successfully

In this scenario, we end up with inconsistent event logs:

```
n8nEventLog.log (main)
- n8n.workflow.started for execution 1
- n8n.workflow.failed for execution 1

n8nEventLog-worker.log (worker A)
- n8n.node.{started|finished} events for execution 1

n8nEventLog-worker.log (worker B)
- n8n.workflow.started for execution 2
- n8n.node.{started|finished} events for execution 2
- n8n.workflow.success for execution 2
```

This is because of our lifecycle hooks setup:

- Main uses `getLifecycleHooksForScalingMain` which includes `hookFunctionsWorkflowEvents`
- Worker uses `getLifecycleHooksForScalingWorker` which excludes `hookFunctionsWorkflowEvents`
- Subexecutions use `getLifecycleHooksForSubExecutions` which includes `hookFunctionsWorkflowEvents`

This event log inconsistency impacts crash recovery, which assumes all events for an execution are in the event log for a given instance. This means crash recovery [wrongly identifies execution 1 as unfinished](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/c229e915eafda0e09c881c46ab921dca46715ef1/packages/cli/src/eventbus/message-event-bus-writer/message-event-bus-log-writer.ts#L220-L240) (instead of finished with an error) leading it to wrongly amend details for a finished execution (instead of skipping it), which will also lead to another crash recovery on the next restart, as the details are incomplete. 

In short, this means every worker tries to recover its own finished failed executions (instead of only unfinished crashed ones), which the worker does not even have the data for, and so this cycle repeats on restart. The root solution would be to straighten out our hooks setup and have event logs for workers remain with workers, but lifecycle hooks are so central and so legacy that this would be a big dedicated effort.

Hence for now, this fix filters out finished executions downstream and defers crash recovery logging until after we know which were the actually recovered execution IDs.

title: fix(editor): Maintain back button when installing community nodes
body:
## Summary

Maintain back button when installing community nodes. The problem was that verified official community nodes are now part of the `visibleNodeTypes` (see https://linear.app/n8n/issue/NODE-3009/distinguish-official-verified-nodes-from-community-built-ones) and we weren't updating `mergedNodes`, which is derived from `visibleNodeTypes`. 

Updating `mergedNodes` has to be done manually since the root view stack only passes the `mergedNodes` as a value (ie: It is not a `ref` or `computed`). Without doing a manual update, the problem would only be solved for unofficial verified nodes. Hence, we need to manually update the stack to solve the problem for both unofficial verified community nodes and official verified community nodes.

We do not need to worry about unverified nodes because they are not in Strapi, and they do not get displayed in the Node Creator panel.

title: fix: Postgres node with ssh tunnel getting into a broken state and not being recreated
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

Review commit by commit.

- **extract pool clean up logic into private function**
- **remove code that never worked correctly**
- **clean up using an abort controller**
- **bump lastUsed time of ssh clients when the pool lastUsed time is bumped**

**What we're doing:**

1. creating an ssh client, connecting to the server
2. creating a local TCP server as a proxy
3. setting up the proxy to create a port-forwarding from the local port to the remote pg instance through the ssh client
4. creating a pg pool connecting to the local proxy

All packets send to the local proxy are send through the ssh client to the remote pg instance.

We have 3 different connections/servers that need to be maintained:
1. ssh client
2. TCP server
3. pg pool

The TCP server uses a randomly assigned port (we're asking the OS to just give us a port that is free).

**What can go wrong:**

1. If the pg pool looses connection, it will try to create a new one. ✅
2. If the ssh client looses the connection we close the TCP server and never retry to recreate the whole setup. ❌
3. If the TCP server looses the connection we don't do anything (but since that one is fully local, there is a low chance of anything going wrong here)

Additionally we never update the TTL of the ssh client, which means it will always be closed after 5 minutes (the default at least), so we're always creating problem 2 if the pool is used continuously.

I'm assuming this is what happens.

Additional problems are that we don't log anything about the life cycle of theses connections. So we don't know which one of them was closed in which order and why.

**What this PR does:**

Fix the immediate issue of the TTL of the ssh client not being bumped, by adding a `wasUsed` callback that `configurePostgres` can use to update the ssh client's last use. For this I added `SSHClientsManager.updateLastUsed`.

Refactor this to use an AbortController that connects everything and allows everything being cleaned up if one part fails.

Add logs for errors and clean up logic. For that I had to add a logger to the `ConnectionPoolManager` and the `SSHClientsManager`.

## Summary
This PR adds support for rerankers in the retrieve operation of vector stores that's used by QA chain nodes. 

Changes in retrieve operation:
- Get and return reranker and VectorStore if reranker is connected

- Handle response from the vector store operation (with and without reranker)
- With reranker build a ContextualCompressionRetriever which combines the base retriever (vector store) and a compressor (here the reranker) and calls them internally in the correct way
- Without a passed reranker it will behave as before

Describe what the PR does and how to test.

Open the executions filter to the right of the button so that it doesn't hide the executions list while open.

Third suggestion on that ticket is starting to list available Execution Data keys on the picker. Some nodes, like `AI Agent`, `Structured Output Parser` and `Default Data Loader`  have parameters that change the inputs of the node when adjusted. title: feat(core): Link error workflow's Error Trigger nodes to the parent execution that errored
body:
## Summary

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc38bc37-fd16-4ea3-bf44-10ba5fe57ed6)

Show a link to the parent execution that caused the error workflow to trigger on `Error Trigger` nodes, like we show on sub workflows `When Executed by Another Workflow` nodes. The link will show up as `View parent execution <id>`.

This is accomplished by providing similar metadata as we do on sub workflow executions when error workflows are executed. While I feel this is the correct and consistent way to implement this (rather than inspecting the input data of Error Trigger nodes at frontend) this also means that this metadata will only be present on new errors that happen after this change has been deployed. On older errors the link simply won't show up.

Also added a test for `executeErrorWorkflow()` while touching it as it had none.

Originally, our ORM logic was under `strict: false` from the `tsconfig.json` in `cli` but now all ORM logic is in `@n8n/db`  with `strict: true`. This strictness change is likely surfacing type issues that have long existed in `cli`.

title: chore(core): Enable local sandbox provider in Instance AI evals (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

- Allow `LocalSandbox` under `NODE_ENV=production` when `E2E_TESTS=true` so the eval Docker image can run the builder in sandbox mode without provisioning Daytona credentials.
- Wire the eval CI container with `N8N_INSTANCE_AI_SANDBOX_ENABLED=true` and `N8N_INSTANCE_AI_SANDBOX_PROVIDER=local`.
- Add a unit test covering the relaxed gate.

- [x] I have seen this code, I have run this code, and I take responsibility for this code.

## Why

Today the e2e/mock-layer evals run the builder in the deprecated string-based tool path because no sandbox provider is wired up in CI. Daytona would match prod fidelity but adds external-service dependency, billing, and a flaky cold-start. Local provider gives us most of the production behaviour (real `tsc`, real `tsx`, real filesystem) without the vendor cost — good enough for an eval signal.

## Local validation

Single-scenario smoke (`contact-form`, dev server):

| Metric | Tool mode | Sandbox=local |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build time | 129.6s | 148.2s (+19s) |
| Pass rate | 3/5 | 3/5 |
| Disk / builder | — | ~14MB |

Failures in both runs were identical pre-existing `builder_issue`s (Telegram crash + Gmail invalid email), not sandbox-induced.

## Caveats

- **Persisted admin settings can override env vars.** `instance-ai-settings.service.ts` loads `sandboxEnabled` from DB if present, beating env. Fresh CI containers start with no DB state, so this should be fine — but worth keeping an eye on the first CI run.
- **Per-build disk overhead.** Each builder snapshots up to 100 prior workflows into its workspace dir (~14MB). For a full suite, expect ~1GB disk pressure within the eval container. CI runner has 14GB; fits, but a future tuning candidate (lower the `limit: 100` in `sandbox-setup.ts` for eval mode).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI eval workflow passes
- [ ] Verify CI builder logs show local-sandbox activity (`workspace-builders/` dir, npm install, tsc)
- [ ] Pass rate roughly matches the prior tool-mode baseline

title: fix(Basic LLM Chain Node): Parse plain object output from structured output parser
body:
## Summary

The Basic LLM Chain node (v1.9+) fails with `Failed to parse agent steps` when wired up to a Structured Output Parser. The chain pipes the model output through `getAgentStepsParser()`, which only handles `string`, `BaseMessage`, `AgentAction[]`, and `AgentFinish` shapes. Models that produce structured JSON directly as a plain object (e.g. through tool-bound structured output) fall through to the final `throw`.

This PR adds a fallback branch in `getAgentStepsParser()` that stringifies a plain non-array object and feeds it to the supplied `outputParser`, letting the parser validate against its schema. Existing branches are unchanged, so the regression case for `AgentAction[]` without `format_final_json_response` still throws.

### Root cause

In [`promptUtils.ts`](packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/chains/ChainLLM/methods/promptUtils.ts) the type guards run in this order: `string` → `Array` → `BaseMessage` (`instanceof`) → `AgentFinish` (has `returnValues`). A plain object like `{"output":{"isValid":false,"message":"..."}}` matches none of these and reaches `throw new Error('Failed to parse agent steps')`. The wrapper was added in #22936 to support OpenAI Responses API + tools; this PR extends it to also handle plain structured output without removing that support.

### Changes

- `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/chains/ChainLLM/methods/promptUtils.ts` — add a final fallback branch that runs `outputParser.parse(JSON.stringify(steps))` for plain non-array objects.
- `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/chains/ChainLLM/test/promptUtils.test.ts` — two regression tests covering the bug scenario (`{output: {...}}`) and an arbitrary plain object shape.

### How to test

1. Create a workflow with a Basic LLM Chain node (version 1.9 or later).
2. Connect a Structured Output Parser configured with a JSON schema.
3. Execute the workflow.
4. Expected: the parsed object is returned. Previously: `Failed to parse agent steps`.

`pnpm --filter @n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain test ChainLLM` — 85/85 passing (83 existing + 2 new).

title: fix(core): Allow sending timezones from .npm folder
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

When running `npx n8n`, npm download and store the n8n package under .npm/_npx folder.
By default, express does not allow sending file from a path that contains a `.`
Thus, the /rest/options/timezones endpoint returns 404, even though the timezones file exists. This makes the timezone list in the workflow settings empty.
This PR fixes it by allowing this specific sendFile to respond with files inside a `.` folder

title: fix(core): Normalize trailing slash when setting CORS headers for test webhooks
body:
`WebhookRequestHandler.setupCorsHeaders` calls `TestWebhooks.getWebhookMethods` to set the `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` header, but `getWebhookMethods` is trailing slash sensitive, which leads a request like this to incorrectly fail to find the webhook:

```
curl -X POST 'https://domain.com/webhook-test/register/' \
-H 'Origin: https://domain.com' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
-H 'Accept: */*' \
--data-urlencode 'key=value'
```

This is not an issue for production webhooks because `ActiveWorkflowManager.addWebhooks` normalizes the path before persisting the webhook.

Fixes #13591

title: Feat/extend wordpress node
body:
## Summary

This PR enhances the existing WordPress node in n8n by adding three main feature sets and their corresponding tests:

1. **Excerpt support**  
   - **What it does**: Adds a new “Excerpt” field to both the “Create” and “Update” actions for WordPress posts/pages.  
   - **How to test**:  
     1. In an n8n workflow, configure a WordPress “Create Post” (or “Create Page”) node. You should now see an “Excerpt” input.  
     2. Provide sample text in “Excerpt” and run the workflow. In WordPress, verify that the newly created post/page has the correct excerpt displayed in the editor and on the front end (if your theme shows excerpts).  
     3. For the “Update” action, pick an existing post/page, change its “Excerpt” value, execute the node, then confirm in WordPress that the excerpt was updated correctly.

2. **Featured Media dropdown**  
   - **What it does**: Introduces a “Featured Media” dropdown in both “Create” and “Update” for posts and pages. This dropdown is populated dynamically with all images currently available in the connected WordPress instance.  
   - **How to test**:  
     1. Ensure your WordPress site has at least one image uploaded to the Media Library.  
     2. In n8n, configure a WordPress “Create Post” node. The “Featured Media” field should now present a dropdown list of image titles (or IDs).  
     3. Select one image from that list and run the workflow. In WordPress, verify that the post/page’s featured image is set correctly.  
     4. Repeat for the “Update” action: pick an existing post/page, change its featured media via the dropdown, rerun, and confirm the change in WordPress.

3. **Future status datepicker**  
   - **What it does**: Previously, selecting “future” as the post/page status required manually typing a date string. Now, selecting status = “future” automatically shows a datepicker control where the user can pick the exact date/time for scheduled publishing.  
   - **How to test**:  
     1. In both “Create Post” and “Create Page” nodes, set “Status” to “future.” A datepicker should appear below.  
     2. Pick a future date (e.g. tomorrow at “2025-06-02 10:30”). Run the node and verify in WordPress that the post/page is scheduled for that date/time.  
     3. For “Update,” load an existing draft or published page, set status to “future,” choose a datepicker value, rerun, and confirm WordPress shows it as scheduled for the selected timestamp.

4. **Automated tests**  
   - Unit tests have been added for:  
     - Excerpt field behavior (both create & update)  
     - Featured Media dropdown population and selection  
     - Future-status datepicker behavior  
   - These tests mock WordPress API responses so that CI can validate each of these new input fields and their HTTP payloads.

## Summary
This PR adds a new "Ignore Mode" option to the Local File Trigger node, allowing users to choose between:

title: refactor(core): Decouple database entity registration
body:
## Summary

As part of the extensions project, this PR allows modules to contribute their own database entities:

- merge module pre-init into the module entrypoint e.g. `InsightsModule`
- add database entity registration `entities()` to the module entrypoint

Preinit was merged into the module entrypoint because the entrypoint is now slim enough that we can load it cheaply enough (even with entities), simplifying the module setup. Preinit might have been premature optimization, but open to discussion.

This is a follow-up to #15409. For now, module loading lives at `BaseCommand` but soon we'll set up a dedicated module loader service similar to #14722.

title: test(core): Relax assertions for testing the maxTeamProjects quota
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

This test failed for MySQL.
This is because we don't retry when we get a deadlock error.
I don't think we need to retry automatically. 
If a user creates a project at the exact same time another user does it, they will get an error and can retry from the FE. 
This is only here to prevent malicious attacks where someone sends hundreds of requests in the same instant. I doubt a real user would ever hit this.

So to fix this I relaxed the assertion. It only checks that we didn't create too many projects, but does not care anymore about the exact number.

title: fix(core): Solve memory leak in `TaskRequester`
body:
## Summary

Taking a [heap snapshot](https://share.cleanshot.com/k505FnHx) after running a workflow like [this](https://n8n.to/task-runner-memory-leak) shows a substantial retained memory for the map at `LocalTaskRequester.pendingRequests`. This map never clears the stored `TaskRequest` where `TaskRequest.data` is a sizeable object. Removing this map shows heap size returns [back to normal](https://share.cleanshot.com/qVprLw15) after every execution.

This `pendingRequests` map was introduced in the initial task runners PR [here](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/10698/files#diff-84baff9ad3450c5b5aaf27cd4cbb3ce2fdba762f927ca80706b684ae45616639R121) but it has been unused since then, i.e. it is being populated but never read. I assume this map was intended as a temporary store for the full request details in this interim phase before the request is given a `taskId`, potentially for error handling, but this was never implemented. The two people involved in that PR back then are not available to confirm.

title: feat(core): Add config to override default database ping interval and default idle connection timeout
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

When using postgres or mysql/mariadb as database, typeorm uses a connection pool. When the dabatase password for the current user changes (password rotation for instance), the db-connection ping function that checks the liveness of the db will most likely re-use an existing connection from the pool, that is kept and not refresh when user db password changes. Thus the ping will succeeded, and n8n will still be up even though new connection from the pool will fail.

To fix that, I suggest to offer the possibility to change the database ping interval as well as the idle connection timeout for a connection in the pool.

That way, a user could setup the idle connection timeout to be less than the ping connection timeout, so that a new connection is created for each ping, thus re-validating the credentials.

We should see later if we want this behavior (each ping connection to be new) to be by default.

title: feat(core): Add recover mechanism for pg when pool is unexpectedly full on connection not closed
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->
When an underlying tcp error occur on the postgres connection, we can enter a state where the pg-pool (node-postgres driver used by typeorm) do not close the pool connections, but those connections enter a closed state.
The node-postgres community seem to have encountered this issue as well in a hard to reproduce manner. Eg: https://github.com/brianc/node-postgres/issues/2262#issuecomment-2838302908

This impact the connection status, because all pool connections are used, even though not available because closed.
This PR suggest adding a recover mechanism for those connections to try and clean the ended ones on failure.

title: feat: add Netgsm SMS Integration
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a new integration node for Netgsm, a leading telecommunications provider in Turkiye. Netgsm is the country’s first and only Mobile Virtual Network Operator (MVNO) and fixedline/landline operator, offering scalable and reliable messaging solutions via REST APIs.

This node allows users to send SMS messages using the following endpoint:
`https://api.netgsm.com.tr/sms/rest/v2/send`

Users can configure authentication credentials (usercode, password) and customize message details such as:

- Recipient number(s)
- Message text
- Message header (alphanumeric or numeric sender ID)

The node returns the raw JSON response from the Netgsm API. A successful response looks like:
```
{
  "code": "00",    //code = "00" indicates success. A non-00 code (e.g., 30, 40) indicates failure, and the API returns HTTP 406 in such cases.
  "jobid": "17377215342605050417149344",
  "description": "queued"
}
```

How to Test

1. Add the Netgsm node to your workflow.
2. Provide valid Netgsm credentials.
3. Set a Turkish mobile number as the recipient.
4. Enter your message text.
5. Execute the node and confirm that the message is successfully sent (you can check the response or your device).
6. You can obtain test credentials by registering at [Netgsm](https://www.netgsm.com.tr/).

title: feat(core): Add endpoint for querying credentials used in workflows
body: ## Summary We are missing an endpoint that can be used to query which credentials are used by workflows within a folder and its subfolders. Doing this without a dedicated endpoint on the UI is inefficient as we would have to first resolve the folder tree and then fetch every workflow one by one, and this could be _many_ requests. Instead lets add an endpoint on the backend that does this there, returning a list of unique credentials used in workflows. This is the same data that has been previously exposed as `usedCredentials` data on single workflow requests, and what the workflow sharing modal uses already to be able to display which credentials should be also shared when transferring ownership of a workflow. Now, with this endpoint doing the same when moving a folder becomes possible, listing all credentials used by workflows within that folder. ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts https://linear.app/n8n/issue/ADO-3161/fe-combine-change-owner-and-move-to-folder-modals ## Review / Merge checklist - [ ] PR title and summary are descriptive. title: fix(core): Use fresh connection when pinging db to prevent stale connection in pool
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->
When using postgres or mysql/mariadb as database, typeorm uses a connection pool. When the dabatase password for the current user changes (password rotation for instance), the db-connection ping function that checks the liveness of the db will most likely re-use an existing connection from the pool, that is kept and not refresh when user db password changes. Thus the ping will succeeded, and n8n will still be up even though new connection from the pool will fail.

To fix that, I suggest to use a fresh connection instead of an existing one, by creating a new datasource with minimal overhead options.

I also suggest to increase the ping schedule time to 10s to compensate for the added overhead of creating a new datasource

title: fix(core): Fix timezone-dependent test failures in Insights weekly compaction
body:
## Summary

Fixed timezone-dependent test failures in the insights compaction service that were causing `compactDayToWeek` tests to fail when run in non-UTC timezones.

**Root Cause:** Tests were using `getDay()` (local timezone) instead of `getUTCDay()` (UTC timezone) to verify that weekly insights start on Monday. Since insights data is stored in UTC format, this caused failures in non-UTC environments where UTC midnight dates could shift to the previous day in local time.

**Changes:**
- Changed test assertions from `getDay()` to `getUTCDay()` for proper UTC date handling
- Simplified SQLite week calculation expression for better clarity

**Testing:** All 16 insights compaction tests now pass consistently across timezones. Previously, tests would fail for developers in timezones like PST/PDT but pass in CI (UTC environment).

title: feat: Implement multipart upload for generic S3 node
body:
Refactors the generic S3 node to support uploading files larger than 2GB by implementing multipart S3 uploads.

Key changes include:
- Added helper functions to `packages/nodes-base/nodes/S3/GenericFunctions.ts` for:
    - `s3CreateMultipartUpload`: Initiates a multipart upload.
    - `s3UploadPart`: Uploads individual file parts.
    - `s3CompleteMultipartUpload`: Completes the multipart upload.
    - `s3AbortMultipartUpload`: Aborts a multipart upload in case of errors.
- Modified `packages/nodes-base/nodes/S3/S3.node.ts`:
    - The `upload` operation now uses the new multipart functions when handling streamable binary data (`binaryData.id` is present).
    - It reads the file in chunks (`UPLOAD_CHUNK_SIZE` of 5MB) and uploads them sequentially.
    - Includes error handling to abort the multipart upload if any step fails.
    - The existing logic for non-streamable binary files and text-based uploads is preserved.
- Added new tests:
    - A workflow test (`S3.multipartUpload.test.json`) for large file uploads.
    - Unit tests in `GenericFunctions.test.ts` for the new multipart helper functions.

This change allows the generic S3 node to handle large file uploads efficiently without requiring the entire file to be loaded into memory, addressing the previous >2GB limitation.

  was not returning executions with "waiting" status.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/236c085a-cd2f-44e8-9910-9ed1d7e57b27)

## Root Cause

  The public API handler was excluding ALL active executions
  (including waiting ones) from results by calling
  `getActiveExecutions()` and excluding those IDs. This was
  intended to hide truly running executions, but waiting
  executions should be visible as they are paused and waiting for
  external input.

## Changes

  1. **Primary Fix**: Modified public API handler to filter out
  only non-waiting active executions
  2. **Consistency Fix**: Updated internal execution service to
  include waiting executions as "current" status
  3. **Test Coverage**: Added integration test to verify waiting
  executions are properly handled

## Testing

  - [x] Added integration test `should treat waiting executions as
   current, not completed`
  - [x] Verified fix works in Docker environment
  - [x] All existing tests pass

title: fix(core): Fix license reloading flow in scaling mode
body:
## Summary

Ever since the license coexists with pubsub, long before multi-main, we have been relying on the SDK's `onFeatureChange` to instruct workers to reload the license. See #7252 from 2023.

But `onFeatureChange` was only ever meant to report diffs in entitlement featuresets, e.g. a license having two different consecutive entitlements (t1 to t2, and t2 to t3) where the transition happens in-between renewals.  `onFeatureChange` relies on [multiple timer offsets](https://github.com/n8n-io/license-management/blob/2a6897fb637270253c138930a96e6c6bc717bd78/packages/sdk/src/LicenseManager.ts#L904-L915) that partly overlap with the license lifecycle, but do not overlap with renewal events. The SDK already has a separate renewal system (on init, on request, on cron) for handling license validity, but until last week the SDK had no callback for renewals. 

We're seeing reports of the license intermittently expiring prematurely on workers and followers, so this PR ensures the consumer sends the reload-license command on _both_ featureset diffs and license renewals. This was never caught before perhaps because workers typically restart more frequently than the most common license renewal period.

In future, we should re-evaluate if `onFeatureChange` adds value or can be removed to simplify things on both the SDK and the consumer side. I have no visibility into how often this entitlement transition scenario actually happens, or if `onFeatureChange` was only intended as future-proofing and is unused in practice.

Follow-up to  #15629

title: fix(editor): Display form errors when there are multiple form pages
body:
## Summary

If a form has multiple pages and an error happens between the pages and the end of the form the form wouldn't show any errors, and the user submitting the form wouldn't know that something went wrong.

This could happen with a simple setup like this

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/56b67bc7-1852-449b-854a-88f9ee3d49fd)

[form-error.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20410859/form-error.json)

where the form fails between the second page and form end (or between first and second pages with no form end, same thing happens).

There was another problem with queue mode and forms that had been previously circumvented by making the UI poll for the form state,  but there were some problems in that implementation.

This PR fixes this by checking at `autoDetectResponseMode` if the current node is a form node, not just form trigger node and seeing if its connected to other following form (end) nodes, and staying in `formPage` mode if so.

Second part of the fix is not prematurely running the `checkExecutionStatus` checks, which lead to problems if form submission lasted for more than 1000ms. Moving that to only happen once the form has been submitted fixes that, and while at that fix the clearing of the interval (using wrong variable).

This fix requires PR https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/15643 to work in queue mode, which fixes form submission never responding in that mode.

title: fix(core): Resolves response promise for active execution on job finished in queue mode
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

On form submission in scaling mode, when the form trigger is followed by a form page, the second form submit "responsePromise" is never resolved, and the form post thus never resolves.
There is currently a workaround setup in the UI for this that fetches the execution data to know whether the job is finished or not, and update the form UI accordingly. But this comes with issues of its own, like this one: https://linear.app/n8n/issue/NODE-2557/form-node-form-shows-success-when-there-was-an-error

What we want to do is resolve the responsePromise when a form is submitted in queue mode, so that form submission properly finishes, and we can adapt the UI workaround to prevent race conditions: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/packages/cli/templates/form-trigger.handlebars#L861

I need insights to know if resolving the response promise from the job-finished msg is safe enough though.
Also, we noticed that for webhooks (in queue mode), both messages are listened to ('responde-to-webhook' and 'job-finished'), meaning that the promise will be resolved twice. This seems fine but still..

title: refactor(core): Remove last license runtime check
body:
## Summary

As discussed before, `onFeatureChange` is [unnecessary complexity](https://n8nio.slack.com/archives/C035KBDA917/p1740566157792319?thread_ts=1740565893.290659&cid=C035KBDA917) where we pay the price of state management only to have a way to prevent users whose license expires at runtime from benefiting from multi-main until their next restart. This complexity is not worth it and removal here follows the same reasoning as for [removing the S3 license runtime check](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/13532/files#diff-6214891477a43f04e46fe559080efdfba4e6aa8cc345dc5ecc906820af9a9234L109).

This is the first part of simplifying license state management in scaling mode. Next we'll add an `onLicenseRenewed` callback to the SDK and then do away with `onFeatureChange` altogether.

title: Update LmChatXAiGrok.node.ts
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the “Argument not supported on this model: presencePenalty” error when using the xAI Grok Chat Model with `grok-3-mini` or `grok-3-mini-fast`. Previously, even when `presencePenalty` was left at its default of `0`, the parameter was still sent in the request body and caused a 400 Bad Request from the xAI API. With this change, we now conditionally remove `presencePenalty` from the options object whenever it remains unset (i.e. equals `0`), preventing the unsupported-argument error and restoring normal Grok mini model usage.

## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts

Instead of:

```js
$set: { key: { nested: 1 } }
```

```js
$set: { 'key.nested': 1 }
```

To update only the `nested` field without losing other data inside `key`.

title: feat(core): Update data model for Evaluations (no-changelog)
body:
## Summary

This PR updates the data model for the Evaluations feature.
In short, new design differs from the previous iteration in the following key aspects:
- There's no concept of Test Definition anymore
- Process of 'setting up evaluation' happens in a workflow itself (by adding specific nodes)
- Test Runs are now related to a Workflow entity, not Test Definition
- There's no concept of Test Metric as well, metrics configuration happens in a special Evaluation nodes added to a workflow
- Node mocking feature is out of scope for now, might be re-implemented again in the future
- Previously past executions played the role of test cases source. Now test cases would be provided by the Evaluation Trigger. Concept of 'past execution' is obsolete now

To keep the PR size manageble we isolated only the following changes as part of this PR:
- DB migrations
- Removing obsolete entities
- Patching the Test Runner and corresponding API controllers to not fail the build (Test Runner is not functional now, changes to the logic will follow in a separate PR)
- Patching tests
- It was a good occasion to remove obsolete counters `failedCases`, `totalCases` and `passedCases` from Test Run entity. They've been replaced by storing full details of each `TestCaseExecution`

title: fix(core): Resolve Webhook registration for API-created workflows
body:
## Summary

This PR addresses a critical issue where Webhook nodes within workflows created and activated via the n8n API failed to correctly register their production Webhook URLs. This misregistration led to `404 Not Found` or `500 Internal Server Error` responses when attempting to trigger these webhooks. Additionally, the n8n UI would display a randomly generated UUID path for these webhooks until the workflow was manually saved.

The core of the fix involves ensuring the correct initialization, setting, and persistence of essential webhook parameters (`parameters.path` and `node.webhookId`) to the database during workflow activation. This is achieved through:

1.  **Enhanced `active-workflow-manager.ts` logic**:
    *   Ensuring `node.webhookId` and `node.parameters.path` are set (typically to `node.id`) if not already defined for webhook nodes.
    *   Implementing reliable state comparison using `lodash.cloneDeep` before saving workflow entities to accurately detect changes in node parameters and `webhookId`.
    *   Correctly flagging `workflow.staticData.nodesParametersChanged = true` when modifications occur, forcing a database update.
    *   Applying `lodash.cloneDeep` when loading workflow data (`nodes`, `connections`, `staticData`, `settings`) to prevent unintended modifications to cached entities and ensure accurate comparisons.
    *   More immediate calls to `webhookService.populateCache()` after webhook data is stored and relevant database entities are updated to ensure cache coherency.

2.  **Standardized Webhook Path Handling**:
    *   Refined `getNodeWebhookPath` in `n8n/packages/workflow/src/NodeHelpers.ts` to consistently generate webhook paths, primarily based on `node.webhookId` (which is set to `node.id`).
    *   Corrected path comparison logic in `executeWebhook` within `n8n/packages/cli/src/webhooks/live-webhooks.ts` by normalizing paths (e.g., removing trailing slashes) before comparison to reliably match incoming requests to stored `IWebhookData`.

These changes ensure that webhook URLs are generated predictably, persisted correctly, and looked up reliably, resolving the 404/500 errors.

**How to Test:**

1.  **Manual API cURL/Postman Test**:
    *   Using the API, create a simple workflow containing a Webhook node (e.g., named "WebhookTrigger", HTTP method GET) followed by another node (e.g., NoOp).
    *   Activate this workflow via the API.
    *   Retrieve the workflow details via API to find the Webhook node's `id`.
    *   Construct the production Webhook URL. According to the corrected logic, this should typically be `YOUR_N8N_URL/webhook/NODE_ID` (e.g., `http://localhost:5678/webhook/abcdef123456` if `NODE_ID` is `abcdef123456`).
    *   Send a GET request to this constructed URL using `curl` or Postman.
    *   **Expected Result**: A `200 OK` response (or the response configured in the NoOp node if the Webhook node's `responseMode` is set to wait for downstream execution). No 404 or 500 errors should occur.

2.  **n8n UI Verification**:
    *   Open the n8n UI and navigate to the workflow that was created and activated via the API in the previous step.
    *   Inspect the Webhook node. The "Production URL" displayed in the UI should now consistently match the path based on the node's ID (e.g., `YOUR_N8N_URL/webhook/NODE_ID`), not a random UUID.

title: fix(Google Drive Node): Incorrect MIME type when uploading files on cloud
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

Update the Google Drive Node to pass in the custom header specifying the MIME type when doing a [resumable upload](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/manage-uploads#initial-request). 

When `N8N_DEFAULT_BINARY_DATA_MODE` is `default`, the binary data is a `Buffer`, so it gets sent as a [single request](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/a1ee96d5605e28c36283f11b741501349dcf39f8/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/Drive/v2/actions/file/upload.operation.ts#L101), where `Content-Type` is specified correctly, whereas if `N8N_DEFAULT_BINARY_DATA_MODE` is `filesystem`, binary data gets sent in 2MB chunks and the [initial request](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/a1ee96d5605e28c36283f11b741501349dcf39f8/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/Drive/v2/actions/file/upload.operation.ts#L120) needs to have the `X-Upload-Content-Type` header set, specifying the MIME type. This explains why this was discovered on the cloud version

title: fix(core): Load insights module on webhook instance to save insights on webhook workflows
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

Currently, only main instances load the insights module and listen to `workflowExecuteAfter` hook. 
The problem is, when using webhook servers, those webhook instances listen to webhooks, enqueue the job, asynchronously waits for it to finish and run the `workflowExecuteAfter` hook. The main instance never run the hooks, and thus the insights module never catches the workflow execution to save the insights data.

So in the current state of how the webhook instance work, we need to load the insights module on webhook instances for webhook triggered workflow to save insights.

I tested this with webhook triggered workflow, as well as workflow with a wait node that resumes on webhook call (although in that case, wait resuming is fired by the main instance, which then catches the job success, so it was already working before this PR).

title: feat(editor): Use resource locator at Simple Vector Store memory key and allow cross workflow use
body:
## Summary

This PR changes `Simple Vector Store` to use the Resource Locator component instead of a simple string field on the memory key picker to make selecting the same vector store on multiple nodes easier.

This PR also changes the `Simple Vector Store`'s behaviour to allowing sharing of these vector stores between workflows. Previously the memory key user picks has been prefixed on the backend with `${workflowId}__` to avoid conflicts. On the new 1.2 version of the `Simple Vector Store` this prefixing has been removed, and the given is `memoryKey` is used as is, making it possible to select the same in-memory vector store on multiple workflows.

To support creating new value on the `ResourceLocator` component support for this was added - previously something similar was done on [WorkflowSelectorParameterInput](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/components/WorkflowSelectorParameterInput/WorkflowSelectorParameterInput.vue) component, but now it is supported for any nodes rendering `type: resourceLocator` fields by providing the extra `typeOptions` and methods.

This clip showcases the new picker &using the in-memory vector store on another workflow.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e5a565e-a2c0-45ba-b78d-318712695a70

If user doesn't touch the key picker the default value is used - but this is now shared between workflows using the new 1.2 `Simple Vector Store` nodes. Old 1.1 versions of this node will still use workflow scoped separated vector stores with the default.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06700465-e887-4887-b0f1-d22041d248f8

Using empty name for the store is treated as default value.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d100ae44-8c08-4540-bf35-4fe80c85f467

Old <=1.1 `Simple Vector Store` nodes still scope the vector stores they create, but new 1.2 version vector stores can take them into use - they show up with the workflow ID prefix on the list. 1.1 version nodes cannot take vector stores created by >1.2 version nodes into use, users should upgrade their nodes instead or use the vector store created by the older node on the new one.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/27efe865-3d38-42c2-a05b-b827e3ec449e

title: fix(core): Load config early to fix `N8N_CONFIG_FILES`
body:
## Summary

The move to `@n8n/db` altered module loading order, so now the `typeorm` decorators in `packages/@n8n/db/src/entities/abstract-entity.ts` are being evaluated before `packages/cli/src/config/index.ts`. Specifically, those decorators are reading `GlobalConfig.database.type` _before_ we've loaded `database.type` from the file specified by `N8N_CONFIG_FILES`, leading those decorators to stay with the default value `sqlite` and so wrongly choose column types and timestamp syntax when the database type is not `sqlite` when set via `N8N_CONFIG_FILES`.

```
Data type "datetime" in "AnnotationTagEntity.createdAt" is not supported by "postgres" database.
```

This PR loads the config early to have all values ready in time for the `typeorm` decorators. `N8N_CONFIG_FILES` is deprecated and will be removed in v2, but it's still in use.

title: fix(editor): Fix partial chat executions
body:
## Summary

This PR addresses two bugs related to Chat Trigger nodes:

1.  **Incorrect Partial Execution with Chat Trigger:**
    *   **Bug:** When partially executing a workflow, submitting a message in the chat modal would only run the Chat Trigger itself, not the intended sequence of nodes up to the selected one.
    *   **Fix:** Modified `ManualExecutionService` and `WorkflowExecute` to correctly propagate and use `triggerToStartFrom` data for initializing partial executions. `useRunWorkflow` was updated to accurately determine `startNodes`, ensuring the correct execution path is built when a chat trigger is involved.

2.  **Phantom Item in Chat Trigger Output:**
    *   **Bug:** A phantom empty item could appear in a Chat Trigger's output if it was executed directly (i.e., being both the `destinationNode` and `triggerToStartFrom`).
    *   **Fix:** `ManualExecutionService` now avoids unnecessarily recreating the node execution stack if the `destinationNode` is the chat trigger itself, instead using the direct trigger data.

**Key Changes:**
*   **`ManualExecutionService`**: Improved handling of `triggerToStartFrom`, especially when `startNodes` are initially empty for partial runs or when the destination is the trigger itself.
*   **`WorkflowExecute`**: Now accepts and utilizes `triggerToStartFrom.data` to initialize the execution stack.
*   **`useRunWorkflow` (editor-ui)**: Refined `startNodes` determination logic, particularly when a Chat Trigger is the `destinationNode`, to ensure correct data sourcing and prevent duplication.

title: feat(editor): Improve manual description in nodes as tools
body:
## Summary

This PR enhances the way manual descriptions are generated for nodes used as AI tools. It introduces a more descriptive and context-aware approach for generating tool descriptions that better reflect the actual functionality of nodes.

## What's Changed

### Behavior Details

- **Existing nodes**: For nodes already set up with the default description, they will keep it to avoid breaking existing workflows
- **Updates**: Descriptions will only be updated automatically when opening the node and changing the resource or operation
- **New nodes**: For newly created nodes, the description will be automatically generated
- **Manual edits**: If the user updates the description manually, it will stop being updated automatically

### New Helper Functions

Added two new utility functions in `NodeHelpers.ts`:

- `makeDescription()`: Generates human-readable descriptions for nodes based on their parameters and type definition
    - Formats generated:
        - `{action} in {displayName}` - when operation has a defined action (e.g., "Create a new user in HTTP Request")
        - `{operation} {resource} in {displayName}` - when resource and operation exist but action is missing (e.g., "create user in HTTP Request")
- Node's default description - as fallback when resource or operation is missing

- `getToolDescription()`: Determines when tool descriptions should be updated and calculates the new description

### Updates to Node Settings Component

- Modified `NodeSettings.vue` to automatically update the tool description when parameters change

title: AI Agent context option to implement the classical RAG approach
body:
## Summary

The context option makes it easy to apply the classic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach using the AI Agent node. Unlike vector stores or other databases used as tools that the model may choose to call when needed, the context option allows you to attach relevant information to every user prompt explicitly, regardless of the model’s internal decision-making. This helps make agent behavior more consistent and reduces the risk of hallucinations.

A key feature of the context option is that it adds context only to the user’s latest message right before sending it to the model. This context isn’t saved in the conversation history, so it doesn’t fill up the model’s context window or waste tokens. By adding context only to the last user prompt, we ensure the model gets useful information while keeping token usage efficient.

## Why This Option Is Needed

I was building a virtual consultant for a company website and wanted two things: accurate answers from our vector store and low token costs. When I tested cheaper, smaller models like `gpt-4o-mini `or `gemini-2.0-flash`, they gave correct answers to the first question but then ignored the vector store on subsequent queries—hallucinating data instead. I tried system prompts to force them to query the vector database for every company-related question, but nothing worked.

By contrast, larger models such as ` gpt-4o` followed the instructions, used the vector store correctly, and returned accurate results—but at more than sixteen times the token cost of `gpt-4o-mini`. It didn’t make sense to pay so much extra just to ensure reliable tool usage.

What I needed was a way to supply relevant context on every prompt—regardless of the model’s internal decision-making—without bloating the conversation history and wasting tokens. This issue is common when building consultant-style agents, so I’ve proposed this context option in the PR.

## Сompliance with n8n contribution requirements

- [x] Description of the option is added to the description.ts.
- [x] Unit tests for new option is added to `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/agents/Agent/test/ToolsAgent.test.ts`.
- [x] Sample workflow files added: `cypress/fixtures/aiAssistant/workflows/context_option_test_workflow.json` and `context_option_use_case_workflow.json`.

title: fix(editor): Don't render `now` when `startedAt` is `null`
body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

Executions can fail before they were started in queue mode. This happens when the worker looses the connection to postgres, but not to redis.
Then fetching or updating the execution fails, the error gets propagated to the main instance which marks the execution as failed. Then the execution won't have `startedAt` set.

This leads to the executions appearing as always new. Additionally they block all other executions in the executions list because `startedAt: null` is considered larger than a date and thus comes first when sorted descendingly.
This was dubbed "ghost executions" by some customers, because they assumed the executions would continue running.

title: BigQuery Node: Prevent infinite loop in BigQuery executeQuery with contin…
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a bug in the BigQuery executeQuery node that caused an infinite loop when:

- A query job was queued (e.g. using wildcard tables),
- The job failed with an error,
- The “Continue On Fail” option was enabled.

The root cause was that errored jobs were not removed from the polling queue, resulting in an endless while loop. This fix ensures such jobs are added to the completedJobs array, allowing the loop to exit cleanly.

How to test:

1. Configure a BigQuery node with a query that triggers a queued job (e.g. using * in table names).
2. Enable "Continue On Fail".
3. Provide an intentionally invalid query that results in a job-level error.
4. Observe that the node no longer gets stuck and the error is handled properly.

body:
## Summary

<!--
Describe what the PR does and how to test.
Photos and videos are recommended.
-->

This fixes a race condition that allows creating more projects than the license allows.
This is fixed by using a serializable transaction.
This does not fix it for the legacy sqlite driver, since the driver does not work well with transactions (can lead to data loss). This is not an issue though since that this driver is only used by the community edition and that edition does not allow creating team projects at all.

Additionally it refactors the ProjectService to use LicenseState instead of License.

    *   The deployment script `deploy-cloud-run.sh` has been updated to be non-interactive and to utilize environment variables for configuration, making it suitable for CI/CD environments.

title: fix(editor): Issue with context menu disabling most options when importing template
body:
## Summary

When creating a new workflow from a template, right-clicking on nodes shows most context menu options disabled. This issue occurs specifically in the following flow:

1. User clicks "get started with n8n cloud" → redirected to `https://app.n8n.cloud/register?templateId=1747`
2. After redirection to user instance at `https://[instance].app.n8n.cloud/templates/1747/setup`
3. For templates without credential requirements → redirects to `https://[instance].app.n8n.cloud/workflow/new?templateId=1750`
4. When the workflow renders, right-clicking on node shows most context menu options disabled

### Root Cause
The `ContextMenu.vue` component relies on the `useContextMenu()` composable, which uses the `isReadOnly` computed property to determine which options are enabled:

```typescript
const  isReadOnly = computed(
    () =>
        sourceControlStore.preferences.branchReadOnly ||
        uiStore.isReadOnlyView ||
        !workflowPermissions.value.update ||
        workflowsStore.workflow.isArchived,
);
```

When creating a workflow from a template, we weren't making the workflow shareable (basically adding all scopes for the role), causing `!workflowPermissions.value.update` to return true, which disabled most context menu actions.

### Solution

Created a new combined method `getNewWorkflowDataAndMakeShareable` that combines getting new workflow data and making it shareable, as these two are frequently used together.

### Testing

1. Import a template by going to `http://localhost:8080/templates/1747/setup`. Template ID does't matter as long as it's a valid one.
2. Right-click on any node in the workflow.
3. Verify that context menu options are properly enabled.
4. Test various context menu actions to ensure they function correctly.
5. Verify manually created workflows still function as expected.

### Before:

### Now:

This PR implements support for partial execution for all tool nodes. To support all kinds of tools this adds a new hidden node that is able to call it's connected tool (or toolkit) with a specified query and optionally tool name for toolkit executions. ### Editor-UI
- Refactored existing solution to send request parameter instead of overwriting parameters on the nodes directly
- Modal supports specific cases for choosing the tool in a MCPClient and sending queries to VectorStores and Code Tools

title: fix(core): Prioritize workflow execution with existing execution data on worker
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the issue of wait node not working in queue mode and OFFLOAD_MANUAL_EXECUTIONS_TO_WORKERS=true on manual execution.
What happens is that the worker re-executes the flow from the manual trigger, and re-executes the wait node, thus leading to an infinite wait / resume / wait / resume / ... loop.

Indeed, manual executions when running in the workers are always "restarted" from the manual execution context: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/n8n%401.91.2/packages/cli/src/scaling/job-processor.ts#L173

But wait resume workflow are a special kind of manual executions that need to keep certain execution data to resume properly:
- the `waitTill` is necessary for the execution engine to know to proceed with the wait node directly (and disable it to prevent re-execution)
- the nodeExecutionStack is necessary to start from the wait node directly
See: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/n8n%401.91.2/packages/core/src/execution-engine/workflow-execute.ts#L1322

I decided to fix that by applying the same "priority" logic on workflow execution from the job processor than for the runMainProcess (without worker): https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/n8n%401.91.2/packages/cli/src/workflow-runner.ts#L271
- if there is the necessary existing executionData, just run from that (I check the existence of `execution.data?.executionData` because just `execution.data` is not enough to run from it)
- otherwise, run manually as before

I ran some manual tests, but I'm not 100% sure about the potential regressions with this logic change.

body:
## Summary

This PR adds OAuth2 compatibility for TikTok by introducing support for a custom `code_challenge` format (`hex`) in the OAuth2 credential implementation. TikTok's PKCE flow requires the code challenge to be in `hex` format instead of the default `base64`.

Additionally, a new credential `TikTok OAuth2 API` was created that leverages this functionality, allowing users to authenticate with TikTok's API using the correct PKCE configuration.

### How to test:

* Create a new TikTok OAuth2 credential.
* Confirm the `code_challenge` generated uses `hex` encoding.
* Complete the TikTok OAuth2 flow successfully.

This PR enhances the folder retrieval endpoint to return the path from a folder to the root, allowing clients to display breadcrumb navigation or full folder paths in the UI.

title: fix(editor): Fix sticky button disappearing on window resize
body:
## Summary

The bug occurred because the component was calculating the wrapper's bounding rectangle only once during initial mounting. When the window was resized, the actual DOM element position would change, but the stored boundary values remained the same. This created a mismatch between where the component "thought" the button was and its actual position, causing the visibility detection to fail after any window resize.

The solution:
- Extracts the boundary calculation logic into a separate `setWrapperRect()` function
- Adds a window resize event listener that recalculates the button's boundary rectangle

title: refactor(core): Overhaul community packages installation code
body:
## Summary

This PR changes how we install community nodes so that
1. We don't do an `npm init` anymore. we [added](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/3934) that code to handle issues with versions of node that we haven't supported in a few years now.
2. We don't need to do an `access` check when trying to ensure that the `downloadFolder` exists. it's an unnecessary call that be avoided simply by switch to `mkdir -p`.
3. We use some explicit flags with `npm install` to ensure that
    - we do not install any dev, peer, or optional dependency
    - we so not symlink any `bin` scripts
    - every package is installed in an isolated manner, so that they all get their own copies of their dependencies
    - `audit` and `fund` steps are disabled, to speed up the installation process

title: refactor(core): Tear down `OrchestrationService`
body:
## Summary

As part of the extensions project, this PR tears down the legacy `OrchestrationService` to disentangle `Publisher` and `Subscriber` so pubsub functionality can later be used by both `cli` and `@n8n/sdk`.

Notes:

- `OrchestrationService.shutdown` had a TODO to use the `@OnShutdown` decorator instead of using it already, like `Publisher` and `Subscriber`. I assume this is because the `@OnShutdown` decorator makes the order implicit and so it's not trivial to ensure the correct order here, so I decided not to use the decorator either for now. Let's do this separately.
- In future we should ensure orchestration-related services are imported only if needed. Currently we're already importing `Publisher` elsewhere e.g. in `ActiveWorkflowManager` regardless of execution mode, so there is no benefit in preserving in this PR the conditional import that `OrchestrationService` was doing.
- `WorkflowService` had an orchestration service leftover from when we [used to send an event there](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/7643/files#diff-7d67ec9cff33725c9ad95818dd85427cbe23d9343e50da7d07e19af565e526f7R378).

title: refactor(core): Move all repositories to `@n8n/db`
body:
## Summary

As part of the extensions project, this PR moves all repositories to `@n8n/db` to give both `cli` and `@n8n/sdk` access to them.

- `packages/cli/src/databases/repositories/__tests__` were kept in place because many of these tests require integration test utils which still live in `cli`. In future we'll have an `@n8n/integration-test-utils` package.
- `SettingsRepository.dismissBanner` was mutating the legacy `config` object, so I had to refactor it so that `OwnerController.dismissBanner` does this instead.
- `TestDefinitionRepository` required `ForbiddenError` and `TestRunRepository` required `NotFoundError` - these errors were changed to `UserError` and `UnexpectedError` respectively, because they are part of a large error hierarchy still living in `cli` and because repositories should not throw response-related errors.
- Many repositories are still entangled with `ListQuery.Options`. Since this is one small type, I decided to duplicate it into `@n8n/db` and add a deprecation label to stop it from being used anymore.
- `truncate` in the test DB relies on dynamic imports, which after the move started causing typeorm to throw `EntityMetadataNotFoundError` during truncation, even though all entities were registered as usual. I chalked this up to dynamic imports working differently across package boundaries. Hence I refactored `truncate` to take entity names and use those to find the repositories and truncate their tables.
- The `EntityName` type temporarily hardcodes the insights entity names. Later this week I'll work on dynamically loading module entities.

> [!NOTE]
> Please don't be discouraged by the size! What matters is the above - the rest are lintfixed imports and renamed typechecked args which need no review.
